--- Page 4 ---
AURORA

Dawn in its Inception,
that is:
the Root or Mother
of
Philosophy, Astrology
and Theology,
from true Ground,
Or
Description of Nature,
how everything has been
and came to be in the beginning:
how Nature and the Elements came into being as creations,
also concerning both qualities, Evil and Good; from whence all things
have their origin, and how they now stand and work, and how
it will be at the end of this time: also how God's and
Hell's Kingdom is constituted, and how humans
became creatures in each.
All set forth from true Ground, diligently, in recognition
of the Spirit in God's will.
By
Jacob Böhme,
in Görlitz, in the Year of Christ 1612.
at the age of 37 years, Tuesday in Pentecost.
All newly revised, and diligently corrected and improved
according to the Author's own Manuscript.

New Edition.

Berlin and Leipzig, 1780.
by Christian Ulrich Ringmacher.

--- Page 5 ---
<meta>Continuing from the title page of the 1780 edition of Aurora, which established Jacob Böhme’s foundational work on the origins of nature, the qualities of good and evil, and the kingdom of God.</meta>

# Preface
### of the
# AUTHOR
### concerning this book
### to the favorable reader.

->Favorable Reader,<-

1. I compare the whole of philosophy, astrology, and theology <note>original: *Philosophiam, Astrologiam, und Theologiam*</note>, together with their mother, to a precious tree that grows in a beautiful pleasure garden.

2. Now the earth, in which the tree stands, continually gives sap to the tree, from which the tree possesses its living quality <term>quality: Böhme uses "Qualität" to describe the inherent power, property, or essential nature of a thing</term>; the tree itself grows from the sap of the earth, becoming large and spreading its branches.

3. Now, just as the earth works upon the tree with its power so that it may grow and increase, so the tree continually works with its branches to the best of its ability, desiring to always bring forth much good fruit.

4. But if the tree brings forth little fruit—and that which it does bear is quite small, maggoty, and worm-eaten—the fault lies not with the tree's will, as if it deliberately desired to bear bad fruit (since it is a precious tree of good quality); rather, the fault lies in the fact that great cold, heat, mildew, caterpillars, and vermin often fall upon it. For the quality in the depths, cast down from the stars, corrupts it so that it produces little good fruit.

5. Yet the tree has this nature: the larger and older it becomes, the sweeter the fruit it bears. In its youth, it bears little fruit, for this is caused by the rough and wild nature of the soil and the excess moisture within the tree; and though it may blossom beautifully, yet [the blossoms] fall

yet in the process of growing, its apples mostly fall off, unless it happens to stand in a very good field.

6. Now the tree also possesses a good, sweet quality within itself, but against it are three others that are contrary: the bitter, the sour, and the harsh <term>harsh: Böhme’s term "herbe" refers to an astringent, sharp, or contracted state, often associated with the first stage of creation or the "cold" fire</term>. Now, as the tree is, so also its fruits will be, until the sun works upon them and makes them sweet, so that they receive a lovely taste; and its fruits must endure through rain, wind, and storms.

7. But when the tree becomes old, so that its branches wither and the sap can no longer rise to the heights, then many green shoots sprout out from around the trunk at the bottom, and finally even from the root, and they reveal the old tree as it once was—a beautiful green shoot and little tree—before it became quite old. For nature, or the sap, defends itself until the trunk becomes completely dry; then it is cut down and burned in the fire.

### Now note what I have indicated with this parable:

8. The garden of this tree signifies the world; the field signifies nature; the trunk of the tree signifies the stars; the branches signify the elements; the fruits that grow on this tree signify human beings; the sap in the tree signifies the clear Deity <term>Deity: Böhme often uses "Gottheit" (Godhead) to refer to the pure, underlying divine essence that flows through all creation</term>. Now human beings have been made out of nature, the stars, and the elements; but God the Creator rules in everything, just as the sap does in the whole tree.

9. Nature, however, has two qualities within itself until the judgment of God: one that is lovely, heavenly, and holy; and one that is fierce, hellish, and thirsty <note>original: "durstige," implying a dry, consuming longing or the parched nature of the "wrath" of God</note>.

10. Now the good quality always works with full diligence to bring forth good fruit; therein the Holy Spirit rules and provides sap and life. The evil quality also wells up and drives with full diligence to always bring forth evil fruit; for this, the Devil provides the sap and hellish wages.

11. Now both of these are in the tree of nature, and human beings are made from the tree and live in this world in this garden between both in great danger; and upon them fall sometimes sunshine, sometimes rain, wind, and snow.

---

<page-num>VII</page-num>
<header>of the Author.</header>
<sig>* 3</sig>
<meta>catchword: There-</meta>

12. That is, if a person raises their spirit into the Deity, then the Holy Spirit wells up and qualifies <term>qualifies: "qualificiret" in Böhme’s usage means to operate, interact, or take on a specific character or "quality"</term> within them; but if they let their spirit sink into this world, into the lust of evil, then the Devil and the hellish sap well up and rule within them.

13. Just as the apple on the tree becomes maggoty and worm-eaten when frost, heat, and mildew fall upon it, and it easily falls off and perishes: so it is also with the human being when they let the Devil rule within them with his poison.

14. Now, just as good and evil well up, rule, and exist in nature, so they do also in the human being. But the human being is God’s child, whom He has made from the best kernel of nature, to rule in the good and to overcome the evil. Although evil clings to them—just as in nature evil clings to the good—they can nevertheless overcome the evil; if they raise their spirit into God, the Holy Spirit wells up within them and helps them to victory.

15. Just as the good quality in nature is powerful enough to triumph over the evil—for it is and comes from God, and the Holy Spirit is the ruler within it—so also is the fierce quality powerful to triumph in wicked souls, for the Devil is a powerful ruler in the fierceness <term>fierceness: "Grimmigkeit" is a central concept for Böhme, referring to the wrathful, dark, or destructive aspect of nature and God</term> and is an eternal prince of the same.

16. But the human being threw themselves into the fierceness through the fall of Adam and Eve, so that evil clings to them; otherwise their wellspring and impulse would be in the good alone. But now it is in both, and it is as St. Paul says: "Do you not know that to whom you present yourselves as slaves in obedience, you are that one’s slaves whom you obey, whether of sin leading to death, or of obedience to God leading to righteousness?" Romans 6, verse 16 <note>original: "Röm. 6. vers 16"</note>.

17. Because the human being has the impulse in both, they may reach for whichever they will; for they live in this world between both, and both qualities—evil and good—are within them. Whichever one the human being enters into <note>original: "wallet," literally "boils" or "moves within"</note>, with that one they will be clothed, whether in holy or hellish power.

18. For Christ says: "My Father will give the Holy Spirit to those who ask Him for it," Luke 11, verse 13 <note>original: "Lucä 11. vers 13"</note>. Furthermore, God has commanded good to the human being and forbidden evil, and He still daily allows preaching, calling, and shouting, to admonish the human being toward the good.

<summary>Böhme uses the allegory of a tree to explain the dual nature of the world and humanity, where the "sap" of the Godhead flows through all things, but individuals must choose between the holy and fierce qualities. He interprets the human condition as being caught between these two opposing forces, emphasizing the power of the Holy Spirit to help the soul overcome evil.</summary>
<keywords>allegory of the tree, qualities, fierceness, Grimmigkeit, Holy Spirit, the Fall, dualism, nature of man, choice, salvation</keywords>

<meta>Continuing from the previous page, Böhme is concluding his point that while God does not desire evil, the human condition is caught between two opposing forces within nature.</meta>

<page-num>VIII</page-num>
<header>Preface</header>

By this one clearly recognizes that God does not desire evil, but rather wills that His kingdom come and His will be done, on earth as it is in heaven.

19. However, because man has been poisoned by sin, the **wrathful quality** <term>wrathful quality: Böhme’s term "grimme Qualität" refers to the harsh, destructive, or "dark" side of nature that exists in tension with God’s love</term> as well as the good quality rules within him. Now half-dead and suffering from great lack of understanding, man can no longer recognize God his Creator, nor nature and its workings. Therefore, Nature has applied its highest diligence from the beginning until today—and to this end God has given His Holy Spirit—so that at all times she has birthed and prepared wise, holy, and sensible people who have learned to recognize Nature as well as God their Creator. These people have always been a light to the world through their writing and teaching. In this way, God has prepared His Church on earth for His eternal praise; against this, the Devil has raged and stormed, spoiling many a noble branch through the **wrath** in nature, of which he is prince and god.

20. When Nature has often prepared a learned, sensible person with beautiful gifts, the Devil has applied his highest diligence to seduce that person into fleshly lusts, into pride, and into the desire to be rich and powerful. In this way, the Devil has ruled within him, and the **wrathful quality** has overcome the good. From such a person's understanding, art, and wisdom, heresy and error have grown, which mocked the truth and caused great error on earth; such a person has been a good army commander for the Devil.

21. For the evil quality in nature has struggled with the good from the beginning and continues to do so, exalting itself and spoiling many a noble fruit in the mother’s womb. This is clearly seen first with Cain and Abel, who came from one mother’s womb. From the womb, Cain was a despiser of God and proud, whereas Abel was a humble, God-fearing man. One sees this also with the three sons of Noah, as well as with Abraham with Isaac and Ishmael, but especially with Isaac with Esau and Jacob, who pushed and struggled against each other in the mother’s womb. Therefore God also says: *Jacob I have loved, and Esau I have hated.* <note>original: "Jacob habe ich geliebet, und Esau gehasset." citing Genesis 25:23</note> It is nothing other than that both

<meta>catchword: both</meta>

<page-num>IX</page-num>
<header>of the Author.</header>

both qualities in nature have struggled violently with one another.

22. For when God was surging <term>surging: Böhme uses "wallen" to describe the active, boiling, or moving presence of divine or natural forces</term> in nature at that time and wished to reveal Himself to the world through the pious Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, and wished to prepare for Himself a Church on earth for His glory and majesty, then wickedness and its prince, Lucifer, also surged in nature. Because there was both evil and good within man, both qualities could rule in him; for this reason, an evil and a good man were born of one mother at the same time.

23. This is also clearly seen in the first world, as well as in the second until the end of our time: how the heavenly and hellish kingdoms in nature have always struggled with each other and stood in great labor, like a woman in childbirth.

24. This is seen most clearly in Adam and Eve, for there a tree grew up in Paradise of both qualities, evil and good. There Adam and Eve were to be tested to see if they could endure in the good quality, in the angelic kind and form. For the Creator forbade Adam and Eve from eating of the fruit, but the evil quality in nature struggled with the good and brought Adam and Eve into a desire to eat of both. Therefore, they immediately received an animal-like kind and form, and ate of both evil and good; they were forced to multiply and live in an animal-like way, and many a noble branch born of them was spoiled.

25. Afterward, one sees how God worked in nature when the holy fathers were born in the first world, such as Abel, Seth, Enosh, Cainan, Mahalalel, Jared, Enoch, Methuselah, Lamech, and the holy Noah: these proclaimed the name of the Lord to the world and preached repentance, for the Holy Spirit worked within them.

26. On the other hand, the hellish god also worked in nature and birthed mockers and despisers, first Cain and his descendants. It went with the first world as it does with a young tree that grows, turns green, and blossoms beautifully, but brings forth little good fruit because of its wild nature. Thus, nature in the first world brought forth little good fruit, even though it blossomed beautifully in worldly art and opulence; for that could not take hold of the Holy Spirit, who worked in nature then just as He does now.

He argues that both divine and hellish forces work through nature to influence human history and the development of the soul.</summary>

27. Therefore God spoke: *it repents me that I have made man* <note>original: "es reuet mich, daß ich die Menschen gemacht habe" — quoting Genesis 6:6</note> and He stirred up Nature so that all flesh died that lived upon the dry land, down to the very root and stem, which remained standing. With this, He fertilized and prepared the wild tree so that it might bear better fruit. But when it turned green again, it soon brought forth both good and evil fruits among the sons of Noah. There, mockers and despisers of God were soon found again, and hardly a good branch grew on the tree that brought forth holy, good fruits; the other branches bore and brought forth the wild heathens.

28. But when God saw that man was thus dead in his understanding, He moved Nature once again and showed humanity how both evil and good existed within it, so that they might flee the evil and live in the good; and He let fire fall from Nature and ignited Sodom and Gomorrah as a terrifying example to the world.

29. However, as the blindness of men gained the upper hand and they would not allow themselves to be taught by God’s Spirit, He gave them laws and teachings on how they should conduct themselves, and He confirmed these with wonders and signs so that the knowledge of the true God might not be extinguished.

30. But even with this, the light did not wish to come to the day, for the darkness and **wrath** <term>wrath: "Grimmigkeit," Böhme’s term for the harsh, rigorous, or "dark" fire of nature</term> in Nature resisted it, and the Prince of that darkness ruled with great power.

31. But when the Tree of Nature reached its "middle age," it began to bear several mild, sweet fruits, indicating that from then on it would bear lovely fruit. For then the holy prophets were born from the sweet branch of the tree, who taught and preached of the Light which would in the future overcome the **wrath** in Nature.

32. Also, among the heathens, a light in Nature arose so that they recognized Nature and its operation—though this was only a light within wild Nature and not yet the Holy Light. For wild Nature was not yet overcome, and Light and Darkness wrestled with one another for a long time until the Sun rose and compelled this tree with its heat so that it bore lovely, sweet fruits.

33. That is, until the Prince of Light came from the heart of God and became a man in Nature, and wrestled in His human body, by the power of the Divine Light, within wild Nature.

<meta>catchword: 34. The-</meta>

<column-break/>

<page-num>xi</page-num>
<header>of the Author.</header>

34. That same princely and royal branch grew up in Nature and became a tree in Nature, spreading its branches from the **East** to the **West** <note>original: "von Orient bis in Occident"</note> and embracing all of Nature. It wrestled and fought with the **wrath** that was in Nature and with the Prince of that wrath, until it overcame and triumphed as a King of Nature, and took the Prince of Wrath prisoner in his own house, as in Psalm 68.

35. When this happened, many thousands of legions of precious, sweet little twigs grew out of the royal tree that had grown in Nature; these all had the scent and taste of the precious tree. And even though rain, snow, hail, and storms fell upon them, so that many a little twig was torn and struck from the tree, still other twigs kept growing. For the **wrath** in Nature and its Prince stirred up great storms with hail, thunder, lightning, and rain, so that many magnificent twigs were indeed often torn from the sweet and good tree. But those same twigs tasted so lovely, sweet, and full of joy that no tongue of man or angel can express it; for they had great power and virtue within them, serving for the health of the wild heathens. Whichever heathen ate from the twigs of this tree was delivered from the wild way of Nature in which he was born, and became a sweet twig in the precious tree, turning green in the tree and bearing precious fruits just like the royal tree.

36. Therefore many heathens ran to the precious tree where the precious twigs lay, which the Prince of Darkness had torn off with his stormy winds; and whichever heathen smelled these torn-off twigs became healthy from the wild **wrath** that was innate to him from his mother.

37. But when the Prince of Darkness saw that the heathens were scrambling for the twigs and not for the tree, and saw his great loss and damage, he ceased his storming toward the **East** and **South** <note>original: "Aufgang und Mittag"</note> and stationed a **merchant** <note>The "merchant" is likely a critique of the institutional church or clergy who Böhme believed "sold" the grace and works of the saints (the twigs) for profit</note> under the tree, who gathered up the twigs that had fallen from the precious tree.

38. And whenever the heathens came and asked for the good and powerful twigs, the merchant offered them the same...

to sell the same for money, so that he might gain **usury** from the precious tree. For this is what the Prince of **Wrath** <term>wrath: "Grimmigkeit," a key term for Böhme referring to the harsh, ego-driven, and "dark" fire within nature</term> demanded of his merchant, because the tree had grown in his land and spoiled his field.

39. Now when the heathens saw that the fruits of the precious tree were for sale for money, they ran in heaps to the **merchant**, and bought the fruit of the tree; they even came from distant islands to buy, yes, from the very ends of the world.

40. When the merchant saw that his goods were worth so much and were so pleasing, he devised a trick so that he might collect a great treasure for his master; he sent out traders into every land and had his goods offered for sale and highly praised. But he **adulterated** the goods, and sold other fruit as the good fruit—fruit that had not grown on the good tree—simply so that his master’s treasure might grow large.

41. But the heathens and all the islands and peoples who dwelt on earth had all grown out of the **wild tree**, which was both good and evil. Therefore, they were half-blind and did not see the good tree, even though it stretched out its branches from the sunrise to the sunset; otherwise, they would not have bought the false goods.

42. Because they did not know the precious tree, which nevertheless stretched its branches over them all, they all ran after the merchants and bought mixed, false goods for good ones, believing they served their health. But because they all longed so intensely for the good tree that hovered over them all, many of them became healthy through the great desire and longing they bore toward the tree. For the **scent of the tree**, which hovered over them, made them healthy from their wrath and wild birth, and not the merchant’s false goods; this lasted for a long time.

43. Now when the **Prince in the Darkness**, who is the source of wrath, malice, and perdition, saw that people were becoming healthy from his poison and wild nature through the scent of the precious tree, he became angry and planted a wild

**wild tree** toward the North <note>original: "Mitternacht" — literally "midnight," but in the geographic and mystical language of the time, this signifies the North</note>. This grew out of the wrath in nature, and he had it proclaimed: "This is the Tree of Life; whoever eats of it will become healthy and live eternally." For in the place where the wild tree grew, there was a wild spot, and the peoples there had not recognized the true light from God from the beginning until that time, and still do not recognize it today. And the tree grew on **Mount Hagar**, in the house of **Ishmael** the mocker. <note>Böhme is using a 17th-century allegorical framework here, identifying the rise of Islam with the biblical Ishmael (son of Hagar), portraying it as a "wild tree" competing with the "precious tree" of the Gospel.</note>

44. But when it was proclaimed regarding the tree: "Behold, this is the Tree of Life," the wild peoples ran to it—those who were not born of God but of wild nature—and they loved the wild tree and ate of its fruit. And the tree grew and became large from the sap of wrath in nature, and spread its branches from the North toward the East and West. The tree, however, had its source and root in wild nature, which was both evil and good; its fruit was the same.

45. But because the people of this place had all grown out of wild nature, the tree grew over them all and became so large that its branches reached into the **worthy land**, beneath the holy tree.

46. This was the reason the wild tree became so large: the people under the good tree all ran after the merchants who sold the false goods, and they ate of the false fruit, which was also evil and good, and they imagined they would become healthy through it, while they always left the holy, good, and powerful tree standing. Meanwhile, they became ever blinder, more weary, and weaker, and they could not prevent the wild tree in the North from growing. For they were far too weary and weak; they saw well enough that it was a wild, evil tree, but they were too feeble to stop its growth. If they had not run after the merchants with the false goods and eaten of the false fruit, but had instead eaten of the **precious tree**, they would have become powerful enough to resist the wild tree.

47. But because they played the harlot with the wild nature in the land of men, following their hearts' desires in hypocrisy, wild nature ruled over them, and the wild tree grew

tree grew high and wide over them, and corrupted them with its wild power.

48. Then the Prince of <term>Wrath: "Grimmigkeit," the harsh, dark, or fiery quality in nature that stands in opposition to divine light</term> in nature gave the tree its power, to ruin the people who ate of the trader's wild fruit. Because they forsook the Tree of Life and sought their own cleverness—just as Mother Eve did in Paradise—their innate "own-quality" <note>Self-centered nature or ego</note> ruled over them, and they fell into such a "strong delusion," as Saint Paul says in <margin>2 Thessalonians 2:11</margin> <note>original: "2 Thess. 2, 11"</note>.

49. And the Prince of Wrath stirred up war and stormy winds from the wild tree out of the **North** <note>original: "Mitternacht" (Midnight), Böhme's term for the North</note> over the nations who were not born from the wild tree; and they fell in their weariness and weakness before the tempest that came out of the wild tree.

50. And the Merchant under the good tree flattered the nations toward the **South** <note>original: "Mittag" (Midday)</note> and **West** <note>original: "Abend" (Evening)</note>, and toward the North; he praised his wares highly and deceived the simple-hearted with cunning. He made the clever into his traders and shopkeepers so that they too might have their profit from it, until he brought it to the point that no one could rightly see or recognize the Holy Tree anymore, and he claimed the land as his own property.

51. Then he had it proclaimed: <margin>2 Thessalonians 2</margin> **"I am the trunk of the good tree, and I stand upon the root of the good tree; I am grafted into the Tree of Life. Buy my wares which I sell to you, and you shall be healed of your wild birth and live eternally. I have grown from the root of the good tree and have the fruit of the Holy Tree in my power; I sit upon the throne of divine power and have authority in Heaven and on Earth. Come to me and buy—"**

**"—buy from me with money the fruit of life."**

52. Then all the nations ran to him and bought and ate until they fainted. All the kings from the South, West, and North ate of the trader's fruit and lived in great impotence; for the wild tree of the North grew ever taller over them and destroyed them for a long time. And it was a miserable time on earth, such as had never been since the world began; yet the people thought it was a good time, so severely had the Merchant under the good tree blinded them.

53. But in the evening, the Mercy of God took pity on the misery and blindness of humanity and moved the good tree once more—that glorious, divine tree that bore the fruit of life. Then a branch grew out of the precious tree near the root and turned green; to it was given the sap and spirit of the tree. It spoke with human tongues and showed everyone the precious tree, and its voice resounded far into many lands.

54. Then the people ran to see and hear what was happening. There they were shown the precious and virtuous Tree of Life, of which humanity had eaten in the beginning, and they were delivered from their **wild birth**.

55. And they were greatly rejoiced and ate of the Tree of Life with great joy and refreshment. They received new strength from the true Tree of Life and sang a new song about the true Tree of Life; they were delivered from their wild birth and hated the Merchant with his shops and false wares.

56. But all those who hungered and thirsted for the Tree of Life came, even those who sat in the dust, and they ate of the Holy Tree. They were healed of their unclean birth and of the **wrath** of nature in which they had lived, and they were grafted into the Tree of Life.

57. Only the traders of the Merchant and their hypocrites—those who had practiced usury with the false wares and gathered their treasures—did not come; for they were drowned in the usury of the Merchant's **harlotry** <note>Spiritual adultery or idolatry</note> and in death.

58. Because their shame, deceit, greed, and malice were now made manifest, they became silent and stayed behind; they were ashamed to do penance for their abominations and idolatry and to go with the hungry and thirsty to the fountainhead of eternal life. 59. Now when the Merchant saw that his deceit was revealed through his false wares, he became very angry and despondent. 60. Favorable reader, this is a short report of the two qualities in nature from the beginning to the end: how two kingdoms arose from them, a heavenly and a hellish, and how they surge and strive against each other in this time, and how it will go with them in the future.

84. ...what God is, and how nature, the stars, and the elements are constituted within the essence of God; and from where all things have their origin; how heaven and earth are formed, as well as angels, men, and devils; also heaven and hell, and everything that is a created thing; and also what the two <term>qualities: Böhme uses 'Qualität' to describe an active force or 'source-spring' of being—either 'sweet' (good) or 'fierce' (evil).</term> are within nature, originating from a true foundation in the knowledge of the Spirit, and in the drive and surging of God.

85. 2. Through **Astrology**, the powers of nature, the stars, and the elements are addressed—how all creatures have emerged from them, and how these forces drive, rule, and work in everything; and how both evil and good are wrought through them in humans and animals. From this arises the fact that evil and good rule and exist in this world, and also how the kingdoms of hell and heaven consist within it.

86. It is not my intention to describe the course, location, or names of all the stars, or how they have their conjunction, opposition, or square each year, or what they effect hourly or yearly.

87. Such things have been learned over long ages by highly wise, clever, and spirited men through diligent observation, attention, deep thought, and calculation. I have not studied or learned these things, and I leave them to the scholars to handle; rather, my intention is to write according to the Spirit and the sense, and not according to outward observation.

88. 3. Through **Theology**, the Kingdom of Christ is addressed—how it is constituted, how it is set in opposition to the kingdom of hell, and how it fights and struggles against the kingdom of hell within nature; also, how humans through faith and the Spirit can overcome the kingdom of hell, triumph in divine power, and attain eternal salvation, bringing it away as a victory in the struggle. Also, how a person, through the working of the hellish quality, throws themselves into corruption, and finally, how both shall come to an end.

89. The main title: **The Day-Spring at its Rising** <note>original: "Morgenröte im Aufgang." This is the famous "Aurora," Böhme's first work. 90. I do not wish to explain this title, but rather leave it to be judged by the impartial reader who wrestles within the good quality in this world.

91. Now, when **Master Clever-wit** <note>original: "Meister Klügling," a derisive term Böhme uses for those who rely on intellectual pride rather than spiritual revelation.</note>—who is characterized by the fierce quality—comes across this book, he will hold the opposing view, just as the kingdoms of heaven and hell surge against one another. First, he will say that I have climbed much too high into the Godhead and that such a thing is not becoming of me. Second, he will say that I boast of the Holy Spirit, so I must also live accordingly and prove it with miracles. Third, he will say I do this out of a desire for fame. Fourth, he will say I am not learned enough for it. Fifth, the great simplicity of the author will greatly offend him, as is the custom of the world—to look only at what is high and to be offended by simplicity.

92. Against these biased clever-wits, I will set the Patriarchs of the first world; they were also but low and despised people, against whom the world and the devil raged and stormed. As in the time of Enoch, when the holy fathers first began to preach powerfully of the Name of the Lord; they did not ascend into heaven with their bodies and see everything with their eyes, but rather the Holy Spirit revealed itself in their spirit. Afterwards, one sees this in the second world as well with the holy Patriarchs and Prophets, who were all but simple people, and some were merely cattle-herders.

93. Also, when **Christ the Messiah**, the hero of the struggle in nature, became a man—though He was a Prince and King of men—He nevertheless kept Himself in great simplicity in this world, and was merely a common inhabitant of the world. Likewise, His Apostles were all but poor, despised fishermen and common folk. Indeed, Christ Himself thanks His heavenly Father that He had hidden these things from the clever and wise in this world and revealed them to babes. The human soul also sees such things, but in this world only piece by piece. It also often slips away from her so that she sees nothing, for the devil attacks her fiercely in the grim source <term>Grimm-Quell: Böhme’s term for the wrathful, dark, or "fierce" quality within nature and the human soul that opposes the light</term> which is in the soul, and often covers the noble mustard seed <note>A reference to the biblical "grain of mustard seed" (Matthew 13:31), representing the smallest spark of divine light or faith</note>; therefore, man must always be in struggle.

105. In such a way, in such knowledge of the spirit, I will write in this book of GOD our Father, in whom all is, and who himself is all; I will deal with how everything became distinct and creaturely <note>original: "schiedlich und creaturlich" — referring to how the unified divine essence became individual, created beings</note>, and how everything drives and moves in the entire Tree of Life.

106. Here you will see the true ground of the Godhead, and how it was one Being before the times of the world; also how the holy angels were created, and from what: also of the terrible fall of Lucifer along with his legions; also from what heaven, earth, stars, and elements came to be, as well as the metals and stones in the earth, and all creatures: How the birth of life and the physicality <term>Leiblichkeit: the state of having a body or material form</term> of all things is: also what the true heaven is, wherein GOD and his saints dwell, and what the wrath of GOD and the hellish fire is, and how everything became ignitable: in summary, what or how the Essence of all Essences <note>original: "Wesen aller Wesen" — a common mystical term for the ultimate reality or the "Being behind all beings"</note> is.

107. The first 7 chapters deal quite simply and comprehensibly with the essence of GOD and angels through parables, so that the reader might go from one step to another, finally coming into the deep sense and true ground. In the 8th chapter, the Depth in the divine essence begins, and so forth, the further one goes, the deeper it becomes: Many a species <note>original: "Species" — here meaning specific topics or types of knowledge</note> is often repeated and described ever more deeply, for the sake of the reader's, and also my own, slow comprehension.

108. But what you do not find explained enough in this book, you will find bright and clear in the 2nd and 3rd; for because of our corruption, our knowledge is piecemeal <note>original: "stückwerk" — a reference to 1 Corinthians 13:9, "For we know in part"</note>, and not all at once perfectly complete: although this book is a wonder of the world, which the holy soul will well understand.

109. Herewith I recommend the reader into the gentle and holy love of GOD.

<header>Interpretation of the Title Figure concerning the AURORA.</header>

When a twofold dawn breaks at midnight, and two suns rise at the same time; then a great glorious day is at hand, and the Bridegroom <note>The "Bridegroom" is a traditional mystical and biblical figure for Christ or the divine union between God and the soul</note> is already approaching.

Six days are appointed for labor and misery, where one may well draw breath so that life and strength may be maintained, but not rest until the evening of the sixth is passed, nor exult until the seventh has begun.

And before such a day comes, the works of all six days, from the first to the last, are gathered and brought before the eyes of the Lord; he looks through everything everywhere exactly, what is corrupted, forgotten, and neglected, so that he may measure out to each one his reward according to his labor; for in the seventh, everything that was wrought in the six days must stand in the showing <term>im Schau: being revealed or put on display for divine inspection</term>.

But so that no one may be overtaken in his day's work, the Lord measures out the short time of the earth with the heavenly compass, lets the sun stand still for a whole day, makes hours into years, and delays our short misery with his longsuffering, so that he may promote us in all things toward perfect works, and our joy on the Sabbath.

Therefore he lets the fires be announced early and calls out at this midnight: Behold, the bridegroom comes, go out to meet him. So that everyone in his office may make himself ready and keep himself prepared with his works: The servants on watch with profit <note>original: "Wucher" — in this context, the "increase" or "usury" of spiritual talents, as in the Parable of the Talents</note>, and the virgins with trimmed lamps when the Lord and Bridegroom comes; everything must be prepared and arranged, for whoever wants to gather wood on the Sabbath day, or buy oil when the Bridegroom holds the wedding in the locked castle: he will be stoned and banished with mockery into the darkness, where there is wailing and gnashing of teeth. But to prevent such a thing, he warns faithfully and says: What I say unto you, I say unto all, watch.

# **Chapter 1.**
## **Of the Investigation of the Divine Being in Nature: Of Both Qualities.**

Although flesh and blood cannot grasp the divine Being, the spirit can, when it is enlightened and ignited by God. But if one wishes to speak of God—of what God is—one must diligently weigh the powers in nature, as well as the whole of creation: the heavens and the earth, the stars and the elements, and the creatures that have come from them, as well as the holy angels, devils, and men, and even heaven and hell.

2. In such contemplation, one finds two **qualities**: a good one and an evil one, which in this world are in one another as if they were a single thing, across all powers, in stars and elements, and in all creatures. Furthermore, no creature exists in the flesh in its natural life unless it possesses both qualities within itself.

3. Here one must now consider what the word <term>Quality</term> <note>Böhme uses the word "Qualität" but connects it linguistically to "Qual" (pain/torment) and "Quelle" (source/wellspring), implying a "driving, surging source" of being.</note> means or is. A quality is the "moving-source" or the driving force of a thing. Take, for example, heat: it burns, consumes, and drives everything that enters it which is not of its own property. Conversely, it enlightens and warms everything that is cold, wet, and dark, and makes soft things hard. It contains two "species" within it: namely, the Light and the Fierceness. One should take note of this.

4. The Light, or the Heart of heavenly joy, is in itself a lovely, joy-filled sight, a power of life, an enlightenment, and a vision of things that are far off. It is a part or a spring of the kingdom of heavenly joy. It makes everything in this world living and mobile; all flesh, as well as trees, leaves, and grass, grow in this world in the power of the Light, and have their life within it, as in that which is Good.

12. The second <term>species</term><note>Böhme uses the Latin word "species" to refer to a specific type, aspect, or outward manifestation of a spiritual force.</note> is fierceness <note>original: "Grimigkeit" — this refers to the wrathful, harsh, or "grim" aspect of nature that causes conflict and destruction.</note>; for when it gains power, it crushes and spoils everything just like heat does. No life can exist within it if the heat does not resist it. The fierceness of the cold is the destruction of all life and a house of death, just as the fierceness of heat is.

### On the <term>Interaction</term><note>original: "Qualificirung" — Böhme's specific term for how different forces or "qualities" (like heat and cold) blend, influence, and act upon one another to create reality.</note> of Air and Water.

13. Air has its origin in heat and cold; for heat and cold drive forth powerfully from themselves and fill everything, out of which comes a living and weaving movement. But when the cold softens the heat, the quality of both becomes thin, and the bitter quality draws it together so that it becomes comforting. However, the air has its origin and greatest movement from the heat, and the water from the cold.

14. Now these two qualities constantly struggle with one another: the heat consumes the water, and the cold constrains the air. Yet the air is the cause and spirit of all life and all movement in this world, whether it be in the flesh or in everything that grows out of the earth; thus everything has its life from the air, and nothing that is in this world and moves can exist without the air.

15. The water also wells up in all living and weaving things in this world; in the water consists the body of all things, and in the air the spirit, whether in the flesh or in the plants of the earth. And both of these come from heat and cold, and <term>interact</term> with one another as a single thing.

16. Now, however, in these two qualities, two distinct <term>species</term> are to be noted: namely, the living and the deadly effect. The air is a living quality when it is gentle within a thing; then the Holy Spirit rules in the gentleness of the air, and all creatures are joyful within it. But it also has the fierceness within itself, so that it kills and destroys through its terrible elevation <note>original: "grausame Erhebung" — likely referring to violent storms, pressure, or the "rising up" of a quality into an extreme state.</note>. Yet the interaction takes its origin from this fierce elevation, so that it wells and drives in everything, from which life has its origin and stands. Therefore, both must exist in this life.

### On the influences of the other qualities in the three elements: Fire, Air, and Water.

#### On the bitter quality.

19. The bitter quality is the heart in all life, just as it draws the water together in the air and also disperses it so that it becomes distinct; so it is also in all creatures, as well as in the plants of the earth: for foliage and grass have their green color from the bitter quality. If the bitter quality dwells gently in a creature, it is a heart or joy within the same; for it separates all other evil influences and is a beginning or cause of joy or laughter.

20. For when it is moved, it makes a creature tremble and full of joy, and elevates the same with the whole body; for it is like a glimpse of the heavenly kingdom of joy, an elevation of the spirit, a spirit and power in all plants from the earth, a mother of life.

21. The Holy Spirit surges and drives mightily in this quality, for it is a piece of the heavenly kingdom of joy, as I will prove hereafter. But it also has another <term>kind</term><note>original: "Species."</note> within itself, namely <term>fierceness</term><note>original: "Grimmigkeit" — the wrathful or harsh aspect of nature.</note>, which is truly a house of death, a corruption of all good, a decay and consumption of life in the flesh. For if it raises itself too much in a creature and ignites in the heat, it separates flesh and spirit, and the creature must die the death: for it wells up and ignites the element of fire, in which no flesh can endure amidst the great heat and bitterness. But if it ignites in the element of water and becomes welling therein, it brings the flesh into sickness and disease, and finally into death.

**A**ll of this, as recounted above, is called a <term>quality</term><note>original: "Qualität" — for Böhme, a "quality" is not just a trait, but an active, "qualifying" force that powers existence.</note> because everything in the deep above the earth, on the earth, and in the earth works together (qualifies) as one thing; and yet it has many kinds of power and effect, though only one mother from which all things come and surge forth. All creatures are made from and have come out of these qualities, and they live within them as in their mother. Likewise, the earth and stones have their origin there, and everything that grows out of the earth lives and surges from the power of these qualities; no reasonable person can deny this.

2. This twofold <term>source</term><note>original: "Quell" — a wellspring or fountainhead of energy.</note>, evil and good in all things, all stems from the stars; for just as the creatures on earth are in their quality, so too are the stars. For through a twofold source, everything has its great mobility—running, racing, surging, driving, and growing.

3. Thus, <term>gentleness</term><note>original: "Sanftmuth" — the quiet, light-filled property of nature.</note> in nature is a still rest, but <term>fierceness</term><note>original: "Grimmigkeit" — the wrathful, harsh, or energetic property.</note> in all powers makes everything mobile, running, and racing, and moreover, brings forth birth. For the driving qualities bring desire into all creatures for both evil and good, so that everything desires, mixes, increases, decreases, becomes beautiful, perishes, loves, and hates one another.

4. There is in all creatures in this world a good and evil will and source: in humans, animals, birds, fish, worms, as well as in everything that exists—in gold, silver, tin, copper, iron, steel, wood, herbs, leaves, and grass—as well as in the earth, in stones, in water, and in everything that one can investigate.

5. There is nothing in nature that does not have both good and evil within it; everything seethes and lives in this twofold drive, whatever it may be—except for the holy angels and the fierce devils, for they are decided <note>meaning they have been separated into their respective realms</note>; and each lives, qualifies, and rules in its own quality.

The holy angels live and qualify in the light, in the good quality, in which the Holy Spirit rules. The devils live and rule in the fierce quality, in the quality of fierceness and wrath or destruction.

6. But they were both—the evil and the good angels—made out of the qualities of nature, from which all things have come; only the "qualifying" <note>the way the forces interact</note> within them is unequal.

The holy angels live in the power of the gentleness of the light and the kingdom of joy; and the devils live in the power of the rising or elevating torment of fierceness, terror, and darkness, and they cannot grasp the light, into which they themselves have thrust themselves through their own self-elevation, as I will write hereafter concerning the creation.

8. But if you will not believe that everything in this world stems from the stars, I will prove it to you; if you are not a blockhead and have a little reason, then take note of what follows.

9. Firstly, look at the sun: it is the heart or the king of all stars, and gives light to all stars from the rising to the setting, and illuminates everything and warms everything; everything lives and grows in its power; moreover, the joy of all creatures stands in its power.

10. Now, if the same were taken away, it would become entirely dark and cold; likewise, no fruit would grow, and neither human nor animal would be able to multiply, for the heat would be extinguished, and the seed in everything would become cold and frozen.

13. Just as the spirit of a person rules within the whole body in all the veins and fills the entire human being, so also the Holy Spirit fills all of nature and is the Heart of Nature; it rules within the good <term>qualities</term><note>Böhme uses "quality" to mean an active, living force or power, rather than just a passive trait.</note> in all things. If you now have this Spirit within you, so that it enlightens and fills your own spirit, then you will understand what is written hereafter. But if not, it will happen to you as it did to the wise pagans, who became lost in their wonder at creation and sought to explore it through their own reason. In their thinking, they came before the very face of God yet could not see it, for they were stone-blind in the knowledge of God. It was just like the children of Israel in the wilderness, who could not look upon the face of Moses; therefore, he had to place a veil over his face whenever he approached the people. This was because they did not understand or know the true God and His will, even though He walked among them. Thus, the veil was a sign and a prefigurement of their blindness and lack of understanding. Just as a piece of work cannot grasp its master, so too a human being cannot grasp or know God his Creator, unless the Holy Spirit enlightens him. This happens only to those who do not trust in themselves, but place their hope and will in God alone and walk in the Holy Spirit; they are one spirit with God.

14. If one now wishes to rightly contemplate the sun and stars along with their <term>body</term><note>original: "Corpus" — the physical, material manifestation.</note>, their effects, and their qualities, one finds the divine essence right within them, in that the powers of the stars are Nature itself.

15. If one contemplates the whole <term>cycle</term><note>original: "curriculum" — the path or course of the stars.</note> or the entire circuit of the stars, it is quickly found that this is the Mother of all things, or Nature itself, from which all things have come to be, in which all things stand and live, and through which everything moves. All things are made from these same powers and remain within them eternally. And although at the end of this time they shall be transformed, when the good and evil shall be separated, nevertheless, angels and humans shall exist eternally in God within the power of Nature, from which they took their first beginning.

16. But here you must lift your mind into the spirit and contemplate how all of nature with all its powers—including the width, depth, height, heaven, earth, and everything within it and above the heaven—is the Body of God!

17. You must not think that the whole triumphing Holy Trinity—God the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit—is contained within the physical <term>body</term><note>original: "corpus"</note> of the stars. 19. The interior or hollow space in the body of a human represents the "depth" between the stars and the earth. The whole body with everything in it signifies Heaven and Earth: the flesh signifies the earth and is also made of earth; the blood signifies the water and is also made of water. The breath signifies the air and is also air. The entrails or intestines signify the effect or "consumption" of the stars; everything that has come to be from their power, which they have made themselves, they themselves consume again, and it remains in their power. And the intestines are also the consumption of everything that the human shoves into his bowels, everything which has grown out of the power of the stars.

The liver signifies the element of Water and is indeed the water, for from the liver the blood comes into the whole body and all the limbs; the liver is the mother of the blood.

22. The feet signify what is near and far, for in God, near and far are one thing; and a person can come near or go far by means of their feet. But wherever a person may be, they are neither near nor far within nature, for in God, it is all one thing.

23. The hands signify the **Omnipotence of God** <note>original: "Allmacht Gottes"</note>. For just as God can change everything within nature and make of it whatever He wills, so also can a person change everything that has grown or come to be out of nature with their hands, and make from it what they will. With their hands, a person governs the work and essence of all nature, and thus they truly signify the omnipotence of God.

24. The entire body up to the neck signifies and is the round circle of the movement of the stars, as well as the depths between the stars, wherein the planets and elements govern. The flesh signifies the earth, which is congealed and has no movement of its own; likewise, the flesh has in itself no reason, comprehension, or movement, but is moved solely by the power of the stars, which govern within the flesh and the veins.

25. Similarly, the earth would bring forth no fruit, nor would any metal grow within it—neither gold, silver, copper, iron, nor stone—if the stars did not work within it. Not even a tiny blade of grass would grow from it without the working of the stars. The head signifies Heaven; it is connected to the body by the veins and the paths of power, and all powers go out from the head and the brain into the body, into the <term>source-veins</term><note>original: "Quelladern" — the pulsing channels of life-force.</note> of the flesh.

26. But now, Heaven is a lovely hall of joy wherein all powers exist, just as they do in the whole of nature, in the stars and elements, but they are not so hard, driving, and tormenting. For every power of Heaven has only one species or form of power—bright and quite gently <term>pulsing</term><note>original: "quallende" — from "Quelle" (source/spring), referring to the way life-force wells up or flows like a fountain.</note>, not evil and good mixed together as in the stars and elements, but pure and clear. It is made from the "middle of the waters," <note>A reference to the Genesis creation account of the firmament separating the waters.</note> but not in such a <term>manifesting</term><note>original: "qualificirende" — the way a force interacts or takes on a specific quality.</note> way as the water in the elements, for the <term>fierceness</term><note>original: "Grimmigkeit" — the harsh, wrathful, or bitter aspect of nature.</note> is not within it.

27. Nevertheless, Heaven belongs to nature, for from Heaven the stars and elements have their origin and power. For Heaven is the heart of the water, just as in all creatures, as well as in everything that

is in this world, water is its heart; and nothing exists without water, whether it be within the flesh or outside the flesh, in the plants of the earth, or in metal and stones; thus, in all things, water is the kernel or the heart.

28. Likewise, Heaven is the heart in nature, wherein all powers are, just as in the stars and elements; it is a soft and gentle substance of all powers, just like the brain in the head of a person.

29. Now, Heaven ignites the stars and elements with its power so that they <term>well up</term> and drive; likewise, the head of a person is like Heaven. Just as in Heaven all powers are gentle and lovely, and moreover full of joy and <term>interact</term><note>original: "qualificiren" — the harmonious operation of divine qualities.</note> together, so in the head or brain of a person, all powers are gentle and full of joy. And just as Heaven has a closure or a firmament above the stars, and yet all powers go out from Heaven into the stars, so the brain has a closure or a fortress before the body, and yet all powers go out from the brain into the body and into the whole person.

30. The head has within it the five senses—seeing, hearing, smelling, tasting, and feeling—wherein the stars and elements <term>operate</term>. And therein arises the <term>Sidereal</term><note>original: "Sideriſche" — relating to the stars or constellations.</note>, stellar, or **Natural Spirit** <note>original: "Naturgeiſt"</note> in humans and animals. In these, both evil and good well up, for it is a house of the stars. The stars take such power from Heaven so that they can make a living and moving spirit within the flesh of humans and animals. The movement of Heaven makes the stars movable; likewise, the head makes the body movable.

31. Here, now, open the eyes of your spirit and behold God your Creator. Here now is the question: from where does Heaven have or take such power, that it makes such movement in nature?

32. Here you must now look above and beyond nature, into the light-holy, triumphant, divine power, into the unchangeable, **Holy Trinity** <note>original: "Dreyfaltigkeit"</note>. This is a triumphant, pulsing, movable essence, and all powers are within it, just as in nature. For that is the eternal Mother of nature, from which heaven, earth, stars, elements, angels, devils, humans, animals, and everything have come to be, and in which everything stands.

...[was] made into a creature by this aforementioned Being, through the power that goes out from Him.

34. God, however, in His **Trinity**, is unchanging; rather, everything that exists in Heaven, on Earth, and above the Earth has its source and origin in the power that proceeds from God.

35. You must not think that evil and good spring forth from or exist within God; rather, God is Himself the **Good**, and He even takes His name from "the good" <note>original: "Gott... hat auch den Namen von dem guten". Böhme often connects the German word for God (Gott) with the word for good (gut)</note>. He is the triumphant, eternal joy. Yet all powers proceed from Him—those that you can investigate in nature and those that exist in all things.

36. Now you might say: "There is indeed both evil and good in nature; since all things come from God, then evil must also come from God."

37. Look, a human being has within them **gall** <note>original: "Galle." In Böhme’s time, bile or gall was one of the "four humors" believed to govern health and temperament</note>, which is a poison; yet a person cannot live without this gall. The gall makes the <term>Sideric spirits</term> <note>These are "star-spirits" or astral forces within the body that govern movement and emotion</note> mobile, full of joy, triumphant, or laughing, for it is a source of joy. But if it "ignites" within one of the elements, it ruins the whole person; for the wrath in the Sideric spirits comes from the gall.

38. This happens when the gall rises and runs to the heart; it then sets the element of fire ablaze, and the fire ignites the Sideric spirits, which govern the blood and veins within the element of water. Then the whole body trembles with the wrath and poison of the gall. Joy has exactly the same source, and comes from this same substance, just as wrath does. That is: when the gall is ignited in the "loving" or <term>sweet quality</term>—in that which is dear to the person—then the entire body trembles for joy. In this state, the Sideric spirits are also sometimes affected when the gall rises too high and ignites in that sweet quality.

39. But such a physical substance does not exist in God, for He does not have flesh and blood. Instead, He is a **Spirit** in whom all powers reside (John 4:24), just as we pray in the Lord's Prayer: *Yours is the power* (Matthew 6:13). And as Isaiah writes of Him: *He is Wonderful, Counselor, Power, Hero, Eternal Father, Prince of Peace* (Isaiah 9:6).

40. The **bitter quality** <note>Böhme identifies "bitterness" as one of the fundamental forces of the universe, providing the "sting" or drive necessary for life</note> is also in God, but not in the same way as gall is in a human being. Rather, it is an everlasting power—an exalting, triumphant source of joy.

<page-num>13</page-num>

41. And although it is written in the books of Moses (Exodus 20:5; Deuteronomy 4:24): *I am an angry, jealous God*, this does not mean that God becomes angry within Himself, or that a "fire of wrath" rises within the Holy Trinity. No, that cannot be. For it is written: *upon those who hate me*—it is within that very creature that the fire of wrath rises.

42. If God were to become angry within Himself, all of nature would burn. This will indeed happen once in nature on the Last Day, but not within God Himself. Within God, triumphant joy shall burn, just as it has never been otherwise from eternity, and never will be otherwise.

43. Now, this exalting, surging, triumphant joy in God makes Heaven triumphant and mobile; and Heaven makes the stars and elements mobile; and the stars and elements make the creatures mobile.

44. From the powers of God, Heaven came to be; from Heaven, the stars came to be; from the stars, the elements came to be; and from the elements, the Earth and the creatures came to be. Thus everything has its beginning—even the Angels and Devils. They came to be before the creation of Heaven, the stars, and the Earth, out of that same power from which Heaven, stars, and Earth were made.

45. This is a short introduction or guide on how one should contemplate the divine and natural Being. From here on, I will describe the true ground and depth of what God is, and how everything is constituted within the Being of God.

46. This has remained partially hidden from the world until now, and man could not grasp it with his **reason**. But because God wishes to reveal Himself in **simplicity** in these latter times, I let His impulse and will prevail. I am only a tiny spark. Amen.

### Concerning God the Father.

2. When our Savior Jesus Christ teaches His disciples to pray, He spoke: "When you wish to pray, say: Our Father, who art in Heaven," Matt. 6. This does not mean that Heaven could contain or encompass the Father, for it is itself made out of the divine power.

3. For Christ says: "My Father is greater than all"; John 10:29. And in the Prophet, God says: "Heaven is my throne, and the earth is my footstool," Isaiah 66. Also: "What kind of house will you build for me? I encompass the heavens with a span, and the earth with a <term>measure</term> <note>original: "Dreylinge". This refers to an ancient dry measure, often translated in Böhme’s era as a "third" of a larger unit or simply a small vessel for measuring dust or grain.</note>." Isaiah 40:12. Also: "In Jacob will I dwell, and Israel shall be my tent." Psalm 135:4. Sirach 24:13.

4. But that Christ calls His Father a "Heavenly Father" means that His Father's radiance and power appear entirely pure, bright, and clean in Heaven; and that above the <term>circle</term> <note>original: "Cirk". Refers to the "vault" or "orb" of the visible sky.</note> or boundary which we see with our eyes and call "Heaven," there appears the entire triumphant, Holy Trinity—Father, Son, and Holy Spirit.

5. Also, Christ distinguishes herewith His Heavenly Father from the "Father of Nature," which is the stars and elements; these are our natural father, from which we are made, and in whose impulse we live here in this world, and from whom we take our food and nourishment.

6. He is, however, our Heavenly Father so that our soul may constantly yearn for Him and desire Him; yes, it constantly thirsts and hungers for Him. The body hungers and thirsts for the Father of Nature, which is the stars and elements, and that same father also feeds and waters it. But the soul thirsts and hungers for the Heavenly Holy Father, and He also feeds and waters it with His Holy Spirit and the <term>fountain of joy</term> <note>original: "Freudenquall". A characteristic Böhmean word meaning a source, spring, or "boiling up" of divine joy.</note>.

7. Now, however, we do not have two fathers, but only one,

### Concerning the Substance and Attribute of the Father.

8. Now, when one considers all of nature and its attributes, one sees the Father: when one looks upon the heavens and the stars, one sees His eternal power and wisdom. As many stars as stand beneath the heavens—which are indeed innumerable and incomprehensible to reason, and some even invisible—so many and manifold is the power and wisdom of God the Father.

9. Every star in the sky has a different power and quality than the next, which also creates so many distinctions in and among the creatures on earth, in the whole of creation. Now, all powers that are in nature originate from God the Father: such as light, heat, cold, air, water, and all powers of the earth—bitter, sour, sweet, harsh, hard, soft—and everything that cannot be recounted; all of it has its source in the Father.

10. But if one wishes to compare the Father with something, one must compare Him to the round sphere of the heavens. You must not think that each power in the Father stands in a particular part or place in the Father, like the stars in the sky; no, but the Spirit shows that all powers in the Father are within one another, like one single power. One has an image of this in the Prophet Ezekiel, in the 1st chapter; he sees the Lord in spirit and in a symbolic form like a wheel, where four wheels are within one another, and all four were the same, and when they moved, they moved straight ahead; whichever side the wind blew, all four went ahead, and none needed to turn. Thus also is God the Father; for all powers in the Father are within one another like one power, and all powers exist in the Father in an unsearchable light and clarity.

11. ### Concerning GOD the Son.

13. Now, if one wishes to see GOD the Son, one must again look upon natural things, otherwise I cannot write of Him: the Spirit sees Him well, but one cannot speak or write of it, for the divine being consists in power, which does not allow itself to be written or spoken. We must therefore employ parables for ourselves when we wish to speak of GOD, for in this world we live in <term>fragments</term> <note>original: "Stückwerk". Meanwhile, let the beloved reader look toward the meaning of the Spirit, and it will not fail; he will also receive a little spark of power from it, if only he hungers for it.

**22.** In this way, the Son of GOD is also always born from eternity out of all the powers of His Father—and not made—and is the heart and radiance out of all the powers of His heavenly Father: a self-subsisting person, the center, or, in the deep, the <term>body of radiance</term> <note>original: "Corpus des Glanzes".</note>. For the Father's power begets the Son from eternity to eternity forevermore. **23.** Thus, the Father is the self-subsisting being of all powers, and the Son is the heart in the Father, who is always born out of all the Father’s powers and who illuminates the Father's powers in return. Just as the sun does not shine out from the other stars (even though it has its origin from the other stars), so too the Son does not shine out from the powers of the Father as far as His "body" is concerned. And although He is always born from the powers of the Father, He nevertheless shines back into the powers of the Father, for He is a different person than the Father, but not a different GOD. He is eternally in the Father, and the Father begets Him from eternity to eternity forevermore, and the Father and the Son are one GOD, of the same essence in power and omnipotence. The Son sees, hears, tastes, feels, smells, and perceives everything, just as the Father does; in His power, He lives and is everything that is good, as in the Father, but evil is not in Him.

**27.** The three elements—fire, air, and water—have three kinds of movement or <term>qualifying</term> <note>original: "qualificirung". **28.** Just as the three elements—fire, air, and water—go out from the sun and stars and are one body within each other, creating the living movement and the spirit of all creatures in this world: so also does the Holy Spirit go out from the Father and the Son, and creates the living movement in all the powers of the Father. It is a moving welling, like a spirit or a <term>matter</term> <note>original: "Materia". Böhme often speaks of divine "stuff" or substance that is not yet physical matter.</note>—except that it does not have reason, for it is not the Holy Spirit; furthermore, the fourth element <note>Earth</note> also belongs to a natural spirit if it is to have reason. Thus, it goes out from GOD the Father (into His deep) out of all His powers, and brings forth the radiance, the heart, or the Son of GOD in His <term>center</term> <note>original: "Centro".</note>: this is compared to the round sphere of the sun, which shines above itself, below itself, and beside itself; and the radiance, along with all powers, goes out from the Son of GOD into the whole Father.

**30.** Now, in the whole deep of the Father, there is nothing outside of the Son but the manifold and immeasurable or unsearchable power of the Father, and the unsearchable power and light of the Son; this is, in the deep of the Father, a living, all-powerful, all-knowing, all-hearing, all-seeing, all-smelling, all-tasting, all-feeling Spirit, in whom all power and radiance and wisdom exists, just as in the Father and the Son.

**31.** Just as the power and radiance of the sun and all stars exist in the four elements, so it is also in the whole deep of the Father: and this is truly called the Holy Spirit, who is the third self-subsisting person in the Godhead.

->Of the Holy Trinity.<-

**32.** When one speaks or writes of three persons in the Godhead, you must not think that there are therefore three Gods, where each rules and governs for himself like earthly kings on earth. No, such a substance and being does not exist in GOD; for the divine being stands in power, and not in a body or flesh.

**33.** The Father is the entire divine power from which all creatures have come, and has always been from eternity; He has no beginning nor end. The Son is in the Father, the Father’s heart or light, and the Father brings forth the Son from eternity to eternity forevermore; and the Son’s power and radiance shine back into the whole Father, just as the sun shines in the whole world.

He clarifies that the Trinity is not three separate gods but a unified divine essence of power and light rather than physical flesh.</summary>

**35.** The Holy Spirit proceeds from the Father and the Son, and is the third self-subsistent person in the Deity. Just as the elements in this world proceed from the sun and the stars, and are the moving spirit in all things in this world: so also is the Holy Spirit the moving spirit in the whole Father. He proceeds from eternity to eternity evermore from the Father and the Son, and fills the whole Father; he is nothing less or greater than the Father and the Son; his <term>weaving power</term> <note>original: "webende Kraft". **37.** You say there is but a single essence in GOD, and that GOD has no Son; now open your eyes and look at yourself. Now take note: in your heart, veins, and brain you have your spirit; all the power that moves in your heart, veins, and brain, in which your life stands, signifies GOD the Father. Out of that same power, your light rises up, so that in that same power you see, understand, and know what you ought to do; for that same light shimmers in your whole body, and the whole body moves in the power and knowledge of the light; that signifies GOD the Son. For just as the Father begets the Son out of his power, and the Son shines in the whole Father: so also the power of your heart, your veins, and your brain begets a light that shines in all your powers, in your whole body. Open the eyes of your mind and think upon it, and you will find it to be so.

46. Thus also the spirit arises in birds and worms, and everything has its <term>threefold source</term> <note>original: "dreyfachen Quell". 47. Now note; in a piece of wood, stone, or herb there are three things, and nothing can be born or grow if even one of these three were to remain absent from a thing. First is the **power**, from which a body comes to be, whether it be wood or stone or herb: hereafter there is in the same a **sap**, which is the heart of a thing: thirdly, there is within it a **wellspring power**, scent, or taste, which is the spirit of a thing, from which it grows and increases; if now one of these three is missing, no thing can exist.

48. ### The 4th Chapter.
## Concerning the Creation of the Holy Angels, an Instruction or Open Portal of Heaven.

-> 1. <-

The learned ones and almost all writers have had much and great anxiety in searching, composing, and striving within nature, and have brought forth many and various opinions as to when and how, or out of what, the holy angels were created. Likewise, what the terrible fall of the Grand Prince Lucifer might have been! Or how he became such an evil and fierce devil, where such an evil source originated, or what drove him to it?

2. Although this foundation and great mystery remained hidden from the world, and even human flesh and blood cannot grasp or comprehend it, yet the GOD who made the world wants to reveal Himself now at the end, and all great mysteries shall become manifest: to indicate that the great day of revelation and final judgment is now near, and is to be expected daily, on which day what was lost through Adam will be brought back again, and on which the kingdom of heaven and the kingdom of the devils will be separated in this world.

3. ### Of the Divine Quality.

4. Now that you have thoroughly heard in the third chapter about the Trinity in the divine being, I will now clearly show here the power and effect, as well as the **qualities** or **qualifying** <note>original: "Qualitäten oder Qualificirung". Böhme uses these terms to describe the active, driving forces or essential properties that "qualify" or give character to a substance.</note> in the divine being, or from what the angels were actually created, or what their body and power may be?

5. As I also mentioned before, in GOD the Father is all power that no man can reach with his senses, yet one recognizes this clearly in the stars and elements, as well as in the creatures in the whole of the creation of this world.

6. All power is in GOD the Father and proceeds from Him, such as light, heat, cold, softness, sweetness, bitterness, sourness, tartness, sound, and that which is impossible to speak of or comprehend; all of this is in GOD the Father within one another as one power, and yet all powers move in his outgoing. However, the powers in GOD are not qualifying in such a manner as they are in nature within the stars and elements, or in the creatures.

7. No, you must not think so, for Lord Lucifer, in his self-exaltation, made the powers of the impure nature so burning, bitter, cold, tart, sour, dark, and impure; but in the Father, all powers are mild, soft, like heaven, and entirely full of joy, for all powers **triumph** <note>Böhme frequently uses "triumphing" to describe the harmonious, joyful interaction of divine forces.</note> within one another, and the sound of them rises from eternity to eternity. Therein is nothing but love, gentleness, mercy, and friendliness—such a triumphing, rising spring of joy, where all voices of the heavenly realm of joy surrender, which no man can say, nor compare with anything. But if one wishes to compare it, one must compare it to the soul of man; when the soul is kindled by the Holy Spirit, it is then so full of joy and triumphing, and all powers rise up in it and triumph, so that they lift up the animal body until it trembles; that is a true glimpse of the divine quality, as the quality is in GOD; in GOD, everything is Spirit.

8. The quality of water is not of such a running and

<column-break/>

<page-num>27</page-num>

qualifying manner in GOD as it is in this world, but it is a Spirit entirely bright and thin, in which the Holy Spirit rises up as a power. The bitter quality qualifies within the sweet, tart, and sour, and love rises therein from eternity to eternity: for the love in the light and clarity goes out from the Heart or Son of GOD into all the powers of the Father, and the Holy Spirit moves in everything.

9. And this is in the depth of the Father just like a divine **Salitter** <term>Salitter: A term Böhme likely derived from "saltpeter" (Salniter), representing the divine "marrow" or the fundamental spiritual matter from which the universe is formed.</term>, which I must of necessity compare to the earth; for before its corruption, the earth was such a Salitter, but not so hard, cold, bitter, sour, and dark, but rather like the depth or the heaven—entirely bright and pure, wherein all powers were good, beautiful, and heavenly; but Prince Lucifer corrupted it so, as will follow hereafter.

10. This heavenly Salitter, or powers within one another, give birth to heavenly, joyful fruits and colors, all kinds of trees and shrubs, upon which grows the beautiful and lovely fruit of life: likewise, in these powers, all kinds of flowers rise up with beautiful heavenly colors and scents. Their taste is manifold, each according to its quality and kind, entirely holy, divine, and full of joy, so that every quality bears its fruit; just as in the corrupted **pit of destruction** <note>original: "Mordgruben", literally "murder-pits." Böhme uses this to describe the fallen state of the earth.</note> or dark valley of the earth, all kinds of trees, shrubs, flowers, and fruits rise up, as well as beautiful stones, silver, and gold within the earth—this is a prototype of the heavenly generation.

11. Nature works with the greatest diligence in the corrupted and dead earth so that it might give birth to heavenly form and kind, but it gives birth to dead, dark, and hard fruits, which are no more than a prototype of the heavenly ones: moreover, they are entirely fierce, bitter, sour, tart, hot, cold, hard, and evil, and there is barely a good spark within them. Their sap and spirit are mixed with the hellish quality; their smell is a stench; thus has Lord Lucifer prepared it, as I will then clearly prove hereafter.

12. Now, when I write of trees, shrubs, and fruits, you must not understand it in an earthly way, like this world, for it is not my meaning that a dead, hard, wooden tree or stone grows in heaven, consisting of earthly quality. No, but my meaning is heavenly and spiritual, yet truly and actually so; I mean no outward thing other than how I set it down in the letter <note>original: "im Buchstaben". Böhme means that while the words are literal, the reality they describe is purely spiritual.</note>.

13. In the **Divine Splendor** <note>original: "göttlichen Pomp". Böhme uses this term to describe the majestic, visible manifestation and internal activity of the heavenly realm.</note>, there are primarily two things to consider: first, the **Salitter** <term>Salitter: A central term in Böhme’s cosmology, referring to the "divine saltpeter" or the living, spiritual substance that acts as the "soil" or foundational matter of heaven.</term> or the divine powers. These are a moving, **welling** <note>original: "quallende".
