14. The second form of heaven in the Divine Splendor is the **Mercurius** <term>Mercurius: Borrowing from alchemy, Böhme uses "Mercury" to represent the principle of sound, resonance, and the "vibration" that brings the still Salitter to life.</term> or the **Sound**. Just as there is sound within the *Salitter* of the earth—from which grow gold, silver, copper, iron, and the like, out of which all kinds of instruments for sound or joy can be made, such as bells, pipes, and everything that rings out—so too is this same sound present in all creatures on earth; otherwise, all would be silent.

15. Now, through this same sound in heaven, all powers are proven, so that everything grows full of joy and is born quite elegantly. Just as the divine powers are many and varied, so too the Sound or *Mercurius* is many and varied. When the powers rise up in GOD, one stirs the other and they surge into one another, and there is a constant mixing. Then, out of this, all kinds of colors emerge, and in those colors grow all kinds of fruit. This rises up in the *Salitter*, and the *Mercurius* or Sound also mingles and rises up in all the powers of the Father; then, tones and sounds rise up in the heavenly kingdom of joy. If you were to bring together many thousands of kinds of instruments and stringed play in this world, and tuned them all together in the most artistic way, and had the most skillful masters to play them, it would still only be like a dog’s barking compared to the divine Sound and **Music** that rises up through the divine sound from eternity to eternity.

16. If you now wish to contemplate the heavenly Divine Splendor and glory—what it is like, what kind of growth, pleasure, or joy is there—then look diligently at this world: what kind of fruits and growths come from the *Salitter* of the earth, from trees, shrubs, herbs, roots, flowers, oils, wine, grain, and everything that is there and that your heart can only search out—that is all a **prototype** <note>original: "Vorbilde". An earthly reflection or foreshadowing of a higher reality.</note> of the heavenly Splendor.

17. For earthly and corrupted nature has, from the beginning of its

<meta>catchword: its</meta>

its creation until today, always worked so that it might bring forth the heavenly form, both in the earth and in men and animals. One sees this very well: how every year new arts come forth. This has lasted from the beginning until this day, but nature has not been able to bring forth divine power and quality; therefore, its fruit is half dead, corrupted, and impure.

18. You must not think that in the Divine Splendor, animals, worms, or creatures of the flesh come forth as in this world; no, rather I mean only the wonderful **proportion**, power, and skill within them. Nature works with the highest diligence so that it might bring forth heavenly figures or forms in its power, as one then sees in men, animals, birds, and worms, as well as in the growths of the earth—that everything is born in the most artistic way. For nature would gladly be free of **vanity** <note>A reference to Romans 8:20, suggesting that the natural world groans to be released from its current state of decay.</note>, so that it might bear the heavenly form in holy power.

20. The fruits are not a dead, hard, bitter, sour, and tart **carcass** <note>original: "Aas". But the infected lust and craving of the Devil, who had infected and corrupted the *Salitter* out of which Adam was made, brought man into evil lust to eat of both qualities, evil and good; of which I shall hereafter write clearly and also provide proof.

### Of the Creation of the Angels.

22. The Spirit shows and points out brightly and clearly that before the **Creation of the Angels** <note>original: "Erschöpfung der Engel". In Böhme's time, "Erschöpfung" referred to the "out-pouring" or creation from a source, rather than tiredness.</note>, the divine essence with its rising and qualifying was from eternity, and also remained so during the creation of the angels, as it still is today, and will also remain so in eternity.

23. The **Place** <note>original: "Locus". 24. But it became the kingdom of the Great Prince Lucifer during the creation of the angels <insert>[Understand: according to the **second principle** <note>original: "andern Principio". 25. By this, he intended to become as high, light, and powerful as the Son of GOD, but he became a fool. Therefore, this **Place** could not persist in its burning quality within GOD; thus, the creation of this world followed. At the end, at a time determined by GOD, this world will be returned to its first place, just as it was before the creation of the angels. Lord Lucifer will be given a cavern, tomb, or hole therein for his eternal dwelling, remaining forever in his ignited quality. 26. GOD, in His **welling** <note>original: "Wallen". The philosophers have held the opinion that GOD made the angels only from light; but they have erred. They are not made from light alone, but from all the powers of GOD.

27. As I have previously shown, two things are especially notable in the depth of GOD the Father: first, the power—or all the powers of GOD the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit. These are lovely, delightful, and manifold, yet they are all within one another as a single power.

28. Just as the power of all the stars governs within the air, so it is in GOD; however, in GOD, every power manifests with its

its specific effect. Following this, there is the **Sound** within every power, and the sound resonates according to the quality of each power. Within this resonance stands the entire heavenly kingdom of joy. From this divine **Salitter** and **Mercurius** <term>Mercurius: The active principle of "Mercury," representing sound, movement, and the expression of the powers.</term> were all angels made—understand: from the body of nature.

29. You might now ask: How were they made or born, or what kind of form is that?

Indeed, if I had an angel’s tongue and you had an angel’s understanding, we would speak of it quite finely. But as it is, only the Spirit sees it, and the tongue cannot exalt it, for I have no other words than the words of this world. However, if the Holy Spirit is within you, your soul will surely grasp it.

30. See, the entire Holy **Trinity** <note>original: "Dreyfaltigkeit".</note> has, with its welling, fashioned a **Body** <note>original: "Corpus".</note> or image out of itself, like a "little God," yet not as vast in its extent as the entire Trinity, but somewhat according to the size of a creature.

31. In GOD there is no beginning nor end, but the angels have a beginning and an end—though not in a measurable or comprehensible way. For an angel can be large at one moment and soon small; their rapid change is as quick as human thoughts. All qualities and powers are within an angel, just as they are in the entire Godhead.

32. But you must understand this rightly: they are made and fashioned together out of the **Salitter** and **Mercurius**—that is, out of the "Dawning" <note>original: "Aufgange". This refers to the rising or breaking forth of divine light.</note>. Consider this comparison: the elements go forth from the sun and stars, and they create a living spirit within the **Salnitter** <note>original: "Salnitter", a linguistic variation of Salitter.</note> of the earth. The stars remain in their orbits, yet the spirit nonetheless receives the quality of the stars.

33. Now, the spirit is a distinct thing according to its composition, and has a substance like all the stars; and the stars are and remain a distinct thing, each free for itself. Nevertheless, the quality of the stars governs within the spirit. But the spirit can and may raise or lower itself within its qualities, or may live in the influences of the stars as it wills; for it is free, having received the qualities it contains as its own property.

34. And though it has them initially from the stars, they are now its own—just as when a mother has the seed within her; because she has it, and because it is a seed, it belongs to the

Likewise, the mother’s food is not the child’s property; rather, the mother gives it out of love because she gave birth to the child.

37. She may also cast the child out of her house if it refuses to obey her, and she may withdraw her food from it, which is exactly what happened to the principality of Lucifer.

38. In the same way, GOD may withdraw his divine power, which exists outside the angels, when they rise up against him. But when that happens, a spirit must wither and perish, just as when the air—which is also his mother—is withdrawn from a human, he must die. Thus, angels also cannot live apart from their mother.

## The 5th Chapter.
### Of the corporeal Substance, Essence, and Property of an Angel.

Here the question arises: What kind of **body** <note>original: "Corpus"</note>, form, or shape does an angel have, or how is he fashioned? Just as a human is created in GOD'S image and likeness, so too are the angels; for they are the brothers of humanity. In the resurrection, humans will have no other form or image than the angels, as our King Christ himself testifies (Matt. 22:30). Furthermore, the angels here on earth have never revealed themselves to humans in any shape other than the human form.

2. Since we are to be like the angels in the resurrection, the angels must indeed be shaped like us; otherwise, we would have to take on a different image in the resurrection, which would contradict the original creation.

3. Moreover, Moses and Elijah appeared to Christ’s disciples in their own form and shape on Mount Tabor, even though they had already been in heaven for a long time. And Elijah had been taken into heaven with a living body, yet he had no other shape than the one he had on earth (2 Kings 2:11). Also, when Christ ascended to heaven, two angels hovered in the clouds and spoke to the disciples: "You men of Israel, why do you look up? This JESUS will come again just as you have seen Him go to heaven" (Acts 1:11). It is indeed bright and clear that He will return on the Last Day in such a form, with a divine, glorified body, like a Prince of the holy angels—which shall be the humans.

4. The Spirit also shows bright and clear that angels and humans share one image. For in the place of the cast-out Lucifer’s legions—from the very **place** <note>original: "Loco"</note> where Lucifer sat and from which he was made—GOD made another angel: that was Adam. This would have remained so had he only stayed in his **clarity** <note>original: "Klarheit"; refers to divine radiance or glory.</note>. But there is still the certain hope of the resurrection, when we will again receive angelic clarity and purity.

->Now you ask: How then are the angels created according to the image of GOD?<-
->Answer.<-

5. Firstly, the body fashioned together is inseparable and indestructible, and it is incomprehensible to human hands. For it is condensed from the divine power, and that same power is so bound together that it can never be destroyed eternally. Just as little as anyone or anything can destroy the whole Godhead, so little can anything destroy an angel; for every angel is fashioned together from all the powers of GOD—not with flesh and blood, but from divine power.

9. Now, all the power that is within the whole angel generates that same light, just as GOD the Father generates his Son at his heart. Thus, the angel’s power also generates its own "Son and Heart" within itself, and this in turn illuminates all the powers within the whole angel. Afterward, out of all the powers of the angel, and also out of the light of the angel, a fountain flows out and wells up through the whole angel: this is his spirit, which rises up into all eternity. 10. Then that same spirit wells up from all the powers of the angel and rises into the **mind** <note>original: "Gemüthe." In Böhme's thought, this is the seat of the soul's disposition and will.</note>. There, it has five open gates; there, it can look around at what is in GOD, and also what is in itself. It proceeds, however, out of all the powers of the angel, and also out of the light of the angel, just as the Holy Spirit proceeds from the Father and the Son, and it fills the entire **body** <note>original: "Corpus"</note>.

has its princely throne, where it sees everything that is outside of it, and hears everything, and tastes everything, and smells everything, and feels everything.

### On the Interacting Qualities of an Angel.
<note>original: "Qualificirung." For Böhme, this refers to the way different spiritual forces or "qualities" work together and influence one another.</note>

19. Now the question is: what kind of interaction of qualities does an angel have?

->Response.<-

The holy soul of man and the spirit of an angel are and have one substance and being. There is no difference in this, except for the quality itself in its bodily governance <note>original: "Regiment." This refers to how the body is ruled or directed by spiritual forces.</note>. That which interacts from the outside in man through the air has a corrupted, earthly quality; on the other hand, however, man also has a Divine and heavenly quality, hidden from the creatures. But the holy soul understands this well, as the royal prophet David says: "The Lord rides upon the wings of the wind" (Psalm 104:3). In the angel, however, the divine quality interacts, entirely Holy, Divine, and Pure.

20. A simple person might ask: what do you mean by "interacting qualities" <note>original: "Qualificiren."</note>? Or what is that? By this, I mean the power that enters the **body** <note>original: "Corpus"</note> of the angel from the outside, and goes out again—just as a person draws breath and lets it out again; for therein stands the life of the **body** and also of the spirit.

21. The quality from the outside ignites the spirit in the heart, in the first fountain-well, from which all powers in the whole **body** become active. Then that same quality rises in the bodily spirit—which is the natural spirit of the angel or man—up into the head. There it has its princely seat and governance, and there it has its councils, according to which it directs itself and acts.

22. The first council is the eyes. They are influenced <note>original: "inficiret." In Böhme's time, this meant "to imbue" or "to affect with a quality," not necessarily a disease.</note> by all things they look upon, for they are the light. Just as the light goes out from the Son of GOD into the whole Father, into all powers, and influences all the powers of the Father; and in turn, all the powers of the Father influence the light of the Son of GOD, from which the Holy Spirit arises.

23. Thus the eyes work upon a thing they look at, and that thing works back into the eyes; and the council of the eyes brings it into the head before the princely seat, where it is approved...

24. The second council is the ears. They also have their rising up out of all powers in the whole **body** through the spirit. Their fountain-well is the **Mercury** <note>original: "Mercurius." Böhme uses this alchemical term to represent the principle of sound, movement, and communication.</note> or Sound, which rises up out of all powers. Just as in all the powers of GOD the **Mercury** rises and sounds—within which stands the heavenly tone or joy—and the tone goes out from all powers; and in the joining of the spirit in GOD, it raises itself when one power moves another and tones or sounds. Then the tone or sound goes out and rises up again into all the powers of the Father, and all the powers of the Father are in turn influenced by it, so that they are always pregnant with the tone and always give birth to it again in every power.

25. Thus also is the second council in the head, the ears. They stand open, and the sound goes through them out into everything that sounds. Wherever the **Mercury** sounds and raises itself, there the **Mercury** of the spirit also enters, and is influenced by it, and brings it before the princely seat in the head. There it is approved by the other four councils.

But when it does not please the whole princely council in the head after it is tested, he lets it go again and does not bring it to the mother, the heart.

27. The third princely council is the nose. There the fountain-well rises out of the **body** in the spirit into the nose; there it has two open gates. Just as the praiseworthy and lovely fragrance goes out from all the powers of the Father and the Son, and tempers itself with all the powers of the Holy Spirit—wherefrom the Holy Spirit and highly precious scent rises up out of the fountain-well of the Holy Spirit and flows in all the powers of the Father, and ignites all the powers of the Father, so that they in turn become pregnant with the lovely fragrance and give birth to it in the Son and Holy Spirit:

28. So also in the angel and in man, the power of scent rises up from all the powers of the **body** through the spirit and travels out the nose, and mingles <note>original: "inficiret."</note> itself with all fragrances...

31. O man, let this be said to you, for the Spirit zealously strives in this matter; leave off from pride, or it will go with you as it did with the devils; it is no joke, the time is very short, you will soon taste the hellish fire.

But if it is not good, the tongue spews it out before it comes before the princely council: but if it should happen that it pleases the tongue and tastes good, yet does not serve the whole body, it is still rejected when it comes before the council, and the tongue must spew it out and touch it no more.

council also rises from all the powers of the body in the spirit up into the head. For just as all powers go out from God the Father and the Son into the Holy Spirit, and one stirs <note>original: "rüget." In Böhme’s thought, this implies one force affecting, stimulating, or setting another in motion.</note> the other, from which the sound or Mercury arises, so that all powers ring and move: otherwise, where one did not stir the other, nothing would move; and this stirring makes the Holy Spirit moveable, so that He rises in all powers and stirs all the powers of the Father, wherein the heavenly kingdom of joy or triumph then arises, as well as sounding, ringing, birthing, blooming, and growing—all of this has its rising from the fact that one power stirs the other. For Christ says in the Gospel: "I work, and my Father works also." (John 5:17). By this very stirring or working He means that all power goes out from Him and bears the Holy Spirit, and in the Holy Spirit all powers are already stirred by the proceeding of the Father. Therefore the Holy Spirit surges and rises from eternity to eternity, and in turn kindles all the powers of the Father and makes them stir, so that they are always pregnant.

34. This very same form exists also in angels and men, for all powers in the body rise up, and one stirs the other, otherwise the angel and man would feel nothing: But if only one member is moved too much, it cries out to the whole body for help, and the whole body stirs itself, like a great riot, as if the enemy were present, and comes to the help of that same member, and delivers it from the pain. As you can see, if you only hit your finger hard, or bruise or wound it, or wherever it may be in a member, the spirit soon runs to that same place to the mother, the heart, and complains to the mother; and if the pain is somewhat great, the mother wakes up all the members of the whole body, and everything must come to the aid of that member.

35. Now note, thus one power stirs the other without ceasing in the whole body, and all powers rise up into the head before the princely council, which approves the stirring of all powers. If a member stirs itself too much and does harm to any princely councilor—as through seeing, if it wanted to love that which does not belong to it, as Lord Lucifer did, who saw the Son of God and loved the high light, and moved and stirred himself too much, intending to become equal to Him or even more beautiful and higher—the councilors abolish such stirring.

### The 6th Chapter.
### How an Angel and Man are God's Likeness and Image.

1. Behold, as the essence is in God, so also is the essence in man and angels; and as the divine Body <note>original: "Corpus"</note> is, so also is the angelic and human. Only this is the distinction: that an angel and man are a creature and not the whole essence, but rather a son of the whole essence, whom the whole essence has brought forth. Therefore, he is rightly subject to the whole essence, since he is the son of its body. And if the son sets himself against the father, then it is indeed right if the father thrusts him out of his house; for he sets himself against the one who generated him, and by whose power he became a creature. For if one makes something out of that which

<meta>catchword: that</meta>

<column-break/>

<page-num>41</page-num>
<header>Chapter 6. Morning Redness in the Rising.</header>

is his own, then indeed, if the same does not turn out according to his will, he has the right to do with it what he wants: to make a vessel for honor or for dishonor <note>A reference to Romans 9:21, comparing God to a potter.</note>, which is also what happened to Lucifer.

->Now take note:<-

2. The whole divine power of the Father speaks out the Word from all qualities—that is, the Son of God. Now this same sound or the same Word that the Father speaks goes out from the Father’s saltpeter <note term="Salniter">Saltpeter: In Böhme’s "divine chemistry," this is the explosive, creative energy of nature.</note> or powers, and out of the Father’s Mercury <note term="Mercurio">Mercury: Representing the "sound," "voice," or the active, moving spirit that communicates between the powers.</note>, sound or tone. Now, the Father speaks this out in Himself, and this same Word is indeed the brilliance out of all His powers; and when it is spoken, it no longer sticks in the Father’s powers, but it sounds and echoes in the whole Father back into all powers.

3. Now this same Word, which the Father speaks, has such a sharpness that the tone of the Word goes instantly and swiftly through the whole depth of the Father, and this same sharpness is the Holy Spirit. For the Word that is spoken remains as a brilliance or a glorious mandate <note>i.e., a command or decree</note> before the King; but the sound that goes out through the Word performs the Father’s mandate, which He has spoken through the Word, and that is the birth of the Holy Trinity.

4. Now behold, an angel and man are also like this: the power in the whole body has all the qualities, just as is in God the Father.

5. Now just as in God the Father all powers rise up from eternity to eternity, so also all powers in the angel and man rise up into the head; for they can rise no higher, because he is only a creature that has a beginning and an end. And in the head is the divine council-seat, and it signifies God the Father; and the five senses or qualities are the councilors, who have their influences from the whole body out of all powers.

6. Now the five senses always hold council in the power of the whole body, and when the council is resolved, then the joined judge speaks it out into his center, or into the middle of the body as a word, into the heart; for that is the fountain-spring of all powers, from which it also takes its rising.

7. Now, there it stands in the heart, in a self-subsisting person gathered together from all powers, and it is a word; and that signifies God the Son. Now it goes out from the heart—

### Of the Mouth.

10. The mouth signifies that you are a non-omnipotent son of your father, whether you be an angel or a human; for through the mouth you must draw your father’s power into yourself if you wish to live. An angel must do this just as much as a human, and although he does not require the element of air in the same way a human does, he must nonetheless draw the Spirit into himself through the mouth, from which the air in this world originates.

11. For in heaven there is no such air [as ours], but the qualities are entirely gentle and full of joy, like a lovely rustling; and the Holy Spirit is among all qualities in the <term>Salitter</term> <note>A term Böhme coined, likely from "Salniter" (saltpeter), referring to the divine "earth-substance" or the crystalline power of heaven.</note> and Mercury. And an angel must also make use of this, otherwise he cannot be a moving creature; for he must also eat of the heavenly fruits through the mouth.

12. But you must not understand this in an earthly way; for an angel has no intestines, nor flesh or bone, but is joined together from divine power in a form and manner like a human, with all members like a human. However, he does not have the birth-organs <note>original: "Geburtsglieder," referring to genitals.</note> nor an exit below <note>A reference to the anus; Böhme believed the digestive system was a consequence of the Fall.</note>, for he has no need of them.

13. For man only received his birth-organs, and also his exit, in the miserable Fall. An angel drives nothing out from himself except the divine power which he grasps with his mouth to kindle his heart; and the heart kindles all the members, and he drives that same power out through his mouth again when he speaks and praises GOD.

14. The heavenly fruits which he eats, however, are not earthly; and though they are in form and shape like the earthly ones, they are nonetheless only divine power, and thus have such a lovely taste and scent that I can compare it to nothing in this world; for they taste and smell of the Holy Trinity.

15. You should not think of this as if it were perhaps a mere image, like a shadow; no, the Spirit shows brightly and clearly that in the heavenly pomp, in the heavenly Salitter and Mercury, there grow divine trees, shrubs, flowers, and many things of which this world is but an image. Just as the angels are, so too are the plants and fruits—all made from divine power.

16. You must not compare these growths of heaven to those of this world at all; for in this world there are two qualities, one evil and one good, and much grows through the power of the evil quality—that does not grow in heaven. For heaven has only one form; nothing grows there that is not good. Only Lord Lucifer prepared this world in such a [corrupted] way. Therefore Mother Eve <note>original: "Heva"</note> was ashamed when she had eaten of that which had been prepared through the evil quality; likewise, she was ashamed of her birth-organs, which had been fashioned for her through this bite of the apple.

17. Now, such a [physical] substance does not exist regarding the angelic and heavenly fruit; there are indeed certainly and truly all kinds of fruits in heaven, and not just images, and the angels take them with their hands and eat them, just as we humans do. But they need no teeth for it, nor do they have any, for the fruit is of divine power.

18. Now, all this which an angel uses, which is outside of him for the building up of his life, is not his bodily property held by natural right; rather, the heavenly Father gives it all to them out of love. Their body is indeed their property, for GOD gave it to them as a possession; and what is given to one as his own or as property is his by natural right, and he who takes it back without a legal agreement does not act rightly. GOD does not do this either; therefore, an angel is an eternal, imperishable creature who exists for all eternity.

19. But now, what use would the body be to him if GOD did not feed him? He would have no mobility and would lie there...

### Chapter 7.
### Concerning the region, place, and dwelling, as well as the dominion of the angels, how it stood in the beginning after the creation, and how it came to be so.

->1.<-

At this point the Devil will defend himself like a biting dog, for his shame will be uncovered here; he will give the reader many a hard shove and constantly cast it into doubt, suggesting it is not so. For nothing hurts him more than when one throws his former glory in his face—how he was such a beautiful prince and king. When this is thrown in his face, he rages and storms as if he would assault the world.

2. Now, should a reader come across this chapter in whom the fire of the Holy Spirit is somewhat weak, I fear the Devil will beset him and provoke him to doubt whether things are truly as they are written, so that his kingdom might not stand so naked and his shame not be so entirely exposed. If he can bring doubt into a heart regarding this, he will not fail to use his art, effort, and labor: I see well beforehand that he has this in mind.

3. Therefore, I wish to have the reader warned to read with diligence and to remain patient until he comes to the creation and the dominions of this world; then he will find it proved clearly and brightly from nature.

->Now mark:<-

4. When GOD the Almighty decreed in His counsel that He would make angels or creatures out of Himself, He made them out of His eternal power and wisdom, according to the form and manner of the Trinity in His Godhead, and according to the qualities in His divine being.

5. Firstly, He made three royal dominions <note>original: "Regimente" — refers to the governing orders or kingdoms of the angelic hosts.</note>, according to the number of the Holy Trinity, and each kingdom had the order, power, and quality of the divine being.

6. Here, lift up your mind and spirit into the depth of the Godhead, for here a door is being opened.

### Of the Nativities of the angelic Kings, how they came to be.

This is also more thoroughly described in the second and third books.

### Of the Ground and Mystery.

37. If one wishes to discover the mystery and the deepest ground, one must diligently look upon and consider the creation of this world, the government and order, as well as the qualities of the stars and elements. Although this is a corrupted and twofold being, <note>Böhme refers to the world being "twofold" because it contains both good and evil qualities after the fall.</note> and is also not living and understanding—for it is only the corrupted Niter and Mercury in which King Lucifer held sway, wherein there is evil and good—it is nevertheless the true power of GOD, which before its corruption was bright and pure, just as it is now in Heaven.

38. These powers of the stars and elements were, after the horrific fall of Lucifer's kingdom, again composed into such an order by the Creator as the kingdom of the angels stood in divine splendor before his fall. Only you should not think that the angelic kingdom with its creatures was rotated around in such a way as the stars are now, which are only powers and are rotated around in this way for the sake of the birth of this world.

40. The sun stands in the midst of the deep, and is the light or heart out of all the stars; for when the <term>Niter<gloss>Salitter</gloss></term> and <term>Mercury<gloss>Mercurius</gloss></term> existed within the kingdom of Lucifer before the creation of the world, and interacted with one another, God pulled the heart out from all those powers and made the sun from it. Therefore, it is the brightest of all, and in turn illuminates all the stars; and all stars work within its power, and the sun itself possesses the power of all stars, and with its brilliance and heat it ignites the power of all stars, and every star receives according to its power and kind from the sun.

41. The angelic kingdom is also constituted in this way: the sun signifies the highest throne-angel, the <term>Cherub<gloss>Jerubin</gloss></term> or King in an angelic kingdom—just as Lord Lucifer was also one before his fall. He had his seat in the <term>Center<gloss>Centro</gloss></term> or in the midst of the kingdom, and ruled with his power in all his angels, just as the sun rules in all the powers of this world, in the Niter and Mercury—that is, in the soft and the hard, in the sweet and the sour, in the bitter and the sharp, in the cold and the heat, in the air and the water. As one then sees in winter, when it is so severely cold and the water turns to ice, the sun nevertheless shines warmly through all the cold, regardless of the fact that snow and ice freeze in the path through which its brilliance passes.

42. But I will show you the true mystery here: see, the sun is the heart of all powers in this world, and is fashioned together from all the powers of the stars, and in turn illuminates all stars and all powers in this world, and all powers become operative within its power. <insert>Understand this magically, for it is a mirror or likeness of the eternal world.</insert>

## Chapter 8.

### Concerning the entire <term>Corpus<gloss>Body or structure</gloss></term> of an angelic kingdom; the great Mystery.

->1.<-

The angelic kingdoms are formed throughout according to the divine being, and have no other shape than the divine being has in its Trinity: the only difference is that their bodies are creatures that have a beginning and an end, and that the kingdom in which they have their <term>district<gloss>Revier</gloss></term> is not their physical property held by natural right—as they hold their bodies by natural right—but rather the kingdom belongs to God the Father. He made them out of his powers and may place them wherever he wills; otherwise, their body is made according to and out of all the powers of the Father. And their power generates light and knowledge within them, just as God generates his Son out of all his powers: and just as the Holy Spirit proceeds from all the powers of the Father and the Son, so also in an angel, their spirit proceeds from their heart, from their light, and from all their powers.

2. Now take note: just as an angel is fashioned in his physical body with all its members, so also is an entire kingdom fashioned; it is together like one angel.

### Concerning the Third Circumstance or Species.

26. The third quality or the third Spirit of God in the Father’s power is the **bitter quality**; it is a penetration or compelling of the sweet and harsh qualities; it is trembling, penetrating, and ascending.

->Note this here:<-

27. The harsh quality is the kernel or stock, or sourness or contraction; and the sweet is the light mitigation or softening; and the bitter is the penetration or triumphing, which rises and triumphs in the harsh and sweet. This is the source of joy or the cause of the laughing, uplifting joys, from which a thing trembles and exults for joy, from which heavenly joy arises. Furthermore, it is the formation of all kinds of red colors in its own quality; in the sweet it forms all kinds of white and blue; in the harsh and sour, all kinds of green and dark and mixed colors with manifold shape and smell.

28. The bitter quality is the first spirit from which life becomes stirred, from which mobility takes its origin, and it is rightly called *Cor* <note>original: Latin "Cor" — Heart</note> or Heart; for it is the trembling, cooing, elevating, penetrating spirit, the triumphing or joy, an elevating source of laughter. In the sweet quality the bitter is softened, so that it becomes entirely lovely and joyful. But if it is too greatly elevated, moved, or ignited, then it ignites the sweet and harsh qualities, and is like a tearing, stinging, and burning poison, just as when a person has a tearing plague-boil <note>original: "Pestilenz-Beule"</note>, from which he cries "ach" and "woe."

### Of the Fourth Circumstance or Species.

33. The fourth quality or the fourth source-spirit in the divine power of God the Father is the **Heat**, which is the true beginning of life, and also the true spirit of life. The harsh, sour, and sweet qualities are the <term>Salitter</term> <note>Salitter: Böhme’s term for the divine "saltpeter" or the crystalline, foundational matter of the universe</note> which belongs to the body, out of which the body is formed. For in the harsh stands the cold and the hardness, and it is the contraction and drying; and in the sweet stands the water and the light or radiance, and the entire matter of the body. or forming, and the heat is the spirit, or the ignition of life, from which the spirit arises in the body, which wells up in the whole body and shines out beyond the body, and creates the living movement in all qualities of the body.

34. ### The Great Mystery of the Spirit.

35. Now these qualities are mixed in the body as if they were all only one quality, and yet each quality wells up in its own power and goes out. Each quality goes out of itself into the others and stirs the others—that is, it infects the others; from this, the other qualities receive this will—that is, they approve of this quality's sharpness and spirit, whatever is in it, and they are always mixing.

36. Now the harsh quality, along with the sour, always draws the other qualities together, and grasps and holds the body and dries it, for it dries all other powers and holds them all through its infection: and the sweet softens and moistens all the others and tempers itself with all the others, from which they become fine, lovely, and gentle.

37. And the bitter makes all the others stir and move, and divides it into limbs, so that each limb in the tempering of all powers receives a source-wellspring <note>original: "Quellbrust" — literally 'source-breast,' implying a fountainhead of energy</note>, from which mobility arises.

38. And the heat ignites all qualities; from this the light breaks forth in all qualities, so that one sees the other; for when the heat works in the sweet moisture, it generates the light in all qualities, so that one sees the other.

39. From this arise the senses and thoughts: that one quality sees the other, which is also tempered in it and with it, and approves it with its sharpness, so that it becomes one will, which rises up in the body into the first wellspring, into the harsh quality.

40. There, the bitter quality in the heat penetrates through the harsh, and the sweet in the water lets it through gently; there the bitter in the heat travels through the sweet water out of the body and makes for itself two open gates: these are the eyes, the first sensibility.

### Now mark the end <note>original: "Ende" — here meaning the goal, result, or outer manifestation</note> of nature in this world.

48. Now when the sweet quality thus flees before the bitter, sour, and harsh, the harsh and bitter hasten after it so vehemently, as after their best treasure; and the sweet presses so vehemently from them, and labors so hard to press through the harsh quality, that it tears through the body and yields outside the body, out and over the earth, and hastens so hard until a long **stalk** <note>original: "Halm"</note> grows.

49. Then the heat presses upon the stalk above the earth, and the bitter quality is then ignited by the heat and receives a shock from the heat, so that it is terrified; and the harsh quality dries it out: there, the harsh, sweet, and bitter and the heat struggle with one another, and the harsh always creates its dryness in its coldness; then the sweet moves aside, and the others hasten after it.

50. But when it sees that it is to be captured—that the bitter presses so hard upon it, and the heat from outside also presses upon it—it makes the bitter fervent and ignites it: then it makes a leap through the harsh quality and rises up again; thus a hard **node** <note>original: "Knoten" — the joint or swelling on a plant stem</note> is formed behind it at the place where the struggle was, and the node gets a little hole.

51. But when the sweet quality leaps through the node, it has infected <note>original: "inficiret" — used here in the sense of 'influenced' or 'transformed'</note> the bitter so hard that it is quite trembling; and as soon as it comes above the node, it quickly expands on all sides, intending to flee from the bitter: and in such expansion, its body remains hollow in the middle, and in that trembling leap through the node, it gets even more stalks or foliage, and is now joyful that it has escaped the war.

52. And now when the heat from outside thus presses upon the stalk, the qualities within the stalk are ignited and press through the stalk; they are influenced by the sun in the outward light and give birth to the **colors** in the stalk according to the nature of their quality.

Meanwhile, the heat from the outside always dries up the sweet water in the stalk, and the stalk becomes thinner and thinner; the higher it grows, the thinner it becomes, until it can no longer escape.

55. Then the **sweet quality** gives itself up as a captive; thus the bitter, sour, sweet, and harsh rule all at once among one another. The sweet quality still expands somewhat, but it can no longer escape, for it is imprisoned.

56. 57. Then the **sweet quality** pushes gently from itself, and small, subtle little leaves grow in the head, which are of the nature of all the qualities. For the sweet water is now like a pregnant woman who has received the seed, and she pushes ever forth from herself until she bursts the head open.

58. Then she also pushes forth in the little leaves, like a woman giving birth; but the little leaves or blossoms no longer have her color and shape, but rather those of all the other qualities, for the "sweet mother" must now give birth to the children of the other qualities. And when the sweet mother has given birth to the beautiful green, blue, white, red, and yellow little flowers or children, she becomes quite weary and can no longer nourish these children; nor does she wish to have them long, since they are only her step-children, who are very delicate.

59. Because they are then too powerless for this strong spirit and cannot raise themselves up, they let their noble power depart from them, and this smells so lovely that one’s heart laughs; but they must wither and fall off, because they are too delicate for this spirit.

65. ...herb above the earth, since the **sweet water** is <term>Primary</term> <note>original: "Primus" — the dominant or ruling force in a mixture</note> within it. You cannot ignite a stone, for the **harsh quality** is Primary inside it; you also cannot ignite the earth itself, unless the other qualities are first overcome and boiled out. This can be seen in gunpowder <note>original: "Pulver" — literally "powder," referring here to the explosive properties of saltpeter and sulfur</note>, which is yet only a flash or a spirit of terror, wherein the devil forms himself in the wrath of God; I will describe and prove this in detail in another place.

67. Now you will say: "But one cannot ignite water so that it shines!" Yes, dear human, here lies the mystery: the wood that you ignite is also not the fire itself, but a dark block; the fire and light take their origin from it alone. However, you must understand this as coming from the **sweet quality** of the water, and not from the block—that is, from the **oiliness** <note>original: "Fettigkeit" — Böhme uses this to describe the flammable, life-giving essence or "sulfur" within a substance</note>, which is the spirit within.

68. Now, in the elemental water on earth, sweetness is not the Primary or ruling regent; rather, the **harsh**, **bitter**, and **sour** qualities rule. Otherwise, water would not be deadly, but would be like the water from which the Heavens were created. I will prove to you that in the elemental water on earth, the harsh, sour, and bitter quality is Primary.

69. Take grain, wheat, barley, oats, or whatever you wish, where the **sweet quality** sits as Primary within, and soak it in elemental water, and <term>distill</term> <note>original: "brenne" — literally "burn," referring to the process of distilling spirits or alcohol</note> it afterward; then the sweet quality will take the rule from the others. If you then ignite that same "water" [alcohol], you will see the spirit that remained in the water from the **oiliness** of the grain, which has overcome the water. You see the same in flesh: the flesh itself does not burn or shine, but the fat alone burns and shines.

70. Now you might ask: "How does this happen, or what form does it take?" See, in flesh, the **harsh, sour, and bitter** qualities are Primary, but in the fat, **sweetness** rules. Therefore, a fat creature is always more joyful than a lean one, because the sweet spirit wells up more strongly in it than in the lean one. For the light of nature, which is the spirit of life, shines more brightly in it than in the lean one; for in that same light within the sweet quality stands the triumphing or the joy. Then the harsh and bitter qualities triumph within it, for they rejoice that they are refreshed, fed, watered, and enlightened by the sweet and light quality. For in the harsh—

<meta>catchword: harsh</meta>

<column-break/>

<page-num>67</page-num>
<header>Ch. 8 Morning Redness in the Rising.</header>

—harsh there is no life, but only the harsh, cold, hard death; and in the bitter there is no light, but only the dark, bitter, and raging pain—the house of trembling and grim, fearful misery.

71. Therefore, when these [harsh qualities] are "guests" of the **sweet and light quality**, they become influenced and lovely, and furthermore entirely full of joy, and they triumph within a creature. Therefore, no lean creature is joyful, unless the heat is Primary within it; that is, even if it is lean and has little fat, it nonetheless possesses an excellent sweetness. Conversely, many a creature has much fat and is yet entirely melancholic; the cause is that its "fatness" is inclined toward the elemental water, where the harsh and bitter qualities are quite strong.

72. If you are a rational human, then look: the spirit that raises itself out of the heat takes its exit, its ascent, and its shining within the **sweet quality**. Therefore, the sweet quality is its "friendly will," and it rules in **gentleness**; and gentleness and humility are its own house. And that is the kernel of the Godhead, and therefore He is called **GOD**, because He is sweet, gentle, friendly, and kind. And therefore He is called **Merciful** <note>original: "Barmherzig" — literally "merciful" or "pitiful," though Böhme will break the word down phonetically</note>, because His sweet quality rises up in the harsh, sour, and bitter ones, and refreshes, quickens, moistens, and enlightens them, so that they do not remain a dark valley.

73. Then understand your mother tongue [German] correctly; you have as deep a ground within it as in Hebrew or Latin. Even if the scholars exalt themselves in those languages like a proud bride, it matters not; their art is at its last dregs. The Spirit shows that before the end, many a layman will know and understand more than the cleverest Doctors know now; for the door of heaven is opening. Whoever does not blind themselves will surely see it; the bridegroom crowns his bride, Amen.

74. See, the word *Barm* [the first part of "Merciful"] is only on your lips, and when you speak *Barm*, you close your mouth and "growl" afterward <note>referring to the 'm' sound ending the syllable</note>; and that is the **harsh quality** that encloses the word. That is, it shapes the word together so that it becomes hard or resonant, and the bitter quality cuts it apart.

75. This is to say: when you speak the syllable **Bar**, the last letter **R** purrs and murmurs like a trembling breath, and that is caused by the **bitter quality**, which is a trembling force. Now, however, the word **Barm** <note>The first part of the German word for Mercy, *Barmherzigkeit*</note> is a dead, incomprehensible word that no one understands; this signifies that the two qualities, the **harsh** and the **bitter**, are a hard, dark, cold, and bitter being that has no light within itself. Therefore, one cannot understand their power outside of the light.

76. But when one speaks the word **Barmherz** <note>Adding the syllable for "heart"</note>, then one presses the second syllable, **Herz** (Heart), out from the depths of the body, from the heart; for the true spirit speaks the word **Heart**, which rises up from the heat of the heart, in which the light goes forth and wells up.

77. Now see, when you speak **Barm**, the two qualities—harsh and bitter—form the word **Barm** very slowly together, for it is a long, powerless syllable because of the weakness of those qualities. But when you speak **Herz**, the spirit in the word **Heart** shoots out as fast as a flash of lightning, and gives the word distinction and understanding. But when you speak the suffix **Ig**, you catch the spirit in the midst of the other two qualities, so that it must remain within and form the word.

78. This is how the divine power is: the harsh and bitter qualities are the <term>Salitter</term> <note>original: "Salitter" — Böhme's term for the divine "saltpeter" or the fundamental substance of heaven's power</note> of divine Omnipotence; the sweet quality is the core of **Mercy**, according to which the whole Being, with all its powers, is called **God**. The heat is the core of the Spirit, from which the light proceeds, and it ignites itself in the midst of the sweet quality and is captured by the harsh and bitter ones, as if in their center; therein the **Son of God** is born, and that is the true **Heart of God**.

79. And the flame or flash of the light, which shines instantly in all powers—just like the sun in the whole world—that is the **Holy Spirit**, who proceeds from the clarity of the Son of God and is the flash and the sharpness; for the Son is born in the midst of the other qualities and is held within the other qualities.

There, the bitter quality rages and storms, seeking rest or nourishment, but finds none; it seethes within the body like a famished poison.

88. Then, when the **heat** ignites the sweet quality—intending to soften its heat in the sweet water so that it may rise and shine throughout the entire body—it finds nothing but a hard, dry, and sweet source where there is no juice within, for it is entirely dried up by the harshness.

89. It then ignites the sweet source, intending to refresh itself, but there is no more sap. Instead, the sweet source now burns and glows like a hard, parched stone, and it can no longer ignite its light. The entire body now remains a **valley of darkness** <note>original: "Finsterthal"</note>, where nothing is inside but a fierce, hard cold in the harsh quality; a hard, glowing fire in the sweet quality, in which fierce heat rises for all eternity; and a raging, storming, stinging, and burning in the bitter quality.

107. O you Guardians of Israel <note>A reference to the clergy and religious leaders of Böhme's time</note>, why do you sleep? Thus speaks the Lord: "Will you not pasture my people, whom I have entrusted to you?" Behold, I have set you upon Moses' Seat <note>original: "Mosis Stul," referring to the position of religious authority and teaching</note> and entrusted my flock to you, but you care only for the wool and not for my little sheep. With it, you build your palatial houses, but I will set you upon the Seat of Pestilence, and my Shepherd shall pasture my little sheep eternally.

<summary>Böhme delivers a passionate rebuke of the devil’s pride and a warning to humanity against worldly greed and complacency. He contrasts the "angelic garment" of man's origin with the "devil's mask" of a sinful life, while also criticizing corrupt religious leaders for neglecting their flocks.</summary>

# Morning Redness in the Rising. Ch. 9.

108. O you beautiful world, how heaven mourns for you, how you grieve the elements! O malice, when will you cease? Wake up, wake up, and give birth, you sorrowful woman; see, your Bridegroom comes and demands fruit from you. Why do you sleep? See, he knocks! <note>Böhme uses the "Bridegroom" metaphor from the Bible (Matthew 25) to represent Christ’s return or the soul's awakening.</note>

109. O lovely love and clear light, stay with us, for evening is drawing near. O truth, O justice and righteous judgment, where have you gone? The spirit wonders, as if it had never seen the world before. Oh, why do I even write of the world’s malice? I am compelled to do it, and yet the world gives me the devil’s thanks in return? Alas! Amen.

## Chapter 9.

### Concerning the lovely, kind, and merciful love of God.

#### The great heavenly and divine Mystery.

->**I.**<-

Since I write here of heavenly and divine things which are quite foreign to the corrupt nature of man, the reader will no doubt wonder and be offended by the author’s simplicity. This is because the corrupt natural impulse looks only for what is high—like a proud, wild, lustful, and harlot-like woman who, in her heat, is always looking for handsome men to woo.

2. So too is the haughty, corrupt nature of man; it looks only for what glitters and parades before the world. It imagines that God has forgotten the miserable, and that this is why He plagues them. Nature thinks the Holy Spirit looks only toward the high things: toward the art <term>art: Böhme often uses "art" (Kunst) to mean academic learning or human cleverness</term> of this world and toward great and deep study.

3. But if you wish to see if it is truly so, just look back and you will find the foundation. Who was Abel? A shepherd. Who were Enoch and Noah? Simple people. Who were Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob? They were cattle herdsmen. Who was Moses, that dear man of God? A cattle herdsman. Who was David when the Lord’s mouth called him? A shepherd. Who were the prophets, great and small? Common and lowly little people; some were just farmers and shepherds who were merely the world’s 

<column-break/>

# Ch. 9. Morning Redness in the Rising.

foot-cloth <note>original: "Fußhader." A rag used to wipe or scrub feet; a metaphor for being treated as trash or a doormat.</note>; they were held to be nothing but fools. And even though they performed wonders and signs, the world still looked only at what was high, and the Holy Spirit had to be their footstool—for the proud devil has always wanted to be a king in this world.

4. Now, how did our King Jesus Christ come into this world? Poor and in great sorrow and misery, and he had nowhere to lay his head (Matthew 8:20).

5. Who were his apostles? Poor, despised, unlearned fishing-servants. Who believed their preaching? The poor, lowly little people. The high priests and scribes <term>scribes: the "Schriftgelehrten" or biblical scholars of the day, whom Böhme often contrasts with those who have direct spiritual experience</term> were Christ’s executioners, who cried out: "Crucify him, crucify him!" <note>original Latin: "Crucifige, Crucifige"</note> (Luke 23:21).

6. Who has always stood most firmly by the Church of Christ? The poor, despised little people; they have shed their blood for Christ’s sake. Who has corrupted the true, pure Christian doctrine and always attacked it? The scribes, popes, cardinals, bishops, and great crowds of the powerful. Why did the world follow them? Because they had a grand appearance and paraded before the world. Such a proud harlot is corrupt human nature!

7. Who swept the Pope’s greed, idolatry, finances, and deceit out of the churches in Germany? A poor, despised monk <note>A reference to Martin Luther.</note>. By what power or might? Through the power of God the Father and through the strength of God the Holy Spirit.

8. What is still hidden? The true doctrine of Christ? No, but rather "Philosophy" <note>By "Philosophy," Böhme means "Theosophy"—the deep, hidden understanding of how God, nature, and humanity are interconnected.</note>, and the deep ground of God: the heavenly joy, the revelation of the creation of angels, the revelation of the devil's horrific fall (from which evil comes), the creation of this world, the deep ground and mystery of man and all creatures in this world, the Last Judgment and the transformation of this world, and the mystery of the resurrection of the dead and of eternal life.

9. These things shall rise up from the depths in great simplicity. Why not in the heights of "art"? So that no one may boast that he has done it, and so that the devil's pride might be uncovered and brought to nothing. Why does God do this? Out of His great love and mercy for all peoples, and to show that there is now at hand...

<summary>In this opening to Chapter 9, Böhme argues that divine wisdom is revealed to the simple and lowly rather than the academic or powerful, citing biblical figures and Martin Luther as examples. He promises to reveal the "deep ground" of creation and the mysteries of the spiritual world through this humble perspective.</summary>

For God does not look upon what is high—for He alone is high—but He looks to see how He may help the lowly. ->Now note.<-

Lovely love, which is the fifth source-spirit <term>source-spirit: Böhme’s term (*Quellgeist*) for the seven fundamental forces or "qualities" that constitute the nature of both God and the universe</term> in the divine power, is the hidden fountain that the corporeal being cannot grasp or encompass, except when it rises within the body; then the body triumphs in it and bears itself in a friendly and lovely manner. For it does not belong to the forming of a body, but rises within the body like a flower from the earth.

Now this same source-spirit initially takes its origin from the sweet quality of water.

->Understand this, however it may be; note it here properly.<-

13. First is the astringent <note>original: *herbe*; this represents the contractive, cooling force that creates structure and hardness.</note> quality, then the sweet, then the bitter; the sweet is located in the middle between the astringent and the bitter. Now, the astringent always makes things hard, cold, and dark; and the bitter tears, drives, rages, and cuts. These two qualities rub and drive each other so hard, and boil so intensely, that they generate heat; this heat is dark within the two qualities, like the heat in a stone.

14. When one takes a stone, or some other hard thing, and rubs it on wood, both things heat up; now,

this same heat is only a darkness, and there is no light within it; so it is also in the divine power. Now, the astringent and bitter qualities, without the sweet water, rub and drive each other so hard that they generate the dark heat and ignite it within themselves.

15. And this together is the wrath of God, the fountain and origin of hellfire—as can be seen in Lucifer. He elevated himself and squeezed himself together so hard with his legions that the sweet source-water dried up within him—the water in which the light ignites and in which love rises. Therefore, he is now eternally an astringent, hard, cold, bitter, and hot, as well as a sour, stinking wellspring. ->Now further into the depth.<-

16. When the astringent and bitter qualities rub each other so hard that they generate heat, the sweet quality—the sweet source-water—is in the middle between the astringent and the bitter; and the heat is born in the sweet source-water between the astringent and bitter qualities, through the astringent and bitter qualities.

17. There, the light ignites in the heat within the sweet source-water; this is the beginning of life. For the astringent and bitter qualities are the beginning and a cause of the heat and the light; thus, the sweet source-water becomes a shining light, like the blue, bright sky.

18. And that same light source-water ignites the astringent and bitter qualities; and the heat, which is born from the astringent and bitter qualities in the sweet water, rises out of the sweet source-water through the bitter and astringent qualities. And it is in the bitter and astringent qualities that the light first becomes dry and shining, as well as mobile and triumphant.

19. 20. Then the bitter quality trembles and disperses the hardness...

### Note this with deep understanding.

21. How could love and joy not be there, where life is born in the midst of death, and light in the midst of darkness? You may ask, how does this happen? Indeed, if my spirit sat in your heart and welled up within your heart, your body would feel and grasp it; but otherwise I cannot bring it into your mind, nor can you grasp or understand it, unless the Holy Spirit ignites your soul so that this light shines in your own heart. Then this light is born in you just as it is in God, and it rises in your astringent <term>astringent: Böhme's term is *herb*, referring to a cold, contracting, and harsh force that provides structure but can be bitter without the light</term> and bitter quality in your sweet water, and triumphs as it does in God: when this happens, then you will first understand my book, and not before.

->Note.<-

22. When the light is born in the bitter quality, that is, when the bitter and dry welling catches the sweet spring-water of life and drinks it, the bitter spirit becomes alive in the astringent spirit, and the astringent spirit is now like a pregnant spirit, pregnant with life, and must always give birth to life. For the sweet water, and the light within that sweet water, now rise continually in the astringent quality, and the bitter quality triumphs continually therein, and it is nothing but pure laughter and joy, pure loving.

23. For the astringent quality loves the sweet water, (1.) because the spirit of light is born in the sweet water, and it drenches the astringent, hard, and cold quality, and enlightens and warms it; for in the water, heat, and light, there stands the life.

24. Furthermore, the astringent quality loves the bitter one, because the bitter triumphs within the astringent through the sweet water—that is, through the water, heat, and light—and makes the astringent mobile, wherein the astringent can also triumph.

25. Thirdly, the astringent quality loves the heat, because the light is born in the heat, by which the astringent quality is enlightened and warmed.

26. And the sweet quality also loves the astringent, (1.) because it dries the sweet quality so that it does not become thin, like elemental water, and so its quality persists in power, and so that in the astringent quality the light born within it becomes shining and dry. In addition, the astringent quality is a cause of the heat which is born in the sweet water, in which the light rises and in which the sweet water stands in great clarity.

27. Secondly, the sweet quality also loves the bitter, because it is also a cause of the heat, and also because the bitter spirit triumphs and trembles in the sweet water, heat, and light, making the sweet one mobile and alive.

28. Thirdly, the sweet quality loves the heat exceedingly much, so much that I can compare it to nothing; take an illustration (though it is far too meager) of two young people of noble constitution <note>original: *complexion*; referring to the humoral balance or temperament of a person</note>: when they heat each other in the fire of love, such a fire arises that, could they take each other into their bodies or transform themselves into one, they would do so. But this earthly love is only cold water and not true fire; one can find no true comparison in this half-dead world, except for the resurrection of the dead on the last day, which is a perfect comparison for all divine things receiving true love.

29. However, the sweet quality loves the heat so much because it gives birth to the light spirit within it, which is the spirit of life; for life arises in the heat, otherwise, where heat were not present, everything would be a dark valley. Just as life is dear, so too is heat dear to the sweet spirit, and the light within that heat.

30. And the bitter quality also loves all other source-spirits: first the sweet, for in the sweet water the bitter spirit is refreshed, and it quenches its great thirst therein, and its bitterness is softened therein and gains its light life; and in the astringent it has its body, in which it triumphs and cools and softens itself; and in the heat it has its power and strength, in which its joy stands.

31. And the heat quality also loves all the other qualities, and the love within it toward the others is so great that it cannot be compared to anything, for it is born from the others. The astringent and bitter qualities are the father of the Heat, and the sweet spring-water is its mother, who conceives, retains, and gives birth to it; for through the harsh driving of the astringent <term>astringent: *herb* in German, referring to the cold, contracting force that provides structure</term> and the bitter, the Heat is produced, rising up within the sweet quality as if within wood.

32. If you will not believe this, then open your eyes and go to a tree; look at it and reflect. First, you see the whole tree. Take a knife and cut into it, and taste it as it is: first, you will taste the astringent quality, which draws your tongue together—now, this same quality also holds and draws together all the power of the tree. Afterward, you taste the bitter quality, which makes the tree mobile, so that it grows, turns green, and develops its branches, leaves, and fruit. Afterward, you taste the Sweetness, which is quite gentle yet sharp, for it receives its sharpness from the astringent and bitter qualities.

33. Now, these three qualities would be dark and dead if the Heat were not within them; but as soon as springtime comes and the sun reaches the earth with its rays and warms it, the spirit in the Heat becomes alive within the tree. Then the spirits of the tree begin to turn green, grow, and bloom. For the spirit rises in the Heat, and all the spirits rejoice within it and live within it, and there is a heartfelt love between them. The Heat, however, is born through the power and drive of the astringent and bitter qualities in the sweet water; but they must use the sun's heat for the ignition, because the qualities in this world are half-dead and too powerless—a condition for which King Lucifer is a cause, which you will find explained in the account of his fall and the creation of this world.

### Of the Friendly Love, Loveliness, and Unity of these Five Source-Spirits of God.

34. Although it is impossible to write enough of this with human hands, the enlightened spirit of man sees it nonetheless; for it rises in the same form and birth as the light does in the divine power, and also in those same qualities that are in God.

35. This alone is to be lamented in man: that his qualities are corrupted and half-dead. Therefore, the spirit of man—or his fountain-springs <term>fountain-springs: *Quellen*, the internal movements of the soul's qualities</term>—cannot reach any perfection by rising or igniting in this world.

36. On the other hand, there is great reason to rejoice that the spirit of man, in its necessity, is illuminated and ignited by the Holy Spirit, just as the sun ignites the cold heat in a tree or plant, whereby the cold heat becomes alive.

->Now note.<-

37. Just as the members of a human body love one another, so also do the spirits in the divine power. There is nothing there but pure longing, desiring, and fulfilling, as well as triumphing and rejoicing in one another. For through these spirits come understanding and distinction in God, in angels, humans, beasts, and birds, and in everything that lives. For in these five qualities rise seeing, smelling, tasting, and feeling, and it becomes a rational spirit.

38. When the light rises, then one spirit sees the other; and when the sweet spring-water in the light goes through all the spirits, then one tastes the other. At that point, the spirits become alive, and the power of life penetrates through everything. In that same power, one smells the other, and through this welling and penetrating, one feels the other. And there is nothing but a heartfelt loving and friendly seeing, pleasant smelling, pleasant tasting, and lovely feeling—a beautiful kissing, eating and drinking of one another, and walking together in love.

39. This is the lovely bride who rejoices in her bridegroom <note>Böhme uses the traditional mystical imagery of the "Marriage of the Soul," where the individual's inner qualities unite with the Divine</note>; therein is love, joy, and delight; there is light and clarity; there is a lovely fragrance; there is a friendly and sweet taste. Oh, and eternally without end, how can a heavenly creature sufficiently rejoice therein? Oh Love and Loveliness, you have no end; one sees no end in you! Your depth is unsearchable; you are thus everywhere, only not in the fierce devils—they have corrupted you within themselves.

### Question.

**Do you now say: Where then are these lovely spirits to be found; do they dwell only within themselves in heaven?**

### Answer.

40. This is the other open gate of the Godhead; here you may open your eyes wide and awaken the spirit in your half-dead heart, for this is no delusion, poem, or fantasy.

### Observe.

41. The seven Spirits of God encompass in their circle or space the Heaven and this world, and the breadth and depth outside and above the Heavens, above the world, and under the world, and in the world—yes, the entire Father, who has neither beginning nor end. They also encompass all creatures in Heaven and in this world, and all creatures in Heaven and in this world are formed out of these spirits and live within them as in their own property. And their life and reason are born within them in such a way as the divine being is born, and also in that same power. And out of that same *corpus* <note>Latin: "body"</note> of the seven Spirits of God, all things are made and have come forth: all angels, all devils, the heaven, the earth, the stars, the elements, humans, animals, birds, fish, all worms, the wood and trees, as well as stones, herbs, and grass, and everything that exists.

### Now you ask:

Since God is everywhere and is himself everything, how does it happen that in this world there is such cold and heat, and moreover, all creatures bite and strike one another, and there is nothing but sheer fierceness <term>fierceness: *Grimmigkeit* in German, referring to the "wrathful" or "dark" side of nature when it is out of balance</term> in this world?

> [The cause is the first four forms of nature, where each one is hostile to the other outside of the Light, and yet they are the causes of life.]

42. Behold, this is the cause and the malice: when King Lucifer sat in his kingdom like a proud, haughty bride, his circle encompassed the place where the created heaven now is (which is made from water), and also the place of the created world up to heaven, as well as the depth where the earth is now. All of that was a pure and holy Salitter <term>Salitter: Böhme's term for the divine "salt-nitre" or the fundamental "stuff" of the divine realm</term>,

litter, where the seven Spirits of God were perfect and lovely, just as it is in Heaven—though they are still perfect in this world, you must only note the circumstances correctly.

43. When King Lucifer rose up, he rose up in the seven source-spirits and ignited them with his uprising, so that everything became completely burning. The harsh quality became so hard that it gave birth to stones, and so cold that it turned the sweet spring-water into ice. And the sweet spring-water became quite thick and stinking, and the bitter quality became quite raging, tearing, and raving, from which poison arose; and the fire or heat became entirely zealous, burning, and consuming, and it was altogether an evil temperance and mixture.

45. Now the source-spirits have become so fierce in their ignition that one always ruins the other with its evil source; so also do the creatures now, who are made from the source-spirits and live in that same drive, where everything bites, pushes, and envies one another according to the nature of the qualities.

46. And then two parts will come of this kingdom: one part the humans will obtain with their King Jesus Christ; the other, the devils with all godless people of malice.

47. This is thus a short introduction, so that the reader might understand the divine mystery all the better. In the fall of the devil and in the creation of this world, you will find everything described in detail according to its length; therefore, we have exhorted the reader to read everything in its proper order, so that he will come upon the right foundation.

## The 10th Chapter.
### Concerning the 6th Source-Spirit in the Divine Power.

->1.<-

The 6th source-spirit <term>source-spirit: *Quellgeist* in German; Böhme’s term for the seven fundamental forces or "qualities" that constitute the divine being and all of creation</term> in the divine power is the Sound or Tone, so that everything within it sounds and rings; from this follows speech and the distinction of all things, as well as the ringing and song of the holy angels. Within it also resides the formation of all colors and beauty, as well as the heavenly realm of joy.

Now you ask: what is the Tone and Sound, or how does this spirit take its source and origin?

->Observe:<-

2. All seven Spirits of God are born into one another; one always generates the other. None is the first, and none is the last; for the last generates the first just as much as the first generates the second, third, fourth, and so on until the last.

3. However, that one is called the first and another the second, and so forth, is viewed according to which one is the first in the formation and shaping of a creature. For they are all seven equally eternal, and none has a beginning or an end. And because the seven qualities always generate one another, and none exists outside the others, it follows that there is one single, eternal, almighty God.

4. For when something is born out of or within the divine being, it is not formed by one spirit alone, but by all seven. And if a creature—which exists just like the whole being of God—corrupts itself, elevates itself, or "ignites" itself within one source-spirit, it does not ignite only one spirit, but all seven.

5. Therefore, that same creature is an abomination before the whole of God and all His creatures, and must stand in eternal enmity and shame before God and all creatures.

6. The Sound or Mercury <note>original: *Mercurius*. In Böhme's theosophy, Mercury represents the "expressed word," the spirit of sound and communication that gives form to the divine will.</note> takes its origin in the first quality, that is, in the harsh and hard quality.

->Observe in the depth.<-

7. Hardness is the fountain-well of the Sound; however, it cannot generate it alone. Rather, Hardness is the father to it, and the whole Salitter <term>Salitter: A term Böhme uses for the divine "sap" or the "salt-nitre" of the heavenly earth; the fundamental substance of the divine realm</term> is the mother. Otherwise, if Hardness alone were both father and mother of the Sound, a hard stone would also have to ring out; but as it is, it only thuds and knocks, like a seed or a beginning of the Sound—and that it certainly is.

8. But the resonance or voice rises in the middle Center within the Flash, where the Light is born out of the Heat, where the Flash of Life goes up.

->Observe how this happens.<-

9. When the harsh quality rubs against the bitter one, so that the Heat rises in the sweet source-water, then the Heat ignites the sweet source-water like a Flash. That same Flash is the Light; it travels in the Heat into the bitter quality, and there the Flash is "decided" <note>or "distinguished"</note> according to all power.

10. For in the bitter quality, all powers are distinguished, and the bitter quality catches the Flash of Light as if it were terribly startled; and with its trembling and startling, it travels into the harsh and hard quality, and there it is caught bodily <note>original: *corporlich* / *corpus*</note>. And the bitter quality is now pregnant with the Light, and it trembles within the harsh and hard quality, and moves within it, being caught in the harsh quality as if in a body.

11. And when the spirits now move and wish to speak, the hard quality must open itself, for the bitter spirit with its Flash bursts it open; and then the Sound goes out, and is pregnant with all seven spirits, which distinguish the word as it was resolved in the Center—that is, in the middle circle, when it was still in the counsel of the seven spirits.

12. And for this reason, the seven Spirits of God created a mouth for the creatures, so that when they want to speak or sound, they do not first need to tear themselves apart; and therefore all veins and power-spirits or source-spirits go into the tongue, so that the Sound or Tone goes out gently.

->Here observe specifically the meaning and mystery.<-

23. Every spirit has its own wellspring, and even though it is born from the others: so also is the comprehensibility of man. ### Now note further here concerning Mercury, Tone, or Sound.

33. All qualities take their initial origin in the center; note where the fire is born, for there the flash of life of all qualities rises up, and is caught in the water, so that it remains luminous, and is dried in the astringency <note>original: "Herbigkeit"</note>, so that it remains corporeal and will shine brightly.

### Note here.

34. Light a piece of wood, and you shall see the mystery: the fire ignites in the hardness of the wood; that is now the astringent, hard source, the Saturn-source, which makes the wood hard and firm. <term>Saturn: *Saturnus*; the quality of contraction, cold, and "thing-ness" that gives spirit a material form.</term> But the light—that is, the flash—does not consist in the hardness, otherwise a stone would burn too; rather, the light consists in the sap of the wood, which is the water. As long as there is sap in the wood, the fire shines as a glowing light; but when the sap in the wood is consumed, the shining light goes out, and the wood becomes a glowing coal.

35. Now behold, the fierceness <note>original: "Grimmigkeit"; often refers to the raw, untempered energy of the dark foundation</note> that rises up in the light does not consist in the water of the wood; rather, when the heat rises in the hardness, the flash is born; the sap in the wood catches it first, from which the

36. But you should know this mystery: that the bitterness is already in the wood beforehand, otherwise the fierce bitterness would not be born so suddenly in the natural fire.

37. For just as the body of the fire is born when one lights wood, in exactly such a way is the wood born in the earth and above the earth.

39. For every spirit among the seven spirits of God is pregnant with all seven spirits of God, and they are all in one another like one spirit; none is outside the other: only such a birth takes place therein, and thus one gives birth to the other, in and through itself, and the birth lasts from eternity to eternity.

42. For when you rouse yourself in your body against something, whether against love or in wrath, whichever you rouse yourself against, you ignite that quality, and it burns in your incorporated spirit. In the **flash**, however, that same **source-spirit** <term>Source-spirit: *Quellgeist*; Böhme’s term for the seven fundamental forces—such as bitterness, heat, and sound—that flow through all existence.</term> is awakened.
