Then it is time to extinguish it, or the fire will become too great; then it burns and consumes, and does damage to its neighbor.

->Now you might say:<-

43. How can one extinguish the ignited fire? Listen: you have the **sweet source-water** within you; pour it into the fire, and it will go out. If you let it burn, it consumes the sap in all seven source-spirits, so that you become dry. When that happens, you are a brand of hell and a poker for the hellish fire, and there is eternally no counsel for you. <note>A "brand of hell" refers to a piece of wood destined for the fire; a "poker" (*Schürknittel*) is a tool used to stoke the flames.</note>

44. But when you look at something that you love, and awaken the spirit in the heart, you ignite the fire in the heart; it burns first in the sweet water like a glowing coal. While it only smolders, it is merely a gentle delight within you and does not consume you. But if you stir the heart even more and ignite the sweet source so that it becomes a burning flame, then you ignite all the source-spirits; then the whole body burns and reaches out with mouth and hands.

45. This fire is the most harmful, and has caused the most ruin since the world began, and is very difficult to extinguish. For when it is ignited, it burns in the sweet water, in the **flash of life**, and must be extinguished through bitterness—which is a miserable water indeed, or rather, fire itself. Therefore, a very sorrowful mind follows when one must give up that which burns in their love-fire in the sweet source-water.

46. But you should know this: that in the governance of your mind, you are your own master. No fire arises in the circle of your body and spirit unless you awaken it yourself. It is true that all your spirits well up within you and rise up in you, and certainly one spirit always has greater power and strength in you than another. For if the governance of the spirits were the same in one person as in another, we would all have one will and one form. But they are all seven within the power of your incorporated spirit, which spirit is called the **soul**.
[“She has within herself the first **principle** <note>original: *Principium*</note>, the soul's spirit has the second, and the sidereal spirit in the elements has the third, as does this world.”] <note>Böhme divides reality into three "principles": the dark fire-world (1st), the light love-world (2nd), and the external physical world (3rd).</note>

47. So if a fire arises in a source-spirit, it is not hidden from the soul; she may immediately awaken the other source-spirits that are opposed to the ignited fire and may extinguish it. But if the fire wants to become too great, she has her **prison** where she may lock up the ignited spirit—namely, in the hard, astringent quality—and the other spirits must be its jailers until their wrath passes and the fire is extinguished.

->Note what this is:<-

48. When a source-spirit drives you too harshly toward a thing that is against the laws of nature, you must turn your eyes away from it. If that does not help, then take that same spirit and throw it into prison. That is, turn your heart away from temporal lust, from gluttony and drunkenness, from the riches of this world, and think that today is the day of your body's end; turn away from the world's vanity and call earnestly to God, and surrender yourself to Him.

49. When you do this, the world mocks you, and you must be its fool; carry this cross with patience, and do not let the imprisoned spirit out of its prison again. Trust God; He will set upon you the crown of divine joys.

50. But if the spirit breaks out of prison again, put it back in; hold your ground against it as long as you live. If you only maintain yourself so much that it does not completely ignite the fountainhead of the heart—whereby your soul becomes dry firewood—and each source still has its sap when you depart from here, then the ignited fire will, on the Last Day <note>original: *Jüngstentage*</note>, be to you...

# The Dawn in the Rising. Chapter 10.

...[it shall] do no harm, and will not cling to your **sap-spirits**, but after this anxious tribulation, you will be a triumphing angel of God in the resurrection. <note>The "sap-spirits" (*Saftgeister*) refer to the vital, fluid energies that Böhme believed carried the life-force through both the human body and the cosmos.</note>

51. Now you might say: Is there then also a conflict between the spirits of God? No; although I show here their earnest birth—how the spirits of God are born so earnestly and severely, whereby everyone may well understand the great earnestness of God—it does not follow from this that there is any disunity between them.

52. For the most inward, deepest birth in the **kernel** <term>Kernel: *Kern*; the essential, innermost point of a thing's being.</term> is such that no creature can grasp it in the body (*corpus*), but rather in the **flash**, where the hidden spirit is born; there it is grasped, for that spirit is also born in such a way and in such power. <note>The "flash" (*Blitz*) is Böhme’s term for the sudden moment of spiritual ignition or enlightenment where raw energy is transformed into light and consciousness.</note>

53. But the gate of my **mind** is opened for me, so that I can see and recognize it; otherwise, it would remain well hidden from me until the day of the resurrection from the dead. It has also been hidden from all people since the world began, but I let God have His way.

54. In God, all spirits triumph like one spirit, and one spirit always soothes and loves the other, and there is nothing but pure joy and delight. Their severe birth, however, which happens in the hiddenness, must be so; for life, understanding, and omniscience are born in this way, and that is an eternal birth that is never otherwise.

55. You must not think that in heaven there is perhaps a body (*corpus*) that is born only in such a way, which one might call "God" above everything else. No; rather, the entire divine power, which is itself heaven and the heaven of all heavens, is born in this way. And that is called **God the Father**, from whom all holy angels have been born, and in whose power they also live. And the spirit of all angels in their body is also born in this way, always and eternally, as is the spirit of all human beings.

56. For this world also belongs to the body (*corpus*) of God the Father, just as heaven does. But the spirits in the vastness of this world were ignited by King Lucifer in his prideful elevation, so that everything in this world is as if half-faint and dead; therefore, we poor humans are so very blinded and live in great danger.

<meta>catchword: 57. You</meta>

<column-break/>

# Chapter 10. The Dawn in the Rising.

57. But you should not think that the heavenly light is entirely extinguished in the **source-spirits** of God in this world. No; it is only a **darkness** which we cannot grasp with our corrupted eyes. But if God were to take away the darkness that hovers over the light, and if your eyes were opened, you would see right here in the place where you stand, sit, or lie in your chamber, the beautiful face of God and the entire heavenly gate. You would not first need to cast your eyes up into the sky, for it is written: **"The word is near you, namely on your lips and in your heart."** <note>original citation: Deut. 30, 14. Rom. 10, 8. Böhme is quoting the Bible to argue that the divine reality is a present, internal experience rather than a distant location.</note>

58. God is so near to you that the birth of the **Holy Trinity** also happens in your heart; all three Persons are born in your heart: God the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit.

59. Now, when I write here of the **center** (*centro*) or the middle—that the fountain-spring of the divine birth is in the middle—it does not mean that there is a specific place in heaven or a specific body where the fire of divine life rises and from which the seven spirits of God go out into the entire depth of the Father. Rather, I speak in a bodily, or angelic, or human way, for the sake of the reader's lack of understanding—in the manner in which angelic creatures were formed, and how it is in God everywhere.

60. For you can name no place, neither in heaven nor in this world, where the divine birth is not thus; whether it be in an angel or a holy person, or outside of them. Wherever a **source-spirit** is stirred in the divine power—wherever that place may be, except only in the devils and in all godless, damned people—there the fountain-spring of the divine birth is already present. There all seven source-spirits of God are already there, just as if you enclosed a physical, creaturely circle and had the entire Godhead specifically within it, exactly as it is born in a creature; so it is also in the entire depth of the Father at all ends and in all things.

61. And in such a way, God is an almighty, all-knowing, all-seeing, all-hearing, all-smelling, all-tasting...

<meta>catchword: ...tasting</meta>

<summary>Böhme explains that God is not a distant entity but a pervasive divine power whose "birth" occurs everywhere, including within the human heart. He clarifies that the struggle of creation is not a conflict in God but a necessary process for life and joy, though it has been obscured in our world by Lucifer's fall.</summary>

# The Dawn in the Rising. Chapter 10.

...[all-]knowing, all-feeling GOD, who is everywhere, and who tests the hearts and kidneys of all creatures. <note>original: "Herzen und Nieren prüfet." A biblical idiom (Psalm 7:9) meaning God examines the most secret thoughts and deepest emotions.</note> In such a way, Heaven and Earth are His, and in such a way all devils, along with all godless people, must be His eternal prisoners. They must suffer eternal pain in the **divine substance** <term>Divine substance: *Salitter*. Böhme’s term for the fundamental "earthly" or material quality of the divine realm, which can be corrupted into "hell" if "ignited" by wrath.</term> which they have corrupted and set on fire in their **place** <note>original: "Loco"</note>, and bear eternal disgrace and shame besides.

62. For the entire beautiful face of God, together with all the holy angels, will shine beautifully, gloriously, and clearly above them, below them, and on all sides next to them. All the holy angels, along with all holy people, will eternally triumph over them, under them, and beside them. They will sing with great joy, delight, and loveliness of God’s holiness, of their royal government, and of the sweet fruit of the heavenly growth. This will resonate in many voices according to the quality of the Seven Spirits of God.

63. By contrast, the devils, with all godless people, will be squeezed into a hole. There, a hellish stench, torment, and rising vapors will be found. The hellish fire, the hellish cold, and the bitterness will burn eternally in their **body** <note>original: "Corpus"</note> as well as in their **territory** <note>original: "Revier"</note>, according to the nature of the "ignited" spirits of God. Indeed, if they could only be locked in a hole where the angry face of GOD did not touch them, they would be satisfied and would not have to endure eternal disgrace and shame.

64. But there is no help; their torment only grows the more they mourn it. The more they mourn, the more the hellish fury ignites. They must lie in hell like dead bones, like scorched sheep in the fire. Their own stench and horror gnaw at them. They dare not lift their eyes for shame, for they see nothing in their realm but a stern judge; and above themselves and on all sides, they see eternal joy.

> "It is not that they grasp or see it,
> "but they have a knowledge of it in the **Center** <note>original: "Centro"</note>."

65. There is only "alas" and "woe," wailing and screaming, and no salvation. To them, it is as if it is always thundering and lightning, for that is how the ignited spirits of GOD behave. The first quality, **Harshness**, produces a hard, rough, cold, and bitter quality. The second, **Sweetness**, is parched like a glowing coal when there is no more sap in the wood; it thirsts, and there is no refreshment there.

3. **Bitterness** tears like a hot pestilence and is as bitter as gall. 4. **Fire** burns like fierce sulfur. 5. **Love** is an enmity. 6. **Sound** is nothing but hard pounding, like a hollow sound of fire, as if a thunderclap occurred. The realm of the 7th **body** <note>original: "Corpus"</note> is a house of mourning. Their food is an abomination and grows out of the fury of every quality: Alas, and eternally without end! There is no time there; another King sits upon their throne, who holds an eternal judgment; they are only his footstool.

66. Oh, beauty and pleasure of this world! O wealth and proud splendor! O power and authority! Your unjust judgment and great magnificence, with all your pleasure, all lie in a heap and have become hellfire. Now eat, now drink, now paint yourself with it, now rule within it—you beautiful goddess, how you have become a whore! Your shame and disgrace shall last eternally.

### Chapter 11.

#### Concerning the 7th Fountain-Spirit in the Divine Power.

The seventh Spirit of GOD in the divine power is the **Body** <note>original: "Corpus"</note>, which is born from the other six spirits. In it, all heavenly figures exist; within it, everything is formed and shaped; and within it, all beauty and joy arise. This is the true Spirit of Nature—indeed, Nature itself—in which **tangibility** <note>original: "Begreiflichkeit"</note> resides, and in which all creatures are formed in Heaven and on Earth. Yes, Heaven itself is formed within it, and all naturalness in the whole of GOD resides in this Spirit. If this Spirit did not exist, there would be neither angel nor human, and GOD would be an unsearchable Being, consisting only of unsearchable power.

2. Now the question is: what is this form? If you are a rational **Mercury-spirit** <term>Mercury-spirit: *Mercurius-Geist*. In Böhme’s alchemical language, this refers to a mind that is spiritually mobile, perceptive, and capable of understanding the "language" of nature’s forces.</term> who penetrates through all seven Spirits of GOD, and approves and sees them as they are, then by the explanation of this 7th Spirit, you will understand the working and the essence of the entire Godhead and grasp it in your mind.

3. But if you understand nothing by this Spirit, then leave this book alone and do not judge the cold or the warm within it...

Just let your judging be, or you will receive a wicked reward, of which I faithfully wish to have warned you; wait until the next life, and then the gates of heaven will be opened to you, and then you will also understand it.

### Now note the depth.

4. **H**ere I must grasp the whole divine **Body** <note>original: "Corpus"</note> in the middle by the heart, and explain the whole **Body**, how nature comes to be; there you will see the highest ground, how all seven Spirits of God always beget one another, and how the Godhead has no beginning nor end. Therefore, behold the delight of your spirit, and the eternal, divine kingdom of joy—the heavenly bliss and bodily joys which have no end in eternity.

### Now note.

5. **W**hen the **Flash** <term>Flash: *Blitz*. A central concept in Böhme’s work, representing the sudden ignition of divine light and consciousness that transforms the "dark" qualities of nature into "light" qualities.</term> rises in the **Center** <note>original: "Centro"</note>, then the divine birth stands in full effect; in God it is always and eternally so, but in us poor children of the flesh, it is not. In this life, the triumphant divine birth lasts in us humans only as long as the **Flash** lasts; therefore our knowledge is piece-meal, but in God the **Flash** stands unchangeably, always and eternally so.

6. Behold, all seven Spirits of God are born at the same time; none is the first, and none is the last. But one must look at the core of how the divine birth rises, otherwise it cannot be understood; for the creatures cannot grasp all seven within each other at once, but they look upon them. However, when one Spirit is stirred, it stirs all the others, and so the birth stands in full power. Therefore, it has a beginning in man, but in God it has none; for that reason I must write in a "creaturely" way <note>Böhme means he is explaining things from a limited, human perspective that uses time and sequence, even though God exists outside of them.</note>, otherwise you would understand nothing.

7. Behold, all seven Spirits would be a dark valley without the **Flash**; but when the **Flash** rises in the heat between the **harsh** <term>Harsh: *herb*. The quality of contraction, cold, and "pulling together."</term> and the **bitter** qualities, it becomes shining in the **sweet water**, and in the flames of heat it becomes bitter and triumphant and living, and in the **harsh** quality it becomes bodily, dry, and bright.

8. Now these four Spirits move in the **Flash**, for all four become living within it; now the power of these four rises in the **Flash**, as if life were rising up, and the risen

power in the **Flash** is **Love**, which is the fifth Spirit. This same power surges so lovably in the **Flash**, as if a dead spirit were becoming alive, and were suddenly placed into great clarity.

9. Now, in this surging, one power stirs the other; first the **harsh** knocks, and the **heat** makes a bright sound in that knocking, and the **bitter** power divides the sound, and the **water** makes it soft; that is the sixth Spirit.

10. Now the **Sound** <note>original: "Thon" / "Ton". The seven fundamental forces that "well up" to form the reality of God and the universe.</term>; and it is just like the seed of the other six Spirits, which they have all **embodied** <note>original: "corporiret"</note> together there, making one Spirit out of it, which has the quality of all Spirits; and that is the seventh Spirit of God in the divine power.

11. Now this Spirit exists in its color like the blue of the sky; for it is born from all six Spirits. Now, when the **Flash**, which exists in the midst of the heat, shines into the other Spirits so that they rise in the **Flash** and beget the seventh Spirit, then the **Flash** also rises in the birth of the six Spirits into the seventh.

12. But because the seventh has no particular quality in itself, the **Flash** cannot become brighter in the seventh; rather, it catches from the seventh the bodily essence of all seven Spirits, and the **Flash** stands in the middle between these seven Spirits, and is born of all seven.

13. And the seven Spirits are the **Father of the Light**, and the **Light** is their **Son**, whom they always beget from eternity to eternity in this way; and the **Light** illuminates and makes the seven Spirits living and joyful always and eternally, for they all take their rising and life in the power of the **Light**. Conversely, they all beget the **Light**, and are all at once the **Father of the Light**; and the **Light** begets no Spirit, but makes them all living and joyful, so that they always stand in the birth.

14. Behold, I will show it to you once more, in case you might perhaps grasp it, so that this high labor does not happen in vain without use.

15. The **harsh** quality is the first Spirit; it pulls together and makes everything dry. The **sweet** quality is the second Spirit; it softens it. Now the third Spirit is the **bitter** Spirit,

### The Holy Gates.

19. But the Light, which stands in the middle of all seven spirits, and in which the life of all seven spirits resides, and through which they all seven become triumphant and full of joy—wherein the heavenly kingdom of joy arises, so that all seven spirits give birth—is the **Son** of all seven spirits. The seven spirits are his **Father**, who give birth to the Light; and the Light gives birth to life within them. The Light is the **Heart** of the seven spirits, and this Light is the true **Son of God**, whom we Christians worship and honor as the second person in the Holy Trinity.

21. The **Flash**, or the Root, or the **Heart**, which is born within the powers, remains standing in the center, and that is the **Son**. This is the true **Holy Spirit**, whom we Christians honor and worship as the third person in the Godhead.

### What advantage then do the Christians have?

30. Much; for they know the way of life and know how they should rise from the Fall. But if one chooses to remain lying down, he will be cast into the pits, where he must perish with all the godless heathens. Therefore, look to what you do and who you are; you judge others and are blind yourself. But the Spirit says you have no cause to judge him who is better than you. Do we not all have one flesh, and does our life not consist in God, whether it be in love or in wrath? For what you sow, that you shall reap.

31. God is not the cause of your being lost; for the law to do right is written into nature, and you have that same book in your heart. You well know that you should act kindly and friendly toward your neighbor; so you also well know that you should not disgrace or defile your own life—that is, your body and soul.

32. Truly, in this lies the kernel and the love of God. God does not look at anyone's name or birth; rather, whoever moves in the love of God, moves in the light, and the light is the heart of God. Now, if someone sits with God in their heart, who shall spit them out? No one, for they are born in God.

33. O you blind and half-dead world, stop your judging! O you blind Jew, Turk, and Heathen, stop your blasphemy and give yourself over to the obedience of God and walk in the light. Then you will see how you should rise in your Fall, and how you should defend yourself in this world against the hellish **fierceness** <term>Fierceness: *Grimmigkeit*. This refers to the dark, consuming, and wrathful quality of nature when it is not tempered by the light of God's love.</term>, and how you can overcome and live eternally with God.

34. Truly there is only one God; but when the veil is taken away from your eyes so that you see and recognize Him, then you will also see and recognize all your brothers, whether they be Christians, Jews, Turks, or Heathens. Or do you think that God is only the God of Christians? Do not the Heathens also live in God? Whoever does right is dear and acceptable to Him. <note>original: Geschicht. 10, 35. Referring to Acts 10:35: "In every nation whoever fears Him and works righteousness is accepted by Him."</note> Or what did you, who are a Christian, know of how God wanted to redeem you from evil? What friendship did you have with Him, or what covenant did you have with Him, when God let His Son become a man to redeem the human race?

is he only your King? Is it not written: *He is the comfort of all nations?* <note>Haggai 2:7-8. Böhme uses the older verse numbering.</note>

35. Listen: through one man sin came into the world, and through that one it pressed through unto all (Romans 5:18); and through One came redemption into the world, and through that One it pressed through unto all. What does a person’s learned knowledge <note>original: "Wissenschaft" — here meaning formal education or theological training</note> matter now? For you also did not know how God intended to deal with you when you were dead in your sins.

36. Now, just as sin rules without distinction through one over all, so also mercy and redemption rule through One over all. However, blindness has befallen the Heathens <note>Non-Christians or pagans</note>, Jews, and Turks <note>A common 17th-century term for Muslims</note>; yet they nevertheless stand in the **anxious birth** <term>anxious birth: *ängstliche Geburt*. But God is everywhere, and he looks upon the ground of the heart. If, however, the light is born within them in their anxious birth, who are you to judge them?

37. See, you blind human, I will show it to you: go into a meadow, and there you see many kinds of herbs and flowers. You see bitter ones, you see harsh ones, sweet, sour, white, yellow, red, blue, green, and many others. Do they not all grow out of the earth? Do they not stand next to one another? Does one begrudge the other its beautiful form? If, however, one among them were to raise itself too high with its growth and wither because it does not have enough sap, what can the earth do about it? It gives that one its sap just as well as the others. But when thorns grow among them and the reaper <note>original: "Mäyer" — a field-steward or harvest official</note> comes to gather the harvest, he cuts them down with the rest and throws them away, and they are burned in the fire; but the various flowers he gathers into his barns.

38. So it is also with humans. There are many kinds of gifts and skills; one is much clearer in God than the other. But as long as they do not wither in the spirit, they are not rejectable; but when the spirit withers, it is good for nothing but firewood.

39. If, then, the Turks are of the **harsh quality** and the Heathens of the **bitter quality**, what is that to you? <term>quality: *Qualität*. In Böhme’s system, this refers to the fundamental forces or "source-properties" of nature (bitterness, heat, sweetness, etc.) that make up both the physical and spiritual worlds.</term> If the light becomes shining within the harsh and bitter quality, then it also gives light. You, however, are born in the heat, where the light rises in the sweet spring-water; see to it that the heat does not burn you up—you might well need to quench it.

40. Thus you say now: "Is it then right that the Heathens, Jews, and Turks persist in their blindness?" No; but I say this: how can he see who has no eyes? What does the poor layman know of the tumult the priests <note>original: "Pfaffen" — a derogatory term for clergy who Böhme felt were more interested in dogma than spirit.</note> make in their drunkenness? He goes along in his simplicity and gives birth with anxiety.

41. Thus you say now: "Did God then blind the Turks, Jews, and Heathens?" No; rather, when God kindled the light for them, they lived in their heart’s lust and would not allow themselves to be guided by the Spirit, and so the outward light was extinguished. However, it is not so completely extinguished that it could not be born in a person, since humanity is from God and lives in God, be it in love or in wrath.

42. Now, if a person yearns, should he not become pregnant in his yearning? And if he is pregnant, he can also give birth. But because the outward light shines upon him, he does not recognize his son whom he has born; however, when the light rises on the Last Day, then he shall see Him.

43. See, I tell you a mystery: it is already the time for the Bridegroom to crown his Bride. Guess, Fritz, <note>A German colloquialism similar to "Guess what?"</note> where does the crown lie? Toward midnight <note>The North</note>, for in the midst of the harsh quality, the light becomes bright. But from whence comes the Bridegroom? From the midst, where the heat gives birth to the light; he travels toward midnight into the harsh quality, and there the light becomes bright. What do those toward midday <note>The South</note> do then? They have fallen asleep in the heat, but a storm-weather will wake them; among them, many shall be terrified unto death.

44. What do those of the evening <note>The West</note> do then? Their bitter quality wants to rub against the others, but when they taste the sweet water, their spirit becomes gentle. What do those in the morning <note>The East</note> do then? You have been a proud bride from the beginning; the crown has always been offered to you from the beginning, but you thought yourself too beautiful before; you live with the others.

49. 50. You may also understand it by this comparison: as if seven people began a friendly game of joy, where each one triumphs over the other, and a third comes to the aid of the conquered one. and yet one contended against the other in pastime or love.

51. Such also is the working of the six spirits of God in the seventh; now one has a strong rising, now the other, and so they wrestle with each other in love. Then all kinds of fruit of life, as well as all kinds of colors and growths, arise in the seventh.

52. Now, according to whichever quality is strongest, the body of the fruit and the colors are formed: in this struggling or wrestling, the Godhead forms itself into infinite and unsearchable varieties of kinds, ways, and shapes.

53. For the seven spirits are seven main sources. When the Mercurius rises within them, it puts everything into motion; the bitter quality moves and distinguishes it, and the tart quality dries it.

> “Nature and the **Threefoldness** <note>original: *Dreyzahl*. Refers to the Holy Trinity.</note> are not one and the same; they are distinct, even though the Threefoldness dwells in Nature, yet ungrasped. It is nonetheless an eternal bond, as is clearly explained in our second and third books.”

Now note here how the formation occurs in Nature within the seventh spirit.

54. The sweet water is the beginning of Nature, and the tart quality draws it together so that it becomes natural and tangible, to speak in an earthly <note>original: *englisch*, likely meaning "angelic" or "heavenly" in this context, though often translated as "English" in modern German. 56. But when the bitter quality rises within it, it divides and forms itself as if it were alive, or as if life were rising there, and it forms itself into a greenish shape, like a green flash—to speak in human terms—from which one's sight fades and one cannot look upon it.

63. This, as related above, is now the beautiful and holy heaven, which exists thus in the entire Godhead, which has neither beginning nor end, and which no creature can reach with its senses.

64. Yet you should know this: that in one place, one quality shows itself more powerfully than the others; then another triumphs,

then the third, then the fourth, then the fifth, then the sixth, then the seventh. Consequently, the holy angels cannot rejoice enough, nor walk enough in love therein, nor sing the beautiful **We praise Thee, O God** <note>original: *TE DEUM LAUDAMUS*</note> enough, according to every quality of the great God, according to His wondrous revelation, wisdom, beauty, colors, fruit, and form. 65. And although I have written here how everything becomes, and how everything forms and shapes itself, and how the Godhead rises up, you must not think that there is perhaps a state of rest or an extinguishing, and then it rises up again like that.

66. Oh no; rather, I must write in "piece-work" <note>The original *Stückwerk* refers to the biblical idea of "knowing in part" (1 Corinthians 13:9).</note> for the sake of the reader’s lack of understanding, so that he might grasp something and come to his senses.

Then the spirit sees the divine and heavenly essence—not outside the body, but in the **wellspring** <term>wellspring: original *Quellbrunn*. For Böhme, this is the internal source or fountain where the divine qualities flow and interact.</term> of the heart, the flash <note>original: *Pliz* (Blitz). 69. For man is made from all the powers of God, from all the **seven spirits of God** <term>Seven Spirits: In Böhme's theology, these are the seven fundamental qualities (such as sweetness, bitterness, heat, etc.) that constitute both the nature of God and the created world.</term>, just as the angels are. However, because man is now corrupted, the divine birth does not always spring up within him, nor does it spring up in everyone. 70. But when the flash is caught in the wellspring of the heart, it rises through the seven source-spirits into the brain, like a **morning glow** <note>original: *Morgenröte*. 71. Within this, the spirit now sees into the depths of the Godhead. For in God, "near" and "far" are one and the same thing; and that same God, of whom I write in this book, is just as much in his **Trinity** <note>original: *Dreyheit*.</note> in the body <note>original: *Corpus*.</note> of holy souls as he is in heaven. From this I take my knowledge and from no other thing; I wish to know nothing else but that same God, and He also creates the certainty of my spirit, so that I constantly believe and trust in Him.

72. And even if an angel from heaven told it to me, I would still not be able to believe it, much less grasp it, for I would always doubt whether it were truly so. But when the sun itself rises in my spirit, then I am certain of it, and I see for myself the arrival and birth of the holy angels and of all things, both in heaven and in this world. For the holy soul is one spirit with God; although it is a creature, it is nonetheless equal to the angels. Also,

the human soul sees much deeper than the angels; the angels see only into the heavenly splendor, but the soul sees both the heavenly and the hellish, for it lives between both.

73. Therefore, the soul must endure being squeezed, and must wrestle every day and hour with the devil—that is, with the hellish quality. It lives in great danger in this world, which is why this life is rightly called a **vale of tears** <note>original: *Jammerthal*. A traditional term for the earthly world of suffering and trial.</note>, full of anxiety, constant choking, warring, fighting, and striving.

74. But the cold and half-dead body does not always understand this struggle of the soul; it does not know what is happening to it. Instead, it feels melancholy and anxious, moving from one room—indeed, from one place—to another, seeking rest or relief <note>original: *abstinenz*. It often feels as if it were entirely cast off by God, but it does not understand the struggle of the spirit—how the spirit lies now above and now below, and what a fierce warring and fighting there is between the hellish and heavenly qualities. I leave it to every holy soul to consider which fire the devils blow upon and which the holy angels extinguish.

75. You should know that I do not write here as if this were a history told to me by others; rather, I must constantly stand in that same battle, and I find it to be a great struggle, where I—like all people—often have a leg knocked out from under me.

76. But for the sake of this fierce struggle and fight, and for the sake of the zeal we have with one another, this revelation was given to me, as was the fierce drive to put all of this onto paper.

77. What might follow entirely here or hereafter, I do not fully know; I only know that certain future mysteries in the Deep are shown to me.

78. For when the flash rises in the **Center** <term>Center: original *Centro*. But it cannot easily grasp it, for it happens as if by heat-lightning: the flash of fire opens up and soon disappears again.

79. This is also how it happens in the soul: when it breaks through in its struggle, it beholds the Godhead like a flash, but the wellspring of sin soon covers it up again. For the **old Adam** <note>The "old Adam" refers to the fallen, earthly nature of humanity that remains bound to physical desires and sin.</note> belongs to the earth, and does not belong in the Godhead with this flesh.

## The 12th Chapter.
### Concerning the birth and arrival of the holy angels, as well as their government, order, and heavenly life of joy.

<insert>1. [The Word of the LORD <note>original: *Verbum DOMINI*</note> grasped the source-spirits <term>source-spirits: original *Quellgeister*. 1. Now the question arises: What, then, is an angel exactly? Behold, when God created the angels, He created them out of the seventh source-spirit, which is Nature or the Holy Heaven.

2. You must understand the word "Created" as if one were saying: to draw together or to drive together, just

<meta>catchword: like</meta>

like the earth is driven together; thus, when the whole of God moved, the harsh quality <note>original: *herbe qualität*. This is the first of the seven source-spirits, characterized by contraction, coldness, and drawing things into solid form.</note> contracted the Salitter <term>Salitter: A term Böhme adapted from "saltpeter." To him, it represents the divine "sap" or the crystalline mineral-substance of the heavenly world from which all forms are solidified.</term> of nature and dried it out, and thus the angels became. Just as the quality was in its movement in every place, so also the angel became.

->Mark the Depth.<-

3. There are seven spirits of God; they have all seven moved, and the light within them also moved, and the spirit that goes out from the seven spirits of God also moved.

4. Now the Creator, according to His Trinity, also wanted to create three hosts <note>original: *Heere*. This can mean armies, hosts, or great multitudes.</note> not far from one another, but one next to the other like a circle. Now note: as the spirits were in their surging or rising, so also the creatures became. In the center of each host, the "heart" of each host was corporized together; from that, an angelic King or Grand Prince came to be.

5. Just as the Son of God is born in the middle of the seven spirits of God, and is the life and heart of the seven spirits of God, so also an angelic king was created in the middle of his territory out of nature—or out of the natural heaven—from the power of all seven source-spirits. And he was now the heart in a host, and held the quality, mightiness, or strength of his whole host within himself, and was the most beautiful among them.

6. Just as the Son of God is the heart and the life, and the strength of all seven spirits of God, so also is a king of the angels in his host.

7. Now, just as in the divine power there are seven principal qualities from which the Heart of God is born, so also several mighty prince-angels were created according to each main quality in each host. I do not know their exact number, but they are leaders of the other angels alongside the King.

8. Here you should know that the angels are not all of one quality, nor are they all equal to one another in power and might. Every angel indeed has the power of all seven source-spirits within him, but in each one, some single quality is the strongest; according to that quality, he is also glorified. For as the Salitter was in each place at the time of creation, so also the angel became; and according to the quality that is strongest in the angel, he is named and glorified.

9. Just as each of the meadow flowers receives its color from its own quality <term>quality: Böhme uses the word *Qualität* to describe the fundamental forces or "source-spirits" of nature and divinity.</term>, and also has its name according to its quality, so it is with the holy angels: some are strongest in the harsh <note>original: *herben*. 10. Now, when the light of the Son of God shines upon them, they are like a brown flash, entirely bright in their quality. Others are of the water quality, and these are light, like the holy heaven; and when the light shines upon them, it looks like a crystal sea.

11. Some are strongest in the bitter quality; these are like a precious green stone that looks like a flash of lightning. When the light shines upon them, it appears like a reddish-green light, as if a carbuncle <note>A carbuncle is a deep-red gemstone, historically believed to glow with its own internal light.</note> were shining out of it, or as if life itself had its origin there.

12. Some are of the heat quality; these are the brightest of all, yellowish and reddish, and when the light shines upon them, it looks like the flash of the Son of God. Others are strongest in the love quality; they are a sight of the heavenly kingdom of joy, entirely light. When the light shines upon them, it looks like light blue—a lovely sight.

13. Some are strongest in the quality of sound <note>original: *Thon*. Böhme links sound/tone to the creative "Word" and the harmony of the spheres.</note>; these are also light, and when the light shines upon them, it looks like a rising flash, as if something were about to raise itself there.

14. Others are of the whole of nature, like a general mixture; when the light shines upon them, it looks like the holy heaven, which is formed out of all the spirits of God.

15. But the King is the heart of all qualities, and has his territory in the center like a fountain, just as the sun stands in the middle of the planets and is a king of the stars and a heart of nature in this world: just so great is a Cherub <note>original: *Jerubin*.</note> or Angel-King.

16. And just as the other six planets are commanders alongside the sun and give their will to the sun so that it may rule and work within them, so all angels give their will to the King, and the Prince-angels are in council with the King.

17. But you should know here that they all have a will of love among one another; no one envies another for his form or beauty, for as it goes among the spirits of God,

<column-break/>

Chapter 12. Morning Glow at Sunrise. 117

so it also goes among them. Also, they all possess divine joys at once, and all enjoy heavenly food together; in this, there is no difference. Only in the colors and the strength of power is there a difference, but in perfection there is nothing lacking, for each has the power of all the spirits of God within them. Therefore, when the light of the Son of God shines upon them, the quality of each angel manifests itself through colors.

18. I have told of only a few forms and colors, but there are many more which I will not write for the sake of brevity. Just as the Godhead manifests itself in infinity with its rising, so there are also unfathomably many kinds of colors and forms among the angels. I can show you no right likeness in this world other than the blooming earth in May, which is but a dead and earthly preview.

### Of Angelic Joy.

->Now the question is:<-

What then do the angels of God do in heaven, or why, or for what purpose did God create them?

19. You misers might take note of this—you who strive in this world after pride, honor, fame, power, money, and goods, and squeeze the sweat and blood out of the poor, and squander their labor, and imagine you are better than the simple layman: for what did God create you?

->Question.<-

Why did God create Prince-angels, and not make everyone equal?

20. See, God is a God of order; as it goes, flows, and is in His government within Himself—that is, in His birth and in His rising—so also is the order of angels.

21. Just as in Him there are primarily seven qualities by which the whole divine being is driven, manifesting itself in these seven qualities unto infinity (and yet the seven qualities are the *First* <note>original: *Primus*.</note> in infinity, through which the divine birth exists eternally and unchangeably in its order): And just—

...just as the heart of life is born in the midst of the seven spirits of God, from which divine joy arises, so also is the order of the angels.

22. The prince-angels are created according to the spirits of God, and the Cherubim <note>original: *Jerubin*. Böhme’s idiosyncratic spelling of Cherubim.</note> according to the heart of God: just as the divine being works, so also do the angels. Whatever quality arises in the being of God and shows itself particularly in its working—such as in the rising of the throne or the divine working, wrestling, or struggling—that same angelic prince who is most strongly devoted to that quality begins his round-dance <note>original: *Reygen*. A traditional communal circle dance, used here to describe the rhythmic, harmonious movement of the divine forces.</note> with his legions, with singing, sounding, dancing, rejoicing, and triumphing.

23. This is a heavenly music, for everyone sings according to the voice of their own quality, and the prince leads the dance, just like a cantor <note>A cantor is a lead singer or choir director in a church.</note> with his students; and the King rejoices and triumphs with his angels, to the honor of the great God and for the increase of heavenly joys. This is in the heart of God like a holy play, and for this they were created: for the joy and honor of God.

24. Now, when the heavenly music of the angels arises, then in the heavenly splendor—in the divine <term>Salitter: A term Böhme uses to describe the living, spiritual "earth" or substance of heaven from which all divine forms grow.</term>—all kinds of growth, all kinds of figures, and all kinds of colors arise; for the Godhead shows itself in infinite and unsearchable ways, colors, forms, and joys.

25. Now, whichever source-spirit <note>original: *Quellgeist*. These are the seven fundamental forces in Böhme's cosmology that "well up" to form all reality.</note> in the Godhead shows itself particularly at that time with its rising and loving-wrestling—as if it had become the foremost—that same prince-angel immediately begins his heavenly music with his devoted angels according to his quality, with singing, sounding, piping, and all kinds of heavenly art that arises in the spirits of God.

26. But when the Center arises in the midst—that is, when the birth of the Son of God shows itself particularly as a triumph—then the music or joys of all three royal kingdoms of the entire creation of all angels arise.

27. What kind of joy may be there, I leave for every soul to ponder; I cannot grasp it in my corrupted nature, much less write of it. With this song, I summon <note>original: *citire*. A legal or formal term for calling someone to appear; here, Böhme invites the reader to experience the truth in the afterlife.</note> the reader into that life; there he himself will be in the midst of the round-dance, and only then will he give belief to this spirit. What he does not understand here, he shall have there in direct sight.

28. You should know, this is not sucked out of any stone, but
<meta>catchword: but</meta>

# Chapter 12. Morning Glow at Sunrise. #

but when the flash arises in the Center, the spirit sees and recognizes it. Therefore, take heed and do not play too mockingly in this place, or you will be found a scorner before God, and it may well go for you as it did for King Lucifer.

->Now the question arises:<-
->**What do the angels do when they are not singing?**<-

29. Behold, what the Godhead does, they do also. When the spirits of God lovely bear one another within themselves and rise up into one another—like a lovely embracing <note>original: *halsen*. Literally "necking," but used by Böhme to describe the most intimate spiritual union.</note>, kissing, and eating of one another, in which taste and smell the life arises and the eternal refreshment (of which you can read at length earlier)—so also do the angels walk with one another in a friendly, gracious, and lovely way in the heavenly territory. They behold the wonderful and lovely form of heaven and eat from the gracious fruits of life.

->Now you ask:<-
->**What do they talk about with one another?**<-

30. Behold, you magnificent, proud, and haughty human! The world is becoming too small for you here, and you think no one is your equal; here, consider whether you have an angelic nature in you, or a devilish one?

->To whom shall I now compare the angels?<-

31. I will rightly compare them to little children who, in the month of May <note>original: *Mayen*. For Böhme, May is a symbol of the eternal spring of Paradise.</note> when the beautiful little roses bloom, go among the beautiful flowers together and pluck them, making fine little wreaths from them, carrying them in their hands, rejoicing, and talking constantly of the many forms of the beautiful flowers. They take each other by the hand when they go among the beautiful flowers, and when they come home, they show them to their parents and rejoice, and then the parents likewise have a joy in the children and rejoice with them.

32. This is also what the holy angels do in heaven: they take each other by the hand and walk in the beautiful Heavenly May, and talk of the lovely and beautiful growths in the heavenly splendor, and eat of the gracious fruits of God, and use the beautiful little flowers of heaven...

# Morning Glow at Sunrise. Chapter 12. #

...little flowers for their play, and make beautiful little wreaths for them, and rejoice in the beautiful May-time <note>Böhme uses "May-time" (Mayen) to symbolize the eternal springtime of heaven, where everything is in constant bloom and renewal.</note> of God.

33. There is nothing there but a heartfelt love, a gentle affection, a friendly conversation, a gracious dwelling together, where one always sees their joy in the other and honors the other. They know of no malice, or cunning, or deceit; instead, the divine fruits and loveliness are held in common by all. One may use them just as much as another; there is no resentment, no envy, no ill-will, but rather their hearts are bound together in love.

34. In this the Godhead has its highest pleasure, just as parents have in their children when their dear children in heaven behave so kindly toward one another; for the Godhead within itself also plays in this way, one source-spirit <note>original: *Quellgeist*. Böhme’s term for the seven fundamental forces or "qualities" that flow through and constitute God’s being.</note> within the other.

35. Therefore the angels can do nothing else but exactly what their Father does, just as our angelic King Jesus Christ testified when he was with us on earth, as it stands in the Gospel, where he spoke: *Truly, truly, the Son can do nothing of himself, but what he sees the Father do, that the Son also does in like manner*, John 5:19. Also: *Unless you turn back and become like children, you cannot enter the kingdom of heaven*, Matthew 18:3.

36. By this he means that our hearts should be bound in love, like the holy angels of God, and that we should act kindly and lovely toward one another, and love one another, and outdo one another in showing honor, like the angels of God.

37. Not that we should deceive or lie to one another, or snatch the morsel from someone else's mouth out of great greed; nor that one should strut, parade, and look down upon the other who cannot use his wicked devilish cunning.

38. Oh no, the angels in heaven do not do so; rather they love one another. No one thinks himself more beautiful than the other, but each has his joy in the other, and rejoices in the other’s beautiful form and loveliness, from which their love for one another rises up, so that they lead each other by the hands and kiss one another kindly.

<column-break/>

### Observe the Depth. ###

39. Just as when the flash of life <note>original: *Blitz des Lebens*. In Böhme's system, this is the sudden ignition of divine light and consciousness within the spiritual substance.</note> rises up in the midst of the divine power, where all the spirits of God receive their life and rejoice greatly, there is a lovely and holy embracing, kissing, tasting, feeling, hearing, seeing, and smelling. So it is also with the angels: when one sees, hears, and feels another, the flash of life rises in his heart, and one spirit embraces the other, as it is within the Godhead.

->Here note the ground and highest mystery of the angels of God.<-

40. If you now wish to know where their love, humility, and friendliness come from—which rises up in their hearts—then observe what follows.

41. Every angel is fashioned like the entire Godhead, and is like a little God; for when God created the angels, he created them out of himself. Now, God is in one place just as in another; everywhere there is the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit.

42. In these three names and powers stand heaven and this world, and everything your heart can think of; and even if you were to draw a tiny circle that you could barely see into, or that you could hardly distinguish, the entire divine power is still within it. The Son of God is born within it, and the Holy Spirit goes forth within it from the Father and the Son. If it is not in love, then it is in wrath, as it is written: *With the holy you are holy, and with the perverse you are perverse* <note>original: *bey den Heiligen bist du heilig, und bey den Verkehrten bist du verkehrt*. A translation of Psalm 18:26.</note>. These latter awaken the wrath of God over themselves, which also stands in all the spirits of God in the place where it is awakened; conversely, where the love of God is awakened, it also stands in the full birth of the entire Godhead of that place.

43. And in this there is no difference; the angels are created one like the other, all out of the divine <term>Salitter: Böhme's term for the fundamental, living spiritual "earth" or matter of the heavenly realm.</term> of heavenly nature. This alone is the difference between them: that when God created them, each individual quality was at its peak of movement, in its highest birth or rising. From this it has come to pass that the angels are of many different qualities.

...they are, and have various colors and beauty, and yet everything is from God.

Now every angel has all the <term>qualities</term><note>Böhme refers to the "seven qualities" or "source-spirits" (Quellgeister) which he believes constitute the nature of God and all reality.</note> of God within them, but one is the strongest in them; according to that one, the angel is named, and in that one, they are glorified.

45. Now, just as the qualities in God always beget one another, rising up and loving one another from the heart, and as one always receives its life from the other—and as the lightning rises up in the heat within the <term>sweet water</term><note>A Böhmean term for the gentle, nourishing aspect of the divine substance, contrasted with "bitter" or "sour" qualities.</note>, from which life and joy have their origin—so it is also within an angel. Their inner birth is nothing other than the outer birth outside of them in God.

46. Just as the Son of God is born outside the angels in the middle <term>well-spring</term> in the heat within the sweet water from all seven spirits of God, and in turn illuminates all seven spirits of God, from which they have their life and joy; so too, in like manner, the Son of God is born within an angel in the middle well-spring of their heart in the heat within the sweet water, and in turn illuminates all seven source-spirits of the angel.

47. And just as the Holy Spirit proceeds from the Father and the Son, and forms and shapes and loves everything; so too the Holy Spirit in the angel goes out to their fellow brothers, and loves them, and rejoices with them.

48. For there is no difference between the spirits of God and the angels, except for this: that the angels are <term>creatures</term><note>By "creatures," Böhme means created beings with a finite beginning, as opposed to the uncreated, eternal Godhead.</note>, and their bodily essence has a beginning. However, their power, from which they are created, is God Himself, and is from eternity and remains in eternity. Therefore, their agility is as swift as human thoughts; wherever they wish to be, they are there instantly. Furthermore, they can be large or small, however they wish.

49. And that is the true essence of God in heaven, indeed heaven itself; if your eyes were opened, you would see it clearly right here on earth at the place where you are. For if God can let a human spirit see—which is nevertheless stuck in the body—and can reveal Himself to it in the flesh, then He can surely also do that outside the flesh, if He wills.

50. O you house of sin of this world, how you are surrounded by hell and death! Wake up, the hour of your

rebirth is at hand; the day is breaking, the <term>morning glow</term><note>The "Morning Glow" (Morgenröte/Aurora) is Böhme's central metaphor for the dawning of divine wisdom and the end of spiritual darkness.</note> is showing itself. ### Concerning the total heavenly joy of all three kingdoms of the angels.

51. Here the Spirit shows that wherever an individual angel is created, that same place or <note>original: "Locus"</note> location in heavenly nature—within which and out of which they became a creature—is their own seat, which they possess by <term>natural right</term>, as long as they remain in God’s love. For it is the place they have had from eternity, before they became a creature; thus the same <term>Salitter</term><note>Böhme’s unique term for the "divine earth" or the crystalline substance of the heavenly realm.</note> stood in the place from which they came to be. Therefore, that same seat remains theirs by natural right as long as they move within God's love.

52. But you should not think that God is thereby bound, such that He may not drive them out if they move otherwise than God first created them. For as long as they remain in obedience and in love, the place is theirs by natural right; but when they exalt themselves and ignite the place in the <term>wrath-fire</term><note>The "wrath-fire" represents the dark, consuming aspect of God's power that manifests when the harmony of love is broken.</note>, they set their Father's house on fire and become a source of opposition against the location from which they were made, making two things out of what was one before their exaltation.

53. When this happens, they keep their bodily natural right for themselves, and the location keeps its own for itself as well. But if the creature (which has a beginning) wants to set itself against the first thing (which was before the creature and has no beginning), and wants to destroy the location which they did not make—in which they were created as a creature in love—and wants to turn that same love into wrath-fire, then love rightly spews out the wrath-fire along with the creature.

54. From this, the laws in this world also arise; for when a son sets himself against the father and strikes the father, he has forfeited his paternal inheritance, and the father may thrust him out of the house. But as long as he is in the father's obedience, the father has no power to disinherit him.

55. This worldly law takes its origin from the

57. For just as the spirits of God always rise up into one another and have a love-play in their birth—yet each spirit retains its natural seat or its *locum* <note>original: "Locum," place.</note> in the birth of God, and it never happens that the heat transforms into cold, or the cold into heat, but rather each retains its natural place and rises up in the other, from which life has its origin.

58. 63. 71. Oh, what a beautiful mirror you are for the holy angels; just smell your sweet love and humility—does it not smell of hell? This party is all invited as guests in the coming chapter.

<column-break/>

### Concerning the royal Primacy <note>original: "Primat," referring to the supreme authority or rank.</note> or power of the three angelic Kings.

72. Just as the Godhead in its essence is threefold <note>original: "dreyfältig," referring to the Trinity.</note>, in which the outflow from the seven spirits of God shows and births itself threefold—as Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, one God, in which the entire divine power consists, along with everything that exists—and yet the three persons in the Godhead are not a separable essence but are within one another: so also in the same manner, when God moved and created the angels, three special angels were formed from the best core of nature, from the essence of the Trinity within the nature of God, and in such authority and power as the Trinity has within the seven spirits of God.
73. For the Trinity of God rises up within the seven spirits of God <note>The "seven spirits of God" or "source-spirits" (Quellgeister) are Böhme's fundamental forces of nature, such as contraction, expansion, and light.</note>, and is in turn the life and heart of all seven spirits. Likewise, the three angelic kings have each risen up in the nature of their host or place, and each is a natural lord of his place over the government of the angels. But the Trinity of the Godhead, which is unchangeable, retains the *locum* <note>original: "Locum," Latin for "place" or "station."</note> for itself, while the king retains the government of the angels.
74. Now, just as the Trinity of the Godhead is a single essence in all ends of the entire Father, and is bound together like the members in a man's body—and all places are like one place, even if one place has a different office than another, just as a man's limbs do, yet it is One Body of God—so also the three angelic kingdoms are bound together, and not each separately divided. No angelic king may say: "This is my kingdom; no other king may enter here."
75. Although it is his original natural hereditary kingdom, and remains his, yet all other kings and angels are his true natural brothers, born of one Father, and they all inherit their Father's kingdom together.
76. Just as each of the source-spirits of God has its natural seat of birth and retains its natural place <note>original: "Natur-Locum."</note> for itself, and yet with the other spirits is the one God—for if the others were not there, it would not be either; also, one rises up in the other—so it is also constituted with the primacy of the holy angels, and it has no other form than that which is in God.

77. Therefore they all live friendly and peacefully with one another in their Father’s kingdom, like dear little brothers; there is no boundary as to how far one may go or not.

->Now a simple person might ask:<-

->By what means do the angels travel, or upon what do they steady their feet?<-

78. I want to inform you here of the true ground, and there is no other in heaven than what you find here in the literal word <note>original: "im Buchstaben," referring to the plain, written explanation</note>, for the spirit looks into this depth without wavering, and it is also quite graspable.

79. The entire nature of heaven stands in the power of the 7 <term>source-spirits</term> <note>original: "Quellgeister," the seven fundamental qualities or forces that Böhme believes flow from God to create all reality</note>, and in the seventh consists the nature or tangibility of all qualities: this is now entirely light, and thick like a fog, yet completely transparent like a crystalline sea, so that one can see through everything; indeed, the entire depth above and below is like this.

80. Now the angels also have such bodies, but solidified more dryly together <note>original: "trockener zusammen corporiret," suggesting a more defined, though still spiritual, form</note>, and their body is also the core of nature, the best or most beautiful brilliance from nature.

81. Now, they steady their feet upon the 7th spirit of God, which is as thick as a fog and bright as a crystalline sea; within it they ascend and descend, wherever they wish. For their agility is as fast as the divine power itself, yet one is swifter than another, each according to their particular quality.

82. In this same seventh spirit of nature, heavenly fruit or colors also arise, as does everything that is tangible; and it is just like a form as if the angels were to dwell in the depths between heaven and earth, where they climbed up and down, and wherever they were, their foot rested as if it stood upon the earth.

83. The ancients have depicted the angels to men with wings, but they need none; instead, they have hands and feet like humans, but in a heavenly manner.

84. On the day of the resurrection of the dead, there will be no difference between the angels and humans; they will have one

### Concerning the King or Grand Prince Michael.

86. Michael means "God’s Strength" or power, and he bears the name in deed; for he is solidified from the 7 <term>source-spirits</term> as a core from them, and stands there now as if in the place of God the Father.

87. 88. 89. Afterwards, he created Prince-Angels according to the 7 <term>source-spirits</term>, according to their quality, such as Gabriel, an angel or prince of the throne or of swift messages, as well as Raphael and others more in the kingdom of Michael.

91. Although they cannot change themselves corporally like God Himself, who created them, they nevertheless rule corporally and are obligated and bound to them, just as body and soul are bound to one another.

92. For the King is their head, and they are the King’s members; and the <term>source-princes</term> <note>original: "Quellfürsten," high-ranking angels who govern the fundamental forces or "sources" of celestial nature</note> are the King’s advisors or officers, just like the five senses in a human being, or like the hands and feet, or the mouth, nose, eyes, and ears, with which the King carries out his business.

93. Now, just as all angels are bound to the King, so also is the King bound to God his Creator, like body and soul. The body signifies God, and the soul signifies the angelic King who is within the body of God. He became a <term>creature</term> <note>In Böhme's vocabulary, a "creature" is any created being, emphasizing that even the highest angels are not self-existent like God</note> within the body of God and remains eternally in the body of God, like a soul in its nest; therefore God has also glorified him as highly as His own property, or as the soul is glorified within the body.

94. Thus the King or Grand Prince Michael looks like God the Father in his glorification or clarity, and is a king and prince of God upon the mountain of God, and holds his office in the depth within which he was created.

95. That same circle or space in which he and his angels were created is his kingdom, and he is a dear son of God the Father in nature—a natural son in whom the Father takes His joy.

96. You must not compare him to the Heart or Light of God, which is present in the whole Father and has neither beginning nor end, just like God the Father Himself.

97. For this prince is a creature and has a beginning; but he is within God the Father and is bound with Him in His love as His dear son, whom He created out of Himself.

98. Therefore He has set upon him the crown of honor, of might, and of power, so that in heaven there is nothing higher nor more beautiful, nor anything mightier, than God Himself in His Trin-

### Concerning the other King, now called Lucifer, on account of his fall.

99. Now, King Lucifer, close your eyes a little and stop up your ears a little, so that you hear and see nothing; otherwise you will be cruelly ashamed that another sits upon your throne, and that your shame shall be made so completely manifest before the end of the world—which you have nevertheless kept hidden and suppressed from the world wherever you could. Now I will describe your royal primacy, not to please you, but to please mankind.

100. This highly powerful, magnificent, and beautiful king lost his true name in his fall; for he is now called **Lucifer**, which means "one cast out from the light of God." His name was not so in the beginning, for he was a natural prince or king of the **Heart of God** <note>Böhme refers to the "Heart of God" as the second person of the Trinity, the source of light and love</note> in the bright light, the most beautiful among the three Kings of the angels.

### Concerning his creation.

101. Just as Michael was created according to the quality, kind, and property of God the Father, so also was Lucifer created according to the quality, kind, and beauty of God the Son, and was bound in love with Him as a dear son or heart. His heart also stood in the center of the light, as if he were God Himself, and his beauty was above all things. For his enclosure or chief mother <note>his primary source of being</note> was the Son of God; there he stood as a king or prince of God.

102. His district, place, and space, along with his entire host, in which he became a creature and which was his kingdom, is the created heaven and this world in which we dwell with our King, Jesus Christ.

103. For our King sits in divine omnipotence, just as King Lucifer once sat, upon the royal throne of the cast-out Lucifer; and the kingdom of King Lucifer has now become His. Prince Lucifer, how does that taste to you?

## Concerning the third angelic King, named Uriel.

108. This gracious prince and king has his name from the light, or from the flash or outflow of light, which signifies God the **Holy Spirit**.

109. Just as the Holy Spirit goes forth from the light, and forms and shapes everything, and rules in everything: so also is the power and grace of a <term>Cherubim</term> <note>original: "Jerubin"</note>, who is the king and the heart of all his angels; that is, whenever his angels merely look upon him, they are <term>influenced</term> <note>original: "inficiret," literally "infected," but used by Böhme to describe a positive spiritual permeation or resonance</note> by the will of their king.

110. Just as the will of the heart influences all members of the body, so that the entire body does as the heart has determined, or as the Holy Spirit rises in the <term>center</term> <note>original: "Centro"</note> of the heart and illuminates all members in the whole body: So also the Cherubim influences all his angels with his entire brilliance and will, so that they are all together like one body, and the king is the heart within it.

111. Now this magnificent and beautiful prince is formed according to the manner and quality of the Holy Spirit, and is indeed a magnificent

magnificent and beautiful prince of God, and is bound in love with the other princes as one heart.

113. 115. In such color and manner does the nature-heaven of God show itself in the rising of the spirits of God: when the light of the Son of God shines therein, it is like a bright sea of the colors of the stones mentioned above.

119. The Spirit bears witness that it will be but a short time before the **flash** <note>original: "Blitz." 122. This is why Christ also ordained baptism, or the rebirth of the Holy Spirit in water, because the birth of light rises in the sweet water of the heart. This is a very great mystery and has remained hidden from all people since the beginning of the world until today; I intend to describe and prove this clearly in its proper place.

### Now observe the form of heaven.

123. When you look at this world, you have a prototype of heaven: the stars signify the angels; for just as the stars must remain unchanged until the end of this time, so the angels must remain eternally unchanging in the eternal time of heaven.

124. The elements signify the wondrous <term>proportion</term> <note>original: "Proporz," referring to the balanced relationship between different forces.</note> and change of the heavenly form; for just as the deep between the stars and the earth always changes in its form—now it is beautiful and bright, now cloudy, now wind, now rain, now snow; now the deep is blue, now greenish, now whitish, now dark.

125. So also is the change of heaven in many kinds of colors and forms, but not in the same way as in this world; rather, everything follows the rising of the Spirits of God. The light of the Son of God shines eternally within it, yet there is at times a greater rising in the birth than at others; therefore, the wondrous wisdom of God is incomprehensible.

126. The earth signifies the heavenly nature or the **7th Nature-Spirit** <note>In Böhme’s system, there are seven properties or "qualities" of nature; the seventh is the "Essentiality" or the body in which the other six act.</note>, in which the formations, shapes, and colors rise: the birds, fish, and animals signify the many kinds of shapes of the figures in heaven.

127. You should know that the Spirit in the flash bears witness that all kinds of figures indeed rise in heaven—resembling the animals, birds, and fish of this world, but in a heavenly form, clarity, and manner—as well as all kinds of trees, shrubs, and flowers. But just as they rise, so they pass away again; for they are not incorporated into a permanent body like the angels, but rather figure themselves thus in the birth of the rising quality within the Nature-Spirit.

128. When a figure is formed in one Spirit so that it exists, and another Spirit wrestles with it and overcomes it, the figure is then broken apart or changed, all according to the nature of the qualities; and this in God is like a **holy play**. <note>original: "heiliges Spiel." This refers to the concept of *divine play*, where the universe is seen as the spontaneous, joyful expression of God’s creativity.</note>

129. Therefore, the creatures—such as animals, birds, fish, and worms in this world—were not created for an eternal essence, but for a transitory one, just as the figures of heaven also pass away. I place this here only as an introduction; you will find it described in detail during the account of the creation of this world.

# The 13th Chapter.
## Concerning the Terrible, Lamentable, and Miserable Fall of the Kingdom of Lucifer.

1. Before this mirror I wish to summon all proud, greedy, envious, and angry people; there they shall see the origin of their pride, greed, envy, and wrath, and also the outcome and final reward.

2. The scholars have brought forth many and various monsters <note>original: "monstra." Böhme uses this term to describe grotesque or distorted theological theories.</note> concerning the beginning of sin and the origin of the devil, and have scratched themselves over it; each one thought he had the matter by the handle, and yet it has remained entirely hidden from them until this day.

3. But because it now wishes to reveal itself completely, as if in a bright mirror, it is well to be presumed that the great day of God's revelation is now at hand, when the fierceness <note>original: "Grimmigkeit." In Böhme's thought, this refers to the harsh, "dark" side of the divine qualities when separated from God's light.</note> and the ignited fire will separate from the light.

4. Therefore, let no one make themselves stone-blind, for the time of the restoration of what man has lost is now at hand; the morning glow breaks forth; it is time to wake up from sleep.

->Now the question is:<-
->What then is the source of the first sins of the kingdom of Lucifer?<-

5. Here one must again take up the highest depth of the Godhead and observe from what King Lucifer was made into a creature, or what the first source of malice in him might have been.

6. The devil and his bands, as well as all godless people who are conceived in corruption, still constantly excuse themselves, saying that God does them wrong by casting them out.

7. The present world also dares to say that God, in His intentional counsel, has so decreed it: that some people shall be saved and some damned, and for that purpose God cast out Prince Lucifer, so that he should be a spectacle of God's wrath.

<meta>catchword: 8. As</meta>

<column-break/>

<page-num>137</page-num>

8. As if hell or evil had existed from eternity, and God had intended in His purpose that creatures should and must be in it; and they scratch and stretch the Scriptures to prove such a thing, though they have neither knowledge of the true God nor understanding of the Scripture—even though some erroneous things have been used in the Scripture. <note>Böhme often critiqued literalist or "dead" interpretations of the Bible that ignored the "living" spirit of the text.</note>

9. Christ says that the devil was a murderer and a liar from the beginning, and never stood in the truth (John 8:44). But because these same "judges" and "disputers" stand by him so faithfully and turn God’s truth into lies—in that they make God out to be a thirsty and fierce devil who created evil and still wants it—they are, together with the devil, murderers and liars.

10. For just as the devil is a founder and father of hell and damnation, and built and prepared the hellish quality for himself as his royal seat: so also are such writers <note>original: "Scribenten." This is Böhme’s common derogatory term for academic or "book-learned" theologians.</note> the master-builders of lies and damnation, who help the devil confirm his lies and make the merciful, lovely, friendly God into a murderer and a zealous destroyer, turning God’s truth into lies.

11. For in the prophet, God speaks: *As truly as I live, I have no pleasure in the death of the sinner, but rather that he turn and live.* (Ezekiel 33:11). And in the Psalms it stands: *You are not a God who wants evil.* (Psalm 5:5).

12. To that end, God gave laws to humanity and forbade evil and commanded good. If God then wanted evil as well as good, He would have to be at odds with Himself, and it would follow that there is a destruction within the Godhead—that one thing runs against another and one thing destroys the other.

13. Now, how all this is constituted, or how malice took its first source, origin, and beginning, I will explain in the highest simplicity in the great depth.

14. Therefore, the Spirit invites and cites all straying people and those misled by the devil to the school before this mirror; there they shall look into the heart of the murderous devil. Whoever

if one does not wish to guard themselves against his lies, though they well could, then there is no counsel for them here or there; whoever wishes to sow with him will also reap with him. In the center of the flash <note>original: "Blitz." 16. Let everyone now see to it that they trade so that they may earn profit for their Lord, for I fear that not every merchant will know how to deal with my wares, since they will be quite unknown to many; likewise, not everyone will understand my language.

17. Therefore, I want everyone to be warned to act cautiously, and not to imagine themselves rich or think they cannot become poor; truly, I have wonderful wares for sale; not everyone will understand them.

18. If someone were to plunge in according to their own headstrong way and fall into ruin, they may blame themselves; they surely need a light in their heart so that their understanding and mind might be governed.

19. Otherwise, let them simply not come into my trading house, or they will deceive themselves; for the wares I have for sale are quite noble and precious, and require a very sharp understanding; therefore, look out for yourself, and do not climb into the heights where you see no ladder, or you will fall.

20. But to me, Jacob's ladder has been shown, upon which I have climbed even into heaven, and have received my wares which I have for sale; if someone now wishes to climb after me, let them also see to it that they are not drunk, but they must be girded with the sword of the Spirit.

21. For they must climb through a terrible depth; dizziness will often come into their head; moreover, they must climb right through the kingdom of hell; what they will have to suffer there in the way of mockery and scorn, they will certainly experience.

22. In this struggle, I have also often had to experience it with a heavy heart; the sun has often been extinguished for me, but
