23. I do not write this to praise myself, but in case it should happen to you likewise, so that you do not entirely despair; for a very rigorous labor belongs to this, for whoever wants to fight with the devil between heaven and hell, for he is a powerful prince.

24. Therefore, see to it that you have on the armor of the Spirit; otherwise, simply do not come into my trading house, or you will trade poorly with these wares. You must renounce the devil and the world if you wish to fight; otherwise, you will not conquer; and if you do not conquer, then leave my book in peace and stay with the old way, or you will receive a bad reward. Do not be mistaken, God will not be mocked. (Galatians 6:7.)

25. It is truly a narrow path that wishes to press through the gates of hell to God; one must suffer many a squeeze and pinch from the devil. For human flesh is quite young and tender, and the devil is rough and hard, as well as dark, hot, bitter, harsh, and cold; the two fit together poorly.

26. Therefore, I wish to have faithfully warned the reader, as if with a preface to this great mystery: if they do not understand this thing, and yet would gladly understand it, let them pray to God for His Holy Spirit, that He might enlighten them with the same.

27. Without the enlightenment of the same, you will not understand this mystery; for there is a strong castle in the spirit of man guarding it, which must first be unlocked: and no human can do that, for the Holy Spirit alone is the key-bearer for it.

28. Therefore, if you wish to have an open gate into the Godhead, you must walk in God's love; I have set this here for your information.

33. In the middle fountain-spring, which is the Heart, the birth arises: the harsh quality rubs against the bitter and the heat; there the light is ignited, which is the Son, with whom he is always pregnant in his body, and who illuminates him and makes him living.

38. For the seven spirits possessed this in perfect knowledge, because they <term>in-qualified</term> <note>original: "inqualiret" – a term Böhme coined to describe how different spirits or qualities intermingle and operate as one unit</note> with God the Father, so that they could see, feel, taste, smell, and hear everything that God their Father did.

46. But when they rose up in a sharp ignition, they acted against the law of nature differently than God their Father acted, and that was a source of opposition against the entire Godhead. For they ignited the <term>Salitter</term> <note>A Böhmean term for the divine "saltpeter" or the fundamental substance of the heavenly realm</note> of the body <note>original: "Corpus"</note>, and birthed a highly triumphant son, who in the "harsh" quality was hard, rough, dark, and cold; and in the "sweet" quality was burning, bitter, and fiery. The tone was a harsh sound of fire; the love was a proud enmity against God.

47. There now stood the ignited bride within the seventh spirit of nature, like a proud beast <note>original: "Bestia"</note>, and now presumed she was above God, and that nothing was her equal. Love had grown cold; the heart of God could not touch her, for there was a repulsion between them. While the heart of God surged forth gentle and lovely, the heart of the angel surged entirely dark, hard, cold, and fiery.

48. Now, the heart of God was meant to work together in the same qualities as the heart of the angel, but that could not be; for it was hard against soft, and sour against sweet, and dark against light, and fire against a lovely warmth, and a harsh pounding against a lovely song.

Hear, Lucifer! Who is now to blame that you have become a devil? Is it God, as you lie?

49. No, you yourself! The <term>source-spirits</term> <note>original: "quellgeister" – the seven primary qualities that Böhme believes constitute both God and the soul</note> in your body, which you yourself are—they have birthed such a little son for you. You cannot say that God ignited the divine substance <note>original: "Salitter"</note> from which He made you; rather, your source-spirits did it, after you were already a prince and king of God.

50. Therefore, when you say God created you thus, or cast you out of your place <note>original: "loco"</note> without sufficient cause, you are a liar and a murderer; for the entire heavenly host bears witness against you that you prepared this grim quality for yourself.

51. If it is not true, then come before God’s face and defend yourself—but you see it well enough anyway, and you do not dare to look upon it. ## Now observe.

55. The entire Godhead has, in its innermost or primordial birth, a very sharp, terrifying sharpness in its core; in this, the <term>astringent quality</term> <note>original: "herbe qualität" – the force of contraction, coldness, and solidification in Böhme’s system</note> is a very terrifying, harsh, hard, dark, and cold contraction, just like winter when it is fiercely cold, such that water turns to ice, and is furthermore quite unbearable.
56. Think: if in winter, when it is so cold, the sun were to be taken away, what a cold and completely rough and hard darkness there would be; no life could exist there.
57. In such a way is the astringent quality within its own innermost core, and for itself alone outside the other qualities in God; for this strictness creates the contraction and the holding of a <term>body</term> <note>original: "Corpus"</note>, and the hardness dries it so that it may exist as a creature.
58. And the <term>bitter quality</term> <note>original: "bittere qualität" – the force of movement and friction</note> is a tearing, penetrating, and cutting bitter source; for it divides and drives apart the hard and astringent quality, and creates mobility. And between these two qualities, heat is born from their hard and fierce bitter rubbing, tearing, and raging; this heat rises up in the bitter and hard quality as a fierce ignition, and passes through as a hard <term>fire-resonance</term> <note>original: "Feuerklang"</note>. From this the hard <term>tone</term> <note>original: "Thon" – Böhme uses this to mean both "sound/resonance" and "clay/substance"</note> arises, and in such a rising or such an ascent, it is enclosed and fastened within the astringent quality, so that it is a body that endures.
59. Now, if in this body there were no further quality that could quench the fieriness of these four qualities, then there would be a constant enmity within it; for the bitter would be against the astringent, in that it storms and tears within it and would burst the astringent apart.
60. Likewise, the astringent would be against the bitter, in that it so contracts and holds the bitter captive that it could not have its own path.
61. And the heat would be against them both, in that with its fierce ignition and rising it makes everything hot and raging, and is entirely against the cold.

<meta>catchword: 62. So</meta>

<column-break/>

62. Thus the tone would be a great enmity within all the others, in that it drives through everything with violence, like a raging thing.
63. Now, this is the very deepest and innermost, hidden birth of God, according to which He calls Himself an angry, jealous God, as is to be seen in the Ten Commandments at Mount Sinai. (Exodus 20:5; Deuteronomy 5:9.) And in such a quality stands hell and eternal perdition, furthermore eternal enmity and a pit of murder; and such a creature the devil has become.
64. But because he is now a sworn enemy of God, and yet the disputers and the devil’s helpers want to force the idea that God willed the evil as well as the good, and that God created some people for damnation—therefore the Spirit of God summons them from eternal enmity before this mirror; there their hearts shall be unlocked, and they shall see what God is, or who the devil is, or how he became a devil.
65. If your heart is not locked in death through your own wantonness and blasphemy and drowned in abominable sins, with no will to turn from them, then wake up and see:
66. I take heaven and earth, furthermore the stars and elements, and all creatures and man himself in his entire substance as a witness, and I will also prove it brightly and clearly in its proper place with all these recounted things, especially in the creation of all creatures.
67. If these things do not suffice for you, then pray to God that He might open your heart; then you will recognize and see heaven and hell, furthermore the entire Godhead in all its quality; then you will surely stop speaking in defense of the devil. I cannot unlock your heart for you.

## Now observe the true birth of God.

68. See, as I have recounted above, the birth of God in His innermost being is thus sharp in these four qualities.

71. And the seven wheels always gave birth to the <term>hub</term> <note>original: "Nabe"</note> in the center according to their turning, so that the hub always existed freely without change, whether the wheels went forward or backward or crosswise, or upward or downward. And the hub always gave birth to the <term>spokes</term> <note>original: "Speichen"</note>, so that they were properly positioned everywhere in the turning, and yet no spoke passed away, but rather they all turned together in this way, going wherever the wind turned them, without needing to turn around.

Yet one would still see all seven wheels, each one's rotation individually, as well as its entire craftsmanship with its **rims** and spokes and its hub. 73. 74. 75. That is, whether they now rise upward or downward, or backward or forward, or crosswise, the Heart of God is always in the middle, and always adjusts itself to each Source Spirit. Thus there is one Heart of God, and not seven, which is always born of all seven spirits, and is the heart and life of all seven spirits.

76. Now the spokes, which are always born of the hubs and wheels, and which fit themselves into all the wheels as they go around, and their root, support, or the points where they stand and from which they are born—these signify God the Holy Spirit, who proceeds from the Father and the Son, just as the spokes proceed from the hub and the wheel, and yet remain within the wheel.

77. Now, just as the spokes are many and always revolve within the wheel, so the Holy Spirit is the <term>master builder</term> <note>original: "Werkmeister" – the active, organizing principle of the Trinity</note> in the wheel of God, and forms and shapes everything within the whole of God.

78. Now the wheel has seven wheels within one another, and one hub that fits itself into all seven wheels, and all seven wheels move on—

### Now observe.

79. The wheel in its embodied construction signifies the <term>astringent quality</term> <note>original: "herbe Qualität" – the force of contraction, cold, and hardness</note>, which pulls the entire bodily essence of the Godhead together and holds it, drying it so that it may endure. And the <term>sweet spring-water</term> is born from the revolving or rising up of the spirits; for when the light is born within the heat, the astringent quality is startled with great joy, and this is like a settling down or a thinning out, and the hard bodily essence sinks down like a gentleness.

80. The <term>startle</term> <note>original: "Schrack" – a sudden divine shock or flash of realization</note> or sight of the light now rises in the astringent quality, quite gently and trembling; this is now bitter within the water, and the light dries it and makes it friendly and sweet.

81. Within this now stands life and joy, for the startle or flash now rises in all qualities, like the aforementioned wheel that turns itself; there, all seven spirits rise within one another and give birth to each other as if in a circle, and the light becomes shining in the midst of the seven spirits, and shines back into all the spirits, and therein all the spirits triumph and rejoice in the light.

82. Just as the seven wheels move around the single hub, as if around their heart that holds them, and they in turn hold the hub: so also do the seven spirits give birth to the Heart, and the Heart holds the seven spirits, and they all give forth voices and a kingdom of divine joy, heartfelt loving, and kissing.

83. For when the spirits surge into one another with their light, turning and rising, life is constantly being born; for one spirit always gives its taste to the other—that is, it <term>infects</term> <note>original: "inſiciret" – here meaning to permeate or influence with its own nature</note> itself with the other.

84. Thus one tastes the other and feels the other, and in the sound, one hears the other; and the sound or tone penetrates from all seven spirits toward the Heart, and rises in the Heart in the flash of light; there, voices and the joyful kingdom of the <term>Son of God</term> are given forth: and all seven spirits

<column-break/>

triumph and rejoice in the Heart of God, each according to its own quality.

85. For in the light within the sweet water, all astringency, hardness, bitterness, and heat are softened and made lovely; and there is nothing in the seven spirits but a lovely wrestling and a wondrous birthing, like a holy play of God.

86. Their sharp birth, however—of which I wrote above—remains hidden like a kernel, for it is softened by the light and the sweet water.

87. Just as a sour and bitter green apple is compelled by the sun to become lovely to eat, and yet one still tastes all its qualities; so also the Godhead retains its qualities, but it wrestles quite gently, like a lovely game.

88. If, however, the <term>Source Spirits</term> <note>original: "Quellgeister" – the seven fundamental properties of divine nature</note> were to elevate themselves and penetrate each other too quickly, rubbing and squeezing each other harshly, then the sweet water would be squeezed out and the fierce heat would ignite; then the fire of all seven spirits would go up, as it did in <term>Lucifer</term>.

89. This is now the true birth of the Godhead, which has been this way from eternity in all places, and remains so for all eternity. ### Of the glorious Birth and Beauty of King Lucifer.

92. Look here, you spirit of murder and lies, I will describe your royal birth: how you came to be in your creation, how God fashioned you, how you became so beautiful, and for what purpose God created you.

93. If you say otherwise, you lie, for heaven and earth—and indeed all creatures, even the entire Godhead—bear witness against you that God created you for His praise out of Himself, to be a prince and a king of God, like the princes Michael and Uriel.

## The Fountain-Vein of Sin.

116. Now, since Lucifer was formed so royally that his spirit rose within him during his formation or building, and was quite beautifully and lovely received by **GOD** and placed into glorification, he should have immediately begun his angelic obedience and course. He should have moved <note>original: "wallen" — to bubble, boil, or move like a living spring</note> in **GOD** (as **GOD** Himself did) like a dear son in the Father's house; but he did not do that.

117. They began a higher, prouder, and more magnificent **working** <note>original: "qualificirung" — the way a quality acts or operates</note> than **GOD** Himself.

118. But as the spirits thus rose up and triumphed so violently within one another, rising against the right of nature, the source-spirits ignited themselves too harshly: specifically, the **harsh quality** <note>original: "herbe qualität" — the astringent, contracting force</note> pulled the **body** <note>original: "Corpus"</note> together too tightly, so that the sweet water dried up.

119. And the powerful and great bright flash—which had risen in the sweet water within the heat, from which the bitter quality arises in the sweet water—rubbed itself terribly hard against the harsh quality, as if it wanted to burst it apart out of great joy.

120. For the flash was so bright that it was, as it were, unbearable to the source-spirits; therefore, the bitter quality trembled and rubbed itself so hard against the harsh quality that the heat was ignited against **nature**—

# Of the First Species.

54. The first spirit is the **astringent quality** <note>original: "herbe Qualität"; the quality of contraction or drawing together</note>. In God, this is a fine, lovely drawing-together, drying, and cooling, and it is used for formation; and although it is somewhat sharp in its depths, it tempers itself with the sweet water so that it is entirely gentle, lovely, and full of joy.

55. And when the light of the sweet water enters into it, it gives its birth to it in a friendly and voluntary way, and makes it dry and bright-shining. And when the <term>Sound</term> <note>original: "Thon"; can mean both 'tone/sound' and 'clay' (Ton), but in Böhme's physics of the spirits, it usually refers to the auditory/vibrational quality of the divine</note> rises up in the light, it adds its sound or ring quite gently and brotherly. Likewise, it accepts the love of all the spirits; it also allows the heat to cool itself in a friendly way, and is a friendly will with all qualities; it also gladly helps to form the spirit of nature and within it all kinds of forms, figures, fruit, and growths according to the will of all six spirits.

56. It is truly a humble father of its children, who loves them from the heart and plays with them in a friendly manner; for it is truly the father of the other six spirits, which are born within it, and it helps to give birth to them all.

57. Now, when God created Lucifer with his host, he created him out of this friendly Godhead, out of himself, out of the <term>Place</term> <note>original: "Loco," from Latin *locus*</note> of heaven and this world; there was no other matter for it. This living <term>Salitter</term> <note>original: "Salitter"; Böhme's term for the divine "saltpeter" or the crystalline, foundational substance of the divine realm</note> was drawn together quite gently, without killing or without great movement.

Thus they also knew well that the Heart of God was <term>the First</term> <note>original: "Primus"</note> in the entire Godhead. ### Why did God allow the evil spirit of Lucifer, which came out of Lucifer’s body, into himself? Could he not have resisted him?

87. You should know that there was no other difference between God and Lucifer than that between parents and their children, and even much closer. Just as parents bear a child from their own body according to their image, and keep it in their house as a natural heir of their body and care for it, so too was the body of Lucifer close to the Godhead. For God born him out of His own body; therefore, He also made him the heir of His goods and granted him the entire <term>Place</term> <note>Latin: Locum</note> in which He created him as his possession.

## The Highest Depth.

88. Here, however, you should know how Lucifer fought against God and angered God; for he could not have done it with his body alone, since his body encompasses nothing further than the place where he stands at that moment. With that, he could not have done much; rather, it is something else.

# Chapter 15.
## Concerning the Third *Species* <note>original: "Species"; refers to a specific type, kind, or form</note> or Quality of the Beginning of Sin in **Lucifer**.

The 3rd spirit in God is the bitter spirit, which arises in the flash of life; for the flash of life rises in the sweet water through the friction of the harsh and hot quality. The **body** <note>original: "Corpus"</note> of the flash, however, remains in the sweet water as a light or heart, standing fine and gentle; and the flash is entirely trembling, and from the shock, fire, water, and harsh spirits, it becomes bitter because of the origin of the water in which it rises.
2. This same flash, or raging shock, or bitter spirit, is captured in the harsh quality, and in the clear light it is glorified within the harsh spirit and becomes highly joyful. This is now the mobility or the root of life which, in the harsh quality, forms the word or makes it distinguishable, so that a thought or will arises in the **body**.
3. Now, this same highly triumphant and joyful spirit is used quite laudably and well for formation in the divine **Salitter** <term>Salitter</term> <note>original: "Salitter"; Böhme’s term for the divine "soil" or "salt-peter" of heaven, the fundamental substance from which all things are formed</note>, for it wells up primarily in **sound** <note>original: "Thon"; can mean tone, sound, or clay, but in Böhme's physics of the "Word," it often refers to the sounding of the divine voice</note> and in love, and is closest to the Heart of God in birth, and is bound with Him in joy; it is itself the source of joy or the rising in the Heart of God.

### Concerning the 4th Species or Form of the Beginning of Sin in Lucifer.

27. The 4th Spirit of GOD is the Heat; it is born between the bitter and the harsh quality, and is conceived in the sweet water; it is shining and luminous, and is the true fountain-spring of life. 36. Now, when I write here of the animal spirit, you must also know exactly what it is or how it is; otherwise, you will read this birth in vain, and it will happen to you as it did to the wise heathens, who climbed up before God’s face and yet could not see it.

37. The soul-spirit is far more subtle and incomprehensible than the body <note>original: "Corpus"</note> or the 7 source-spirits <note>Quellgeister: the seven fundamental forces of Böhme's cosmos (bitter, sweet, harsh, etc.).</note> which hold and form the body; for it proceeds from the 7 spirits, just as God the Holy Spirit proceeds from the Father and the Son.

38. The 7 source-spirits have their collectively incorporated body from nature, that is, from the seventh nature-spirit in the divine power, which I call in this book the Salitter of God...

<meta>continuity: the text continues from the definition of Salitter on the next page.</meta>

...of God, or the "comprehensibility" <note>meaning the tangible or graspable nature of spirit</note> in which the heavenly figures arise. This is a spirit like all 7 spirits, only the other 6 are an incomprehensible being within it; for the divine power births itself in the comprehensibility of the seventh nature-spirit as if hidden, incomprehensible to the creatures.

39. But the animal or soul-spirit births itself in the heart out of the 7 source-spirits in the same manner and way as the Son of God is born; it keeps its seat in the heart and proceeds from that same seat into the divine power, like the Holy Spirit from the Father and the Son; for it also has such a subtlety as God the Holy Spirit, and <term>in-qualifies</term> <note>inqualiret: a Böhmean term meaning to inter-operate, blend qualities, or work in spiritual harmony with.</note> with God the Holy Spirit.

40. When the animal spirit goes out from the body, it is one thing with the hidden deity, and is part of the formation of a thing in nature, just like God the Holy Spirit himself. You have an example of this: when a carpenter wants to build an artistic house, or some other craftsman wants to make an artistic work, the hands (which represent nature) cannot make it first; rather, the 7 spirits are the first builders of it, and the animal spirit shows the 7 spirits the form. Then the 7 spirits form it and make it comprehensible; only then do the hands work according to the image; for you must first bring a work into your mind if you wish to make it.

41. For the soul grasps the highest sense; she sees what God her Father does, and works along in the heavenly formation; therefore she circles a model before the nature-spirits, showing how they should form a thing. And according to this pre-figuring of the soul, all things in this world are made; for the corrupted soul always works so that she might form heavenly forms, but she cannot; for she has for her labor and work only earthly, corrupted Salitter—indeed, a half-dead nature—in which she cannot form heavenly figures.

42. By this you can understand what a great power the spirits of the cast-out angels had in the heavenly nature, and what the substance of the corruption might be—how they corrupted and devastated nature in heaven in their place <note>original: "Loco"</note> with their hideous ignition, from which the terrifying fierceness <note>original: "Grimm"</note> which rules in this world has arisen.

43. Then the ignited nature still burns forever until the last day, and this ignited fire-source is an eternal enmity against God. ### Of the 5th Species <note>original: "Species," meaning type or form.</note> or Form of the Beginning of Sin in Lucifer and his Angels.

44. The 5th source-spirit in the divine power is gracious love, which is the true sight of gentleness and humility; it is also born in the flash of life. When the flash, as a sudden terror, pierces through, whereby joy arises, the foundation of the ignited light remains in the sweet water; it pierces gently after the flash through the fire into the harsh quality, and softens the fire, making the harsh quality quite mild and soft, which is also a birth of the water.

45. But when the fire tastes the mild, sweet, and soft flavor, it softens itself and forms into a gentle warmth, entirely lovely; and a truly friendly life rises up in the fire, and it penetrates the harsh quality with this dear, gentle warmth, stilling the cold fire, making the hard soft, the thick thin, and the dark light.

46. But when the bitter flash, along with the harsh and fire-spirit, tastes this gentleness, there is nothing there but pure longing, desiring, and fulfilling—an entirely gentle and lovely tasting, wrestling, kissing, and the birth of love. For all the fierce births of the source-spirits become entirely gentle, lovely, humble, and friendly in this penetration, and the Godhead truly consists in this.

47. For in the first four source-spirits stands the divine birth, which is why they must also be quite fierce, even though they have their gentle mother, the water, beneath them: and in the fifth stands the gracious love, in the sixth the joy, and in the seventh the formation or comprehensibility.

48. Now then, Lucifer, where is your love? How have you conducted yourself? Is your love also such a fountain? We shall now also examine it, to see what a "dear angel" you have become.

49. Had Lucifer not exalted and ignited himself, his fountain of love would have been nothing other than as it is in God, for there was no other Salitter <note>Böhme’s term for the divine "sap" or substance, derived from the word for saltpeter, representing the fundamental matter of God's kingdom.</note> in him than in God.

50. But when he exalted himself, intending to rule the entire Godhead with his soul-spirit <note>original: "animalischen Geiste." From the Latin *anima*, meaning the breath of life or soul, not "animalistic" in the modern sense.</note>, the foundation and heart of the light—which is the kernel of love in the sweet water—became a grim and pressing fire-source, from which an entirely trembling, burning governance and birth arose within his whole body <note>original: "Corpus"</note>.

51. When the soul-spirit was born in this fierce and harsh birth of fire, it broke out of his body into the nature or Salitter of God with great grimness, and destroyed the gracious love in that Salitter. For it broke through everything quite grimly and fierily, like a tyrant, thinking he alone was God and that he would rule with sharpness.

52. From this has now arisen the great repulsion and eternal enmity between God and Lucifer; for the power of God flows quite gently, lovely, and friendly, so that one cannot even grasp its birth, whereas the spirits of Lucifer flow and tear with a quite harsh, fiery, and rapidly surging movement.

53. You have an example of this in the ignited Salitter of the stars, which, because of this ignited grimness, must roll themselves around with such vanity so quickly until the last day; then the grimness will be separated from them and given to King Lucifer for an eternal house.

54. That this is a great repulsion in God needs no proof; rather, a person may consider what repulsion and displeasure would arise if such a grim fire-source were to emerge in their own body, and how often the entire body would be filled with grimness.

55. This indeed happens to those who take the Devil in as a guest; but while he is a guest, he lies still like a tame little dog; but when he becomes the host, he storms the house, just as he did to the body of God.

56. Therefore, the fire of God’s wrath is still in the "body of God" of this world until the end, and many a creature is swallowed up in the fire of wrath, about which much could be written, but it belongs in its proper place.

### Of the 6th *Species* <note>original: "Species," meaning type or form of being.</note> or Form of the Beginning of Sin in Lucifer and his Angels.

58. The sixth source-spirit in the divine power is *Mercurius* <note>In Böhme’s system, Mercury represents the "Sound" or "Tone" and the power of speech/expression.</note> or Sound, within which distinction and heavenly joys arise. This spirit takes its origin in the fire-flash—that is, in the bitter quality—and rises in the lightning-flash through the sweet water; there it softens itself so that it becomes bright. It is then captured in the harsh quality, where it stirs all the spirits. From this stirring, Sound arises. Its rising source stands in the lightning-flash, and its body or root stands in the sweet water, in Love.

59. Now, this Sound is the divine kingdom of joy, the triumphing, wherein the divine and gentle play of love rises up in God, along with all forms, shapes, and every kind of figure.

60. You should know here that this quality penetrates all spirits quite gently and lovelies with its stirring, in the same way that a lovely and gentle fire of joy rises in a human heart, wherein the soul-spirit <note>original: "animalische" (from the Latin 'anima' for soul). Böhme means the vital, living spirit of the soul.</note> triumphs as if it were in heaven.

61. Now, this spirit does not belong to the formation of the *Corpus* <note>original: "Corpus," meaning the body or physical structure.</note>, but rather to distinction and mobility, especially to joy and to the discernment within the formation.

62. When the soul-spirit is born in the center <note>original: "Centro"</note> of the heart in the midst of the seven source-spirits, so that the will of the seven spirits is embodied <note>original: "corporiret"</note> together, then the Sound carries it out to the body; it is his chariot upon which the spirit rides and executes <note>original: "exequiret"</note> that which is decided in the council of the seven spirits.

63. For the Sound travels through the soul-spirit into the nature of God or into the *Salitter* <note>term: Salitter. Böhme uses this word to describe the divine substance or "earth" of the heavenly kingdom.</note> of the seventh source-spirit in the divine power, which is its primordial mother, and it qualifies with <note>original: "inqualiret," meaning to work together with or take on the qualities of.</note> the same in the shaping and also in the distinction of the formation.

64. Therefore, when King Lucifer transformed his "proud little horse" <note>A metaphor for Lucifer’s prideful drive or ego.</note> in the

65. For when his soul-spirit was born in his body, it lunged out from his body into the *Salitter* of God like a fiery snake from a hole. But when his mouth opened to speak—that is, when the seven spirits had embodied the word in their will and sent it through the Sound into the *Salitter* of God—it was nothing other than if a fiery thunderbolt had struck into the nature of God, or a grim snake that rages and storms as if it wanted to tear nature apart.

67. When the Sound rises in the divine nature, it rises quite gently out of all seven source-spirits at once, and it births the word or figures quite gently.

68. That is: when a source-spirit conceives a will for birth, it penetrates quite gently through the other source-spirits into the center of the heart; there the will is formed and approved according to all the spirits.

71. In such a gentle way, King Lucifer was also supposed to give birth, to work, and according to the law of the Godhead, to help shape things with his soul-spirit in the *Salitter* or in the nature of God, as a dear son in nature.

72. Just as a son in a house helps the father carry out his work according to the father’s way and skill, so also was Lucifer with his angels meant to help form all shapes and growths in the Salitter <note>Böhme uses "Salitter" to describe the divine "soil" or the fundamental chemical-spiritual substance of heaven from which all things are formed.</note> of God, within the great house of God the Father, according to the manner and way of God with his animate spirit <note>original: "animalischen Geiste." 73. For the whole Salitter was meant to be a house of pleasure for the angelic bodies, and everything was meant to rise up and form itself according to the delight of their spirit, so that they would never and eternally have any displeasure in any figure or creature, but rather their animate spirit was meant to be present in all formation. <insert>“The formation from the heavenly essences happens magically, all according to the will and capability of nature and the creatures.”</insert> And the Salitter was meant to be the property of the creatures.

74. 75. For God and the creatures would have been one heart and one will. <insert>“The image from the soul-fire, and the love or the divine center, is in one essence.”</insert>

77. And from this, the wild and evil beasts in this world have their origin; for Lucifer’s host ignited the Salitter of the stars and the earths, and half-killed and corrupted it.

78. For when God performed the creation of this world after the fall of Lucifer, everything was created out of that same Salitter in which Lucifer had sat. Thus, the creatures in this world had to be created out of that same Salitter afterward; they now formed themselves according to the nature of the ignited qualities, both evil and good.

79. 80. This I set down for you here as a guide; you will find it described more fully and demonstrably in the account of the creation of this world.

81. # Chapter 16.
## Concerning the 7th *Species* <note>original: "Species," meaning type or form.</note> or Shape of the Beginning of Sin in Lucifer and his Angels.

1. Here you may truly open your eyes, for you will see the hidden things that have been concealed from all people since the world began; for you will see the murder-pits of the devil and the cruel sins, enmity, and corruption.

2. The devil has taught sorcery to humans to strengthen his kingdom; indeed, had he revealed to humans the true foundation of what lies beneath it, many a person would surely have let it be.

3. Come to my school, you jugglers and sorcerers who lust after the devil! I will show you how you travel to hell with your *Nigromantia* <note>original: "Nigromantia," meaning necromancy or black magic.</note> or art. You pride yourselves that the devil is subject to you and think you are gods; here I will describe the origin of necromancy, for I too have become a knower of nature, but

28. Scholars have had much disputing, questioning, and reflecting regarding the fierce malice in all creatures, as well as in the sun and stars in this world; likewise, there are some such poisonous, evil animals, worms, and plants in this world, which the rational-minded have rightly wondered at. Some have concluded that God must surely have willed the evil too, since He created so much evil; some have given the blame to the Fall of Man, and some to the working of the Devil.

29. 36. And their comprehensibility <note>German: *Begreiflichkeit*. 38. Likewise, no spirit reaches out particularly with its bodily being toward the Heart of God; instead, each spirit encloses its will with the others into the center for the birth of the Heart, so that the Heart and the seven spirits of God are one single will.

39. For this is the law of comprehensibility: that it should not exalt itself into the Incomprehensible. For the power that is embodied together in the center or midst of all seven spirits is incomprehensible and unsearchable, yet it is not invisible; for it is not the power of one spirit alone, but of all seven.

40. Thus, a spirit in its own body—outside of its inherent birth—cannot reach into the whole Heart of God to approve or search everything. Outside of its inherent birth, it comprehends only its own birth within the Heart of God; but all seven spirits together comprehend the entire Heart of God.

->**On the Ignition of the Wrath-Fire.**<-

57. Now, when King Lucifer ignited himself with all his angels, the <term>wrath-fire</term> rose up instantly in the body <note>original: "Corpus"</note>, and the lovely light in the animal spirit was extinguished, and it became a fierce, devilish spirit, all according to the ignition and will of the <term>source-spirits</term>.

58. Now, this animal spirit was then connected with the deity in nature, and could interact with it as if it were one thing: it now stabbed out of the bodies of the devils into the nature of GOD, like a murderer and a thief who desired to murder and rob everything, and bring it under his power. It ignited all seven spirits in nature, and there was nothing then but a harsh, bitter, fiery, and crashing, burning tearing and raging.

59. You should not think that the devil thus mightily overcame the deity: No, rather he ignited the wrath of God—which would have rested in secret for all eternity—and made a murderer's pit out of the <term>Salitter</term> of GOD; for when one puts fire to straw, it burns. GOD did not become a devil because of this.

60. Also, the <term>wrath-fire</term> of GOD in nature does not reach to the innermost core of the heart, which is the Son of GOD; much less into the hidden holiness of the Spirit, but only into the birth of the six <term>source-spirits</term> in the place <note>original: "Locum"</note> where the seventh is born.

61. For in that place, or in that birth, Lord Lucifer became a creature, and his dominion reached no deeper. Had he remained in love, his animal spirit would have reached into the center of the Heart of GOD, for love penetrates through the whole deity.

62. But when his love was extinguished, the animal spirit could no longer enter the Heart of GOD, and his undertaking was in vain; instead, he raged and stormed in nature—that is, in the seventh source-spirit of GOD.

63. Because the power of all seven spirits stood in this one, all seven were also infected in wrath, but only in the external and comprehensible qualification. For the devil could not touch the Heart, nor could he touch the innermost birth of the source-spirits, for the glory of his seven spirits had already died in the first flash of the ignition.

87. Thus, King **Lucifer** is the beginning of sin, a sting of death, an ignition of the wrath of **GOD**, the beginning of all evil, a corruption of this world; and whatever evil occurs, he is the first cause of it.

88. He is also a murderer and the father of lies, a founder of hells, a corrupter of all good, and an eternal enemy of **GOD** and of all good angels and men; with whom I and all people who intend to be saved must strive and fight every day and hour, as against the worst enemy.

### The final Condemnation. <note>original: "Condemnation"</note>

89. But because **GOD** has tested him as an eternal enemy and condemned him to eternal imprisonment—and since he now sees his hourglass before his eyes, and his hellish kingdom has been revealed to me through **GOD’S** Spirit—I also curse him, along with all the holy souls of men, and renounce him as an eternal enemy who has often torn up my vineyard.

90. Furthermore, I renounce all his jurists <note>original: "Juristen." # Chapter 17.
## Concerning the lamentable and miserable condition of corrupted Nature, and the origin of the 4 Elements, in place of the holy Government of God.

1. Although God is an eternal almighty Ruler whom no one can withstand, Nature in its kindling <note>referring to the "ignition" of the qualities of wrath following Lucifer's rebellion</note> has now received a very strange government, which did not exist before the times of wrath.

3. For the six <term>Source-spirits</term> <note>the fundamental forces or "qualities" of Böhme's divine nature</note> gave birth to the seventh Nature-spirit in the place <note>original: "Loco"</note> of this world quite gently and lovelily before the times of wrath, just as happens now in heaven, and not a single spark of wrath had risen within it.

3. Moreover, everything within was entirely light, and yet it required no other light, but the Wellspring of the Heart of God illuminated all, and was a light in everything that shone everywhere unquenchably and unstoppably; for nature was entirely refined <note>original: "dünne," literally "thin," meaning spiritual and non-dense</note>, and everything existed only in power, and it was a truly lovely harmony <note>original: "Temperanz," the balanced state of the qualities before the Fall</note>.

4. As soon as the conflict in Nature began with the proud devils, however, everything in the seventh Nature-spirit in Lucifer’s territory—which is the place <note>original: "Locus"</note> of this world—took on another form and effect.

5. For Nature received a two-fold source, and every outermost birth in Nature was kindled in the fire of wrath, which fire is now called the wrath of God, or the burning hell.

->To this now belongs the innermost sense of understanding; only the place where the Light is born in the heart can grasp this; the external man does not understand it.<-

6. See, when Lucifer with his army awakened the fire of wrath in the nature of God, so that God became angry in Nature in Lucifer’s place, the outermost birth in Nature received another quality: entirely grim, harsh, cold, hot, bitter, and sour. The surging spirit, which previously in Nature had been gently qualified, became in its outermost birth quite elevated and terrible; this is what is now called in the outermost birth the <term>Wind</term> or the element of <term>Air</term> because of its rising up.

7. For when the seven spirits kindled in their outermost birth, they gave birth to such a hard-surging spirit: also the sweet water, which before the times of wrath was entirely refined and intangible, became quite thick and substantial; and the harsh quality became quite sharp and cold-fiery, for it received a severe contraction like salt.

8. For the salt-water or salt, which is still found in the earth today, has its origin and descent from the first kindling of the harsh quality: Likewise, the stones also have their beginning and descent from it, as does the earth.

For just as nature, with its working, wrestling, and rising of the birth, stood at the time of the kindling <note>The "kindling" refers to the moment the spiritual world was corrupted by the fall of Lucifer, causing it to "ignite" with wrath and solidify into matter.</note>, so too has a material substance drawn itself together.

### Now the question arises:
->How did a tangible son come to be from an intangible mother?<-

11. Of this you have a likeness in how the earth and stones came from intangibility.

12. Behold, the depth between heaven and earth is also intangible; yet the qualities of the elements nevertheless, at various times, give birth to a living and tangible flesh within it, such as grasshoppers, flies, and worms.

13. This is caused by the stern contractions of the qualities. In this contracted Salitter, life is then immediately born: for when the heat ignites the harsh quality, life arises, because the bitter quality moves, which is the origin of life.

14. So also, in the same way, the earth and stones have their origin; for when the Salitter in nature was kindled, everything became quite rough, thick, and dark, like a thick, dark mist, which the harsh quality dried out with its coldness.

15. But because the light was extinguished in the outermost birth <note>The physical world of the senses.</note>, the heat was imprisoned within tangibility and could no longer give birth to its life. Because of this, death has entered into nature, so that nature, or the corrupted earth, can no longer help itself. Therefore, another creation of light had to follow; otherwise, the earth would be an eternal, insoluble death. But now she brings forth her fruit through the power and ignition of the created light <note>The sun and the stars.</note>.

### Now one might ask:
->How did it take on a form with this twofold birth?<-

<column-break/>

### Answer.

16. You cannot grasp or understand this better than by looking at your own body. Through the first fall of Adam, with its entire birth, skill, and will, the body became such a house as the place <note>original: "Locus"</note> of this world has become.

17. Firstly, you have the animal flesh; this came to be through the "lust-bite" <note>Adam's eating of the fruit.</note>, for it is the house of corruption.

18. When Adam was made from the corrupted Salitter of the earth—that is, from the seed or mass <note>original: "Massa"</note> which the Creator drew from the corrupted earth—he was at first not such flesh. Otherwise, his body would have been created mortal. Instead, he had an angelic <term>power-body</term> <note>original: "Kraftleib," a spiritual, luminous body not subject to decay.</note>; in this, he was to exist eternally and eat of angelic fruit, which grew for him in Paradise before his fall, before the Lord tested the earth.

19. But because the seed or the mass from which Adam was made was infected with the corrupted longing of the devil, Adam lusted after his mother—that is, to eat of the fruit of the corrupted earth, which had become evil in its external tangibility and so hard and tangible in the wrath-fire.

20. Because Adam’s spirit lusted after such fruit, which was like the corrupted earth, nature also formed such a tree for him, which was like the corrupted earth. For Adam was the heart in nature; therefore, his animal spirit helped to form this tree from which he desired to eat.

21. But when the devil saw that this lust was in Adam, he boldly struck at the Salitter in Adam and infected the Salitter from which Adam was made even more severely.

22. Then it was time for the Creator to build him a woman, who afterwards brought the sin into action and ate of the false fruit. Otherwise, if Adam had eaten from the tree...

16. Where the heated spirit was first in the sweet water within love, there the harsh spirit <note>The "harsh spirit" (herbe Geist) is one of Böhme's seven source-spirits, associated with contraction and coldness</note> drew the matter together, and thus the most noble ore and gemstones were formed.

Regarding the precious stones, however—such as the carbuncle, ruby, emerald, chrysolite, onyx, and the like, which are the very best—they have their origin where the flash of light rose up in love. For that same flash is born in gentleness, and is the heart in the center of the source-spirits; therefore, these same stones are also gentle, powerful, and lovely.

->One might say:<-

### Why then does man in this world love gold, silver, and precious stones above all other things, and use them for the defense or protection of his body?

18. Within this lies the core; for gold, silver, precious stones, and all bright ore have their origin from the Light, which occurred before the times of wrath in the outermost birth in nature—that is, in the seventh spirit of nature.

19. Because every human being is like the "whole house of this world," his own source-spirits also love the core or the very best within corrupted nature, and they use it for their protection and defense.

This refers to the vital living spirit or the "anima," rather than "animalistic" in a modern sense</note>, the door stands open; for it is held back by nothing, and is just like GOD himself in his innermost birth.

## On the Third Birth.

29. Now the third birth is the tangibility of nature, which before the time of God’s wrath was thin, lovely, and bright, so that the source-spirits could see through everything. Within it there were neither stones nor earth, and it required no such light as it does now, but the light was born everywhere in the center, and everything stood within the light.

30. But when King Lucifer was created, he awakened the wrath of God in this third birth, for the bodies of the angels became creatures in this third birth.

31. Because the devils then ignited their bodies, intending to rule over the whole Godhead with their will, the Creator also ignited this third spirit or third birth in nature within his wrath. He took the devil captive within it and prepared an eternal lodging for him there, so that he might not be higher than the whole of God.

Observe here the meaning in the highest depth.
87. **The word Spoke** <note>original: "Sprach" — Böhme's analysis depends on the German pronunciation of "Sprach," which begins with a hissing 'S', moves to a sharp 'p', and ends with a guttural 'ch'.</note> is spoken in a human way; you philosophers, open your eyes, for I will teach you the language of God in my simplicity, as it must be.
88. The word **Spoke** is first caught between the teeth, for they bite together, and the spirit hisses out through the teeth; the tongue bends in the middle, and at the front it points itself, as if it were listening to what was hissing there and was afraid.
89. But when the spirit captures the word, it closes the mouth and grasps it at the back of the palate above the tongue, in the hollow of the bitter and harsh quality.
90. Then the tongue is startled and presses down into the lower palate; at that moment, the spirit travels out from the heart and launches the word—which was held in anger at the back of the palate in the harsh and bitter quality—and it travels through that fierceness, strong and mighty like a king or a prince, and opens the mouth. It rules with a strong spirit from the heart through the entire mouth and outside of the mouth, creating a powerful, long syllable like a spirit that has broken through the wrath. Against this, the wrath—with its grating vibration <note>original: "kirren" — referring to the guttural 'ch' sound at the back of the throat</note> in the harsh and bitter quality in the hollow of the back palate—resists on the tongue and maintains its own right. It remains sitting in its place and lets the gentle spirit from the heart pass through it, and thunders afterward with its grating sound, helping to form and shape the word; yet with its thunder, it cannot leave its seat but remains in its hollow as a prisoner, showing itself to be terrible.

### This is a great mystery.

91. Observe the meaning here: if you grasp this, you rightly understand the Godhead; if not, you are still blind in spirit. **Do not judge**, or you will run here against a strong gate and be captured; if the fire of wrath catches you, you will remain inside it eternally.

92. Now see, you child of man, what a gate to heaven, to hell, and to the earth—indeed, to the entire Godhead—the spirit unlocks for you!
93. You should not think that God spoke in a human way at that time, as if it were only a faint word like that of a man. A man’s word is indeed formed in such a shape, proportion, quality, and skill, but the half-dead human does not understand it; this understanding is very noble and precious, for it is born only in the knowledge of the Holy Spirit.
94. But God’s word, which He spoke in power at that time, encompassed heaven and earth, and the heaven of all heavens—yes, the entire Godhead.
95. For it is written:
> And it was dark upon the deep, and the Spirit of God moved upon the waters.
96. The deep signifies the innermost birth, and the darkness signifies the outermost corrupted birth in which the wrath burned; the water signifies the softening of the spirit.
97. That the spirit hisses through the teeth signifies that the spirit traveled from the heart of God through the wrath; that the teeth remain closed while the spirit hisses and do not open signifies that the wrath did not comprehend the Holy Spirit.
98. 99. For He goes through all closed chambers and births and requires no unlocking, just as the teeth cannot hold Him back from passing through them.

102. Just as the spirit performs its exit and formed will through the teeth, yet the teeth do not move themselves or grasp the spirit's will: so the Holy Spirit, without being grasped by the devil or the wrath of **God**, builds for Himself without ceasing a holy seed and temple in the house of this world.

103. 104. Just as the spirit goes forth from the heart strong and mighty through the murmuring and vibrating of the harsh and bitter quality, and rules as it exits within that harshness and bitterness—remaining incomprehensible to those qualities—like a mighty king: so also the Spirit of **God** rules mightily in the outermost birth of this world, within the wrath-house, and generates for Himself a temple therein, which the wrath-house cannot comprehend.

105. But the fact that the harsh and bitter spirit thus murmurs when the spirit from the heart passes through its house and rules with power, signifies that the wrath of **God** together with the devils are set in opposition to Love in the house of this world; so that throughout the entire duration of this world, these two shall fight and struggle with one another like two warring armies. From this, the human and animal wars and the strife of all creatures take their origin.

111. For the harsh and bitter quality takes the power from the spirit of the heart and infects it; therefore nature has now become too weak in the spirit of the heart and is not able to bring forth the heart's own innermost birth. Because of this, nature has created a female and a male.

The light that rose in the seven spirits of nature had no specific seat or location but shone everywhere. However, it was not bright like the sun, but rather like a sky-blue light according to the nature of the <term>Source-Spirits</term> <note>The "Quellgeister" are the seven fundamental qualities or forces that Böhme believed powered all of existence.</note>, until the actual creation and ignition of the fire in the water occurred within the harsh spirit, along with the sun.

### The 19th Chapter.

# Concerning the created Heaven and the form of the Earth and the Water, as well as Light and Darkness.

## Concerning Heaven.

1. The true heaven—which is our own human heaven where the soul goes when it departs from the body, and where Christ our King has entered, and from whence he came from his Father and was born, becoming a man in the womb of the Virgin Mary—has remained almost entirely hidden from the children of men until now, and they have held many different opinions.

2. The scholars have also "scratched" at one another over this with many strange writings; they have fallen into each other's hair with insults and shaming, whereby the holy name of **God** has been disgraced, his members wounded, his temple destroyed, and the holy heaven desecrated with this blasphemy and hostility.

3. Men have always and in every way imagined that heaven is many hundreds or many thousands of miles away from this earth, and that **God** dwells alone in that same heaven. Some <term>physicists</term> <note>original: "Phisici," referring to natural philosophers or early scientists.</note> even presumed to measure that height and brought forth very strange things.

4. Indeed, before this my own realization and revelation from **God**, I myself held it to be so: that the true heaven was only that which closes itself in a round, light-blue circle high above the stars, believing that **God** had his special being only inside there, and ruled this world solely by the power of his Holy Spirit.

5. But when this gave me many a hard blow—doubtless from the Spirit that took delight in me—I
<meta>catchword: I</meta>

<column-break/>

<page-num>231</page-num>
<header>Chap. 19. Morning Glow at Sunrise. 231</header>

finally fell into a state of hard <term>melancholy</term> <note>In Böhme’s time, melancholy was seen as both a physical ailment and a deep spiritual crisis of the soul.</note> and sadness when I beheld the great depth of this world, along with the sun and stars, as well as the clouds, rain, and snow, and contemplated in my spirit the entire creation of this world.

6. Therein I found in all things both evil and good: love and wrath, in irrational creatures—such as wood, stones, earth, and elements—as well as in humans and animals.

7. Furthermore, I considered the tiny spark that is man, wondering what he might be accounted for before **God** against this great work of heaven and earth.

8. Because I found that there was evil and good in all things, in the elements as well as in the creatures, and that in this world things went as well for the godless as for the pious—and that even the barbaric peoples possessed the best lands and that fortune seemed to favor them even more than the pious.

9. I became therefore quite melancholy and deeply troubled; no Scripture could comfort me, though I was quite well-acquainted with it. In this, the devil certainly would not have been idle, for he often hammered heathen thoughts into me, which I will remain silent about here.

10. But while I was in such tribulation, I earnestly raised my spirit (though I understood little or nothing of what it was) up to **God** like a great storm. My entire heart and mind, along with all other thoughts and will, enclosed themselves within it, wrestling without ceasing with the love and mercy of **God**, refusing to let go until he blessed me—that is, until he enlightened me with his Holy Spirit, so that I might understand his will and be rid of my sadness. Then the Spirit broke through.

11. While I, in such focused zeal, stormed so hard against **God** and all the gates of hell (as if my own strength were still sufficient, being willing to risk my life on it, which surely would not have been in my power without the assistance of **God’s** Spirit), suddenly, after several hard storms, my spirit broke through the gates of hell into the innermost birth of the <term>Godhead</term> <note>original: "Gottheit." Böhme describes a mystical union where the seeker's soul enters the very essence of God.</note>, and was there embraced with love, just as a bridegroom embraces his dear bride.

12. But what kind of triumphing there was in the spirit, I can neither write nor speak of; it can be compared to nothing except that moment where life is born in the midst of death, and it resembles the resurrection from the dead.

13. In this light, my spirit immediately saw through everything, and in all creatures—even in herbs and grass—I recognized **God**: who he is, and how he is, and what his will is. Also, in this light, my will immediately grew with a great urge to describe the essence of **God**.

14. But because I could not immediately grasp the deep <term>births of God</term> <note>Böhme views the internal workings of the Divine as a process of "birth" or "becoming."</note> in their essence or comprehend them with my reason, a full twelve years passed before the true understanding was given to me. It happened as it does with a young tree planted in the earth: at first it is young and tender, and it is pleasant to look at, especially when it begins to grow well; but it does not bear fruit immediately, and even if it blooms, the blossoms fall off. Many cold winds, frosts, and snows pass over it before it grows up and bears fruit.

15. It was the same for this spirit; the first fire was only a seed, not a constant, enduring light. Since that time, many cold winds have passed over it, but the will was never extinguished.

16. This tree also often tested itself to see if it might bear fruit, showing itself with blossoms; but the blossom was knocked off the tree until this very day, when it stands in its first fruit in the process of growing.

17. From this light I now have my knowledge, as well as my will and drive; I intend to write down this knowledge according to my gifts and let **God** rule over it. Even if I should thereby anger the world, the devil, and all the gates of hell, I will watch to see what **God** intends by it. For I am far too weak to recognize his purpose; although the spirit allows some future things to be recognized in the light, I am still far too weak in the outer man to comprehend such things.

18. But the <term>animate spirit</term> <note>original: "animalische Geist," from the Latin "anima" (soul). For Böhme, this refers to the higher soul-spirit rather than just "animal" instincts.</note>, which <term>co-qualifies</term> <note>original: "inqualiret." A technical term Böhme uses to describe how different forces or spirits inter-operate and share the same qualities.</note> with **God**,

<column-break/>

understands it well; the <term>animal body</term> <note>original: "thierische Leib." This refers to the physical, mortal part of a human being.</note>, however, only catches a glimpse of it, just like a flash of lightning. For this is how the innermost birth of the soul presents itself when it tears through the outermost birth, in the elevation of the Holy Spirit, through the gates of hell. But through the outermost birth, it soon closes up again, for the <term>wrath of God</term> <note>Böhme’s concept of "Gottes Zorn" (God's Wrath) is the harsh, dark force of nature that must be overcome by Light and Love.</note> bolts the fortress shut and keeps it imprisoned in its power.

19. Then the knowledge of the outer man is gone, and he goes about in his sorrowful and anxious birth like a pregnant woman who has gone into labor and would always love to give birth, yet cannot, and remains constantly in distress.

20. It is the same with the animal body: once it has tasted the sweetness of **God**, it hungers and thirsts for it forever. But the devil, in the power of **God's** wrath, resists it mightily, and a person in such a course must always stand in an anxious birth; it is nothing but struggling and fighting within one’s own inner workings.

21. I have not written this for my own praise, but for the reader’s comfort, in case they might desire to walk with me on my narrow path, so that they do not immediately despair when the gates of hell and the wrath of **God** meet them and strike them in the face.

22. When we come together across this narrow bridge of fleshly birth onto that green meadow where the wrath of **God** does not reach, then we shall truly delight in the damage we suffered; even if we must now be the world’s fool and let the devil, in the power of **God’s** wrath, roar over us. It does not matter; it will suit us better in that life than if we had worn a royal crown in this one, for this is a very short time, and is not even worthy of being called "time."

-> Now pay attention. <-

23. When you form your thoughts about Heaven—what it is, where it is, or how it is—you do not need to swing your thoughts many thousands of miles from here, for that same <term>location</term> <note>original: "Locus."</note> or heaven is not your heaven. Even if it is connected with your heaven like one body, and is also only one body of **God**, you were not made a creature in that <term>location</term> which is many hundreds of thousands of miles away, but rather in the heaven of this world, which also has such a depth within it that no human number can reach.

24. For the true heaven is everywhere, even in the place where you stand and walk; when your spirit grasps the innermost <term>birth of God</term> <note>Böhme uses "birth" (Geburt) to describe the unfolding layers or qualities of reality.</note> and penetrates through the <term>sidereal</term> <note>sidereal: relating to the stars and the "astral" influences on the soul.</note> and fleshly births, then it is already in heaven.

25. But it is true that a pure, beautiful heaven exists in all three births above the <term>deep</term> <note>The "deep" or abyss refers to the void or the chaotic foundation of the physical world.</note> of this world, in which **God’s** essence rises up together with the holy angels, entirely pure, beautiful, and full of joy; this is undeniable, and he who would deny such a thing would not be born of **God**.

->But you should know:<-

26. That the <term>Locus</term> <note>original: "Locus" (Latin for place). Böhme refers to the specific spatial location of our physical world.</note> of this world, in its innermost birth, <term>inqualifies</term> <note>inqualiret: a term coined by Böhme meaning to intermingle, resonate, or operate within the same quality.</note> with the heaven above us, and is one heart, one essence, one will, one **God**, all in all. (But as for why the location of this world is not called a heaven, and why there is a closure between the upper heaven above us—this is how it is to be understood:)

27. The upper heaven comprises the two kingdoms of Michael and Uriel and all the holy angels who did not fall with Lucifer; and that same heaven has remained as it has been from eternity, before the angels were ever created.

28. The other heaven is this world, in which Lucifer was a king; he ignited the outermost birth in nature, and that is now the wrath of **God**, and it cannot be called **God** or heaven, but rather corruption.

29. Therefore, the upper heaven closes itself off in its outermost birth as far as the wrath of **God** reaches, and as far as the reign of Lucifer reached; for the corrupted birth cannot grasp the pure one.

30. That is to say, the outermost birth of this world cannot seize the outermost birth of the heaven above this world; for they are like life and death against one another, or like a human and a stone against one another.

31. Therefore, there is a firm closure between the outermost birth of the upper heaven and this world; for the <term>firmament</term> <note>original: "Feste." A barrier or solid boundary.</note> between them is death, which reigns at all ends in the outermost birth of this world. Thus, this world is barred, and the outermost birth of the upper heaven cannot enter the outermost birth of this world; there is a great gulf between them.

32. And for this reason we cannot see the angels in our outermost birth, and the angels also cannot dwell with us in the outermost birth of this world; but in the innermost birth, they do dwell with us. And when we fight with the devil, they hold off his blows in the innermost birth and are the protection of holy souls. Therefore, we cannot see or grasp the angels, for the outermost birth of their bodies is incomprehensible to the outermost birth of this world.

33. The second birth of this world stands in life, for it is the sidereal birth, from which the third and holy birth is born, and in which love and wrath struggle with each other. For the second birth stands in the seven <term>Source-Spirits</term> <note>Quellgeister: the seven fundamental properties or forces that Böhme believes drive all of nature.</note> of this world, and is in all places and in all creatures, as well as in man. But now the Holy Spirit also reigns in the second birth and helps to bring forth the third, holy birth.

34. 35. And out of this heart, **Jesus Christ, God’s** Son, entered into all three births in the womb of the Virgin Mary, and truly took them upon himself, so that he—through and with his innermost birth—might take the devil, death, and hell captive in the outermost birth, and overcome the wrath of **God** as a king and prince of victory, and by the power of his birth in the flesh, penetrate through all people.

36. And through such an entry of the innermost birth of the heart of the heaven of this world into the sidereal and outermost births, **Jesus Christ, Son of God** and Mary, has become a Lord and King of this our heaven and the earth, who in all three births reigns over sin, the devil, death, and hell.

In this heaven sits now our King **Jesus Christ** at the right hand of **God** and encompasses all 3 births <note>Böhme uses "births" (Geburten) to describe the different levels of reality: the divine interior, the astral/sidereal realm, and the physical world.</note>, as an almighty Son of the Father, who through and in all 3 births in this world is present in all spaces and places, and grasps, holds, and carries everything as the newborn Son of the Father, in the power and upon the seat of the once great and mighty, but now cast out, cursed, and damned king **Lucifer**, the devil.

39. Because you live in this contested birth, you must bow down and let the devil ride upon you; but as hard as he strikes you, so hard do you strike him back if you defend yourself. For when you struggle against him, you stir up his wrath-fire and destroy his nest; this is then like a great riot, as if you were holding a mighty battle against him.

40. And even though some pain happens to your body, much worse happens to him when he is overcome; then he roars like a lion whose cubs have been stolen, for the grimness and **wrath of God** torments him. But if you invite him in as a guest, he becomes fat and lustful, and overcomes you in time.

41. Thus you have a true description of heaven; and even if you cannot grasp it with your reason, I can grasp it quite well; so just reflect upon it reasonably: what might **God** be?

42. In this world, you see nothing but the deep, and within it the stars and the birth of the elements; would you then say that **God** is not there? Dear one, what then was in this 

<meta>catchword: place</meta>

---

<page-num>237</page-num>
<header>Chap. 19. Morning Glow at Sunrise.</header>

place before the time of the world? If you would say: "Nothing," then you speak without reason; you must surely say that **God** was there, otherwise nothing would have come to be there.

43. Now, if **God** was there, who then pushed him away or overcame him, so that he is no longer there? But if **God** is there, then he is indeed in his heaven, and moreover in his Trinity.

44. The devil, however, has ignited the wrath-bath <note>original: "Zornbad." Böhme's term for the chaotic, angry state of nature caused by the Fall.</note>; from this, the earth and stones, as well as the elements, have become so volatile, and also so cold, bitter, and hot, and have murdered the outermost birth.

45. This is now the business and my entire intention in writing: how it became alive again, and how it births itself anew; and from this, the animal flesh also came to be in the creatures; but the sin in the flesh is the **wrath of God**.

### Secondly, the question and the business in this book is: where then will the wrath of God go?

46. To this the Spirit gives the answer: that at the end of this corrupted time of birth, after the resurrection of the dead, the <term>Locus</term> <note>original: "Locus" (Latin for place). Böhme uses it to mean the physical space occupied by our world.</note> or space where the earth now stands shall be granted to the devil as his property and wrath-house. Yet not through all 3 births, but only the outermost one in which he now stands; the innermost birth, however, will hold him captive in its power and use him as a footstool, which he will eternally be able neither to grasp nor to touch.

47. For it is not the understanding that the wrath-fire shall be extinguished and exist no more; otherwise, the devils would also have to become holy angels again and live in the holy heaven. But if not, then a hole in this world must remain for them as a dwelling.

48. If a person's eyes were only opened, they would see **God** everywhere in his heaven; for heaven stands in the innermost birth. Moreover, when **Stephen** <note>Referring to the martyrdom of St. Stephen in the Book of Acts.</note> saw heaven open and the **Lord Jesus** at the right hand of **God**, his spirit did not first soar into the upper heaven, but rather he penetrated into the innermost birth; there, heaven is at all ends.

49. You must also not think that the **Godhead** is somehow a being that exists only in the upper heaven, or that our soul, when it departs from the body, travels many hundreds of thousands of miles up into the upper heaven. There is no need for that at all; rather, the soul is placed into the <term>innermost birth<note>Böhme’s term for the deepest spiritual level of reality where the divine essence resides, distinct from the physical and astral realms.</note></term>. There it is with **God** and in **God** and with all the holy angels, and it can be above one moment and below the next; it is held back by nothing.

50. For in the innermost birth, the Upper and Lower **Godhead** are One Body, one open gate: the holy angels walk just as much in the innermost birth of this world with our King **Jesus Christ**, as they do in the upper regions of their own territory.

51. And where would the soul of man rather be than with its King and Redeemer **Jesus Christ**? For in **God**, "far" and "near" are as one thing, one single comprehension: everywhere is **Father, Son, and Holy Spirit**.

52. The gate of the **Godhead** in the upper heaven is nothing different, nor anything brighter, than it is in this world. And where could there be greater joy than in the place where, at every hour, beautiful, dear, newborn children and angels come to **Christ**, having broken through death into life? They will no doubt know how to tell of many struggles. And where could there be greater joy than where, in the midst of death, life is being born without ceasing?

53. For every soul brings a new triumph with it, and there is nothing but pure, friendly <note>original: "beneveniren" – a Latinate-German hybrid for "welcoming" or "blessing."</note> welcoming. Think of when the souls of children come to the parents who bore them in their bodies—might there not be heaven in that place? Or do you think I write too earthly? If you come to this "window" <note>Böhme often uses the metaphor of a window or a "glimpse" to describe spiritual insight.</note>, you will not say it is earthly; even though I must use an earthly tongue, there is nonetheless true heavenly understanding beneath it, which I can neither write nor speak of in my outermost birth <note>Refers to his physical, mortal self.</note>.

54. I know well that the word concerning the **three births** will not be able to be grasped in every heart, especially where the heart is too deeply drowned in the flesh and barred shut by the outermost birth. But I cannot give it any other way, for it is so; and even if I write pure spirit—as in truth it is nothing else—the heart still understands only "flesh" when it looks upon it.

### Of the Form of the Earth.

55. Many writers <note>original: "Scribenten"</note> have indeed written that heaven and earth were created out of nothing; but I wonder that among such excellent men not one has been found who could describe the true ground, seeing that this same **God** has been from eternity, He who *is*.

56. Now, where there is nothing, nothing comes to be; every thing must have a root, otherwise nothing grows. Had the seven spirits of nature not been from eternity, there would have been no angel, no heaven, and no earth.

57. The earth, however, has come from the corrupted <term>Salitter<note>A unique term for Böhme, referring to the spiritual "marrow" or divine saltpeter—the essential substance of the divine realm before it was hardened into physical matter.</note></term> of the outermost birth. You cannot deny this: when you look at the earth and stones, you must say that there is a life within them; otherwise, neither gold nor silver, nor herb nor grass would grow within them.

->Now one might ask:<-

### Are all three births also within it?

58. Yes, life penetrates through death. The outermost birth is death; the second is life, which stands in the **wrath-fire** and in love; the third is the holy life.

->Instruction.<-

59. The external earth is a bitter stench and is dead; every person understands this. But the <term>Salitter</term> was murdered through **Wrath**, so that you cannot deny that **God's wrath** is in the earth; otherwise, it would not be so harsh, bitter, sour, and poisonous, nor would it bring forth such poisonous, evil worms. If you were to say that **God** created it so by His own purpose, you would be saying that **God** Himself is wickedness.

60. Dear friend, tell me then: why was the devil cast out? You will certainly say, for the sake of his pride, because he wanted to be above **God**. <note>original: "Rath Fritz" – a colloquial German expression meaning "Guess what, friend" or "Think on that, Fritz," used here to challenge the reader.</note> Guess what? With what? What power did he have? Speak here if you know anything; if you know nothing, then be silent and listen.

61. He sat in the <term>Salitter</term> of the earth before the times of creation, when it was still thin and stood in heavenly, holy birth. He was in the whole kingdom of this world; back then it was not earth and stones, but a heavenly...
