And the spirit breaks through the wrath-fire and births the holy life, which stands in the power of **Love**.

64. And in this same birth, the dead shall rise again—those who have sown a holy seed; but those who have sown in the wrath-fire shall rise in the wrath-fire. For the earth shall become living again, since the **Godhead** in **Christ** has reborn it through his flesh and exalted it to the right hand of **God**; yet the wrath-fire remains in its birth.

65. If you were to say there is no life in the earth, you speak blindly; for you see that herbs and grass grow from it. And if you were to say it has only one kind of birth, you also speak blindly; for the herb and wood that grow from it are not "earth," nor is the fruit on the tree "wood," nor is the power of the fruit "**God**." Instead, **God** is hidden in the **center** <note>original: "Centro"</note> in the innermost birth within all three natural births, and is not recognized except in the spirit of man; likewise, the outermost birth in the fruit cannot grasp or hold him, but He holds the outermost birth of the fruit and forms it.

## The Second Question:

### Why then is the earth so mountainous, stony, and uneven?

66. The mountains became so during the "rubbing together" <note>A reference to the chaotic friction during the Fall or the solidification of matter.</note>; for the corrupted <term>Salitter<note>Böhme’s term for a divine-physical substance, a "spiritual earth" or "saltpeter of the spirit," from which all material things are formed.</note></term> was more prevalent in one place than another, according to how the **Wheel of God** with its indwelling source-spirits was positioned.

67. In those places where the sweet water was **primary** <note>original: "Primus"</note> in the indwelling <meta>catchword: Wheel</meta>

<column-break/>

<page-num>241</page-num>
<header>Chap. 19. Morning Glow at Sunrise.</header>

**Wheel of God**, much earthly, tangible water was formed. But where the harsh quality in the bitterness in the <term>Mercurius<note>In Böhme's alchemy, "Mercurius" (Mercury) represents the active, stinging, or moving force within nature.</note></term> was primary, much earth and many stones were formed. Where the heat in the light was primary, much silver and gold was formed, along with several beautiful stones in the flash of the light; specifically, where **Love** in the light was primary, the noblest stones and the best gold were formed.

68. But as the "clump" of the earth pressed itself together, the water was squeezed out; however, where it was pressed in with the harsh quality among hard rocks, it is still in the earth and has since that time yielded and made several large holes for its passage.

69. In those places where great seas and lakes are found, the water was primary above that region; and because there was not much **Salitter** there, it became like a valley in the earth, and the water remained standing within it.

70. For the thin water seeks the valley and is a **humility** of life, which does not exalt itself as the harsh, bitter, and fire-qualities have done in the creatures of the devils.

71. Therefore, it always seeks out the lowest places on earth; this truly signifies the **spirit of gentleness**, in which life is born, as you can read regarding the creation of man and also earlier concerning his **kind** <note>original: "Species"</note>.

## Of Day and Night.

72. The entire **Godhead** with all powers and workings, together with its indwelling being—as well as its rising, penetrating, and changing—that is, the whole "working" or the whole "birthing," is all understood in the **Spirit of the Word**.

73. In whatever proportion or indwelling birth of the qualities the Spirit grasps and forms the Word and goes out with it, nature also has such an indwelling birth, penetration, rising, wrestling, and victory.

74. For when man fell into sin, he was placed out of the innermost birth into the other two; these soon surrounded him and <term>in-qualified<note>original: "inqualireten." 79. Because these words "Evening and Morning" run entirely contrary to philosophy and reason, it is to be held that Moses is not the original author of them; rather, they were brought down to him by his ancestors, who reckoned all six days of creation into one course and kept the creation since Adam only in a dark word, passing it on to their descendants.

80. For Evening and Morning did not exist before the time of the sun and stars, which were only certainly and truly created on the fourth day; I will prove this from a firm foundation when discussing the creation of the sun and stars.

81. But Day and Night did exist; that I will explain here according to my knowledge. You may once again open the eyes of your spirit wide if you wish to understand it; if not, you will be blind.

82. Just as this great work has remained hidden in man until this day, now (praise **God**) it finally wishes to become Day; for the Morning Glow <note>original: "Morgenröte," the title of the book, representing the dawn of divine enlightenment.</note> breaks forth. 105. Thus you see that the day existed before the time of the sun and stars; for when God said: Let there be Light, Gen. 1. v. 3. then the Light broke through the darkness, and the darkness did not comprehend it, but remained sitting in its seat <note>original: "Sede," referring to its position or foundation</note>.

106. You also see how the wrath of God lies hidden and rests in the outermost birth of nature, and cannot be awakened unless humans awaken it themselves—those who also, with their fleshly birth, <term>inqualify</term> with the wrath in the outermost birth of nature.

107. Therefore, if anyone were condemned to Hell, they must not say that God did it, or that He willed it; rather, the human awakens the fire of wrath within themselves. When this becomes burning, it thereafter <term>inqualifies</term> with God’s wrath and the hellish fire as one single thing.

108. When your Light is extinguished, you see in the darkness; and in the darkness, the wrath of God is hidden. When you awaken it, it burns in you.

109. There is also fire in a stone, but if one does not strike it, the fire remains hidden; but if one strikes it, the fire leaps out. If something is then present that is capable of receiving the fire, it burns and becomes a great fire: so it also happens with a human when they ignite the resting fire of wrath.

### Of the Night.

110. The word Night <note>German: "Nacht"</note> first forms itself in the heart, and the spirit grumbles with the harsh quality, yet it is not entirely comprehensible to the harsh quality; afterward, it forms itself on the tongue. But because it grumbles in the heart, the tongue closes the mouth meanwhile, until the spirit comes and forms itself on the tongue; then the tongue opens the mouth quickly and lets the spirit out.

He emphasizes that spiritual darkness and damnation are not divine punishments, but result from humans "awakening" the latent fire of wrath within their own nature.</summary>

111. The fact that the Word first takes hold in the heart and grunts <note>original: "grunzet." Böhme uses this visceral term to describe the primal, unformed sound associated with the "harsh" or "astringent" quality of nature before it is refined into clear speech.</note> with the harsh quality, signifies that the Holy Spirit took hold in the darkness over the heart of God in the sidereal birth <note>The "sidereal birth" refers to the astral or star-influenced level of existence, which Böhme sees as a bridge between the physical and the spiritual.</note> of the seven source spirits. But that He grunts with the harsh quality signifies that the darkness was a resistance against the Holy Spirit, which the Spirit bore with displeasure.

112. However, that He nevertheless goes through the dark street signifies that the Spirit also goes through the darkness (which is still in quiet rest) and gives birth to the light, provided that the darkness remains still and does not ignite the fire.

113. Here, the judging world—which seeks to condemn a person even in the mother’s womb—should rightly take notice. For such a world does not know whether the <term>Wrath-fire</term> <note>Böhme’s term for the harsh, consuming, and judgmental aspect of nature and divinity.</note> was fully ignited in the fruit by the parents or not; the Spirit of God also moves in the darkness that still stands at rest, and can certainly bring the light to birth out of that darkness. To this end, a person's hour of birth is very beneficial to them, and to some very harmful, yet it is not a matter of compulsion.

114. The fact that the mouth also closes when the Spirit takes hold over the heart, and the harsh quality grunts against and with it, signifies that the whole region or the whole <term>Place</term> <note>original: "Locus"</note> of this world was entirely dark in the sidereal and also in the outermost birth, and became light through the powerful outgoing of the Spirit.

115. But that the bitter spirit does not awaken while the Spirit passes through its <term>Place</term> <note>original: "Locum"</note> signifies the dark night in the outermost birth of this world, which has never grasped the light and will never grasp it in all eternity.

116. From this it follows that creatures see the sidereal light only with their eyes; otherwise, if the darkness were not still in the outermost birth, the sidereal spirit could see through wood and stones, as well as through the entire earth, and would be hindered by nothing, just as it is in heaven.

117. But now the darkness is separated from the light and remains in the outermost birth; therein the Wrath of God rests until the Last Day. Then the Wrath will be ignited, and the darkness will be the house of eternal perdition. Therein Lord Lucifer, with all godless people who have sown into the darkness in the <term>Wrath-field</term> <note>original: "Zornacker." A metaphor for a life lived in accordance with anger, greed, and spiritual darkness.</note>, shall have their eternal dwelling.

118. The sidereal birth, however, in which the natural light now stands and in which the holy birth is born, will also be ignited at the end of this time. Then the Wrath and the holy birth will separate from one another, for the Wrath will not be able to comprehend the holy birth.

119. But the Wrath in the sidereal birth will be given as a life to the house of darkness, and the Wrath will be called the hellish fire. The house of darkness, which is the outermost birth, will be called Death, and King Lucifer will be God therein, and his angels with all damned people will be his servants.

120. In this abyss, all kinds of hellish fruit and formations will then arise, all according to the hellish quality and kind, just as in heaven there are Heavenly things, according to the heavenly quality and kind.

121. Thus you can understand what the creation of Heaven and Earth signifies and is, and what God made on the first day; although the first three days were not divided by evening and morning, but rather one period was counted as twenty-four hours, just as there is one time and day in the heights above the moon.

122. Secondly, it is also counted as a human day because, without doubt, the globe of the earth immediately began its rotation and, in such a time—while God separated the light from the darkness—it turned itself once and performed its course for the first time.

# The 20th Chapter.
## Concerning the Second Day.

1. Concerning the second day, it stands written: And God said: Let there be a firmament <note>original: "Feste"</note> between the waters, and let it be a distinction between the waters. Then God made the firmament, and divided the water under the firmament from the water above the firmament, and it happened so, and God called the firmament, Heaven; then from evening and morning the second day came to be. <note>Genesis 1:6, 7, 8.</note>

<summary>Böhme explains the metaphysical separation of light and darkness within creation, warning of the eventual total separation of the "Wrath-fire" from the "Holy Birth" at the end of time. He then begins an interpretation of the second day of Genesis, focusing on the creation of the firmament.</summary>

2. This description indicates once again that the dear man Moses was not the author of it <note>original: "Autor darzu sey." Böhme often suggests that while Moses received the revelation, the specific wording of Genesis was influenced by later, perhaps less enlightened, editors, or that the true spiritual meaning was veiled.</note>, for it is written quite ignorantly and simply, although it nevertheless possesses quite excellent understanding.

3. Without a doubt, the Holy Spirit did not wish to reveal such things, so that the Devil would not know all the secrets in the Creation. For he himself (the Devil) does not know the creation of light, or how the heaven was made out of the midst of the water.

4. For he can neither see nor comprehend the light and the **holy birthing** <note>original: "heilige Gebärung." This refers to the divine process of generation within the Godhead and nature.</note> which stands in the water of heaven; he can only see the birthing which stands in the harsh, bitter, sour, and hot quality, from which the outermost birth has arisen—that is his royal castle.

5. This is not to be understood as if he had no power in the elemental water to possess it; for the outermost corrupted birth in the elemental water also belongs to the <term>Wrath of God</term> <note>Böhme views "Wrath" as a fundamental quality of nature that has become "ignited" or unbalanced by the fall of Lucifer.</note>, and death is within it, just as it is in the earth.

6. However, the Spirit in Moses means a much different water here, which the Devil can neither understand nor comprehend. If it had been explained for such a long time, the Devil would have learned it from humanity and would, without a doubt, have scattered his hellish chaff into it as well.

7. Therefore, the Holy Spirit kept it hidden until the last hour before evening, when his thousand years are completed, when he shall be set loose again for a short time, as can be read in the Revelation. (Rev. ch. 20 verse 3).

> “again, but the sun will shine warm even
> “before then.”]

8. But because he is now loosed from the chains of darkness, God allows lights to be lit everywhere in this world, so that people may learn to know him and guard themselves against him.

9. Whether or not he is loose, I leave for everyone to recognize; just look at the world by this bright light, and you will find that now all four new sons whom the Devil birthed when he was cast out of heaven are ruling the world: namely 1. **Pride**, 2. **Greed**, 3. **Envy**, 4. **Wrath**: These rule the world now, and are the heart of the Devil, his animalistic spirits.

10. Therefore, only look rightly at the world, and you will find—

19. Therefore I say now, if your heart in your knowledge does not <term>interact</term> <note>original: "inqualiret." A term Böhme coined from the Latin "in" and "qualitas" to describe how different qualities or powers work together, permeate, and influence one another.</note> with God out of a true purpose of love, then you are a hypocrite, liar, and murderer before God; for God hears no one's prayer unless the heart then directs itself in total obedience into God.

20. If you wish to fight against the **Wrath of God**, then you must put on the helmet of obedience and love; otherwise, you will not break through. If you do not break through, then your struggle is in vain, and you remain a servant of the Devil just as much as any other.

21. What does your knowledge <note>original: "Wissenschaft." Who will judge them, when their heart <term>interacts</term> with God? Even if they do not know Him, yet they work in His Spirit in righteousness and the purity of their heart, in true love toward one another; these truly testify that the law of God is in their hearts. (Romans 2:15)

23. But because you know it and do it not, while those others do not know it and yet do it, they judge your knowledge with their actions, and you are found to be a hypocrite—a useless servant who is placed in the Lord's vineyard and will not work in it.

->Now observe.<-

26. Now, if one wishes to rightly consider how God separated the water under the firmament from the water above the firmament, very great things are found here. For the water that rests on earth is a corrupted and deadly essence, just like the earth; it also belongs to the outermost **birth** <note>original: "Geburt." Böhme uses this to describe a realm of existence or a specific state of being produced by the divine "birthing" process of nature.</note>, which stands in death with its tangibility, just like the earth and stones.

Derived from the Latin "sidereus" (starry). 29. Behold, the water in the deep above the earth, which <term>interacts</term> with the elements of air and fire, that is the water of the <term>sidereal</term> birth, in which the **sidereal life** stands, and in which primarily the Holy Spirit moves; through this, it also brings forth the third and innermost birth, which is incomprehensible to the **Wrath of God** within it. This same water is also like air to our eyes.

30. That there is truly water and air and fire within one another in the deep above the earth can be seen and understood by every sensible person.

31. For you often see the entire deep [the sky] quite bright and clear, and in a quarter of an hour it is covered with water-clouds.

32. That is, when the stars from above and the water on earth from below ignite, then water is immediately birthed—which would certainly not happen if the **Wrath** did not also stand in the <term>sidereal</term> birth.

33. 34. But that the element of fire also rules and exists in the depths of air and water, you can see in the lightning; you also see how the light of the sun ignites the element of fire on the earth with its impact, even though it is sometimes very cold high up in the moon's orbit.

35. But now God has separated the tangible <note>original: "begreifliche," meaning that which can be grasped or physically sensed.</note> water from the intangible, and has placed the tangible upon the earth, and the intangible remained in the depths in its own seat, as it has been from eternity.

Böhme uses this term to describe the divine "saltpeter" or the fundamental chemical/spiritual matter of the universe.</note> of the corrupted earth and extinguishes its wrath, so that in the sidereal birth everything stands in life, and the earth bears life through death.

### The Portals of Mystery.

38. But that there is a firmament <note>original: "Feste," referring to the expanse or firmament of Genesis.</note> between the waters, which is called Heaven, has this meaning:

39. The entire depth from the moon down to the earth stands with all its effects in the wrathful and tangible birth, for the moon is a goddess of tangible birth; likewise, the house of the Devil, death, and hell is in the territory and circle between the moon and the earth.

40. There, the fierce wrath of God in the outermost birth in the depths is daily ignited and blown up by devils and all godless people through the great sins of mankind, which still <term>interpenetrate</term> with the sidereal birth in the depths.

41. Now God has made the firmament, which is called Heaven, between the outermost and innermost birth, and it is a distinction between the outermost and innermost birth.

42. For the outermost birth of the water cannot grasp the innermost

46. It is the firmament between the clear Godhead and corrupted nature, through which you must break if you want to come to God. ## The Gates of the Godhead.

Observe now the hidden mystery of God.

49. When you look upon the deep above the earth, you must not say: "The gates of God are not here, where God dwells in His holiness." No, no, do not think so; rather, the entire Holy Trinity—God the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit—dwells in the center beneath the firmament of heaven, and that same firmament cannot contain Him.

50. It is all indeed one *body* <note>original: "Corpus"</note>—the outermost birth as well as the innermost, together with the firmament of heaven, as well as the sidereal birth within it, in which the wrath of God is also present <note>original: "qualificiret," meaning to share in the qualities or nature of something</note>. However, they stand against one another, much like the governance within a human being.

51. The flesh signifies the 1st, or outermost birth, which is the house of death. The 2nd birth in man is the <term>sidereal</term> <note>From "sidereal," meaning relating to the stars. Böhme refers to the astral or psychological influence of the heavens on the human spirit.</note>, in which life stands, and where love and wrath struggle with one another.

52. And this is as far as man knows himself, for the sidereal birth brings forth life within the outermost birth—that is, within the dead flesh.

53. The 3rd birth is born between the sidereal and the outermost, and this is called the <term>animal</term> <note>From the Latin "anima," meaning soul. Böhme is referring to the "soul-life" or the living breath, not "animalistic" in a modern derogatory sense.</note> or the Soul, and it is as large as the whole man. This birth is not understood or grasped by the external man, nor is it grasped by the sidereal man; rather, each <term>source-spirit</term> <note>original: "Quellgeist." Böhme's term for the fundamental forces or "qualities" of divine and natural being.</note> only grasps its own internal root, which signifies heaven.

54. And this same "animal man" must penetrate through the firmament of heaven to God and live with God; otherwise, the whole man cannot come to God in heaven.

55. For every person who wishes to be saved must be, with their internal births, like the whole Godhead with all three births in this world.

56. A man cannot be entirely pure without wrath and sin, for the births in the depths of this world are also not entirely pure before the heart of God (Job 15:15). Instead, love and wrath always wrestle with each other, which is why God calls Himself an angry, jealous God (Exodus 20:5, Deuteronomy 5:9).

57. Now, as man is in the governance of his birth, so also is the whole Body of God in this world; but in the water

<meta>catchword: but</meta>

<column-break/>

<page-num>257</page-num>
<header>Chap. 20. Morning Glow at Sunrise.</header>

but in the water stands the gentle life. Firstly, in the external Body of God in this world, there is the numbed, harsh, bitter, and heated death, in which the tangible water is also numbed and dead.

58. And within this now is the darkness, where King Lucifer with his angels, as well as all fleshly, godless people while still in their living bodies, lie captive; and likewise the departed spirits of damned people.

59. The Heart of God can neither see, hear, feel, smell, nor grasp this birth; it is a "foolish woman" <note>original: "Närrin." Böhme often personifies the corrupted material nature or the lack of divine wisdom as a fool.</note> whom King Lucifer has prepared in this way through his pride.

60. The other birth is the sidereal. You must understand this as the life of the source-spirits; within it, love and wrath are set against each other. In this birth stands the "upper water," which is a spirit of life, and within it or between it is the firmament of heaven, which is made from the midst of the water.

61. This birth now penetrates through the external, numbed birth—straight through death—and brings forth the sidereal life in death. That is, it brings life into the numbed earth, water, and the flesh of animals and men, as well as birds, fish, and worms.

62. And the devil can reach halfway into this birth—as far as the wrath extends—but no deeper; that is the extent of his dwelling. He can go no deeper, and therefore the devil cannot know how the other part of this birth has its root.

63. And up to this point, man has come in his knowledge of the world since his Fall. The other root, which is called Heaven, the Spirit has kept hidden from man until now, so that the devil might not learn it from man and scatter poison into it before man’s very eyes.

64. This other part of the sidereal birth, which stands in love in the sweet water, is now the firmament of heaven, which keeps the ignited wrath captive along with all the devils. For they cannot enter into it. In this heaven dwells the Holy Spirit, who proceeds from the Heart of God and fights against the <term>fierceness</term> <note>original: "Grimmigkeit," often translated as "wrath" or "fury." It refers to the harsh, burning quality of existence apart from God's light.</note>, building Himself a temple in the midst of the fierceness of God’s wrath.

65. And in this heaven dwells the man who fears God, even while still in his living body; for that same heaven is within man just as it is in the deep above the earth. And as the deep is above the earth, so too is man both in love and wrath, until the departure of the soul. Then, when the soul departs from the body, it remains alone either in the heaven of love or in the heaven of wrath.

He explains that "Heaven" acts as a protective firmament separating the divine life from the "wrath" and "darkness" where Lucifer is imprisoned.</summary>

66. Whatever state a person has embraced here at their departure, that is now their eternal, indissoluble dwelling-place, and they can never come out of it; for there is a great gulf between them, as Christ says regarding the rich man in Luke 16:26 <note>original: "Luc. 16. 26."</note>.

67. And in this heaven, the holy angels dwell with us, while in the other part, the devils dwell; and in this heaven, man lives between heaven and hell, and must suffer many a hard blow, temptation, and persecution from the <term>Wrath</term> <note>original: "Grimme," referring to the dark, fierce quality of nature that opposes God's light</note>, and must sometimes let himself be truly martyred and squeezed.

68. The Wrath is called the Cross, and the dear heaven is called Patience; and the spirit rising therein is called Hope and Faith, which <term>shares the qualities</term> <note>original: "inqualiret," a term Böhme uses to describe how different forces or spirits mingle and act upon one another</note> of God, and wrestles with the Wrath until it triumphs and overcomes, as in 1 John 5:4.

69. And herein lies the whole of Christian teaching; whoever teaches otherwise does not know what they are teaching, for their teaching has no foot or foundation, and their heart always flutters and laments, not knowing what it should do.

70. For such a spirit always seeks rest and finds it not; then it is impatient and always seeks something new, and when it finds it, it titillates itself in it as if it had found a new treasure—and yet there is no constancy in it, but it is always seeking abstinence.

71. You theologians, the Spirit here opens door and gate for you; if you will now choose not to see, and if you lead your little sheep to graze on dry moors instead of green pastures, you shall have to answer for that before the earnest and wrathful judgment of God; so take heed.

72. I take heaven as my witness that I am performing here what I must do; for the Spirit drives me to it, so that I am also completely captured by Him and cannot defend myself against Him, regardless of what might happen to me hereafter.

### The Holy Gates.

73. The third birth in the Body of God of this world is hidden under the <term>firmament of heaven</term> <note>original: "Festen des Himmels"</note>, and the firmament of heaven shares its qualities with it, yet not entirely in a physical way, but rather in a creaturely way, just like the angels and the soul of man.

74. And that same third birth is the almighty and holy Heart of God; within it sits our King, Jesus Christ, with His natural body at the right hand of God, as a King

and Lord of the whole body or <term>space</term> <note>original: "Loci," from Latin *Locus*</note> of this world, who encompasses and holds everything with His Heart.

75. And that same firmament of heaven is His throne, and the <term>source-spirits</term> <note>original: "Quellgeister," the fundamental forces of Böhme's cosmology</note> of His natural body rule in the whole body of this world; and everything is connected with them that stands in the <term>sidereal birth</term> <note>the level of existence influenced by the stars and psychological forces</note> within the part of Love; the other part of this world is connected with the devil.

76. You must not think as John Calvin <note>original: "Johannes Calvus oder Calvinus"</note> thought: that the body of Christ is an un-almighty being and encompasses no more than the physical space it occupies.

77. No, child of man, you are wandering in error and do not rightly understand the divine power; for does not every man encompass the whole space or body of this world in his sidereal source-spirits? And the space encompasses the man; it is all one body, only different members.

78. How then should the source-spirits in the natural body of Christ not <term>interact</term> <note>original: "inqualiren"</note> with the source-spirits of Nature? For His body is also made from the source-spirits of Nature, and His heart is <term>soulish</term> <note>original: "Animalisch," from the Latin *anima*, meaning soul</note> from the third birth, which is the Heart of God, which encompasses all angels and the heaven of all heavens—yes, the whole Father.

79. You Calvinists, turn away from your opinion; you are in error. Do not torment yourselves with the idea of tangible substance, for "God is a Spirit" (John 4:24), and death resides in hard tangibility <note>original: "Begreiflichkeit," meaning the state of being graspable or material</note>.

80. The body of Christ is no longer in hard tangibility, but in the divine tangibility of Nature, like the angels.

81. Our bodies also will not consist of such hard flesh and bones in the resurrection, but will be like the angels; and although every form and power will be within them—even every skill, down to the reproductive members (though they will exist in another form), as well as the internal organs—we will nevertheless not have that hard tangibility.

82. For Christ said to Mary Magdalene in Joseph’s garden by the grave after His resurrection: "Touch me not, for I am not yet ascended to my God and to your God" (John 20:17). It was as if He wanted to say: "I no longer have the <term>animal body</term> <note>original: "thierischen Leib," referring to the physical, biological body of the fallen world</note>, and though I show myself to you in my old form, otherwise you could not see me in your animal body."

83. Likewise, during the forty days after his resurrection, he did not always walk visibly among the disciples, but rather invisibly according to his heavenly and angelic property. However, when he wished to speak with the disciples, he revealed himself in a tangible form so that he could speak natural words with them, for that which is corrupted <note>referring to fallen human nature</note> cannot comprehend the divine.

84. This also sufficiently demonstrates that his body possesses an angelic nature, in that he came to his disciples through locked doors, <term>John 20:19</term>.

85. Thus, you should now know that his body <term>shares the qualities</term> <note>original: "inqualiret," Böhme's term for the way spiritual forces mingle and act together</note> of all seven spirits in nature within the sidereal <note>astral or star-influenced</note> birth in the part of Love; he holds sin, death, and the devil captive in his part of Wrath.

86. So you now understand what GOD did on the second day when he separated the water beneath the firmament from the water above the firmament. You also see how you are everywhere in this world in heaven and also in hell, and that you dwell between heaven and hell in great danger.

87. You also see how heaven is within a holy person; wherever you stand or walk or lie, if your spirit only <term>shares the qualities</term> of God, then you are in heaven according to that part, and your soul is in God. Therefore Christ also says: "My sheep are in my hands, and no one will snatch them from me," <term>John 10</term>.

88. Likewise, you see how, according to the Wrath, you are always in hell among all the devils. If your eyes were only opened, you would see wonders; but you stand between heaven and hell, and can see neither, walking as if upon a very narrow bridge.

89. At certain hours, some people have been "stepped back" <note>translated from "hinentritten," suggesting a visionary state or being transported</note> according to their sidereal spirit, and they immediately recognized the gates of heaven and hell. They also pointed out how many a person dwells in hell even while in their living body. These people were indeed mocked, but with great lack of understanding; for it is truly so. I will also describe this in detail in its proper place—what kind of form he <note>the visionary</note> has with them.

# The 21st Chapter.
## Concerning the Third Day.

1. Although the Spirit in the writings of Moses has kept the deepest mysteries hidden within the literal letter, everything is nevertheless described so very orderly that there is no lack in the arrangement.
2. For when God created Heaven and Earth through the Word, and separated the light from the darkness, and gave each thing its <term>place</term> <note>original: "Sedem," from Latin "sedes," meaning seat or position</note>, each immediately began its own birth and <term>interaction</term> <note>original: "Qualificirung"</note>.
3. On the first day, God drove together the corrupted <term>Salitter</term> <note>Böhme’s term for the fundamental "divine sap" or substance of the universe, which here has been tainted by the fall of angels</note>, which arose in the ignition of His wrath, or rather created it through the powerful Spirit; for the word "Created" <note>original: "Schuf"</note> here signifies a "gathering together."
4. In this gathering together of the corrupted Wrath-<term>Salitter</term>, King Lucifer was also driven—as a powerless prince, along with his angels—into the hollow of the Wrath-<term>Salitter</term>, into the <term>place</term> <note>original: "Locum"</note> where the outward, half-dead tangibility is born, which is the space between the Goddess of Nature (the Moon) and the dead Earth.
5. When this had occurred, the deep became bright, and the light separated from the darkness within the hidden Heaven, and the sphere of the Earth turned once within the great wheel of Nature; and herewith

Böhme describes humanity as the "heart" of the earth, originally intended to transcend nature's harshness, but now caught in a struggle between heavenly love and hellish wrath.</summary>

Instead, where you have sown your seed—that is, your soul—in that same part shall the body also arise.

## The Gates of Power.

50. That the body and soul shall find each other again on the day of resurrection, you can see here in the birth of the earth. For the Creator said: "Let the earth bring forth grass, herbs, and fruitful trees, each according to its kind." Then each came forth according to its kind and grew green; and just as it had possessed a heavenly body before the time of the Wrath, so it now received an earthly one according to its mother <note>the material earth</note>.

51. But it is important to consider how everything was enclosed within the Word during the great uprising of the Devil, so that everything came forth in its own essence according to its power and kind, as if it had never been destroyed, but only changed.

52. If this happened at that time, when such murdering and robbing took place <note>referring to the fall of Lucifer</note>, then it will happen much more so on the Last Day. When the earth separates itself in the ignited fire of wrath and becomes alive again, it will certainly be enclosed within the Word of love, just as it has borne its fruit here in that same Word—the grass, herbs, and trees, as well as all kinds of ore, silver, and gold.

53. But because the sidereal birth of the earth stands in love, and the external birth stands in death, each shall remain in its <term>seat</term> <note>original: "Sede," from Latin *sedes*, meaning place or position</note>, and life and death shall separate.

54. Now, where would the soul of a human want to be on the day of rebirth rather than in its father—that is, in the body that bore it?

55. Because the soul remained hidden in the Word during the time the body was in death, and that same Word also preserves the body in its sidereal birth in love, it <term>inter-acts</term> <note>original: "inqualiret," Böhme’s term for different forces or qualities blending and working together</note> through the Word during the time of its concealment with its mother

## The Open Gates of the Earth.

### Now one might ask:

> From what kind of matter or power did the grass,
> herbs, and trees come forth? What is the
> substance and condition of this creation?

58. The simple person says: "GOD made everything out of nothing." But he does not know that same GOD and does not know what He is. When he looks at the earth, along with the depths above the earth, he thinks: "That is not GOD," or "GOD is not there." He always imagines that GOD dwells alone above the blue sky or the stars and governs this world perhaps with a spirit that goes out from Him, but that His <term>body</term> <note>original Latin: "Corpus"</note> is not present here on earth or in the earth.

59. I have also read such opinions in the books and writings of the <term>doctors</term> <note>meaning university-educated theologians or scholars</note>, and that is precisely why so many different opinions and quarrels have arisen among the learned.

60. But because GOD, in His great love, opens the gates of His being to me and remembers the covenant He has with humanity, I will faithfully and earnestly open and unlock all the gates of GOD according to my gifts, as far as GOD allows me.

He critiques the idea that God is distant or "above the stars," asserting instead that the divine presence permeates all of creation.</summary>

61. This is not to be understood as if I were powerful enough in these things, but rather as much as I am able to grasp. For the essence of GOD is like a wheel, where many wheels are crossed within one another, made into one another above and below, and always turning with one another. While one sees the wheel and is greatly amazed, yet one cannot learn or grasp its turning all at once; rather, the more one looks at the wheel, the more one learns of its form, and the more one learns, the greater delight one has in the wheel, for one always sees something more wonderful, and a person can never see or learn enough.

62. So also with me; what I do not describe enough in one place regarding this great mystery, you shall find in another; and what I cannot describe in this book because of the length and my own inability to grasp it, you shall find in the others that follow.

63. For this book is the first growth of this <term>little branch</term> <note>Böhme often refers to his own writings as a small branch or sprout of divine wisdom</note> which greens within its mother, just like a child who is learning to walk and cannot yet run very fast.

64. For although the spirit sees the wheel and wants to grasp its form in every place, it cannot do so sufficiently because of the wheel’s turning. But when the wheel comes around again, so that the spirit sees its first conceived form once more, it always learns something more, and becomes ever more favorable toward the wheel, and loves it.

But if you break through in the spirit through the death of the flesh, then you see the hidden GOD. Just as the marrow in the bones breaks through and gives the flesh power and strength, yet the flesh cannot grasp the marrow, but only its power—so also you cannot see the hidden Godhead in the flesh, but you receive its power, and you understand therein that GOD dwells within you.

### Of the Seven Spirits of GOD and Their Activity in the Earth.

73. First, there is the **astringent** <note>original: "herbe," the harsh, contracting force in Böhme’s system</note> spirit. Within the <term>sidereal</term> <note>relating to the stars or astral influences</note> birth of the seven source-spirits, it draws a mass <note>original: "Massam"</note> together in the Earth through the ignition of the "upper birth" above the Earth, and dries it out with its sharp coldness. Just as it draws water together and makes ice from it, so it also draws the water in the Earth together and makes a dry mass from it.

74. After this, there is the **bitter** spirit, which arises in the "flash of fire." This spirit also exists in the matter or mass; it cannot endure being imprisoned in that which is dried out, but rather it rubs itself against the astringent spirit within the dried mass until it ignites the fire. Now, when this happens, the bitter spirit is terrified and gains its life.

->Understand this rightly here.<-

75. In the Earth, apart from herbs or metals, you can perceive or find nothing but the astringent, the bitter, and water. But the water within it is **sweet**, which is entirely contrary to the other two.

76. Furthermore, it is thin, while the other two are hard, rough, and bitter, and one is always against the other. Therefore, there is a constant choking, struggling, and wrestling; but life does not yet exist in the choking of these three. Instead, they are a valley of darkness; they are three things that never agree with one another, but are in an eternal struggle among themselves.

77. And from this, mobility takes its origin. Likewise, God’s Wrath—which rests in the hiddenness—takes its origin from this. The origin of the Devil, of Death, and of Hell also arose from this, as you can read earlier regarding the Fall of the Devil.

### The Depth in the Center of Birth.

78. Now, when these three things—the astringent, the bitter, and the sweet—rub against one another, the astringent quality becomes the *Primary* <note>original: "Primus," the first or dominant force</note>, for it is the strongest. It violently constricts the sweet; for the sweet is gentle and expansive because of its softness, and it must allow itself to be taken captive.

79. When this happens, the bitter quality is also captured within the body of the sweet water and is dried out along with it. Then the astringent, the sweet, and the bitter are inside one another, and they struggle so severely within the dried mass until the mass becomes dry, for the astringent quality draws it ever more tightly together.

80. But when the sweet water can no longer defend itself, **anxiety** <note>original: "Angst," which for Böhme implies a physical narrowing or "squeezing" during birth</note> rises within it, just as it does in a person when they die, when the spirit departs from the body and the body gives itself up to death; so the water gives itself up.

81. And in that rising anxiety, an "anxiety-heat" is born, through which a sweat presses out, just as it does through a dying person. And this same sweat <term>interacts</term> <note>original: "inqualiret," a term meaning to work or qualify together as one essence</note> with the astringent and bitter qualities; for it is their son, whom they have birthed from the sweet water after they murdered it and brought it to death.

82. When this happens, the astringent and bitter qualities rejoice in the son—understand, in the sweat—and each gives him its power and life. They feed upon him like a greedy piglet, so that they soon raise him to be large. For the astringent quality, as well as the bitter, constantly draws the sap out of the Earth and fills the young son with it.

83. But the body that was first drawn together from the sweet water remains dead. Now the sweat of the body, which <term>interacts</term> with the astringent and bitter qualities, possesses the house; it spreads out there and becomes large, fat, and vigorous.

84. But now the two qualities, the astringent and the bitter, cannot leave off their quarreling and ill-will, but they wrestle constantly with one another. The astringent is strong, while the bitter is swift.

85. Whenever the astringent reaches for the bitter, the bitter leaps aside and takes the son’s sap with it; then the astringent presses after it everywhere and seeks to take it captive.

<summary>Böhme describes the "mechanical" birth of material life through the violent interaction of three qualities: the astringent, the bitter, and the sweet. He explains how physical matter is formed when these forces "choke" and "murder" the sweet water, resulting in a "sweat" that becomes the new living body or substance.</summary>

## Now you might say:

# How can God be in this birth?

88. Behold, this is the birth of nature. If the ignited "Wrath-fire" <note>the destructive or "dark" side of divine energy</note> were not present in these three qualities—the astringent, the bitter, and the sweet—you would clearly see where God is.

89. But now the Wrath-fire is in all three; for the astringent is far too cold and contracts the body far too hard; the sweet is far too thick and dark, which the astringent soon seizes, holding it captive and drying it out too much; and the bitter is far too prickly, murderous, and raging. Thus, they cannot become one in this matter.

90. Otherwise, if the astringent were not so hard and ignited in the cold fire, and the water were not so thick, and the bitter were not so elevated and murderous, they could ignite the fire from which the **Light** would arise, and from the Light would come **Love**, and from the "fire-flash" <note>original: "Feuer-Bliß"</note> would come the **Sound** <note>original: "Thon," referring to the divine harmony or voice</note>. Then you would see clearly whether a heavenly body would not be there, in which the light of God would shine.

91. But because the astringent is too cold and dries the water out too much, it captures the hot fire within its coldness and murders the body of the sweet water; it also captures the bitter quality and dries it out as well.

92. In this drying out, the "fatness" <note>original: "das Fette," referring to the essential oil or life-fuel</note> in the sweet water is murdered, which is where the fire would normally ignite. From that same fatness, a harsh and bitter spirit is formed. For when the fatness in the sweet water dies, it transforms into a **sweat of anguish** <note>original: "Angstschweiß," a central Böhmean term for the tension in material existence</note>, in which the astringent and bitter qualities interact <note>original: "inqualiren," a term Böhme coined to describe qualities working within one another</note>.

93. It is not meant that the water dies entirely:

<meta>Catchword: No</meta>

<column-break/>

No, that cannot be; rather, the astringent spirit captures the sweetness or the fatness of the water in its cold fire, interacts with it, and uses it for its own spirit.

94. For its spirit is completely stiffened and in death; therefore it uses the water for its life, drawing out its fatness and taking away its power.

95. Then the water becomes a sweat of anguish, which stands between death and life, and the fire of heat cannot ignite itself. For the fatness is captured in the cold fire, and the whole body remains a "dark valley," which stands in an anxious birth and cannot grasp life.

96. For the life which stands in the Light cannot rise up in the hard, bitter, and astringent body, because it is captured in the cold fire—though it is not entirely dead.

97. You see that all of this is true: take a root that possesses the quality of heat and place it in warm water, or take it into your mouth to make it warm and moist; you will soon see its life and how it begins to operate and work. But while it is outside of heat, it is captured in death and is cold like any other root or piece of wood.

98. Thus you also see that the body of the root is dead; for when the power is out of the root, the body is a dead carcass <note>original: "Aß"</note> and can work nothing. This happens because the astringent and bitter spirits have murdered the body of the water, drawn the fatness to themselves, and expressed their own spirit in the dead body.

99. Otherwise, if the sweet water could keep its fatness in its own power, and if the astringent and bitter spirits rubbed against each other gently within the sweet water, they would ignite the fatness in the sweet water. Immediately, the **Light** would be born in the water and would illuminate the astringent and bitter qualities.

100. From this, they would receive their true life and would be satisfied by the Light, rejoicing greatly within it. From that same living joy, **Love** would arise, and in the fire-flash—through the ascending of the bitter quality within the astringent—the **Sound** would elevate itself. If that were to happen, it would be a heavenly fruit, such as grows in Heaven.

101. But you should know that the earth [contains] all seven source-spirits...

102. The first three—namely the **astringent**, **sweet**, and **bitter**—belong to the formation of the **Body** <note>original: "Corpus"</note>, and within them reside movement and the physical frame. These possess tangibility and are the "birth" or manifestation of the outermost nature.

103. The other three—namely **Heat**, **Love**, and **Sound** <note>original: "Thon," referring to the divine resonance or tone</note>—exist in intangibility and are born from the first three. This is the inward birth, with which the Deity <term>inqualiret</term> <note>a term Böhme coined to describe how God’s qualities intermingle and operate within nature</note>.

104. Now, if the first three were not frozen in death so that they could ignite the heat, you would quickly see a bright, heavenly body, and you would clearly see where God is.

105. But because the first three qualities of the Earth are frozen in death, they remain a "death," and cannot raise their life into the light. Instead, they remain a dark valley in which God's wrath, death, and hell reside, as well as the eternal imprisonment and torment of the Devil.

106. These three qualities from the outermost birth (in which the "Wrath-fire" resides) are not rejected all the way to the innermost core; rather, only the external, tangible body is rejected, and within it, the external hellish torment.

107. Here you see once again how the kingdoms of God and Hell are joined together like one body, and yet one cannot grasp the other. For the second birth—consisting of heat, light, love, and sound—is hidden within the outermost one. It makes the external birth movable, so that the external gathers itself together and gives birth to a physical body.

108. Even though the body exists in external tangibility, it is nonetheless formed according to the manner of the inner birth. For in the inner birth stands the **Word**, and the Word is the **Sound**, which rises up in the flash of fire within the light through the bitter and astringent qualities.

109. But because the sound of the Word of God must rise through the astringent, bitter death, and give birth to a body in the "half-dead" water, that same body becomes both evil and good, dead and alive. For it must quickly draw into itself the sap of **fierceness** <note>original: "Grimmigkeit," the harsh, wrathful aspect of nature</note> and the body of death, and exist in such a body and power as the Earth, its mother.

110. Now, I will prove to you that life lies hidden under and within the death of the Earth, as well as in the "children of the Earth" <note>living creatures and plants</note>.

111. Behold, a person becomes sickly and ill; and if he is not helped, he falls into death through a bitter and astringent herb that grows from the earth, or through a foul, deadly water, or various plants of the earth, or even through foul meat or the loathing of it.

112. But if there is a wise physician, he investigates the patient to see how the harm arose. He takes the same causes of the sickness—be it meat, herb, or water—and distills it or burns it into a powder (whichever method suits the material) and burns away the "outermost spirit" which exists in death. What remains afterward in the water or powder is the <term>sidereal birth</term> <note>from "sidereal," meaning relating to the stars; in Böhme’s time, this referred to the astral or life-giving forces hidden within matter</note> in its seat, where life and death struggle with one another. Both are elevated there, for the dead body has been removed.

113. If you now take a good <term>Theriac</term> <note>an ancient "universal" herbal medicine or antidote</note> or similar substance with this water or powder—to hold captive the rising power of the "wrath" within that sidereal birth—and give it to the sick person in a slightly warm drink, like beer or wine, then the innermost and hidden birth of the substance (which caused the person's sickness through its outermost dead birth) begins to operate.

114. For when it is placed into warm moisture, the life within the substance begins to rise; it would dearly love to elevate itself and ignite in the light, but it cannot because of the "wrath" that opposes it in the sidereal birth.

115. Yet it can do this much: it takes away the person's sickness. For the sidereal life rises through the death and takes away the power from the "sting of death." When it triumphs, the person becomes healthy again.

116. Thus you see how the power of the Word and eternal life lies hidden in the "Center" <note>original: "Centro," the spiritual core</note> within death in the Earth and its children. It greens through death—though death cannot comprehend it—and it always struggles toward the birth of the light. Yet it cannot fully bloom until death is separated from it.

117. It has its life in its seat, and it cannot be taken away; but death clings to it in the outermost birth, as does the wrath within death—for wrath is the life of death and the Devil. And within the wrath also stands the corpor-

### The Depth in the Circle of Birth.

->Now one might ask:<-

How is it then that a *substance* and opportunity exists for this, so that the sidereal <note>pertaining to the stars or the celestial influences on the physical world</note> birth of the Earth has its *qualification* and birthing? Why did it begin one day earlier than the sidereal birth in the depth above the Earth, since the fire in the depth above the Earth is much sharper and more ignitable than the fire in the Earth? And must the Earth not also be ignited by the fire in the depth above the Earth, if she is to bring forth fruit?

118. Look, you understanding spirit, the Spirit speaks with you and not with the dead spirit of the flesh: throw open the door of your sidereal birth wide, and lift one part of the sidereal birth into the light, and let the other remain in wrath; and see to it that your animal birth <term>inqualifies</term> <note>original: "inqualire"; Böhme's term for the active intermingling of spiritual qualities where one thing operates within another</note> completely with the light.

119. If you now stand in such a form, then you are like heaven and earth, or like the entire Godhead with its births in this world. But if you are not thus, then you are blind here, even if you are the cleverest *doctor* <note>original: "Doctor"; here meaning a highly learned scholar or theologian</note> who might be found in the world.

120. If you are so, then lift up your spirit and look through your astrological art, deep sense, and circular measurements. If you cannot grasp it there, it must be born **within you**, otherwise you will grasp neither favor nor art.

121. Should the eyes of your spirit stand open, you must give birth in this way; otherwise your capacity to grasp is a fool’s errand, and it happens to you just as when a painter paints the Godhead on an *epitaph* <note>original: "Epitaphium"; a commemorative tablet or painting</note> and says he has done it rightly, that it is thus. So it happens to the believer and the painter, one like the other, and yet both see nothing but wood and colors, and one blind man touches the other. Truly, you must fight here not with beasts, but with gods.

->Now observe.<-

122. When the entire Godhead moved toward creation in this world, not just one part moved while the other rested; rather, everything stood simultaneously in movement: the entire depth, as far as Lord Lucifer had been a king, as far as the *place* <note>original: "Locus"</note> of his kingdom reached, and as far as the Salitter <term>Salitter</term> <note>Böhme uses this term to describe the fundamental divine "saltpeter" or the "matter" of the spiritual world</note> was ignited in the fire of wrath.

123. The movement of the three births lasted six days and nights, during which all seven source-spirits of God stood in full, moving birth, as did the heart of the spirits; and the Salitter of the Earth turned six times within the great wheel during this time. This wheel consists of the seven source-spirits of God, and in every turn a special work was born according to the source-spirits present.

124. For the first source-spirit is the tart, cold, sharp, and hard birth, and it belongs to the first day; in the sidereal birth, the *astrologers* <note>original: "Astrologi"</note> call it the *Saturnine* <note>original: "Saturnalische"</note>, and it was completed on the first day.

125. For then the hard, coarse, sharp earth and stones came to be and were *incorporated* <note>original: "corporiret"</note> together; additionally, the strong firmament of heaven was born, and the heart of the seven spirits of God stood hidden within that hard sharpness.

126. The *astrologers* assign the second day to the Sun, but it belongs to *Jupiter* <note>original: "Jupiter"</note>, speaking astrologically; for on the second day, the light broke through from the heart of the seven source-spirits through the hard *quality* of heaven, and created a softening in the hard water of heaven, and the light became shining in gentleness.

127. Then gentleness and the hard water separated from one another; the hard remained in its hard seat as a hard death, and the gentle broke through the hard by the power of light.

128. And this is now the Water of Life, which is born in the light of God out of the hard death. And thus the light of God broke through the tart and hard dark death in the sweet water of heaven, and thus heaven was made from the midst of the waters.

137. Therefore, the Earth began to turn green on the 3rd day, when the source-spirits stood in the shock of the Word, or the fire-flash.

# Chapter 22.
## On the Birth of the Stars, and the Creation of the 4th Day.

1. Here we begin to describe the sidereal <note>original: "siderische"; referring to the stars and the celestial influences they exert on the physical world</note> birth, and it is well worth noting what the first title of this book means, which reads: *Morning Glow at Sunrise*. For here, even a very simple person will be able to see and grasp the essence of God.

2. Let the reader not make himself blind through his own unbelief and "thick-headedness" <note>original: "zehe Begreiflichkeit"; literally a "tough" or "leathery" ability to grasp things, implying a mind too dense for spiritual truths</note>, for I have all of Nature with all her children as a witness and proof. If you are merely reasonable, then look around you, look at yourself, and consider yourself rightly; then you will soon find from what kind of spirit I write.

3. I will indeed obediently carry out the command of the Spirit; you, however, must take care and not allow yourself to be locked out of an open door, for here the portals of knowledge stand open.

4. And although the Spirit will run contrary to some astrologers <note>original: "Astrologos"</note>, it does not matter much to me; I must be more obedient to God than to men. They are blind in the spirit; if they do not wish to see, they may remain blind.

->Now take note.<-

5. When the fire-flash rose on the 3rd day from the light (which became shining in the sweet water), this flash was the bitter quality, which is born from the ignited shock of the fire in the water.

6. Thus, the entire nature of this world was pulsating and moving, in the Earth as well as above the Earth, and life began to be born again in all things.

7. From the Earth rose grass, herbs, and trees; and in the Earth rose silver, gold, and all kinds of ore; and in the deep above the Earth rose the miraculous formation of powers.

8. So that you might understand how there is a substance and occasion for all these things and births, I will describe everything one after another, each in its order—

...write, so that you may correctly understand the ground of these mysteries: and I will 1. begin with the Earth; hereafter 2. concerning the Deep above the Earth; and 3. concerning the gathering together and formation of the bodies of the stars; 4. concerning the seven primary qualities of the planets, and their heart, which is the Sun; 5. concerning the four elements; 6. concerning the external, perceptible birth which arises from this entire governance; and 7. concerning the wonderful proportion and skillfulness of the entire Wheel of Nature. <note>The "Wheel of Nature" is a central concept for Böhme, referring to the eternal, rotating movement of the seven "source-spirits" that drive all existence.</note>

9. To this mirror, I now wish to invite all lovers of the holy and highly praised arts of **Philosophy, Astrology, and Theology**; there, I will open up the root and the ground to them.

10. And even if I have not studied or learned their art, and do not know how to work with their circle-measuring <note>This likely refers to the mathematical and geometric tools used by traditional astronomers and astrologers of the 17th century</note>, that gives me no concern; they will nevertheless have so much to learn that many a man will not be able to fathom or grasp it in his entire lifetime.

11. For I do not use their formulas or methods, since I have not learned from them; rather, I have another teacher, which is all of Nature. From this entire Nature, with its inherent birth, I have studied and learned my **Philosophy, Astrology, and Theology**, and not from men or through men.

12. But because men are gods, and possess the knowledge of God the only Father, from whom they have come and in whom they live, I do not despise their formulas of **Philosophy, Astrology, and Theology** at all. For I find that, for the most part, they stand upon a very right foundation, and I will also strive to follow their formulas where I can.

13. For I must indeed say that their formula is my master, and I have my beginning and first knowledge from their formula. I also do not intend to overturn or "improve" their formulas—for I cannot, having never learned them—but rather I leave them sitting in their seat.

14. However, I will not build upon their foundation either; instead, as a hardworking servant, I will scrape the earth away from the root, so that one can see the whole tree with its root, trunk, limbs, branches, and fruits, so that my writing is nothing new, but rather that their Philosophy and mine...

...mine **Philosophy** may be one body, one tree, which bears the same kind of fruit.

15. I also have no command to complain loudly about them or to condemn them, except regarding their vices of pride, greed, envy, and wrath; the Spirit of Nature complains mightily about those, not I—for what would I, poor dust, do, who am almost powerless myself?

17. For a long time, the Spirit has urged them to finally unlock [the door], for the bright day is at hand: yet they go about in their drunkenness and search for the key, even though they have it with them and do not recognize it. Thus, they go about searching in their proud and ambitious drunkenness, just like that farmer who was looking for his horse while he was actually riding it.

18. Therefore says the Spirit of Nature: because they will not wake up from sleep and open the door, I will do it myself.

19. What else could I, a poor simple layman, teach or write of their high art, if it were not given to me by the Spirit of Nature, in whom I live and am? After all, I only hold the status of a layman and receive no salary for this writing; but should I therefore forbid the Spirit from beginning to unlock wherever He wills? I am not the door, but a common bolt <term>Riegel</term> <note>original: "Riegel"; a horizontal bar used to lock a door. ### Daybreak in the Rising. Chapter 22.

36. Come here, you learned doctors! If you are in the right, then give an answer to the Spirit; I wish to question you a little.

37. What do you suppose stood in the place of this world before the time of the world began? Or from what do you suppose the earth and stars were made? Or what do you suppose exists in the depth above the earth, or how did that depth come to be? Or how do you suppose that man is **GOD’S** image, in which **GOD** dwells? Or what do you imagine the wrath of **GOD** to be? Or what displeasure does **GOD** have with man, that He should torment him, seeing as He created him? Why would He reckon sin against him and condemn him to eternal torment!

38. Why then did He create that which man violates <note>original: "vergreift," meaning to sin against or mishandle; Böhme is asking why God created the possibility for sin if He punishes it so harshly.</note>, for that thing must surely be much more evil? Why or from what did that come to be? Or what is the cause or the beginning or the birth of the fierce wrath of **GOD**, out of which hell and the devil came to be? Or how does it happen that all creatures in this world bite, eat, and strike one another, yet sin is reckoned to man alone?

39. Or from what did the poisonous and evil animals and worms, along with all vermin, come to be? Or from what did the holy angels come to be? And finally, what is the soul of man, and the great **GOD** Himself?

40. Give a correct and thorough answer to this, and prove it, and cease your word-wrangling. If you can now prove from your previous writings that you know the one true **GOD**—how He is in love and wrath, and what He is—and can prove that **GOD** is not in the stars, elements, earth, stones, men, animals, worms, in leaves, herbs, and grass, in heaven and earth, and that all of this is not **GOD** Himself, and that my spirit is false, then I will be the first to burn my book in the fire and renounce and curse everything that I have written, and I will submissively allow myself to be instructed.

41. However, I do not mean to say that I cannot err at all, for there are some things not sufficiently explained, and are described as if from a single glance at the great **GOD**, where the <term>Wheel of Nature</term> <note>A central concept in Böhme’s thought, referring to the dynamic, rotating forces of creation and the "seven properties" through which God manifests.</note> turns too quickly, and man, with his half-dead and heavy capacity for grasping, cannot sufficiently catch hold of it.

42. But what you do not find explained and detailed in one place, you will find in another—if not in this book, then in the other.

Now you will say: it is not becoming of me to ask such things, for the Godhead is a mystery that no one can search out.

43. Listen: if it is not becoming of me to ask, then it is also not becoming of you to judge me. But if you boast of the knowledge of the light and of being a leader of the blind, yet are blind yourself, how then will you show the way to the blind? Will you not both fall in your blindness?

But will you now say: "We are not blind, and we clearly see the way of the light"? Why then do you quarrel about the way of the light, which none of you rightly sees?

44. You teach others the way, yet you yourselves are always searching for it, and you grope in the dark and do not see it. Or do you suppose it is a sin if someone asks about the way?

45. O you blind men, cease from your quarreling, and do not shed innocent blood, and do not devastate lands and cities because of it, according to the devil’s will and whim. Instead, put on the helmet of peace and gird yourselves with love for one another, and practice meekness. 47. When you look at the depth between the stars and the earth, would you say: "That is not **GOD**," or "GOD is not here"? Instead, when the Spirit of God's love breaks through my spirit, then the <term>animal birth</term> <note>the biological, sensory life of the human being</note> and the Godhead are one being, one <term>comprehensibility</term> <note>the state of being graspable or understandable</note>, and one light.

## Then you will say: But they do not know Him,
## and do not honor Him.

55. And whatever you look upon, God is there. However, the <term>comprehensibility</term> <note>the tangible, physical world</note> stands in this world in <term>Wrath</term> <note>the harsh, fiery quality of nature</note>, which the devil has ignited; and in the hidden kernel in the midst of the Wrath, the light or Heart of God is born—incomprehensible to the Wrath—and each remains in its own seat.

56. I do not, therefore, boast of the unbelief and stubbornness of the Jews, Turks, and Heathens, nor of their fury and malice against Christians. No, those are nothing but the snares of the devil, who thereby stirs people up into pride, greed, envy, and wrath, so that he may ignite the hellish fire in them. Likewise, I cannot say that these four sons of the devil do not also rule in Christendom—indeed, in every single person.

64. Now, Christians know how they can, by the power of this Tree, press through their death and through His death into His life, and rule and live with Him; thus, through their "breaking-through" and their new birth out of this dead body, they can be with Him in heaven.

65. And even though the dead body is in the midst of hell among all the devils, the <term>new man</term> <note>the spiritual self born of the soul’s union with God</note> nevertheless rules with God in heaven, and the Tree of Life is a strong gate for them, through which they enter into life.

->Concerning the Earth.<-

74. **T**he earth was now the *Salitter* <note>original: "Salitter"—Böhme’s term for the divine "saltpeter" or the fundamental substance of the spiritual world</note>, which was spat out from the innermost birth and stood in death: but when the fire-flash <note>original: "Feuer-Bliz"—a sudden ignition of divine or natural energy</note> rose up in the water through the Word, it was a terror, from which mobility arose in death; and this same mobility in all seven spirits is now the sidereal birth <note>the "star-like" or astral birth governing the physical world</note>.

->The Deep.<-

->Understand this correctly.<-

75. **W**hen, on the third day, the fire-flash ignited in the water of death, life broke through the dead body of the water and the earth.

76. But now, the dead water and earth grasp nothing more than the flash or terror of the fire, through which their mobility arises: but the light which rises quite gently in the fire-flash, that can be grasped by neither the earth nor the dead water.

77. It keeps its seat in the core, which is the fat or water of life, or the heaven; for it is the body of life which death cannot grasp, and yet it rises up in death. Likewise, the <term>wrath</term> <note>the harsh, consuming quality of nature</note> cannot grasp it; rather, the wrath remains in the terror of the fire-flash and creates the mobility in the dead body of the earth and the water.

78. The light, however, presses through quite gently afterwards and forms the birth, which has received its corporated body through the terror of the fire-flash.

->The Plants of the Earth.<-

79. **W**hen the wrathful fire-flash awakens the spirits of nature, which stand in the earth in death, with its fierce terror and makes them mobile, then the spirits begin to give birth to themselves according to their peculiar divine right, as they have done from eternity, and they shape a body together according to the qualities inherent in that place.

80. Whatever *Salitter* had died in death at the time of the ignition of the wrath, and however it was <term>qualifying</term> <note>original: "qualificirend"—meaning how the spirits interact and exert their specific properties upon one another</note> in the inherent life of the seven spirits of God at that same time, so it also

rose up again in the fire-flash at the time of the rebirth, and became nothing new, but only another form of the body which stands in the comprehensibility <note>physicality or the state of being graspable</note> in death.

81. But now the *Salitter* of the earth and the water can no longer change in its dead essence, nor show itself as infinite, as it would do in the heavenly seat; rather, when the fountain-spirits form the body, it rises up in the power of the light.

82. 83. And herein lies the core of the Godhead in the center, in its heaven, which stands hidden in the water of life; if you can, then grasp it.

->Concerning the Metals in the Earth.<-

84. **W**ith the metals, it is exactly the same substance and birth as with the plants above the earth. For the metal or ore stood in the "wheel" of the seventh spirit of nature in the work of love at the time of the ignition of the wrath, where the gentle well-doing is born behind the fire-flash. Therein stands the holy heaven, which shows itself in this birth—when Love becomes the First [Primus]—in such lovely clarity and beautiful colors, like gold, silver, and precious stones.

85. But silver and gold in the dead comprehensibility are only a dark stone compared to the root of the heavenly birth: I only put it here so that you may know from what it has its origin.

86. Because it was the most beautiful rising and birth in the holy, heavenly nature, it is also loved by man in this world above all else. Nature has written well into man's heart that it is better than other stones and earth, but she could not reveal to him the ground <note>the underlying reason or foundation</note> of where it came from or how it became so. By this, you can now notice the daybreak of the day.
