# Daybreak in the Rising. Chapter 22.

87. The first <note>original: "Primus"</note> is manifold and varied, all according to how the *Salitter* <note>Böhme’s term for the fundamental divine substance, likely derived from "salpeter"</note> in the natural heaven was the first in its ascent into the light of love. For every source-spirit <note>original: "Quellgeist"—the seven fundamental forces of nature in Böhme’s system</note> in the heavenly nature possesses the kind and property of all source-spirits, for it is always influenced <note>original: "inficiret"</note> by the others; from this, life and the unfathomable birth of God arise. But according to its own power, it is the first, and that is its own body, from which it takes its name.

88. Now, however, every source-spirit possesses the property of all nature, and during the time when the wrath was ignited, its workmanship was incorporated into death; and from the workmanship of every spirit, earth, stones, ore, and water were formed.

89. Therefore, you find the quality of every spirit in the earth's ore, stones, water, and soil; and for this reason, the earth is of so many and varied qualities, all according to how each source-spirit, with its inherent birth, was the first during the time of the ignition.

90. Nature has nonetheless revealed so much to man that he knows how he can smelt away the foreign matter from the foreign, infected birth of each source-spirit, so that the same source-spirit remains the first in its own primacy <note>original: "Primat"</note>.

91. You have an example of this in gold and silver; you cannot make them pure, so that they are pure silver and gold, unless they are smelted seven times in the fire. When that happens, they remain sitting in their own quality and color in the middle seat, in the heart of nature, which is the water.

92. First, the harsh <term>quality</term> <note>Böhme uses "quality" to mean an active force or property</note>, which holds the <term>Salitter</term> captive in hard death, must be smelted away; that is the coarse, stony dross <note>original: "Aberaum"</note>. After that, the harsh death of the water is removed; from this comes a poisonous parting-water <note>original: "Scheidewasser"—historically, nitric acid used to separate metals</note>, which stands in the rising of the fire-flash in death. This is an evil—indeed, the very most evil—source in death, yes, the harsh and bitter death itself; for that is the place where the life which arises in the sweet water has died in death; this is now separated in the second smelting.

93. Thirdly, the bitterness, which arises in the ignition of the water in the fire-flash, is smelted away; for that same thing is a rager, a stormer, and a breaker, and no silver or gold can endure if it is not yet killed, for it makes everything brittle and manifests in many different colors,

<meta>catchword: then</meta>

---

<page-num>297</page-num>
<header>Chapter 22. Daybreak in the Rising.</header>

then it rides through all the spirits and takes on the colors of all spirits.

94. Fourthly, the fire-spirit, which stands in the cruel anguish and woe of life, must also be smelted away, for it is a constant father of wrath, and from it the hellish woe is born.

95. Now, when the wrath of these four spirits is killed, the ore-*Salitter* remains in the water as a tough matter, and it looks similar to the spirit which is the first in that same ore; and the light, which stands in the fire, colors it according to its own quality, whether it be silver or gold.

96. And now, in the fourth smelting, the matter looks similar to silver or gold, but it does not yet endure and is not yet sufficiently tough and pure; the body is indeed present therein, but not the spirit.

97. When it is now smelted for the fifth time, the spirit of love rises up in the water through the light and makes the dead body living again, so that the matter remaining from the first four smeltings receives again the power that was the property of that source-spirit which is the first in this ore.

98. When it is now smelted for the sixth time, it becomes somewhat harder; there, the life which has risen in love moves and stirs itself; and from that same stirring, the sound <note>original: "Thon"—meaning the resonance or "tone" of the metal</note> arises within the hardness, and the ore gets a clear ring; for the hard, pounding, and bitter fiery matter is gone.

99. In this sixth smelting, I hold that the greatest danger lies for the <term>alchemists</term> <note>those who practice the art of transforming base metals into noble ones</note> with their making of silver and gold. A truly subtle fire belongs here, and it can easily become burnt and "deaf" <note>unresponsive or dull</note>, and also much too soft through a fire that is too cold. It must be a medium fire, so that the spirit in the heart does not become agitated, but rather seethes gently; then it receives a fine, sweet, and gentle sound, and rejoices always, as if it were to ignite itself again in the light of God.

100. But if the fire in the fifth and sixth smelting is too hot, then the new life—which was born in love in the power of the rising light out of the water—is again infected in the grimness in the fire of wrath, and the ore becomes a burnt foam and dross, and the <term>alchemist</term> has filth instead of gold.

And in this movement, it becomes rich and vigorous <note>original: "fett und geil"—in the 17th century, "geil" meant luxuriant or full of growing power</note> once more; it increases and spreads out, and the highest depth is born out of the heart of the spirit, entirely full of joy, as if it wished to begin an angelic triumph. It seeks to manifest itself in divine power and form into infinity, according to the right of the Godhead. 103. And when it is finally completed, it possesses its true power and color and lacks nothing, except for one thing: the spirit cannot raise itself into the light with its body. 104. For dead flesh can only grasp a dead <term>God</term> and yearns only for such a dead <term>God</term>; but it is a <term>God</term> who has plunged many a man into hell.

105. For this reason, you must not take me for an <term>Alchemist</term>, for I write solely from the knowledge of the spirit, and not through practical experience. Although I could indeed indicate more here—how many days and in which hours such things must be prepared—for one cannot make gold in a day, but rather an entire month is required.

106. However, it is not my intention to attempt such a thing, since I do not know how to work with fire, nor do I know the colors of the <term>source-spirits</term> <note>original: "Quellgeister"—the seven fundamental forces of Böhme's cosmos</note> in their outermost birth. These are two great deficiencies; rather, I know them according to another man <note>likely referring to the "inner man" or spiritual self</note>, who does not exist in tangibility.

107. You will find something more and deeper regarding this in the description of the Suns. My intention is directed solely toward describing the whole Godhead—as much as is graspable to me in my weakness—how it is in love and wrath, and how it now births itself in this world. Regarding the

### Chapter 23.
### Concerning the Depth Above the Earth.

1. When man looks at the depth above the earth, he sees nothing but stars and water-clouds; then he thinks there must be another place where the Godhead reveals itself with the heavenly and angelic government <note>original: "Regiment"—the ordered rule or domain of God</note>. He wants to distinguish the depth, along with its government, from the Godhead, for he sees nothing there but stars, and the government between them is fire, air, and water.

2. Then he thinks: <term>God</term> made that out of nothing by His purpose; how could <term>God</term> be in that essence, or how could that be <term>God</term> Himself? He always imagines it is merely a house in which <term>God</term> rules and dwells with His Spirit; he thinks <term>God</term> could not be a <term>God</term> whose essence consists in the power of this government.

3. Many a man might well say: what kind of a <term>God</term> would that be, whose body, essence, and power consisted in fire, air, water, and earth?

4. Look, you uncomprehending man, I will show you the true ground of the Godhead. If this entire essence is not <term>God</term>, then you are not <term>God's</term> image; if there is some foreign <term>God</term> elsewhere, then you have no part in Him. For you are created out of this <term>God</term> and live in the same, and the same constantly gives you power, blessing, food, and drink from within Himself; also, all your knowledge stands in this <term>God</term>, and when you die, you are buried in this <term>God</term>.

5. Now, if there were a foreign <term>God</term> who is outside of this one, who would then make you living again out of this <term>God</term> in whom you have decayed? How would the foreign <term>God</term>, from whom you were not created and in whom you never lived, figure <note>original: "figuriren"—to shape or form</note> your body and spirit together again?

6. If you were of a different matter than <term>God</term> Himself, how then would you be His child? Or how could the man and King Christ be <term>God's</term> bodily Son, whom He has born out of His heart?

7. If His Godhead were a different essence than His body,

...then there would have to be two kinds of Godhead in Him; His body would be from the God of this world, and His heart would be from the unknown God.

9. Behold, this is the true, only God from whom you were created, and in whom you live: When you look upon the deep and the stars and the earth, you see your God; and in that same God you also live and exist, and that same God also governs you, and from that same God you also have your senses, and you are a creature out of Him and in Him—otherwise you would be nothing at all.

10. Now you will say that I write in a Pagan fashion. Listen and behold, and mark the distinction of how all this is; for I do not write as a Pagan but Philosophically. Neither am I a Pagan, but I have the deep and true knowledge of the one great God, who is All.

11. When you look at the deep, the stars, the elements, and the earth, you do not grasp with your eyes the bright and clear Godhead, even though it is indeed there and within them; rather, you first see and grasp with your eyes death, and after that the wrath of God and the hellish fire.

12. But if you lift up your thoughts and consider where God might be, then you grasp the sidereal birth <note>original: "siderische Geburt" — referring to the "astral" or "starry" forces that Böhme believed intermediate between the spiritual and material worlds</note>, where love and wrath surge against one another. However, when you draw faith from the God who governs in holiness within this dominion, then you break through the heavens and grasp God by His holy heart.

13. When this happens, then you are as the whole God is, who is Himself heaven, earth, stars, and elements; and you also have such a dominion within you, and are such a person as the whole God is in the space <note>original: "Loco"</note> of this world.

->Now you say:<-

How should I understand this? Surely the kingdom of God and the kingdom of Hell or the Devil are distinct from one another, and cannot be one body? Also, the earth and stones are not God, just as

as well as the heavens and the stars, nor even the elements; much less can a human being be God, otherwise he could not be cast away by God?

14. Here I will now explain the foundation to you in sequence; keep this question in mind.

->Of the sidereal birth, and the birth of God.<-

15. **B**efore the times of the created heavens, the stars, and the elements, and before the creation of the angels, there was no such wrath of God, nor any death, nor any devil, nor any earth or stones. Likewise, there were no stars, but the Godhead was born within itself, gentle and lovely, and figured into images which were incorporated according to the source-spirits <note>original: "Quellgeister" — Böhme's term for the seven fundamental driving forces or qualities of divine nature</note>, through their birthing, wrestling, and ascending; and they also passed away again through their wrestling and formed themselves into another shape, all according to which source-spirit was the first <note>original: "Primus"</note>, as you can read earlier in this book.

16. But mark this correctly: The earnest and severe birth, from which the wrath of God, hell, and death have come, has indeed been in God from eternity, but was not ignited or prominent. For the whole of God stands in seven species <note>original: "Species" — meaning types, forms, or qualities</note>, or seven kinds of shape or birthing; and if these births did not exist, there would be no God, no life, no angel, nor any creature.

17. And these same births have no beginning, but have birthed themselves thus from eternity; and according to this depth, God Himself does not know what He is. For He knows no beginning, nor anything like Himself, nor any end.

18. Among these seven births in total, none is the first, and none the second, third, or last; rather, all seven are each the first, second, third, fourth, and last. Yet I must set them down one after the other according to the manner of creatures, otherwise you would not understand it; for the Godhead is like a wheel with seven wheels made within one another, where one sees neither beginning nor end.

->Now observe.<-

19. **F**irst, there is the harsh quality <note>original: "herbe Qualität" — the first of Böhme's seven qualities, representing contraction, cold, and sharpness</note>, which is always born of the other six spirits; in itself, it is hard,

# The Rising Morning Redness. Chapter 23.

Cold, sharp, similar to salt, and yet much sharper. A creature cannot fully grasp its sharpness, since it does not exist alone and isolated in a creature; yet, according to the nature of the ignited hellish quality, I know what it is like. This harsh, sharp quality <note>original: "herbe, scharfe Qualität" — In Böhme's system, the "Harshness" is the first quality of nature, acting as a contracting force that gives form and solidity to spirit.</note> draws together and holds the forms and images within the divine body, and it dries them so that they may endure.

20. The second birthing <note>original: "Gebärung" — Böhme uses this term to describe the eternal process by which God's nature is constantly generating itself.</note> is the sweet water. This is also born out of all six spirits; for it is the gentleness <note>original: "Sanftmuth"</note> which is born from the other six and is pressed out within the harsh birthing. It constantly reignites, extinguishes, and softens the harshness, so that the harshness cannot display its severity, even though it would have the power to do so in its own sharpness, apart from the water.

21. The third birthing is the bitterness, which arises from the fire in the water; for it rubs or agonizingly exerts itself within the harsh and sharp cold, and makes the cold mobile, from which movement arises.

22. The fourth birthing is the fire, which arises from the movement or friction within the harsh spirit. This is now sharply burning, while the bitterness is stinging and raging. But when the fire-spirit rubs itself so ragingly in the harsh cold, there is then an anxious, terrifying, trembling, and sharp, contrary birthing.

->Mark this deeply here.<-

23. For I speak here after the devilish manner, as if the light of GOD had not yet ignited itself in these four forms <note>original: "Species" — referring to the four lower qualities: harshness, sweetness, bitterness, and fire.</note>, and as if the Godhead had a beginning. However, I cannot instruct you in any other or closer way so that you might understand it.

24. In this fourth friction there is a hard and quite terrifying, sharp and fierce cold, like a molten and very cold salt-water, which yet would not be water, but such a hard power, like stones. Also within it is a raging, raving, stinging, and burning; the water is always like a dying person, when body and soul part—a completely terrifying anxiety, a birthing-woe.

25. Here, O man, reflect: here you see where the devil and his fierce, angry malice have their origin, as well as GOD’s wrath and the hellish fire, also death and hell, and eternal damnation. You philosophers, <note>Böhme often addresses "Philosophers," by which he means the alchemists and natural scholars of his day, urging them to look beyond material chemistry to the spiritual forces behind it.</note> mark this.

# Chapter 23. The Rising Morning Redness.

26. When these four birthings now rub against one another in this way, the heat becomes the first cause <note>original: "Primus"</note> and ignites itself in the sweet water; then, immediately, the light rises up.

->Understand this rightly.<-

27. When the light ignites, the fire-flash <note>original: "Feuerschreck" — literally "fire-fright" or "fire-terror." It refers to the sudden, shocking transition or "crack" when darkness breaks into light.</note> goes before it, just as when you strike a stone: you see the fire-flash first, and only then does the light catch itself from that fire-flash.

28. Now the fire-flash travels through the harsh quality in the water and makes it mobile; but the light is born in the water and becomes shining, and is an incomprehensible, gentle, and lovely being, which neither I nor any creature can sufficiently write or speak of. Instead, I only stammer like a child that would like to learn to speak.

29. That same light is born in the midst of these four forms, out of the fatness <note>original: "Fetten" — an alchemical term referring to the combustible or life-giving essence of a substance.</note> of the sweet water, and it fills the entire body of this birthing. But it is such a gentle well-being, a pleasant smelling and a pleasant tasting, that I know of no comparison for it, except where life is born in the midst of death; or as if a person sat in a great heat of fire and was suddenly pulled out and placed into such great gentleness, where he had previously felt the pains of the fire, but now they suddenly vanished, and he was placed into such a gentle well-being.

30. Thus, the birthing of the four forms is placed into such a gentle well-being when the light rises within them.

31. But you must understand me rightly here: I write after the manner of a creature, as if a person had been the devil’s prisoner and was suddenly placed out of the hellish fire into the light of GOD.

32. For the light has no beginning in the birthing of GOD, but it has shone in the birthing from eternity, and GOD Himself knows no beginning within it. Only the Spirit opens the gates of hell to you here, so that you may see what the condition is like in the devils and in hell, and how it is in man when the divine light is extinguished and he sits in GOD’s wrath; then he lives in such a birthing, and in such anxiety, pain, and woe.

33. I also cannot describe this in any other form, for I must write as if the birthing of God had a—

->Now mark the gates of God.<-

34. The light, which is now born out of the fire and becomes shining in the water, and fills the entire birthing <note>original: "Gebährung" — Böhme's term for the ongoing, organic process of divine self-generation.</note>, and enlightens it and softens it: that is the true Heart of God or the Son of God. For He is thus forever born from the Father, and is a different Person than the qualities and the birthing of the Father.

35. For the birthing of the Father cannot seize or comprehend the light, nor use it for its own birthing; rather, the light stands free for itself, and is comprehended by no [single] birthing, yet it fills and enlightens the entire birthing, as the Only-Begotten Son of the Father. <note>original: "Joh. 1, 14." — A reference to the Gospel of John: "And the Word was made flesh... the glory as of the only begotten of the Father."</note>

36. And this light I call, in the human birth, the animated birth <note>original: "animalische Geburt" — In the 17th century, "animal" referred to the *anima* or soul; it means the "living" or "soulish" aspect of a human, not "animalistic" in the modern sense.</note>, [,,Understand the image, which blossoms forth ,,from the essences of the soul according to God’s ,,likeness.] or the birth of the soul, which interacts with the qualities <note>original: "inqualiret" — A term Böhme coined to describe how different spiritual forces blend their characteristics.</note> of this divine animated birth; and herein the human soul is one heart with God, provided that it also stands in this light.

37. The 5th birthing in God is now this: when this light thus penetrates quite softly and lovely through the first four birthings, it brings the heart of the sweet water and the loveliest power with it. And when the sharp births now taste it, they become quite soft and lovely, and it is as if life were forever rising up within death.

38. There, every spirit tastes the other and receives purely new power; for the harsh quality now becomes quite gentle, because the power of the light from the sweet water softens it, and in the fire, the gentle love rises up; for it warms the cold, and the sweet water makes the sharp taste quite lovely and soft.

39. And in the sharp and fiery birthings, there is nothing but pure longing for love, tasting, friendly influencing, and a gracious birthing; there is pure love, and all wrath and knightly-severity <note>original: "Ritterkeit" — suggesting a bold, harsh, or defensive strength.</note> are locked away in the Center as if in a great fortress; this birth-

birthing is a truly soft act of benevolence; the bitter spirit is now the living mobility.

40. The 6th birthing in God is now this: when the spirits thus taste of one another in their birth, they become quite full of joy; for the flash of fire or the sharpness from the birth now rises upward and surges just like the air in this world.

41. For when one power stirs the other, they taste of one another and become quite full of joy; for the light is born out of all powers, and penetrates again through all powers. Thereby and therein the exalted joy is born, from which the tone <note>original: "Thon" — Böhme means sound or resonance, suggesting that the harmony of the universe is a kind of divine music.</note> arises. And when the birth now brings forth, this spirit seizes the light and speaks it back into the birth through the surging spirit.

42. And this surging spirit is the third Person in the birth of God, and is called God the Holy Spirit.

43. The 7th birthing exists and maintains its birth and forming in the Holy Spirit; when the same spirit goes through the sharp births, he goes with the tone and forms and builds all kinds of figures, all according to how the sharp births wrestle with one another.

44. For they constantly wrestle with one another in the birth like a play of love; and according to how the birth is rising with colors and tastes, so too are the figures formed.

45. And this birth is now called God the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit; and none is the first, and also none is the last. And even though I make a distinction and place one after the other, yet none is the first and none is the last; rather, they have been thus from eternity in one equal essence and seat.

46. I must only write with distinctions so that the reader understands it, for I cannot write heavenly words, but only human words. It is indeed written quite correctly, yet the essence of God stands in power, and only the spirit comprehends it, and not the dead flesh.

47. Thus you can understand what kind of essence the Godhead is, and how the three Persons are in the Godhead; you must not compare the Godhead to any [physical] image, for it is the birth of all things: even so, if there were not the sharp birthing in the first four species <note>original: "Species" — Böhme uses this term to refer to the fundamental qualities or properties of nature.</note>, there would be no mobility, and the light could not ignite itself, nor could life be born.

48. But now this sharp birth is the origin of mobility and life, as well as the origin of the light, from which the living and rational spirit arises, which distinguishes, forms, and shapes within this birthing. For the harsh, cold birth is a beginning of all things; it is harsh, severe, contracting, and firmly holding, and it forms and draws together from the birthing, making the birth thick, so that it becomes a nature; and from this, nature and comprehensibility <note>original: "Begreifligkeit" — the state of being tangible or graspable by the senses.</note> have their origin in the entire body of God.

49. This nature is now like a dead, unthinking essence, and does not stand within the power of the birth, but is a body in which the power gives birth. It is, however, the body of God, and has all power like the entire birthing; and the birth-spirits take their strength and power from the body of nature, and give birth again and again; and the harsh spirit always draws together again and dries, thus the body and also the birth-spirits subsist.

50. The second birth is now the water, which takes its origin in the body of nature.

->Mark this.<-

51. When the light shines through the harsh, contracted body of nature and softens it, the gentle well-being is born within the body. Then the hard power becomes quite gentle, and melts like ice from the sun, and becomes thin like the water in the air; yet the stock of nature, of heavenly comprehensibility, remains standing. For the harsh spirit and the fire-spirit hold it, and the gentle water—which melts from the body of nature in the igniting of the light—goes through the severe and earnest, cold and fiery birth, and is quite sweet and lovely.

52. By this, the earnest and severe birth is now refreshed, and when it tastes it, it becomes elevated and rejoices; it is a rising of joy, where the life of gentleness is born. For that is the Water of Life;

<page-num>307</page-num>

therein love is born in God, as well as in angels and humans, for everything has one and the same power and birth.

53. And now, when the birth of the powers tastes the Water of Life, they become trembling with the joys of love; and that same trembling or movement, which rises up in the midst of the birth, is bitter. For it rises quickly out of the birth when the Water of Life comes into the birth, like a leap of joy in the birthing.

54. But because it rises so quickly—so that the birth elevates itself so quickly before it is completely infected <note>original: "inficiret" — a term Böhme uses to mean "imbued" or "permeated" by a spiritual quality.</note> with the Water of Life—this same startle <note>original: "Schrack" — a sudden shock or terrifying flash that marks the transition from darkness to light.</note> retains its bitterness from the severe birth; for the initial birth is entirely severe, cold, fiery, and harsh.

55. Therefore, the startle is also so elevating and trembling, for it moves the entire birth and tears itself within it, until it ignites the fire in the hard cruelty, from which the light takes its origin. Then the trembling startle is enlightened with the gentleness of the light, and goes up and down in the birth, crosswise, above itself and below itself, like a wheel with seven wheels made within one another. <note>A reference to the vision of the wheels in the biblical Book of Ezekiel, representing the interconnectedness of God's powers.</note>

56. From this penetrating and turning arises the sound or tone according to the kind of each spirit, and one power always infects the other; for the powers are like bodily brothers in one body, and the gentleness rises up, and the spirit gives birth and reveals itself infinitely.

57. For whichever power now reveals itself most strongly in the turning—that is, in the birthing—the Holy Spirit also forms the figures in the body of nature according to that power's kind, type, and colors.

58. Thus you see how no power is the first, and also none the second, third, fourth, or last; rather, the last gives birth to the first just as the first gives birth to the last, and the middle one takes its origin as much from the last as from the first, second, third, and so forth.

59. You also see how nature cannot be distinguished from the powers of God, but is it not all one body? The Godhead—that is, the holy power of the Heart of God—is born in nature; also the Holy Spirit arises or goes out from the Heart of Light through all the powers of the Father continually, and figures everything and forms everything.

60. This entire birth is now divided into three distinctions—

### The Gates of the Holy Trinity.

61. The whole of birth, which is the heaven of all heavens, as well as this world which is in the body of the whole, as well as the place of the earth and all creatures—wherever you can think or imagine—all that together is God the Father, who has neither beginning nor end. And wherever you can think or imagine, even in the smallest circle you might choose, the whole birth of God is perfect, unceasing, and irresistible.

62. But if it happens that the light is extinguished in a creature or in a place, then the stern birth <note>original: "strenge Geburt" — Böhme uses this to describe the harsh, cold, or fiery qualities of nature when they are not tempered by the Light of the Son.</note> is there, which lies hidden in the innermost kernel within the light. That is now one part.

63. The second part, or the second Person, is the Light, which is always born out of all powers and in turn illuminates all the powers of the Father, and possesses the fountain-well <note>original: "Quellbrunn" — a favorite Böhme term for the source or "springing" of divine energy.</note> of all powers.

64. It is, however, distinguished from the Father as a specific Person because the Father's birth cannot grasp it, and yet it is the Father's Son, who is always born from the Father. You have an example of this in all ignited fires in this world; just reflect upon it.

65. And the Father loves this, His only-begotten Son, so very heartily because He is the light and the gentle delight in His body, through whose power the Father's joy and bliss arise.

66. These are now two Persons, and neither can catch, hold, or comprehend the other; and one is as great as the other, and if one were not, the other would also not be.

67. Here, take note, you Jews, Turks, and Heathens, for this concerns you: the gates of God are opened to you here. Do not harden yourselves, for now is the acceptable time. You are by no means forgotten by God; rather, if you convert, the light and Heart of God will rise within you like the bright sun.

68. I write this as if in the power and perfect knowledge of the great God, and

understand His will in this matter quite well. For I live and am in Him, and I flourish in this work from His root and stem; so must it be. Only take heed: if you blind yourself, there is no more counsel, and you must not say you did not know. Arise, the day is breaking!

69. The third distinction, or the third Person in the essence of God, is the surging Spirit <note>original: "wallende Geist" — often translated as the "moving" or "proceeding" Spirit; it implies a bubbling or flowing motion.</note>, which arises from the rising in the sudden flash <term>Schracke: a momentary shock or "crack" of lightning that marks the transition from darkness/fire to light</term> where life is born. This Spirit now surges in all powers and is the Spirit of Life; the powers cannot again grasp or catch Him, but He ignites the powers and, through His surging, makes figures and images, and forms them according to the way the wrestling birth stands in each place.

70. And if you do not wish to be blind, you should know that "delight" is that same Spirit; but in the place of this world, nature is quite significantly ignited within it in the wrath-fire <note>original: "Zornfeuer" — the state of nature when separated from God's love, often associated by Böhme with the fall of Lucifer.</note>, which Lord Lucifer has done; and the Holy Spirit, who is the Spirit of gentleness, lies hidden therein in His heaven.

71. You need not ask, "Where is this heaven?" It is in your heart; only unlock it. Here, the key is shown to you.

72. Thus there is one God and three distinct Persons in one another, and none can grasp or stop the other, nor fathom the other's origin; but the Father begets the Son, and the Son is the Father’s Heart, and His love, and His light, and is an origin of joys and the beginning of all life.

73. And the Holy Spirit is the Spirit of life, and a Former and Creator of all things, and an executor of the will in God; He has formed and created all angels and creatures out of the body and in the body of the Father, and still sustains and forms everything daily, and is the sharpness and the living Spirit of God. As the Father speaks the Word out of His powers, so the Spirit forms it.

### Concerning the Great Simplicity of God.

74. ...you here, you world-wise person, who are filled with evil cleverness.

75. Mark this, you world-wise jurists: if you will not go before this mirror—the bright and clear face of God—and reflect yourselves therein, then the Spirit offers you birth in the innermost bitter circle <note>original: "herben Cirkel" — the "bitter" or "astringent" quality is the first property of nature in Böhme's system, associated with contraction and harshness.</note> where cleverness is born. For that is the sharpness of God’s anxious birth, and from that very place your cleverness and deep understanding are born.

76. If you wish to be gods and not devils, then make use of the holy and gentle justice of God; if not, you shall forever and eternally give birth within the strict and earnest birth of God. The Spirit says this as a word of God, and not my dead flesh.

77. You should know that I do not suck this knowledge out of dead reason. Instead, my spirit <term>inter-works</term> <note>original: "inqualiret" — Böhme's term for the way different qualities or spirits influence and operate within one another.</note> with God, and <term>attests</term> <note>original: "approbiret" — to experience the truth of something through spiritual participation.</note> to the Godhead: how it is, with all its birth, taste, and smell. I find, therefore, that the Godhead is an entirely simple, gentle, lovely, and still being; that the birth of the <term>Trinity</term> <note>original: "Dreyheit" — Böhme's specific term for the Triune nature of God.</note> of God brings itself forth quite gently, friendly, lovely, and united. The sharpness of the innermost birth can never raise itself into the gentleness of the Trinity, but remains hidden in the depth.

78. And the sharpness in the hiddenness is called God’s Wrath; but the essence of gentleness in the Trinity is called God. Nothing goes out from the sharpness that might destroy or kindle the wrath; rather, the spirits play gently into one another like little children when they rejoice with each other, where each has its task, and they play together and caress one another.

79. The holy angels also carry out such work, and within the Trinity of God there is an entirely gentle, lovely, and sweet being. There, the spirit always rises in the tone <note>original: "Thone" — can mean both sound/music and the "throne" or dwelling place of God.</note>, and one power stirs the other, as if lovely songs or the playing of stringed instruments were rising there.

80. And as the rising of the spirits is in every place, so also the tone forms itself—but quite gently, incomprehensible to the bodies of the angels, yet entirely comprehensible to the animated birth <note>original: "animalischen Geburt" — the soulful, living nature of a being.</note> of the angels. And as the Godhead reveals itself in every place, so also the angels reveal themselves. For the angels are created out of this essence, and they have their princes of the <term>source-spirits</term> <note>original: "Quellgeister" — the seven fundamental qualities of nature and God in Böhme's cosmology.</note> of God among them, just as they are in the birth of God.

81. Therefore, as the essence of God reveals itself in birth, so also do the angels. Whichever power in the birth of God becomes the "First" <note>original: "Primus"</note> at any given time, and jubilates from the heart of God in the Holy Spirit, the angelic prince of that power also begins his song of praise before all others, and jubilates with his host. Now it is one, then it is the other; for the birth of God is like a wheel.

82. But when the heart of God reveals itself specifically with its clarity, then the entire host of all three kingdoms of the holy angels rises up. And in this rising of the heart of God, the man Jesus Christ is King and First; he leads the royal dance with all the holy souls of men until the Last Day. Then the holy humans will become perfect angels, and the godless will become perfect devils, and that into his eternity. Here, reflect yourself, you clever world, and see from where your cleverness comes.

->Now you will say:<-

83. "Yet you seek a much deeper cleverness than we do; you want to climb into the hiddenness of God, which is not fitting for any human. We seek only human cleverness, but you want to be like God and know everything as God is—and moreover in all things, both in heaven and hell, in devils, angels, and humans." Therefore, [you argue] it is surely not wrong to seek subtle, sharp cunning, for it brings honor, power, and wealth.

->The Objection.<-

84. If you follow after me on this ladder, upon which I climb into the depth of God, you will have climbed well. I did not come to this opinion, or into this work and knowledge, through my reason or through my intentional will. I also did not seek this science, nor did I know anything about it. I sought only the heart of God, to hide myself therein from the storm of the devil.

85. But when I reached that point, this great and difficult work was laid upon me: to reveal to the world and to announce the Great Day of the Lord. And because the world lusts so strongly after the root of the tree, it was laid upon me to reveal to them what the whole tree is—thereby signaling that it is the "Daybreak" <note>original: "Morgenröte" — referring to the title of the book and the dawning of spiritual realization.</note> of the day, which God has long ago concluded in His counsel. Amen.

<summary>Böhme contrasts worldly "cleverness" with divine wisdom, describing the harmonious, musical interplay of the Trinity and the angelic hosts led by Jesus Christ. He defends his mystical insights not as a product of his own ambition, but as a divine mandate to reveal the "Daybreak" of God's truth to a world obsessed with power.</summary>

# Aurora: The Daybreak at its Rising. Chapter 23.

86. So you see now what GOD is, and how his love and wrath have existed from eternity, as well as how his birth is. You must not say that you do not live and exist in GOD, or that GOD is something foreign to which you cannot come; rather, wherever you are, there is the gate of God. If you are holy, then according to your soul you are with GOD in heaven; but if you are godless, then according to your soul you are in hellish fire.

## Now mark further.

87. When GOD created all the angels together, they were created out of this generating birth of GOD. Their body was corporated <note>formed into a physical or distinct substance</note> together out of Nature, and within it, their spirit and light were born, just as the Godhead was born. And just as the source-spirits <term>source-spirits</term> <note>original: "Quellgeister" — the seven fundamental qualities or forces that drive all existence in Böhme's system.</note> of GOD always took their power and strength from the body of Nature, so also did the angels; they always took their power and strength from the Nature of GOD.

88. And just as the Holy Spirit formed and shaped everything in Nature, so also the angelic spirit <term>inter-worked</term> <note>original: "inqualirete" — to operate or blend qualities within one another.</note> in the Holy Spirit and helped to form and shape everything, so that everything might be one heart and will, and nothing but pure delight and joy.

89. For the angels are the children of the great GOD, whom he has born in his body of Nature, for the increase of divine joy.

90. Here you should know, however, that the bodies of the angels cannot grasp the birth of God; their body does not understand it either. Only their spirit understands it. The body, however, holds still—just like Nature in GOD—and lets the spirit work and play in love with GOD. For the angels play before GOD and in GOD, just like small children before their parents; by this, the divine joy is increased.

91. But when the great and mighty prince and king Lucifer was created, he did not want to do this; instead, he lifted himself up and wanted to be GOD alone, and he ignited the wrath-fire within himself. All his angels did the same.

92. When this happened, he roared with his ignited fire-spirit into the Nature of GOD. Then the whole body in the Nature of GOD was ignited, as far as his dominion reached. But because his light was immediately extinguished, he could no longer inter-work with his spirit in the two births of the Son of GOD and the Holy Spirit of GOD, but remained standing in the sharp birth of GOD.

<meta>Catchword: 93. For</meta>

***

# Chapter 23. Aurora: The Daybreak at its Rising.

93. For the sharp generating birth cannot grasp the light of GOD and the Spirit of GOD; therefore, they are two distinct persons. <note>In Böhme's thought, "person" here refers to distinct modes or aspects of existence.</note> Therefore, Lord Lucifer, with his strict, cold, and hard fire-birth, could no longer touch or see the heart and the Holy Spirit of GOD, nor taste nor feel them; instead, he was spewed out with his fire-spirit into the outermost Nature, in which he had ignited the wrath-fire.

94. This same Nature is indeed the body of GOD, in which the Godhead is born, but the devils cannot grasp the gentle birth of GOD, which rises up in the light. For their body has died away in the light and lives in the outermost and strict birth of GOD, where the light never again ignites.

95. For their <term>oiliness</term> <note>original: "Fettes" — literally "fatness," referring to the flammable essence or spiritual "fuel" that allows the light to burn.</note> in the sweet water is burned, and a sour stench has come from that same water, in which the light of GOD can no longer ignite, and the light of GOD can no longer walk therein.

96. For the source-spirits in the devils are locked in hard wrath; their bodies are a hard death, and their spirits are a fierce sting of the wrath of GOD. Their source-spirits always give birth to themselves in the innermost sharpness according to the right of the sharp Godhead.

97. For they cannot give birth to themselves in any other way, nor can they die or pass away; instead, they stand in the most anxious birth, and there is nothing but pure fierceness, wrath, and malice in them. The ignited source of fire rises from eternity to eternity, and they can eternally no longer touch, see, or grasp the sweet and light birth of GOD.

## Concerning the Ignited Nature.

<note>The paragraph number is printed as 88, although it follows paragraph 97.</note>
88. Nature, however, was so harshly ignited by GOD, and he became so angry within it, because he was building a dwelling-house for the devils thereby, to keep them imprisoned within it, so that they might be children of his wrath, in whom he might rule with his fierce zeal, and they within the wrath.

# The 24th Chapter.
## On the Incorporation of the Stars.

1. When the entire body of Nature within the space of this world had become stiffened, as if in a hard death, and yet life remained hidden within it, God moved the entire body of Nature of this world on the fourth day, and out of Nature, from the light that had risen, he brought forth the stars. For the wheel of God’s birth moved once again, just as it had done from eternity.

2. It did indeed move on the first day and began the birth within the body of corrupted Nature; for on the first day, life distinguished itself from death, and on the second day, a firmament <note>The "Feste" or firmament refers to the division between the physical and spiritual realms</note> was created in between, and on the third day, life broke through death. For there, the light broke through the darkness and made the dead body of Nature green and movable.

3. Then, on the third day, the body of Nature was in such hard labor and anguish until the fire of love ignited within death; the light of life broke through the stiffened body of death and grew green out of death. However, on the third day, it stood only in the fire-terror <term>fire-terror</term> <note>original: "Feuerschrecke" — the sudden, shocking moment of transition from cold, dark stillness to burning life or mobility.</note>, from which movement arose.

4. But on the fourth day, the light rose up and made its seat in the house of death, which death nevertheless cannot grasp. Just as the strict birth of God—which stands in the innermost core from which life arises—cannot grasp the gentleness and the light of gentleness along with the spirit in that gentleness, so also the dead darkness of this world cannot grasp the light of Nature, nor can any devil.

5. Instead, the light shines through death and has made its royal seat in the midst of the house of death and of the wrath of God; it bears for Him a new Body of God out of the house of wrath, which exists eternally in the love of God, incomprehensible to the old, ignited nature in the outermost birth.

->Now you ask:<-
->How should I understand this?<-

6. I cannot easily write this into your heart, for it is not within everyone’s understanding and grasp—especially where the spirit stands in the house of wrath and does not inter-work <term>inter-work</term> <note>original: "inqualiret" — to blend or operate with the same qualities or essence.</note> with the light of God. I will, however, show this through earthly parables, to see if you might enter a little into the deeper meaning.

7. Look at a tree: it has a hard, coarse bark on the outside which is dead and stiffened; yet it is not entirely in death, but rather in a state of fainting, and there is a distinction between it and the body that grows beneath the bark. The body, however, has its living power and breaks out through the withered bark, bearing many beautiful young bodies <note>branches or shoots</note>, which all nevertheless stand within the old body.

8. But the bark is like a dead thing and cannot grasp the life of the tree; it merely hangs upon it and is a cover for the tree, in which worms nest and thereby eventually destroy the tree.

9. The entire house of this world is just like this: the outer darkness is the house of God’s wrath, wherein the devils dwell, and it is truly the house of death, for the holy light of God has died away within it. <insert>,,Understand, it has entered into ,,its Principle, and the outermost essence ,,of God is to be regarded as if dead, ,,though it still lives in God, but in a different source <note>original: "Quelle" — can mean source, fountain, or quality.</note>.,,</insert>

10. But the body of this great house, which lies hidden under the shell of darkness—incomprehensible to the darkness—is the house of life, where Love and Wrath struggle with one another.

11. Now Love always breaks through the house of death and bears holy, heavenly branches in the great tree, which stand in the light. For they grow green through the shell of darkness, just as the branch grows through the bark of the tree, and they are one life with God.

12. And Wrath also grows green in the house of darkness, and through its infection, it keeps many a noble branch imprisoned in death within the house of fierceness.

13. This is now the sum or the content of the sidereal birth <term>sidereal birth</term> <note>pertaining to the stars (from Latin "sidus"); here referring to the spiritual and physical generation of the celestial bodies.</note>, about which I intend to write here.

Böhme uses the metaphor of a tree's living wood growing beneath its dead bark to illustrate how spiritual life persists within a seemingly dead physical reality.</summary>

### Now the question arises:

### What are the stars? Or what were they made from?

14. They are the power of the seven source-spirits <term>source-spirits</term> <note>original: "Quellgeister." These are the seven fundamental qualities or forces that Böhme believes constitute both God's nature and the physical universe.</note> of God. For when the wrath of God was ignited by the devils in this world, the entire house of this world—within nature or the outermost birth—became stiffened as if in death; from this come the earth and stones. But when that same hard "over-space" was driven together into a lump, the deep became clearer, yet remained entirely dark, for the light within it had died away in the wrath.

15. But the body of God in this world could not remain in death; rather, God moved Himself with His seven source-spirits toward birth.

->But you must understand this high matter correctly.<-

16. The light of God, which is the Son of God, as well as the Holy Spirit, had not died; rather, the light—which from eternity has gone forth from the heart of God and illuminated the nature born from the seven spirits—withdrew from the harshly corrupted nature. Because of this, the nature of this world, with its physical tangibility, remained in death and cannot grasp the light of God, but is instead a dark house of the devil.

17. After this, on the fourth day of creation, God reborn the entire house of this world with its qualities and placed the source-spirits into the house of darkness, so that He might again bear a new body out of it for His praise and honor.

18. For His intention was that He wanted to create another angelic host out of this house. It was to be done like this: He wanted to create an angel, which was Adam, who should bear from himself creatures like himself, who would possess the house of the new birth. And in the middle of time, their King <note>Referring to Christ</note> should be born from the body of a human being and possess the reborn kingdom as a King of these creatures, in the place of the corrupted and cast-out Lucifer.

19. In the fulfillment of this time, God wanted to decorate this house with its qualities as a royal government, and grant the entire house to those same source-spirits,

therewith they might again bring forth creatures and images in the house of darkness and death, just as they had done from eternity, until the entire host of the newly created angels—which were the humans—would be completed. Then God wanted to bolt the devil into the house of darkness in a narrow cave and ignite the entire house again in His light, right up to the cave of the devil.

### Now the question arises:

### Why did God not bolt him up immediately? Then he would not have caused so much misfortune.

20. Behold, this was God’s purpose, and it had to stand: that He wanted to build an angelic host for Himself again out of the corrupted nature of the earth. Understand: a new body that would exist in God eternally.

21. It was by no means God’s intention to give the entire earth to the devil for an eternal dwelling-house, but only the death and the grimness <note>original: "Grimmigkeit," referring to the wrathful, harsh aspect of nature</note> of the earth, which the devil brought into it.

22. For how has the <term>Salitter</term> <note>A term Böhme uses for the "divine sap" or the fundamental chemical/spiritual substance of the universe.</note> of the earth sinned before God that it should stand entirely and utterly in eternal shame? In no way; it was only a body that had to hold still when the devil rose up within it.

23. If He had been intended to grant the devil an eternal dwelling-house immediately, then a new body could not have been built out of that same location. What then had that same space sinned in God that it should stand in eternal shame? Nothing; it would be an injustice.

24. But now it was the intention of God that He wanted to make a beautiful angelic host out of the earth, and for that purpose, all kinds of formations. For everything within it and upon it should turn green and be reborn, as one sees in ore, stones, trees, herbs, and grass, and all kinds of animals according to the heavenly likeness.

25. And even if those same formations were transitory—because they were not pure before God—nevertheless God wanted, at the end of this time, to pull the heart and the kernel out from the new rebirth, and separate it from death and wrath. And the new rebirth should grow green eternally in God outside of this location and bear heavenly fruit once again.

26. But the death of the Earth and the wrath within it were to become an eternal house for Lord Lucifer after the completion of the new birth. In the meantime, Lord Lucifer was to lie imprisoned in the deep above the Earth in the darkness, and there he is even now; he may well expect his fate quite soon.

27. Now, so that such a new birth could be completed without the Devil's will, the Creator was born within the body of this world just as if in the manner of a creature within His source-spirits <term>source-spirits</term> <note>original: "Quellgeistern." Böhme’s term for the seven fundamental forces of nature and God's being.</note>; and all the stars are nothing but the powers of God, and the entire body of this world consists in the seven source-spirits.

28. But that there are so very many stars with such manifold effects—that is the Infinity, which infects <note>or "influences"</note> itself within the seven spirits of God and brings forth in infinity.

29. That the birth, or the body of the stars, does not change in its position, as they have done from eternity, signifies that it shall be a steady birth, whereby the stiffened body of the Earth should be steadily ignited again in the same effect—which nevertheless stands in infinity—and be born anew. So also the house of deep darkness above the Earth, whereby the new body might always be born out of death, until the time and the entire newborn body were completed.

->Now you say:<-

->So are the stars then God, that one should honor and worship them as God?<-

30. The wise heathens <note>original: "Heyden." Referring to the ancient Greeks, Romans, and Egyptians.</note> reached this point as well, and they indeed far surpassed our philosophers <note>original: "Philosophos."</note> with their sharp intellect, but the true door of knowledge remained hidden from them.

31. Behold, the stars are indeed corporately formed out of God, but you must understand the distinction; for they are not the Heart, nor the gentle, pure Godhead, which one should honor and worship as God. Rather, they are the innermost and sharpest birth, where everything stands in struggle and wrestling—where, to be sure, the Heart of God always bears itself, and the Holy Spirit always goes forth from the exit of life.

32. But the sharp birth of the stars cannot again grasp the Heart of God, nor the Holy Spirit. Instead, the Light of God—which opens up within the anxiety—together with the surging of the Holy Spirit, remains free as the Heart for itself, and rules in the midst of the enclosure of the hidden heaven, which is made from the water of life.

33. For from that same heaven the stars received their first ignition, and they are only like a tool which God uses for the birth.

34. It is just such a birth as in man: the body is also the father of the soul, for the soul is born out of the power of the body. And if the body stands in the anxious birth of God like the stars—and not in the fierce, hellish one—then the soul of man inter-qualifies <term>inter-qualifies</term> <note>original: "inqualiret." A Böhmean term meaning to work together, permeate, or share qualities with.</note> with the pure Godhead, like a limb with its body.

35. Thus also the Heart or Light of God is always born in the body of this world, and that same born Heart is one Heart with the eternal, beginningless Heart of God, which is in and above all heavens.

36. It is not born alone in and out of the stars, but in the entire body of this world; however, the stars always ignite the body of this world so that the birth exists everywhere.

->But you must note this well.<-

37. The Light or Heart of God does not take its origin merely from the wild, rough stars, where indeed love and wrath are within one another, but from the Seat where the gentle water of life is always born.

38. For that same water was not seized by death in the ignition of the wrath, but it exists from eternity to eternity, and reaches to all ends in this world; it is the water of life which breaks through death, out of which the new body of God in this world is built.

39. It is in the stars as well as in all ends, but in no place is it tangible or comprehensible; rather, it fills everything all at once. It is also in the body of man, and whoever thirsts after this water and drinks of it, in him the Light of Life ignites, which is the Heart of God; from that, the Holy Spirit immediately wells forth.

->Now you say:<-

### How then do the stars exist in love and wrath?

40. See, the stars have risen out of the enkindled house of God's wrath, just like the movement of a child in the mother's womb in the third month. <note>Böhme frequently uses embryological analogies to explain cosmic processes, reflecting the belief that the macrocosm and microcosm mirror one another.</note> But now, these same stars have received their ignition from the eternal, un-extinguished water of life, for that same water was never extinguished within nature.

41. But when God moved within the body of this world, then on the third day the anguish <note>original: "Aengstlichkeit." In Böhme's system, this refers to the "contraction" or tension of the first qualities of nature as they struggle to give birth to light.</note> rubbed together in the birth of this world; from this the fire-flash arose, and the light of the stars ignited itself in the water of life. For until the third day from the time of the ignition of God's wrath in this world, nature was a dark valley in its anguish and stood in death; but on the third day, life broke through death, and the new birth began.

42. For just so long, and not one hour longer, did the newborn King and Great Prince of this world, *Jesus Christus*, rest in death; and He reborn those first three days of the creation of nature—and that same time spent in death—back into the light. He did this so that this time might again be one time with eternal time, and that no day of death should remain between them: And so that the eternal love, and the newborn love from the new body of nature, should be one eternal love, and that there be no distinction between the eternal love and the newborn love, but rather that the newborn love should reach into the Essence <term>Essence</term> <note>original: "Wesen." Refers to the true, spiritual substance of reality.</note> that has been from eternity, and also for itself into eternity.

43. Thus the newborn love—which rose out of the water of life in the light of the stars and in the whole body of this world—is so completely united with the eternal, beginningless love, that it is one heart and one spirit which carries and sustains everything.

44. In this ignition of the light in the stars and elements, the birth of nature did not transform itself entirely into holy gentleness <note>original: "Sanftmuth."</note> as it was before the time of the wrath, such that the birth of nature would now be entirely holy and pure. No; rather, it stands in its sharpest, strictest, and most anxious birth, where the wrath of God flourishes <note>original: "grünet," literally "greens."</note> without ceasing, like a hellish fire.

45. For if nature, with its sharp birth, had been entirely and completely transformed into love according to heavenly right, then the devils would be back in the holy seat of God.

46. You can also see and understand this quite well by the cruel heat and cold, as well as by the poison of bitterness and acidity in this world, all of which stands in the birth of the stars, wherein the devils lie imprisoned.

47. The stars are only the ignition of the great house; for the entire house is stiffened in death, just like the earth. The outermost birth is dead and stiffened like the bark on a tree, but the sidereal <term>sidereal</term> <note>Refers to the influence and spiritual essence of the stars (Latin: "sidus").</note> birth is the body where the life rises within.

48. This sidereal birth is quite sharp in its body, but the new birth—which rises in the water of life and penetrates through death—makes it gentle. It cannot, however, change the kernel of the sharp birth; rather, it is born out of it and keeps its holy new life for itself, and penetrates through the wrathful death, and the wrathful death does not comprehend it.

49. This love and wrath are now indeed one body, but the water of life is the heaven of distinction <note>original: "Himmel des Unterscheides." A barrier or firmament that allows two opposing qualities to occupy the same space without mixing.</note> between them, so that love does not contain or comprehend the wrath, nor does the wrath comprehend the love. Instead, love rises in the water of life and takes into itself the power from the first and strict birth—the power which is in the light and is born out of the wrath—so that the new body is born out of the old. For the old body, which stands in the strict birth, belongs to the devil as his house, and the new belongs to the kingdom of *Christ*.

->Now the question is:<-

### So then, are not all three persons of the Godhead present in the birth of this world's gentleness?

50. Yes, all three are in this world in the full birth of love, gentleness, holiness, and purity, and are always born in such substance and essence as has happened from eternity.

52. But now, from this one Father, who is both wrathful and also loving, you cannot make two persons; rather, He is one single Father, who is always begetting His dearly beloved Son, and from both of them the Holy Spirit always proceeds.

### Observe the depth in the Center. <note>original: "Centro." Böhme uses this term to describe the inner-most point of divine manifestation or the "heart" of a process.</note>

53. The Father is the single Essence, who is Himself all things, and who has always begotten His dearly beloved Son from eternity; and in both of them, the Holy Spirit has always arisen in the flash <note>original: "Blitze." This "flash" is the moment of ignition where darkness is transformed into light and life.</note> where life is born.

54. But now, from the strict and earnest birth of the source-spirits <term>Quellgeister: Böhme’s term for the seven fundamental forces or "qualities" that drive all of existence</term> of the Father, in which zeal and wrath stand, the body of nature has always become manifest; within it stands the light of the Son as the Father’s heart, which is incomprehensible to nature.

55. For the light is in the middle of the birth, and is the place of life where the gentle life of God is born out of all the powers of the Father, and in that same place the Holy Spirit proceeds from the Father and Son.

56. Now, those same powers of the Father which stand in the ignition of the light are the Holy Father, and the gentle Father, and the pure birth of God; and the Spirit rising within is the Holy Spirit. However, the sharp birth is the body, within which this holy life is always born.

57. But when the light of God shines through this sharp birth, it becomes entirely gentle, and is like a sleeping person, in whom life is always moving while the body rests quite peacefully.

58. Now, the "ignition" has occurred in this body of nature; for the angels were also created out of this body, and if they had not raised themselves up and ignited themselves in their arrogance, their body would have stood eternally in the still and incomprehensible gentleness—just like in the other principalities of the angels outside of this world. Their spirit would have been born eternally in their body of gentleness, just as the Holy Trinity is born in the body of God, and their indwelling spirit would have been one heart, will, and love with the Holy Trinity; for they were created in the body of God for that very purpose: for the joy of the Godhead.

<column-break/>

59. Lord Lucifer, however, wanted to be the most powerful God himself, and he ignited his own body, waking up the sharp birth of God within it. He set himself against the light heart of God, intending to rule within it with his sharpness—which was, however, impossible.

60. But because he raised himself up and ignited himself against the right of the Godhead, the sharp birth in the body of the Father also rose up against him and took him captive as a wrathful son in the sharpest birth; and therein is now his eternal dominion.

61. But when the Father ignited Himself in the body of sharpness, He did not thereby ignite the holy source where His loving heart is begotten, so that His heart should therefore sit in the source of wrath.

62. No, that is impossible; for the sharp birth cannot grasp the holy and pure one. Rather, the holy and pure one penetrates through the sharpness and begets for Him a new body, which stands again in gentleness.

63. And that same new body is the water of life, which is born when the light penetrates through the wrath; and the Holy Spirit is the shaper within it. Heaven, however, is the distinction between the love and the wrath, and is the seat where the wrath is transformed into love.

64. Now, when you look at the sun and stars, you must not think: "This is the holy and pure God," and you must not resolve to ask or desire anything from them. For they are not the holy God, but rather they are the ignited, strict birth of His body, where love and wrath wrestle with one another.

65. But the holy God is hidden in the midst of all these things in His heaven, and you cannot see or grasp Him. The soul, however, does grasp Him, and the siderial birth <term>siderische Geburt: the "astral" or "starry" birth, referring to the physical and psychological influences of the cosmos on the human being</term> grasps Him halfway; for heaven is the distinction between love and wrath, and that same heaven is everywhere, even in yourself.

66. And so, when you worship the holy God in His heaven, you worship Him in the heaven that is in you; and that same God breaks through your heart with His light (and the Holy Spirit within it), and begets your place into a new body of God, which rules with God in His heaven.

67. For the earthly body that you carry is one body with...

71. I write this as a word which is born in its heaven, where the holy Deity is always begetting itself, where the surging Spirit rises in the flash of life; in that very place this word and this knowledge were born, and have risen in the fire of love through the zealous Spirit of God.

72. I well know what the devil has in mind, for that part of the earnest and strict birth, where love and wrath are set against each other, looks into his heart. 74. But I find that the cleverest devil is set against me; he will stir up mockers who will say that I want to search out <note>original: "ausgrübeln"—to obsessively pry into or brood over mysteries through mere human reason</note> the Deity through my own delusion.

76. Yes, dear proud human, the Deity is also a very gentle, simple, and still Being, and does not brood in the depths of hell and death, but in its heaven, where there is nothing but harmonious gentleness; therefore it would not befit me to do such a thing [as prying].

3. It is also not my intention to write of the tree's nests <note>nests: here referring to the intricate, specialized details of worldly sciences or scholarly theories</note> and overturn their knowledge; likewise, I do not build upon their foundation. Instead, I let their knowledge sit in its own seat, since I have not studied it, and I write in the spirit of my own knowledge of the tree's root, trunk, branches, and fruit, as a laborious servant of his Master, to lay bare the entire tree of this world.

4. Not with the intention of bringing something new onto the path—for I have no command for that—but my knowledge stands in this birth of the stars, in the midst of where life is born and breaks through death, and where the surging Spirit arises and breaks through; and it is in this impulse and surging that I also write.

5. I also know full well that the children of the flesh will mock me and say that I should attend to my calling <note>Böhme was a master shoemaker by trade; his critics frequently argued that a manual laborer had no business writing complex theology.</note> and leave these things alone, and rather occupy myself more diligently with that which fills the bellies of myself and my family, and let those philosophize who have studied it and are called to do so.

6. With this temptation, the devil has also given me many a blow and hammered such thoughts into me myself, so that I have often ventured to abandon this; but my intention became too heavy for me. For whenever I thought of my belly and resolved within myself to abandon this undertaking of mine, the gates of heaven were bolted shut within my knowledge.

7. Then my soul became as anxious as if it were captured by the devil, whereby my reason received many a blow, as if the body were to perish; and the Spirit did not let up until it broke through the dead reason again and burst open the gates of darkness, and regained its seat in its proper place, whereby it then always received new life and power.

8. Through this, I then understand that the Spirit must be proven through the cross and tribulation; likewise, I have not lacked for physical temptation, but have always had to stand in battle, so greatly has the devil been against it.

9. But because I sense that my eternal salvation depends upon it, and that by my neglecting it, the gates of light would be closed to me—which is nonetheless the fortress of my heaven, in which my soul hides from the storm of the devil, and which I have nevertheless conquered with great effort and many a hard storm through the love of GOD, through the breaking-through of my Redeemer and King Jesus Christ—so I will let God prevail and take my fleshly reason <term>fleshly reason: Böhme's term for "Vernunft," the logical, earth-bound intellect that cannot grasp divine mysteries without spiritual illumination</term> captive.

10. And I have chosen for myself the gates of the knowledge of light, and will pursue the Spirit's impulse and knowledge. And even if my animal body were to come to the beggar's staff or even perish, I will no longer ask anything about it, and will say with the royal prophet David: "And even if my body and soul should languish, yet you, O God, are my salvation, my comfort, and my heart's confidence." <note>original: "Psal. 73. 26."</note> Upon you I will venture it, and not resist your Spirit; and even if it hurts the flesh, nevertheless faith must soar over reason in the knowledge of light.

11. Therefore, I will not bury His pound in the earth, but lend it out for interest, so that He might not say to me at the time of His demanding: "You wicked servant, why did you hide my pound in the darkness and not trade with it?" Then He would take back what is mine with interest, and take it away from me entirely and give it to another who had traded much with his pound. Therefore, I will sow; He may water it, and let Him prevail.

14. For gentleness surges against wrath, and wrath against gentleness, and thus there are two distinct kingdoms in the single body of this world.

15. 16. For such reasons, a final day of separation <note>Böhme refers here to the Last Judgment or "Scheidetag," the day of parting.</note> has been determined in God, when love and wrath shall separate from one another.

17. Rather, it is only the old body, which is rightly called corrupt nature.

18. However, the fact that it appears as if there were a blue sphere above the stars, so that the place of this world might be closed off from the holy heaven—as men have thought until now—is not so. Rather, it is the "Upper Water" of nature, which is much brighter than the water beneath the moon; when the sun shines through the deep, it appears as a light blue.

19. No man knows how deep or wide the place of this world is; and even if several physicists or astrologers have undertaken to measure the depth with their compasses, their measuring

25. ### Concerning the Ignition of the Heart or Life of this World.

29. When God had brought the body of this world into a proper <term>form</term> <note>original: "formam"; Latin for form or shape</note> in two days, and had made the heaven as a distinction between love and wrath, then on the third day love pressed through the heaven and through the wrath; at that, the old body in death stirred at once and labored toward birth.

30. For love is hot; it ignited the fire-source, which rubbed against the harsh and cold quality of frozen death until the harsh quality grew hot on the third day, by which the mobility—or the harsh earth—became movable.

31. For everything stood in a <term>fire-shock</term> <note>original: "Feuerschracke"; a sudden, terrifying ignition or burst of energy</note> until the fourth day, when the light of the sun ignited; for the whole body labored in birth, like a woman in labor.

32. The harsh quality had been the grasper or the encloser of life, in which the heat—ignited by the love of God—now labored, and it squeezed out the harsh quality like a dead body; but the heat kept its seat in the middle point of the body and pressed through.

### But here you must specifically notice.

37. Just as far as the middle point has ignited itself, so large is the sun; for the sun is nothing other than an ignited point in the body of nature.

### The Supreme Ground of the Sun and All Planets.

42. Here I will have enough attackers who will know how to find fault; for they will not pay attention to the Spirit, but to their old ways, and will say that the <term>astrologers</term> <note>original: "Astrologi"</note> understand it better; they have written on it. They will look at the great open gates of God like a cow looks at a new barn door.

43. I, dear reader, also understand the opinion of the <term>astrologers</term> well; I have also read a few lines in their writings and know well how they describe the course of the sun and stars. I do not despise it, but hold it for the most part to be good and right.

44. However, that I write some things differently, I do not do out of a whim or a delusion, nor because I doubt whether it is so; I need no doubt here, nor can any human being instruct me in this.

45. For I did not obtain my knowledge from <term>academic study</term> <note>original: "Studio"; Latin for formal study or university training</note>. Indeed, I have read of the order and positions of the seven planets in the books of the <term>astrologers</term> and find them to be quite correct; but the root—how they came to be and where they originated—I cannot learn from men, for they do not know it, nor was I there when God created them.

46. But because the gates of the deep and the portals of wrath, as well as the chamber of death, have been unlocked for me in my spirit through the love of God, the Spirit looks through them. I find, therefore, that the birth of nature still stands today and births itself just as it first took its beginning. Everything that rises up in this world—be it humans, animals, trees, herbs, grass, ore, or whatever it may be—everything rises up in its quality and form, and all life, whether it be evil or good, takes its origin thus.

47. For that is the right of the Godhead: that all life births itself in the body of God in one and the same way; although it happens through many kinds of formations, yet all life has one and the same origin.

<column-break/>

# Aurora: Day-Spring Dawning. Chapter 25.

48. Such knowledge I do not see with fleshly eyes, but with those eyes in which life births itself within me. In that same seat, the gates of heaven and hell stand open to me, and the new man <note>In Böhme’s theology, the "new man" is the regenerated spiritual self, while the "old man" is the fallen, earthly self</note> meditates in the midst of the <term>sidereal birth</term> <note>original: "siderischen"; refers to the influence of the stars (sidereal) on the physical and psychological makeup of a person</note>, and the inner and outermost gates stand open to him.

49. Since he still sticks within the old man of wrath and death, yet also sits in his heaven, he sees through both; in such a way he also sees the stars and elements. For in God there is no place of withholding, as the eye of the Lord sees all.

50. Now, if my spirit did not see through His Spirit, I would be a blind stick; but because I see the gates of God in my spirit and also have the drive for it, I will write correctly according to my vision and regard no human authority.

51. You should not understand this as if my "old man" were a living saint or angel: No, fellow, he sits with all people in the house of wrath and death, and is a constant enemy of God, stuck in his sins and malice like all people, and is full of flaws and defects.

52. But you should know this: that he is stuck in a constant, anxious labor of birth and would gladly be free of the wrath and malice, yet cannot. For he is like the whole house of this world, where love and wrath always wrestle with each other, and the new body is always birthed in the midst of the anxiety. For it must be so, if you wish to be born anew; otherwise, no human reaches <term>rebirth</term> <note>original: "Wiedergeburt"; the central Pietist and Böhmean concept of spiritual transformation</note>.

53. Man here always strives for the soft days of the flesh, and for wealth and beauty, and does not know that he thereby sits in the chamber of death, where the sting of wrath aims at him.

54. Behold, I tell it to you as a word of life, which I take in knowledge of the Spirit in the midst of the birth of the new body of this world—over which Jesus Christ is a ruler and King of men, together with his eternal Father. I also take it before the chair of His throne, where all holy souls of men stand before Him and rejoice before Him: that the desire of the flesh for soft living, being rich, being beautiful, being powerful, is a pure <term>hellish bath of wrath</term> <note>original: "Zornbad"</note> into which you press and run as if you were being pulled in; for there is great danger in it.
