55. But if you wish to know how it is, see, I tell you in a parable: when you have pushed your way into wealth and power according to your heart's desire, it is exactly as if you were standing in deep water, where the water always reached up to your mouth, and there was no ground under your feet; instead, you would have to swim with your hands to protect yourself. At one moment you would be deep in the water, at another in the shallows, and yet you would always be waiting in great terror for the moment you might sink to the bottom—where the water would sometimes enter your mouth—and you would be constantly expecting death.

56. In such a form, and no other, do you sit in your lusts of the flesh. If you will not fight, then you will not conquer; instead, you will be murdered in your soft bed. For man constantly has a powerful army before him that continually fights against him; if he will not defend himself, he is captured and slain.

57. But how can one who swims in deep water defend himself well? He has enough to do just protecting himself from the water, and yet he is nonetheless assaulted by the devils.

58. O danger upon danger! Just as our King Christ says: *It will be hard for a rich man to enter the kingdom of heaven; it will be easier for a camel to go through the eye of a needle than for a rich man to enter the kingdom of heaven.* Matthew 19:24. Mark 10:25.

59. But if anyone wishes to be born anew, he must not give himself as a servant to greed, pride, and his own power to delight himself in the will of his flesh; instead, he must fight and struggle against himself, also against the devil and against all fleshly lusts. He must think of himself as only a servant and a pilgrim on earth, who must wander through the dangerous <term>sea of misery</term> <note>original: "Jammermeer"; a common Baroque metaphor for the suffering of worldly life</note> into another world. There he will be a lord, and his lordship will stand in power and perfect delight and beauty; I say this as a word of the Spirit.

->Now observe.<-

60. The sun has its own royal <term>place</term> <note>original: "Locum"; Latin for place or location</note> for itself and does not depart from the spot where it was first created—unlike what some think, that it runs around the earth day and night. Even some <term>astrologers</term> <note>original: "Astrologi"</note> write this, and some have even presumed to measure how far its circumference might be.

61. This opinion is wrong; rather, the earth turns itself around and runs with the other planets as if in a wheel
<meta>catchword: around</meta>

# Chapter 25. Aurora: Day-Spring Dawning.

around the sun. The earth does not remain standing in one place but runs around the sun once in a year, just as the other planets do under the sun—except Saturn and Jupiter, which cannot do so because of their wide circuit and great height, since they stand high above the sun.

->Now the question arises:<-

->What then is the sun, and the other planets? How did they come to be?<-

62. See, the other planets are distinct <term>bodies</term> <note>original: "Cörper"</note> which have their own physical properties and are not bound to one stationary place, but only to their circuit in which they run. The sun, however, is no such body, but rather it is a <term>place</term> <note>original: "Locus"</note> kindled through the light of God.

->Understand it rightly.<-

63. The place where the sun is, is such a place as any place you might choose above the earth. If God willed to kindle the light through the heat, the whole world would be nothing but such a sun; for that same power in which the sun stands is everywhere. Before the time of the <term>wrath</term> <note>original: "Zorn"; referring to the Fall or the disruption of divine harmony</note>, it was just as bright everywhere in the space of this world as the sun is, though not so unendurable.

64. For the heat was not as great then as it is in the sun; therefore, the light was also very gentle. Because of the cruel fierceness of the sun, the sun is distinguished from the gentleness of God. Therefore, one must not say that the sun is an open gate of the light of God; rather, it is like the light in a human eye: the place of the eye belongs to the body, but the light is distinguished from the body.

65. And even though it arises through the heat in the "water" of the body, it is still something special which the body cannot grasp. Such a distinction also exists between God the Father and the Son.

66. Thus, on the fourth day, in the <term>birth-pang</term> <note>original: "Angstgeburt"; Böhme's term for the agonizing process of creation or manifestation out of the divine darkness</note> of this world, the sun rose in the central point of this world and stands still in its eternal physical place; for it cannot take itself from one place and put itself in another.

67. For it is the only natural light of this world, and outside of it there is no more true light in the house of death: And

...although it appears as if the other stars also shine brightly, it is actually nothing; instead, they all take their brilliance from the Sun, as follows shortly.

### The true birth and origin of the Sun and the planets is constituted as follows:

68. Now when the heaven <note>The "heaven" here refers to the firmament, the boundary between the physical world and the spiritual realm.</note> was made as a distinction between the light of God and the kindled corruption of the body of this world, the body of this world was a dark valley and had no light that shone on the outside beyond the heaven; there, all powers stood as if imprisoned in death, and were in such great agony until they grew hot in the center of the body.

69. But when it happened that the agonizing birth stood so intensely in the heat, the love in the light of God broke through the heaven of distinction and kindled the heat. Then, in the heat, within the water or the "fatness" of the water, the shining light rose up and kindled the heart of the water; and this happened in an instant.

70. For as soon as the light truly seized the **body**, the **body** was captured in the light, and the heat was captured and transformed into a certain **gentleness**, and could no longer remain in such agony.

71. Because the heat was startled by the light, its cruel source of fire subsided and could no longer kindle itself further. Also, the breakthrough of love in the light of God through the heaven did not extend any further with its breaking-through at that time, according to God’s purpose; therefore, the sun did not become any larger.

### Concerning the Planet Mars.

72. But when the sun kindled itself, the cruel **fire-shock** <term>Feuerschrack: Böhme's term for a sudden, violent eruption of energy or "terror" that gives birth to a new state of being</term> drove out from the **location** <note>original: "Loco"</note> of the sun, beyond the location of the sun, like a cruel, tempestuous bolt of lightning; and in its bodily essence, it took with it the fierceness of the fire, from which the water became entirely bitter—and the water is the core or the stock of the shock.

73. Now the **astronomers** <note>original: "Astrologi"; in Böhme's time, astronomy and astrology were not yet separate disciplines.</note> write that the planet Mars stands 15,750 miles high above the sun, which I will allow to stand, as I do not work with the **compass**. <note>The "Circul" or compass represents mathematical and geometric measurement, which Böhme contrasts with his own visionary "knowledge."</note> The swift fire-shock traveled that far from its own place until the light also seized it; there it was also captured by the light, stood still, and occupied that place.

74. That the light did not seize it sooner was caused by the earnest wrath and swift lightning; for it was not held by the light until the light had completely permeated it.

75. There it stands now as a rager, a ranter, and the mover of the entire body of this world; for that is also its office: that with its revolution in the wheel of nature it moves everything, from which all life takes its origin.

### Concerning the Planet Jupiter.

76. Now when the bitter fire-shock was captured by the light, the light in its own power pressed even higher into the deep, until it reached the hard and cold seat of nature. There, the power of the first rising from the sun could go no higher, and it remained sitting there bodily and took up that place as its dwelling.

->But you must understand this thing correctly.<-

77. It was the power of the light that remained standing in this place, which is an entirely gentle, friendly, lovely, and sweet essence. Of this, the **astronomers** write that it stands 7,875 miles high above Mars; but it is the mitigator of the destroyer and raging Mars, and a source of gentleness in all life, and also a source of the water from which life is born, as I will mention hereafter.

78. This is how far the power of life from the sun reached, and no higher; however, the brilliance or radiance, which also has its own power, reaches to the stars and through the entire body of this world.

->But you must understand properly what these two planets became.<-

79. When the power of the heart of God pressed from the eternal, undying fountain-source of the water of life through the heaven of distinction and kindled the water in the **location** of the sun, the flash—understand the fire-flash—drove out from the water; it was entirely terrifying and bitter, and from it, Mars was formed.

80. After that same flash, the power of the light followed swiftly after, like a gentle, uplifting life, and it overtook the fire-shock and mitigated it, so that it became somewhat faint and could no longer break through the deep, but remained standing, trembling.

81. But the power proceeding in the light was much more mighty than the **fire-shock**, and therefore it rose higher than the **fire-lightning**, until it came too deep into the severity of nature; there it immediately became faint and stood still.

But he is like a tenant in that same place, who must always wander about in his rented house; the Sun, however, has a house of its own, whereas no other planet has a house of its own.

83. If one wishes to rightly investigate the birth or beginning of the stars, one must properly know the birth of life—how life is born in a body—for it is all one and the same birth.

84. Whoever does not know and understand this also does not know the birth of the stars, for everything together is one body. Every creature, when life is born within it, carries the record of its birth afterward in its body, just like the birth of the natural body of this world; for all life must be born rightly according to the Deity, just as the Deity always births itself.

85. When one rightly considers and ponders this—which, however, cannot happen without the special enlightenment of the Holy God—one finds at the beginning the harsh, cold, and severe birth, which is a cause of material nature or the formation of a thing.

86. Now, if this severe and cold, sharp, contracting power were not there, there would be no natural or bodily being; likewise, the birth of **GOD** would not consist, and everything would be unsearchable.

87. But in this hard, severe, and cold power stands the material being or the body, in which the spirit of life is then born; and out of that same spirit come the light and the understanding, through which the senses and the **confirmation** <note>original: *Approbirung*; refers to the testing or certifying of natural powers</note> of all powers then arise.

88. For when the light is born, it is born in the midst of the body as a heart or spirit out of all the powers; and there it also stands still in its initial place and goes through all the powers.

89. For just as it is born out of all powers and possesses the wellspring of all powers, so it also brings with its

90. Now, as the record and beginning of life is in a creature, so also is the first rebirth of nature of the new life in the corrupted body of this world.

91. And whoever denies this has neither right understanding nor any knowledge of nature; likewise, his knowledge is not born in **GOD**, but he is a mocker of **GOD**.

92. 95. For its birth is also originally out of all powers; therefore, with its light and heat, it is again a spirit and heart in the whole body of this world.

96. Furthermore, you cannot deny that the gall in a creature is originated from the heart, for it has a vein leading to the heart and is the heart's mobility, from which the heat arises.

101. Thirdly, you also cannot deny that the brain in the head of a creature is not the power of the heart; for all powers rise up from the heart into the brain, and from that, the senses of the heart arise in the brain.

102. The brain in the head takes its origin from the power of the heart.

### Note.

103. After the **fire-shock** of the gall—or of Mars—has departed from the light of life, the power then presses out of the heart through the light of life into the head, into the "strict quality"; and when the power can go no higher, it is captured by that strict birth and dried out by the cold.

104. 105. For the brain sits in the "strict birth," and yet in its own body <note>original Latin: *corpus*</note> it is the gentle power of the heart. It truly signifies the new rebirth, which is born anew in its own heaven in the midst of the severity of death and wrath, pressing through death into life. 106. For when the new spirit in the brain is rightly formed into a creaturely nature <note>original: *verthieret*</note>, it then travels back into its mother—into the heart; then it stands as a perfect spirit or image, or as a newborn person, which in man is called the **soul**.

107. ### The 26th Chapter.
## Concerning the Planet Saturn.

1. **Saturn**, the cold, sharp, and strict, harsh ruler, does not take his beginning and origin from the Sun; for he holds in his power the **chamber of death**, and is a dryer-up of all powers, from which corporeality arises.

2. Just as the Sun is the heart of life and an origin of all spirits in the body of this world, so Saturn is a beginner of all corporeality and tangibility. The entire body of this world stands in the power of these two planets, and no creature or formation—nor any movement—can come to be in the natural body of this world outside of the power of these two.

3. His origin, however, is the earnest, harsh, and strict anxiety of the entire body of this world. For when, at the time the "Wrath" was kindled, the light was extinguished in the outermost birth of this world—which birth is the naturalness or tangibility, or the rising of the birth of all source-spirits <note>original: *Quellsgeister*—the seven fundamental qualities of nature</note>—the harsh quality then stood in its sharpest and strictest birth, and contracted the workings of all source-spirits quite harshly and strictly. From this, the earth and stones came to be; and it was indeed the house of death, or the enclosure of life, in which King **Lucifer** was then captured.

20. The birth or the rising of the seven planets and all the stars is nothing other than the way in which life and the wondrous proportion of the Deity has been born from eternity.

All of nature froze like a body of death in which there was no mobility, and he was forced to remain as an eternal prisoner in the darkness.

22. Now, however, holy **GOD** did not wish to leave this place of His body—understand this as the space of this world—to stand in eternal darkness and shame, nor to leave it to the devils as their own property. Instead, He gave birth to a new regime of light and of all seven source-spirits <note>Böhme’s "Quellgeister" are the seven fundamental qualities or forces of God and nature.</note> of the Deity, which the devil could neither seize nor grasp; nor was it of any use to him.

25. Love, or the Word, or the Heart—that is, the only-begotten Son of **GOD** the Father, who is the light and the gentleness, the love and the joy of the Deity (as He Himself said when He had taken on humanity: *I am the light of the world*, <term>John 8:12</term>)—took the place of this world by the heart. He was reborn in the center of this space, in the spot where the mighty prince and king Lucifer had sat before his fall, and where he had first become a creature.

26. And from this kindled place of the Sun, six distinct qualities specifically emerged and were born, all according to the divine right of birth.

30. 33. From this the planet **Venus** has become, for in the house of death it is an excluder of gentleness or loveliness, and a soft penetrator into the hardness of envy, in which the supreme rule of the bitter heat of **Mars** and the heartfelt sensuality of **Jupiter** becomes desirous.

### Of the Planet Mercury.
35. If one wishes to know thoroughly and properly how the life of man, or the beginning of the planets and stars, and the essence of all essences in the deep of this world came to be, one must properly consider the indwelling birth, or the beginning of life in man.
36. For the same takes such a beginning and rising, and stands in such a life, as the birth of the essence of all essences in the body of this world.
37. For the indwelling wheel of the stars and planets is nothing other than how the birth in the seven nature-spirits of the world has risen, within which images and figures—as well as heavenly fruits—have been figured according to the law of the eternal Deity.
38. Because man is made according to the qualification <note>original: "Qualificirung." #### The Great Deep.
41. Before this mirror, the Spirit summons the doctors, but especially the anatomists and human-flayers <note>original: "Menschenschinder." 42. Because they are found in nature to be murderers and evildoers against the spirit and right of God and nature, the Spirit, which co-qualifies <note>original: "inqualiret." 43. 52. Just as God's eternal, unbeginning birth-governance is, so also is the beginning and rising of the 7 planets and stars, and so also is the rising of man's life.

53. When you search and think about what might be in this world and outside this world, or the Essence of all Essences, then you are speculating or meditating within the whole body of God, which is the Essence of all Essences, and which is an unbeginning Being.

54. However, in His own seat, He has no mobility, rationality, or comprehensibility, but is a dark depth that has neither beginning nor end. 71. Just as the Deep or the house of this world is a dark house, where corporeality is born quite thick, dark, anxious, and half-dead, taking its seething from the planets and stars (which ignite the body in the outermost birth, from which the movement of the elements arises),

121. These are hidden words and are understood only in the language of nature.

122. Moses writes rightly that man was created from earth, but at the time when the mass was held by the Word, the mass was not yet "earth." If it had not been held by the Word, that very hour it would have become black earth, as the cold fire of wrath was already within it.

123. For in that same hour when Lucifer rose up, the Father became enraged in the source-spirits against Lucifer's legions, and the heart of GOD hid itself in the firmament of heaven; there, the <term>Salitter: Böhme's term for the divine "matter" or "saltpeter" of the spiritual world</term>—the very fabric of corporeality—was already burning; for outside of the light is the dark chamber of death.

124. The mass, however, was held in the firmament of heaven so that it would not freeze; for when the heart of GOD looked upon the mass with its hot love, the oil within the mass (which rose out of the water through the fire, and from which the light goes forth, and from which the Spirit of Love rises) caught the heart of GOD and became pregnant with a "young son."

125. That was the seed of love, for one love received the other; the love of the mass received the love from the glance of the heart of GOD, and was thereby infected and became pregnant: and that is the birth of the soul. According to this "Son," man is the image of GOD.

<meta>This page follows the title page of Jacob Böhme’s "On Regeneration" (1779 edition), continuing the explanation of the symbolic frontispiece and introducing the author's preface.</meta>

# Indication of the Title Figure of Rebirth

The + <note>The cross symbol, used here to represent both the physical crucifixion and the spiritual intersection of the divine and human.</note> is the birth of all things; the + is also the rebirth. However, to human reason it is a folly and a strange, wondrous speech, because reason is born from the stars and friendly sunshine and thus neither sees nor knows the eternal death that sticks in its root. But whoever feels death's sting becomes aware of the great distress, so that they must sigh anxiously with David: *Out of the depths I cry to you, O Lord.* <note>original Latin: "De profundis"; here quoting Psalm 130:1.</note> For such a person sees that their will is corrupted, inclined toward sin and malice, and has become apostate from God; therefore, they cry out for the rebirth of a new will.

No one, however, sees or feels death who does not search their soul, nor ground their mind and behold the form of their will—who shapes and moves it, whether good or evil works within it, and which has the upper hand.

For here is the bond of eternity, here is the greatest power; here either God or distress must become manifest. Here the light must shine in divine virtues and joys, or the fire must torment and crucify the soul in hellish vices, in darkness, and in eternal death. For two contrary things cannot exist together: God and Mammon; Christ and Belial; the Lamb with the seven eyes and the Dragon with the seven heads. The enmity must be abolished through reconciliation in obedience, or through eternal separation.

Therefore God has placed the + as the power of the <term>Trinity|Dreyzahl; the triune nature of God</term> in the crucified Christ for the rebirth of a new divine will in the light, and for the separation of the evil will into the darkness. This is so that we may work virtues in Him out of the new birth as good fruits of the Holy Spirit—rather than [working] vices and sins out of the fleshly birth in evil works that remain in death and darkness. For where there is no good will, there the power is in the darkness, in the fire, and the soul has become a <term>misbirth|Mißgeburt; a spiritual deformity or failure of development</term> that can perform no good works.

Therefore, see how rebirth is taught in this little book from divine revelation.

<meta>catchword: Pre-</meta>

<column-break/>

## The Author’s Preface

Although I have sufficiently explained this in my other very deep writings and presented it from its foundation, not everyone has such books in hand, nor is it within everyone’s grasp to understand them. Therefore, I have written a short <term>summary|Summam</term> of the new rebirth for the service of the simple children of Christ and at the request of good friends, to see if anyone might wish to learn to know themselves through it.

2. But whoever desires to search the foundation from which this flows and has the gift of understanding, let them read the book *Of the Threefold Life of Man*; also the three books *Of the Incarnation and Birth of Jesus Christ*; likewise the book *Of the Six Points*; of the *Great Mystery* <note>original: "Mysterio Magno"</note>; of the *Three Worlds*, how they stand within one another as one, yet make <term>three principles|drey Principia</term>, that is, three births or beginnings, etc.; also the book *Of the Three Principles* <note>original: "de Tribus Principiis"</note>. There they will find whatever they may ask, as high as a human mind can soar, as well as in the *Forty Questions of the Soul*.

3. This, then, I have written for the hungry and thirsty hearts seeking Christ’s fountain, as my fellow members in the Spirit of Christ. But to the scoffers I have written nothing; for they have their book within themselves, with which they drive the children of Christ under the cross, and against their own will they must be the servants of Christ's children, even if they do not understand it.

# Chapter 1.

->1.<-

Christ spoke: Unless you turn back and become like children, you shall not see the kingdom of God. And again in <term>John 3:5</term>, he says to <term>Nicodemus</term>: Unless someone is born anew from water and Spirit, they cannot enter the kingdom of God. For what is born of the flesh is flesh, and what is born of the Spirit is spirit. Scripture clearly testifies that the fleshly, natural man perceives nothing of the Spirit of God; it is foolishness to him, and he cannot grasp it. <note>Referencing 1 Corinthians 2:14, a favorite verse of Böhme to highlight the limits of human reason compared to spiritual enlightenment.</note>

2. Since we all possess flesh and blood and are moreover mortal—as is evident before our eyes—and yet Scripture also says that we are temples of the Holy Spirit who dwells within us, and that the kingdom of God is within us, and that Christ must take shape within us, and that he wants to give us his flesh as food and his blood as drink. And it says further: Whoever does not eat the flesh of the Son of Man has no life within them. Thus we must earnestly consider what kind of person exists within us who is similar to and capable of receiving the Godhead.

3. For of the mortal flesh, which turns to earth and lives in the vanity of this world,
<meta>catchword: and</meta>

<column-break/>

<page-num>7</page-num>
<header>The First Chapter.</header>

and constantly blasphemes against God, it cannot be said that it is the temple of the Holy Spirit; much less that the new rebirth occurs in this earthly flesh, seeing as it dies and decays, and is a constant house of sin.

4. But if it nonetheless remains true that a true Christian is born of Christ, and that the new rebirth is a temple of the Holy Spirit who dwells within us—and that only the new man, born of Christ, enjoys the flesh and blood of Christ—then being a Christian is no simple matter. <note>The original German "schlecht" here means "simple" or "slight," rather than "bad."</note> And Christianity does not consist merely of history <note>Böhme uses "History" (Historie) to refer to "book-learning" or mere factual knowledge of the Bible that lacks an internal, living experience of God.</note>—that we simply know it and appropriate that knowledge, saying only: "Christ died for us, and has broken death within us and turned it into life; he has paid the debt for us, and we need only comfort ourselves with this and believe firmly that it has happened."

5. For we find within ourselves that sin is alive, desiring, and active in the flesh, and that it is at work. Thus, the new rebirth from Christ must be something else, which does not participate in the sinful flesh and does not desire sin.

For <term>St. Paul</term> says: That in those who are in <term>Christ Jesus</term>, there is nothing damnable. And further: Should we, who are Christians, still be found to be sinners? Far be it; for we have died to sin in Christ.

Thus, a person of sin is not a temple of the Holy Spirit; and yet there is no person who does not sin. For the Scripture says: God has confined all under sin. <note>Referencing Galatians 3:22.</note> **Likewise.** Before you, no living soul is righteous, if you should count their sins. The righteous falls seven times a day: <note>Proverbs 24:16.</note> And yet this must not be understood to mean that the "righteous" part falls and sins, but rather the mortal and sinful part of the person.

7. For a Christian's righteousness is in Christ; that part cannot sin. For **St. Paul** says: Our conduct <note>The original term *Wandel* can mean one's way of life, conduct, or citizenship, as in Philippians 3:20.</note> is in heaven, from whence we await the Savior Jesus Christ. If our conduct is in heaven, then heaven must be within us. Christ dwells in heaven; if we are then his temple, then that same heaven must be within us.

8. But if sin nevertheless assails us—in which the devil has an entrance to us and within us—then hell must also be within us, for the devil dwells in hell. And wherever he is, he is in hell and cannot come out of it. Even if he were to possess a person, he still dwells within that person in hell, as if in <term>God’s wrath</term> <note>Böhme views "God's wrath" not just as an emotion, but as a spiritual "quality" or "source-center" that constitutes the environment of hell.</note>.

9. Now we must rightly consider what and how a person is: And that a true Christian is not merely a "historical" new person—meaning it is not enough that we simply acknowledge Christ and believe that he is God's Son and

<column-break/>

<page-num>9</page-num>

<sig>A 4</sig>

has paid the debt for us. For it is not a matter of an outwardly <term>imputed righteousness</term> <note>A theological term meaning righteousness credited to a person’s account from the outside; Böhme argues this is insufficient without an internal change.</note>—that we only believe it has happened—but rather an inborn, childlike righteousness. Just as the flesh must die, so also must the life and the will of sin die. One must become like a child that knows nothing and sighs only for the mother who gave it birth. In this way, a Christian's will must enter entirely back into the mother—that is, into the Spirit of Christ—and become a child in its own selfhood, its own willing and its own power. There, the will and desire are directed only toward the mother, and a new will and obedience must rise from death out of the Spirit of Christ, in righteousness, which no longer desires sin.

10. For the will that allows vanities into itself and desires them is not reborn; and yet, if a will remains in the reborn person that yearns for vanity and sins, then we must rightly consider the "image" of the person to see how the new rebirth occurs. This is because it does not happen in the mortal flesh, and yet it happens truly within us, in flesh and blood, in water and spirit, as the Scripture says.

->This is now to be considered as follows.<-

13. Likewise, we see how the light shines in the darkness, and the darkness does not grasp the light, yet they dwell one within the other. We also have an example of this in the four elements, which in their original state are only one single element; that element is neither hot nor cold, neither dry nor wet, and yet through movement it divides itself into four properties: fire, air, water, and earth.

# On the New Rebirth.

## Chapter 4.

->I.<-

Here we now rightly understand our New Rebirth, how we can be and remain the Temple of God; yet at this time, according to our outward humanity, [we are] also sinful mortal men. Christ has burst open and unlocked the gate of our inward heavenly humanity, which was shut in Adam, within the human <term>essence</term> <note>original: "Essenz." In this context, it refers to the fundamental spiritual substance of a person that was corrupted in the Fall but remains capable of restoration.</note>; and it now rests solely upon this: that the soul leads its will out of the <term>vanity</term> <note>original: "Eitelkeit." This refers to the temporary, empty, and illusory nature of the physical world as opposed to eternal spiritual truth.</note> of the corrupted flesh and enters through this open gate into the Spirit of Christ.

2. There must be a great and powerful earnestness; not merely a learning and knowing, but a hunger and a great thirst for the Spirit of Christ; for knowledge alone is not faith. Rather, the hunger and thirst for that which I desire—so that I <term>imagine</term> <note>original: "einbilde." For Böhme, imagination is not just "fantasy," but a formative spiritual act where the soul "images" or "forms" itself into what it desires.</note> it into myself and grasp and take it as my own with that imagination—that is faith.

3. The will must depart from the vanity of the flesh and surrender itself voluntarily into the suffering and death of Christ, and into all the mockery of vanity—which mocks him because he departs from his own house in which he was born—and no longer desire vanity, but merely desire the love of God in Christ Jesus.

4. And in such hunger and desire, he imprints the Spirit of Christ within himself, with His heaven-

ly corporeality: That is, his great hunger and desire grasp the Body of Christ as the heavenly essence into his faded image, within which the Word of God’s power is the working life.

5. The soul’s hunger leads its desire through the shattered property of its humanity (the heavenly part) which had faded in Adam: which the sweet love-fire in the death of Christ shattered, when the death of that same true heavenly humanity was broken. Through this desire, the soul’s hunger took the holy heavenly being—as the heavenly corporeality which fills the Father at all ends, and is near to all, and through all—into its own faded corporeality; and thereby the faded heavenly body rises up in the power of God, in the sweet name of **JESUS** <note>original: "JESU." The author emphasizes the name as a source of power.</note>.

6. And that same awakened heavenly spiritual body is a member of Christ and the Temple of the Holy Spirit, a true dwelling of the Holy Trinity, as Christ promised when He said: *We will come to you and make our home in you* <note>original: "Wir wollen zu Euch kommen, und Wohnung in euch machen." A translation of John 14:23.</note>. That same essence of that same life eats Christ’s flesh and drinks His blood: for Christ’s Spirit—as the Word that made itself visible with the humanity of Christ, out of and within our faded humanity, through the being of the outward man of this world—eats its holy essence into its fiery essence; every spirit eats of its own body.

## Chapter Four.

7. And so now the soul eats of this sweet, holy, heavenly food, and it is ignited by the great love in the name of JESUS. From this, its fire of anxiety becomes a great triumph, and the true Sun rises within it, in which it is born with a different will. And here is the "Wedding of the Lamb," which we heartily wish that <term>nominal Christianity</term> <note>original: "Titul- und Mauls-Christenheit." Literally "Title- and Mouth-Christianity," referring to those who are Christians in name and speech only, without inner transformation.</note> might experience for once, moving from the <term>historical account</term> <note>original: "Historie." Böhme distinguishes between "history" (knowing the biblical stories intellectually) and "essence" (experiencing the spiritual reality within oneself).</note> into the actual essence.

8. But the soul does not obtain the <term>pearl</term> <note>original: "Perlein." A reference to the "Pearl of Great Price" from the Parables of Jesus, symbolizing the highest spiritual gift or the presence of the divine within the soul.</note> of holy power during this lifetime, because it still possesses the property of the outer, animal flesh in the outer man as its own. The power of Christ, which is wedded in the Wedding of the Lamb, immerses itself into the Heavenly Image—as into the essence of the heavenly man, who is Christ’s temple—and not into the <term>fire-breath</term> <note>original: "Feuer-Athem." In Böhme's theology, the soul has a "fiery" nature of desire and strength, which must be tempered by the "light" of divine love.</note> of the soul, which for this entire time remains firmly bound to the outer kingdom, to the bond of vanity and the breath of the air, and is in great danger.

9. It [the Spirit of Christ] often casts its rays of love into the soul, from which the soul receives its light; but the Spirit of Christ does not surrender itself to the fire-breath during this time, but only to the <term>breath of light</term>, which was extinguished in Adam. Within that is the temple of Christ, for it is the true holy heaven.

10. Therefore, understand us correctly regarding what the New Rebirth is and how it happens: The outer, earthly, mortal man is not born anew during this time—neither the outer flesh nor the outer part of the soul. They both remain in the <term>vanity</term> <note>original: "Eitelkeit." This refers to the transitory, empty, and fallen state of the material world.</note> of their will that was awakened in Adam. They love their mother in whose body they live—namely, the governance of this outer world—and within that, the "birth of sin" is manifest.

11. The outer man in soul and flesh—meaning the outer part of the soul—has no divine will and understands nothing of God, as the Scripture says: *The natural man perceives nothing of the Spirit of God,* etc. <note>Refers to 1 Corinthians 2:14: "But the natural man receiveth not the things of the Spirit of God: for they are foolishness unto him..."</note>

12. But the fire-breath of the inner world, once it is enlightened, does understand it. It has its great groaning, lamenting, hungering, and thirsting for the sweet wellspring of Christ. It refreshes itself through hungering and desiring—which is true faith—in the sweet wellspring of Christ, from His new body of heavenly essence, like a hungry branch on the vine of Christ.

13. And this is the reason why the fiery soul cannot reach perfection during this time: because it stands bound to the outer bond of vanity, through which the Devil constantly shoots his poisonous rays at it and sifts it, so that it sometimes worships him and becomes poisoned. From this, misery and anxiety arise, so that [it]...

A servant girl in the house knows well what the mistress likes, but that does not make her an heir to the mistress's goods: The devil also knows that there is a God, but that does not make him an angel again; but if the servant girl in the house marries the mistress's son, then she may well come to the inheritance of the mistress's goods.

2. This is also how our Christianity is to be understood: The **Children of History** <note>original: "Historien Kinder." 3. 8. Then if someone says, "I have the will, and would gladly do good, but I have earthly flesh which holds me back so that I cannot; but I shall be saved by grace, for the sake of Christ’s **merit** <note>original: "Verdienst." In this context, it refers to the spiritual credit or "work" Christ performed on behalf of humanity.</note>; for I surely comfort myself with his suffering and merit; he will accept me out of grace, without any merit of my own, and forgive my sin": Such a person acts just like one who knew of a good food for his health but did not eat it, eating instead a poisonous one from which he became sick and died.

9. What does it help the soul to know the way to God and yet not want to walk it, but instead walk the wrong path and fail to reach God? What does it help the soul to comfort itself with the **sonship** <term>sonship (Kindschaft)</term> of Christ, his suffering and death, and to flatter itself, if it will not enter into the childlike birth, so that it might be born a true child out of Christ’s Spirit, out of his suffering, death, and resurrection? Certainly and truly, this "tickling" and flattering oneself with Christ’s merit, without the true inborn sonship, is false and a lie, let whoever will teach it.

10. This "comforting" belongs to the penitent sinner who is in the struggle against sin and God’s wrath, when **temptations** <note>original: "Anfechtungen." A term often used by Jakob Böhme and Martin Luther to describe spiritual trials or "assaults" from the devil that test a person's faith.</note> come and the devil besets the soul; there, the soul should wrap itself entirely in the life and death of Christ, and in his merit.

11. Christ has indeed earned it alone, but he did not earn it as a "merit" for which a reward is given based on labor—that he might gift us the sonship from the outside through his merit and thus take us into sonship. No, he is himself the merit; he is the open gate through death; through that gate we must enter. But he does not take "animals" into his merit, but rather those who turn back and become as children.

12. Those same children who come to him are his earned reward. For he also spoke thus: "Father, the

<meta>catchword: Men-</meta>

men were yours, and you have given them to me, and I give them eternal life." But now, the life of Christ is given to no one unless he comes into Christ’s spirit, into his humanity, suffering, and merit, and is born in his merit as a true child of the merit. We must be born out of his merit and put on the merit of Christ in his suffering and death; not from the outside, with lip-service <note>original: "Mundheucheley." Literally "mouth-hypocrisy" or saying the right words without internal belief.</note>, only by comforting oneself while remaining a foreign child of a foreign **essence** <term>essence (Essenz)</term>. No, the foreign essence does not inherit the sonship, but the inborn essence inherits it.

13. This same inborn essence is not of this world, but in heaven, of which **St. Paul** says: *Our citizenship is in heaven*; the childlike essence walks in heaven, and heaven is within the person. But if heaven is not open within a person, and he only stands before heaven flattering himself, saying: "I am still outside, but Christ will take me in by grace; his merit is indeed mine"—such a person, according to the outer man, is in vanity and sin, and with the soul, he is in hell, as if in God's wrath.

14. Therefore, learn to understand correctly what Christ has taught us and done. He is our heaven; he must take a form within us if we are to be in heaven. Thus, the internal "soul-man" is then in heaven with the Holy Body of Christ, as in the new birth, and the external mortal man is in the world. Of this, Christ says: *My sheep are in my hand, no one can pluck them out of my hand; the Father who gave them to me is greater than all.*

...but from our little pearl, from Christian essence and **knowledge** <term>knowledge (Wissenschaft): in this context, it refers not to modern science, but to a deep, experiential spiritual understanding or "knowingness."</term>, not from the husk and the histories, but from a childlike spirit, from the knowledge of Christ, as a vine on the branch of Christ, from the measure of that knowledge opened within us in God's counsel.

2. They bind us now to the histories, to the stone churches, which would indeed be good in their value if one also brought the temple of Christ into them.

3. They teach that their absolution is a forgiveness of sins; *Likewise* <note>original: "Item"</note>, that the Lord’s Supper takes away sins; *Likewise*, that the Spirit of God is poured in through the office of preaching.

4. All of this would have its place if it were explained correctly, and if one did not only hang upon the **husks** <note>The "husk" (Hülse) is a favorite metaphor of the author for the external form of religion—scripture, ritual, and physical buildings—which he contrasts with the "kernel" or "pearl" of internal truth.</note>. Many a person goes to church for 20 or 30 years, hears preaching, uses the Sacrament, allows themselves to be absolved, and is yet a beast of the devil and of vanity, just like any other. A beast goes into the church and to the Lord’s Supper, and a beast comes away from it again. How shall he eat, who has no mouth? How shall he hear, who has no hearing? Can someone enjoy a food that is locked away from his mouth? How shall he drink, who is far from the water? What does it help me that I go into the stone walls of a church and fill my ears with an empty breath? Or go to the Lord’s Supper and feed only the earthly mouth, which is mortal and perishable? How does that help the soul, which is an immortal life, if the **animal-like man** <term>animal-like man (thierische Mensch): refers to the person who lives only by physical senses and instincts, lacking spiritual awakening.</term> observes the manner of Christ's practice, if the soul cannot reach the jewel of that practice? For *St. Paul* <note>original: "S. 5. The covenant stands; it is proven in the practice. Christ offers us his Spirit in his word—as in the preached word—and in the Sacraments his body and blood, and in brotherly reconciliation his absolution.

6. But what does it help that a beast listens there, and has no hearing for the internal, living word? Nor has it a vessel into which it can lay the word so that it might bring forth fruit? Of such people Christ says: "The devil tears the word from their hearts, so that they do not believe and are not saved." Why? Because the word finds no place in their hearing where it might take hold.

7. So it is also with absolution; what does it help if someone says to me: "I announce to you the absolution of your sins," while the soul still lies completely locked in sins? He who says such a thing to a closed-off sinner is in error, and he who accepts it without the voice of God within him also deceives himself.

8. No one can forgive sin except God alone; the preacher’s mouth does not have forgiveness in its own power. The Spirit of Christ has it in the voice of the priest’s mouth, provided he is also a Christian. But what did it help those who heard Christ teaching on earth, when he spoke: "Come to me, all you who are weary and burdened, I will refresh you"? <note>A reference to Matthew 11:28.</note> What did it help those who heard it and were not weary? Where would the refreshment remain? Since they had dead ears and only heard the external Christ, but not the word of divine power, they were not refreshed. The hypocritical absolution helps an animal-like man just as much; so also do the *Sacraments* help him.

9. In the *Sacraments* it is now open, as it is in the teaching office. The covenant is proven; the measuring of the soul occurs, but in the quality of the soul's mouth. Just as the external beast receives bread and wine—which it could also eat at home—so the fiery soul now receives the Testament according to its quality, as in the wrath of God. It receives the essence of the eternal world, but according to the quality of the dark world. As the mouth is, so is the food that belongs in the mouth. ...see a serious, strict judge, and the saints see him as a dear Emmanuel <term>Emmanuel: A Hebrew name meaning "God with us," used here to describe Christ as a nearby, loving companion rather than a distant judge.</term>.

10 Against the ungodly, God's wrath stands open in his testaments; but toward the holy, heavenly loveliness stands open, and within it, the power of Christ in the holy name of Jesus. 11 In the saints, the Sacraments do not simply "take away" or "forgive" the sinner through the ritual alone; rather, it is like this: When Christ rises, then Adam dies in the **serpent's essence** <note>original: "Schlangen Essenz." 12 It is the same with the office of preaching: The ungodly person hears what the outer soul of the outer world preaches, and he receives it as a **history** <note>By "history," the author means a mere story or factual account that lacks living power or personal spiritual impact.</note>. But if there is any "stubble or straw" in the sermon, he sucks the vanity from it, and his soul sucks from it the false poison and murder of the devil. With this, the soul tickles itself, delighting in hearing how it can judge other people. But if the preacher is also "dead" <note>Spiritually lifeless or lacking true divine inspiration.</note> and sows poison and reproach from his own whims, then the devil is teaching and the devil is hearing. That same teaching is captured in the ungodly heart and brings forth ungodly fruit. Because of this, the world has become a "murder-den" of the devil, so that from both the teacher and the listener, there is nothing inside but vain mocking, blaspheming, scorning, word-wrangling, and biting at the **husk** <note>The "husk" (Hülse) represents the external shell of religion—words and rituals—without the inner "kernel" of truth.</note>.

13 But in the holy teacher, the Holy Spirit teaches; and in the holy listener, the Spirit of Christ hears through the soul and the divine housing of the divine sound. The external hearing goes into the external and works in the external; and the internal hearing goes into the internal and works in the internal.

## The 7th Chapter.

->1.<-

**A** true human being, who is born anew in the Spirit of Christ, exists in the simplicity of Christ and has no quarrel with anyone over religion. He has enough conflict within himself against his animalistic, evil flesh and blood. He always considers himself a great sinner and fears God, for his sins stand openly and are under judgment; for the **Turba** <term>Turba: A Latin term used by the author to describe the "turmoil" or "disturbance" of the divine order—a state of wrath and confusion that traps the soul.</term> encloses them within itself, and the wrath of God scolds him to his face as a guilty person. But the love of Christ breaks through and drives them out, just as the day swallows the night.

2. For the ungodly, however, their sins rest in the sleep of death, and they sprout from the abyss and bear fruit in hell.

3. Christendom in Babel quarrels over **knowledge** <note>original: "Wissenschaft." In the 17th century, this referred to systematic theological doctrine or intellectual study rather than modern laboratory science.</note>—how one should serve, honor, and recognize God, and what He might be according to His essence and will. They poorly teach that whoever does not agree with them in every point of doctrine and opinion is no Christian, but a heretic.

4. Now, I would certainly like to see how one could bring all their sects together into one that could call itself the Christian Church, since they are altogether nothing but despisers of one another, where each crowd slanders the other and cries them out as false.

5. But a Christian belongs to no sect; he can live in the midst of sects and even appear at their worship services, and yet he clings to no sect. He has only one single knowledge, which is Christ within him. He seeks only one
<meta>catchword: Way,</meta>

---

<page-num>43</page-num>
<header>The Seventh Chapter.</header>

Way, which is the desire that he might always gladly do and teach what is right, and he places all his knowing and willing into the life of Christ. He sighs and wishes forever that God's will might be done in him and His kingdom be made manifest within him. He kills sin in the flesh daily and hourly: for the **seed of the woman** <note>A biblical reference to Genesis 3:15, interpreted here as the "inner person" in Christ who overcomes the devil.</note>, as the inner person in Christ, constantly treads upon the head of the devil in vanity.

6. His faith is a desire for God, which he has wrapped in a certain hope; therein he ventures upon the words of the promise. He lives and dies within it, and yet, according to the true person, he never dies at all. For Christ also says: *Whoever believes in me shall never die, but has pressed through from death to life* <note>original: "Wer an mich gläubet, wird nimmermehr sterben..." A paraphrase of John 11:25-26 and John 5:24.</note>. Also, *Streams of living water shall flow from him* <note>original: "Es werden Ströme des lebendigen Wassers von ihm fließen." Referring to John 7:38.</note>, as good teaching and works.

7. Therefore I say, everything that bites one another and quarrels over the **letter** <note>The "letter" refers to the literal text of scripture or rigid dogma, as opposed to the living "spirit."</note> is Babel. The letters all stand in one root, which is the Spirit of God: just as many kinds of flowers all stand in the earth and grow alongside one another. None bites the other over colors, scent, or taste; they let the earth and sun, as well as rain and wind, heat and cold, do with them what they will, yet each one grows in its own essence and property. So it is with the children of God; they have many kinds of gifts and knowledge, but all from One Spirit. They rejoice alongside one another in the great wonders of God and thank the Most High in His wisdom. Why should they quarrel for long over Him in whom they live and are, and whose essence they themselves are?

8. It is the greatest folly in Babel that the devil has made the world quarrel over religion—that they quarrel over self-made opinions, over the letter—even though the Kingdom of God stands in no opinion, but in power and love. Christ also said, and left it to his disciples at the last: *They should love one another; by this everyone would know that they were his disciples, just as he had loved them* <note>original: "Sie sollten einander lieben..." Referring to John 13:34-35.</note>. If people sought after love and righteousness as much as they sought after opinions, there would be no strife on earth: we would live as children in our Father, and would need no law or order.

9. For God is served by no law, but by obedience alone. Laws exist because of the wicked, who do not

## The 8th Chapter.

->1.<-

The whole Christian religion consists in this: that we learn to recognize what we are, where we have come from, how we have entered out of unity into disunity, malice, and injustice, and how we have awakened the same within ourselves. Secondly, where we were in the unity when we were children of God. Thirdly, how we are now in disunity, in conflict and reluctance. Fourthly, where we are traveling to out of this fragile being: where we intend to go with the immortal, and also then with the mortal.

2. In these four points stands our whole religion: to learn to come out of disunity and vanity, and to enter again into **One Tree** <note>The "One Tree" is a recurring image for Christ or the unified body of believers, contrasting with the "fragmented" nature of fallen humanity.</note>, from which we all came in Adam, which is Christ in us. We need not quarrel over anything, nor do we have any conflict; let each one only learn to practice how he may enter again into the love of God and of his brother.

3. Christ's testaments <term>testamenta: The Greek and Latin term for "covenants" or "wills," referring here to the sacraments and the spiritual legacy of Christ.</term> are absolutely nothing else than a brotherly alliance, that God binds himself with us in Christ, and we in him. All teaching should point there, as well as all willing, living, and doing; whatever teaches or does otherwise is Babel and fables, merely a carving of pride, a useless judgment, and a distraction.

-ging spirit in your gift, which does not enter into God's Spirit, into the hope of faith; therefore your gift is only half-given, and you have only half a reward for it.

9. This is also to be understood regarding receiving: If one gives in faith in divine hope, he blesses his gifts in his faith; but he who receives them ungratefully and grumbles in spirit, he curses them in the enjoyment of them: thus everyone keeps what is his; what he sows, that he also reaps.

10. This is also true in the office of teaching: what one sows, that he also reaps. If one sows good seed from Christ's Spirit, it takes root in the good heart and bears good fruit; but in the godless, who are not capable of this, the wrath of God is provoked. 13. Therefore it is highly necessary for the children of God that they pray earnestly and learn to recognize this false building, departing from it with their minds, and not also helping to build it up and persecuting the children of God themselves: lest they be delayed in the kingdom of God and be led astray. As Christ spoke to the Pharisees: **Woe to you Pharisees, you travel over land and water to make one convert to Judaism, and when he has become one, you make him a child of hell, twice as much as you are yourselves.** Which truly also happens in the current factions and sects, among the screamers and teachers of strife.

<header>On the New Rebirth.</header>

14. Therefore, I wish—using the gifts revealed to me by God—to faithfully warn all children of God who intend to be members of Christ <term>members of Christ</term> <note>Following the biblical metaphor from the Epistles of Paul, where the community of believers is described as the "Body of Christ," with each individual acting as a "member" or limb.</note> against such gruesome quarreling and warmongering <note>The original German term is *Blutpaucken*, literally "blood-drumming." This refers to the provocative beating of drums to incite violence, or more figuratively, to the loud, aggressive theological disputes that lead to persecution and bloodshed.</note>. I urge them to withdraw from fraternal strife and to strive simply <note>The original *schlecht* here carries the older meaning of "plainly" or "straightforwardly" rather than its modern meaning of "bad."</note> for love and righteousness toward all people.

15. For if one is a good tree, he should also bear good fruit: even if he must sometimes suffer the swine <note>A common scriptural metaphor for the ungodly or those who lack spiritual discernment, who "trample" and "devour" what is holy without understanding its value.</note> devouring his fruit, he should nonetheless remain a good tree and always desire to work with God; he must not let himself be overcome by any evil. In this way, he stands in God’s field and bears fruit for God’s table, which he shall enjoy eternally. Amen.

->T H E  E N D.<-

<image-desc>A woodcut vignette at the bottom of the text depicts two open books lying on the ground surrounded by plants and flowers. A large palm frond leans over them from the left. In the upper right, a radiant sun with a face (a representation of the divine) shines down upon the books and flora.</image-desc>

<summary>This concluding page of the treatise exhorts believers to abandon religious conflict and "fraternal strife" in favor of love and righteousness. It uses the metaphor of the soul as a "good tree" that continues to bear divine fruit even when faced with worldly persecution.</summary>

<keywords>New Rebirth, Body of Christ, pacifism, spiritual fruit, love and righteousness, religious conflict, Jacob Böhme, mystical agriculture</keywords>
